title: Detransitioner says she was denied opportunity to deliver Talarico a message at CNN town hall
description: Soren Aldaco alleges she was denied an opportunity by CNN to attend a town hall and ask Texas Senate candidate James Talarico questions about his position on gender surgeries.
content: Media Detransitioner says she was denied opportunity to deliver Talarico a message at CNN town hall Detransitioner tells 'Katie Miller Podcast' Talarico should sit face-to-face with someone like her By Hanna Panreck Fox News Published October 26, 2026 7:52pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Detransitioner on what she wanted to ask James Talarico at CNN town hall Soren Aldaco, a 23-year-old detransitioner, alleged during an interview on "The Katie Miller Podcast" wanted to ask James Talarico a question about his past rhetoric on gender at a CNN town hall event this month but didn't get the opportunity. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Detransitioner Soren Aldaco said in an interview Monday that she tried to attend a CNN town hall with Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico earlier this month, but organizers did not respond to her request until the night before the event and allegedly told her she could not participate. During an interview on "The Katie Miller Podcast," host Katie Miller asked Aldaco, a 23-year-old detransitioner who alleged she was groomed online and subsequently pursued medical treatment as a teenager, about her criticism of Talarico and what her message to him would be. "He needs to have a long-form conversation, a real face-to-face with someone like me. And, you know, I tried to when he did the CNN town hall, where he did the 'prove me wrong' [Steven] Crowder format, engaging with constituents, right? We tried to get me in that room to talk to him about this issue and to be able to give him my message through conversation, which I think is most effective. And they actually didn't get back to us until the evening before and said, 'No, we can't get you in that room,' like 'you can't talk to him,'" Aldaco said. TALARICO DISMISSES PAST COMMENTS ABOUT GOD AND GENDER AS 'PROVOCATIVE' WHILE INVOKING CHARLIE KIRK Detransitioner Soren Aldaco claims she was barred from asking Senate candidate James Talarico questions about gender surgery at a CNN town hall. (Soren Aldaco/Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News via Getty Images) CNN and Jubilee Media hosted a town hall with Talarico on Oct. 14, where he faced questions from the audience, as well as questions from moderator Erin Burnett. The Texas Supreme Court ruled on June 26 that Aldaco had not missed the deadline to pursue her claims against a therapist and counseling provider, reversing a lower court's finding that her lawsuit was "time-barred" under the state's two-year statute of limitations for healthcare liability claims. Miller asked her guest what she thinks Talarico is getting wrong in his positions on gender transition policies. "I think he is failing to acknowledge the repercussions of how he's been wrong in the past, because I know he's said, 'Well, I said there were six genders, and I was incorrect. I was misinformed.' And it's like, OK, but what are the repercussions of that? Because I tried to get in contact with you across five bills, four years and two sessions, and you wouldn't talk to me about bills that would have even helped people who still currently identify as trans," Aldaco told Miller. CNN did not return Fox News Digital's request for comment. Talarico was asked about his past comments referring to God as "nonbinary" and using the Bible to justify his pro-choice stance on abortion during the CNN town hall. TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux Theater on Aug. 31, 2026, in Kerrville, Texas. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images) "You've said some concerning things in the past kind of related to faith and social issues. Things such as God is nonbinary, questions about how many genders there really are and your justifications using the Bible for abortion," Sarah Gardner, a Republican small business owner, said to Talarico. "And so, I think that's led a lot of Christian voters to question the authenticity of your faith. And I wanted to ask you a very direct question. Do you believe that the Bible is the absolute source of truth and God's final authoritative word, even when our culture says otherwise?" she asked. Talarico responded, "Yes." TALARICO CAMP SAYS HE OPPOSES TRANS ATHLETES IF UNSAFE OR UNFAIR BUT ACCUSES POLITICIANS OF BULLYING STUDENTS Video "And I think it's important to remember that even the early church, the disciples who actually knew Jesus of Nazareth, the early church, we often talk about as a singular body when, in reality, was more like early churches because there was a lot of disagreement, there was a lot of debate," he said. Talarico then went on to explain his past comments as being "provocative," drawing a parallel to his own interpretation of scripture to Charlie Kirk’s. During an interview last week, Talarico blamed Republican extremism for prompting some of his past controversial remarks, including assertions that God is "nonbinary" and that there are six biological sexes, arguing that those weren't issues he ran for office to discuss. "I was put in a position where I had to fight back against that extremism. So, you mentioned some of my comments on gender or on issues affecting trans people. It's not like I ran for the legislature to talk about these things. Again, if you go back to my first session, I wanted to talk about public education, which is why I ran in the first place," he said, pointing to other issues on which he ran. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Video He continued, "It's kind of ironic that they're clipping these things to make it sound like I'm the one who was talking about this when, in reality, it was the Republican extremists at the Capitol who were obsessed with talking about trans issues, obsessed with talking about people's private parts. That wasn't me. That was them that changed." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Talarico's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News' Robert McGreevy contributed to this report. Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News. title: Raiders coach keeping Kirk Cousins as starting QB despite 4-game losing streak, Fernando Mendoza waiting
description: Kirk Cousins leads the NFL with 16 passing touchdowns, but the Las Vegas Raiders' four-game skid has fans calling for Fernando Mendoza's debut.
content: OutKick Raiders coach keeping Kirk Cousins as starting QB despite 4-game losing streak, Fernando Mendoza waiting Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, will continue developing behind Cousins ahead game against the Jets By Scott Thompson OutKick Published October 26, 2026 7:50pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Texans are 'written off' after losing to Giants, are Bo Nix-Broncos back, Vikings legit? | FTF Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, Kevin Wildes and Greg Jennings react to the New York Giants' big win against the Houston Texans and if the Minnesota Vikings are legit Super Bowl contenders with their 6-0 start. They then debate whether it is time for the Las Vegas Raiders to bench Kirk Cousins for Fernando Mendoza and if the Denver Broncos have finally turned a corner. The crew then break down whether the Kansas City Chiefs or San Francisco 49ers have the more concerning first loss. Everything was going well in Sin City to start the 2026 NFL season, as Kirk Cousins led Klint Kubiak’s new regime to a 3-0 start for the first time since 2021. But the Raiders have lost their last four games, including their most recent 35-21 defeat to the Los Angeles Rams, who got back on track Sunday. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. With the recent skid, some begged the question whether Kubiak would change quarterbacks considering Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, has yet to hear his number called in his rookie season. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak talks to reporters following an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Las Vegas. (AP Photo/David Becker) Kubiak squashed that speculation on Monday. "[Cousins is] playing at a very high level, and he’s got to continue to do that for us to win," Kubiak told reporters, via ESPN. "We got to keep helping all the surrounding areas. [I’m] excited for him to go play against the Jets." So, that settles it: Cousins will be the starting quarterback against the 2-5 Jets on the road this Sunday. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Kubiak invited the debate about Cousins’ job security, though, when he said "everything" would be evaluated after another loss. But when you look at his argument, the numbers back it up for Cousins. He has the most passing touchdowns of any quarterback in the NFL this season (16), while sitting third in passing yards (1,877). He’s completed 62.6% of his passes and thrown only five interceptions to his 16 touchdowns. Cousins also owns a 97.4 quarterback rating through seven games this season. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza works out before an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Las Vegas. (AP Photo/David Becker) But when exactly will the Raiders be bringing Mendoza in, if at all? Kubiak said the Miami product is "going to play football," though his support for Cousins outweighs that notion now. "Kirk is playing really well, and we’re in the hunt," Kubiak added. "It’s really important that we keep playing really well behind him and keep developing Fernando." This was the plan all along for Kubiak, who hoped that Cousins would work his offense efficiently and allow Mendoza time to develop behind him. Las Vegas has hit a rough patch, but Kubiak is poised and confident Cousins and the rest of the team will be back on track against a struggling Jets squad, who gave the Miami Dolphins its first win of the season in Week 7. As for Mendoza, his time will come – just not right now. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins watches Fernando Mendoza warm up before a preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals at Allegiant Stadium on Aug. 13, 2026, in Las Vegas, Nev. (Getty Images) OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "Fernando is going to play at some point. It’s not going to be this week," Kubiak said. If the Raiders lose to the Jets on Sunday, perhaps it’s a conversation worth having again with the first-year head coach. title: Illegal alien pleads guilty to staging fake kidnapping to target Border Patrol
description: Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón allegedly fabricated her abduction, altered her appearance and hid in California to build a lawsuit against Border Patrol.
content: California Illegal alien pleads guilty to staging fake kidnapping to target Border Patrol Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón built a fraudulent narrative to build a case against immigration officials, according to authorities By Bonny Chu Fox News Published October 26, 2026 7:40pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video DHS reports over 1.4M illegal alien departures since January 2025 ‘The Big Weekend Show’ co-host Joey Jones breaks down deportation numbers and illegal immigration enforcement data under the Trump administration. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Federal officials on Monday announced that an illegal alien from Mexico pleaded guilty to staging a fake kidnapping in 2025, falsely claiming she had been abducted by federal agents or people acting on their behalf. Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón, 43, of South Los Angeles, fabricated her disappearance to stir media outrage and build a case for a lawsuit against Border Patrol before going into hiding, according to the Office of First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bilal A. Essayli for the Central District of California. "In June and July of 2025, Calderón faked her apprehension by federal agents or surrogates acting on behalf of federal agents," officials said. According to the attorney’s office, Calderón repeatedly contacted individuals using anonymous and blocked phone calls to build a fraudulent narrative. MEXICAN WOMAN IN US ILLEGALLY CHARGED WITH FAKING HER OWN ICE ‘KIDNAPPING’ Photos allegedly staged to make Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderon appear to have been detained and mistreated in custody, according to an affidavit. (US Department of Justice) She falsely claimed federal agents had abducted and detained her at multiple locations, officials said. As she staged her release, she also altered her appearance to make it appear as though she had been mistreated in custody. Court documents show that on June 25, 2025, Calderón falsely told an individual that immigration officials were taking her into custody near a fast-food restaurant and claimed agents had threatened to break her window. Two days later, Calderón reportedly used caller ID blocking to contact a tenants' rights advocate with another false claim. She allegedly lied that authorities had taken her to San Ysidro and forced her to sign deportation papers. AI VOICE SCAM TRAPS MOM IN 5-HOUR KIDNAPPING NIGHTMARE Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderon is seen in surveillance video at a parking lot. (Justice Department) That same day, she reportedly told another individual that she had been moved to an unknown warehouse, where she was being held with other detainees. "As a result of Calderón’s intentional lies, false information was reported to the media and law enforcement that Calderón had been ‘kidnapped’ by masked men in plain clothes driving an unmarked vehicle, who were acting as federal agents or as surrogates of federal agents," officials said. While Calderón "chose to stay hidden in Bakersfield," her false claims prompted community organizers to demand her release, according to officials. Surveillance video shows Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderon walking to a parked car, according to an affidavit. (US Department of Justice) On July 3, 2025, Calderón again reportedly used caller ID blocking to contact an individual, falsely claiming she would soon be released because of the media coverage. That same day, she traveled from Bakersfield to Tulare County to stage her release from "Border Patrol" and approached an individual about serving as a witness in her case, officials said. FORMER USCIS OFFICIAL, ACCOMPLICE CHARGED IN ALLEGED $960K CITIZENSHIP BRIBERY SCHEME "Calderón also altered her appearance to make it appear that she had been mistreated while in custody. A co-conspirator took photographs of Calderón’s altered appearance," officials said. A photo allegedly shows Calderon at a Bakersfield shopping mall while she was reported missing, according to an affidavit. (Justice Department) For the next two days, Calderón turned off her phones and refused to return calls when she knew law enforcement was looking for her, according to the attorney’s office. Calderón pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to impede, obstruct, impair and defeat the lawful function of Homeland Security Investigations within federal jurisdiction. Her hearing is scheduled for Feb. 8, 2027. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She faces a statutory maximum sentence of five years in federal prison. title: Jon Gosselin claims he's 'perfect strangers now' with six of his kids after years of no-contact
description: Jon Gosselin reveals he hasn't spoken to six of his eight children in years, calling them "perfect strangers" amid Collin Gosselin's memoir.
content: Entertainment Jon Gosselin claims he's 'perfect strangers now' with six of his kids after years of no contact 'Jon & Kate Plus 8' star says he hasn't spoken with twins Mady and Cara in about 13 years By Tracy Wright Fox News Published October 26, 2026 6:46pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Collin Gosselin details alleged abuse, confronts family trauma ‘In the Shadow of Eight’ author tells Fox News Digital about his alleged childhood abuse and isolation. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Jon Gosselin hasn't spoken with most of his children in more than a decade. The reality star, who appeared on "Jon & Kate Plus 8" before his divorce from ex-wife Kate Gosselin, admitted that his strained relationships with six of his kids have made them "perfect strangers now." When Entertainment Tonight asked about the last time Gosselin spoke with most of his children, he admitted, "I haven't talked to them." KATE GOSSELIN CALLED A 'MONSTER' IN SOCIAL MEDIA COMMENTS AFTER SON COLLIN ANNOUNCES MEMOIR Jon Gosselin admitted he hasn't spoken to most of his children in more than one decade. (Tommaso Boddi) TLC aired "Jon & Kate Plus 8" from 2007-09, when the former couple divorced. One year later, the show was rebranded as "Kate Plus 8," which focused on her life following the split, and ran until 2017. Jon and Kate – who have twins Mady and Cara and sextuplets Hannah, Leah, Alexis, Joel, Aaden and Collin — announced their divorce in a broadcast episode of the show. Collin and Hannah began living with Jon in 2018, when Jon admitted that while Collin went "no contact" with his siblings, Hannah was still speaking with her mother. 'JON & KATE' STAR COLLIN GOSSELIN CLAIMS MOTHER ZIP-TIED AND LOCKED HIM IN BASEMENT ROOM AS A CHILD "I mean, I know Hannah has, but I have not personally talked to them," Gosselin told the outlet before adding, "Of course I want to talk to them. It's not about the book stuff, I just want to know how their life is going." Collin Gosselin claimed his mother, Kate Gosselin, had him institutionalized against his will. (Michael Simon) He added, "I mean, we're perfect strangers now. It's been a long time with Mady and Cara ... about 13 years I've been estranged from them." Gosselin noted that he had "no idea why" his two eldest children haven't spoken to him in over a decade. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "And then, the other four, I haven't seen them since before COVID maybe," he said. When asked if he had a message for the six children he lost communication with, Gosselin claimed he's attempted contact in the past, and won't stop trying. Jon and Kate Gosselin share eight children together. They divorced in 2009. (Amy Sussman) HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED "I've tried to reach out to you publicly," he said. "In the early days, I tried to reach out to you privately. I hope you understand that I still love you. I hope one day you reach out to me." Gosselin added, "And please read your brother's book, because I think that will explain a lot. Be your own person. You are all adults now. Form your own opinions and try to take in as much information before you talk ill will or anything about anyone in this family." The reality star's plea came weeks after his son, Collin Gosselin, released an eye-opening memoir about his life in front of the camera, "In The Shadow of Eight: Surviving the Reality of My Childhood." Collin grew up on television as cameras followed the Gosselins for years, first with "Jon & Kate Plus 8" and then "Kate Plus 8." (Donna Svennevik) In the book, Collin, 22, accused his mother of restraining him with zip ties, hitting him when he failed to perform for cameras and isolating him in the family’s basement. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I'd like an apology, simply put, an apology and for her to admit, and just take accountability for what she did," Collin told Fox News Digital earlier this month regarding his mother. "And to say, you know, 'I'm sorry that I've soiled your name, and I've made every effort to bury you, to protect my reputation,' I think that'd be very honest and very powerful for her to say that … just show accountability because everything she's done to protect her reputation, it's all been at my cost." Video Amid the abuse allegations, Kate said that her children know who she "truly" is while responding to fan comments on a birthday post dedicated to her boyfriend, Steve Neild. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Happy Birthday Steve ! Strength isn’t just about enduring—it’s about loving deeply enough to do what is right even when it costs you," one TikTok user wrote in the comments section. "Look at the beautiful life and happily ever after You have found now that You made sacrifices that no Mama should have had to make alone." "When people attack You, it might sting for a moment, but it can never shake who You are. It only confirms that You stood your ground and remained true through it all. God is guiding You two." Gosselin thanked her fans for their support, writing she and her kids know who she is and "that's all that matters." (Kate Gosselin TikTok) CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Kate responded by thanking the fan, before adding, "I know who I am and my kids know who I truly am and to me, that’s all that matters." title: Deadly security risks prompt updated travel warnings for 13 countries
description: Citing Iranian-backed Houthi attacks and escalation risks for Americans, the State Department has now updated advisories for 13 Middle Eastern countries.
content: Travel Deadly security risks prompt updated travel warnings for 13 countries Americans urged to enroll in STEP and prepare emergency departure plans By Andrea Margolis Fox News Published October 26, 2026 6:33pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Airport strikes fuel concerns over escalating attacks, travel disruptions The State Department updated travel advisories for 13 Middle Eastern countries, warning Americans of armed attacks, kidnapping risks and escalating violence following recent strikes by Iranian-backed Houthi forces. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! The U.S. State Department has updated travel advisories for several Middle Eastern countries, warning of potential armed attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces and threats targeting Americans. Five countries — Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen — are listed under the department's highest advisory level, Level 4, which warns Americans not to travel. Eight others, including Israel, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, are designated Level 3, urging travelers to reconsider their plans. AMERICANS WARNED OF KIDNAPPING, EXTORTION AS VIOLENT CRIME GRIPS PARTS OF TOURIST SPOT While the advisory levels largely remained unchanged, all 13 advisories were updated on Friday. The advisories cited recent attacks by Iranian-supported Houthis, including strikes on Riyadh's airport in Saudi Arabia and "other critical infrastructure," the department said. The U.S. State Department has updated travel advisories for 13 Middle Eastern countries, warning Americans about escalating security threats and potential armed attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces. A man is seen looking at flights to Saudi Arabia above. (Piyas Biswas/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) The attacks have resulted in civilian deaths and widespread travel disruptions, with the State Department warning that the hostilities "have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area." SEXUAL ASSAULTS AND SCAMS PLAGUE TOP VACATION HOT SPOT, PROMPTING URGENT ADVISORY Americans traveling to the region also face additional risks, including health concerns in Iraq and Yemen, officials said. The State Department cited attacks on Riyadh's airport, seen above, and other critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia as part of its updated travel warnings for the Middle East. (AFP via Getty Images) Kidnapping and hostage-taking were listed as additional concerns in Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Syria and Yemen, according to the State Department. Recent attacks in the Middle East could lead to further instability, putting travelers at risk of unexpected disruptions and security emergencies, the State Department said. (Atta Kenare/AFP/Getty Images) The State Department encourages Americans traveling to these countries to enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive security alerts and updates from U.S. embassies. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Americans are also urged to monitor local news, prepare to shelter in place if conditions worsen and have an emergency departure plan that does not rely on U.S. government assistance. Fox News Digital reached out to the State Department for additional information. The State Department encouraged Americans traveling to countries covered by its updated Middle East advisories to enroll in a program providing security alerts from U.S. embassies. (AFP via Getty Images) Last week, the State Department raised its travel advisory for Kenya from Level 2, "Exercise Increased Caution," to Level 3, "Reconsider Travel," citing health risks, crime, civil unrest, kidnapping and terrorism. title: Not even sky high gas prices or the Iran war will stop Trump supporters voting MAGA
description: MAGA voters at a Michigan Trump rally dismiss rising gas prices and the Iran war as temporary sacrifices, vowing to back Republicans in midterms.
content: Politics Not even sky high gas prices or the Iran war will stop Trump supporters voting MAGA Trump rally attendees in Michigan call rising costs 'short term pain for long term gain' and back Republicans By Paul Steinhauser Fox News Published October 26, 2026 6:00pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Trump voters unfazed by rising prices, Iran war as midterms loom: 'He's doing the right things' MAGA voters speaking with Fox News Digital outside a President Donald Trump headlined rally in Port Huron, Michigan defend the president amid rising prices and the Iran War: 'He's doing what he has to do.' NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! PORT HURON, Michigan - They're coping with high prices at the gas and diesel pumps and at the supermarket, but the MAGA faithful in this key battleground state remain firmly supportive of President Donald Trump. In conversations with nearly 20 Michigan voters who waited in line for hours to attend a Trump rally in this small city on the shores of Lake Huron, voters made clear they're sticking with Republicans in the midterm elections and view Democrats as "socialists." "He has our best interests at heart. He loves our country and he is doing the right things for us to get back on track," Carol Mocan of Warren, Michigan told Fox News Digital. As they fight to hold their slim House and Senate majorities, Republicans are fighting political history, as the party in power in Washington has traditionally lost seats during midterm election years. The GOP also faces a challenging political climate fueled by persistent inflation tied in part to what polls show is an unpopular war with Iran and Trump's increasingly negative approval ratings. KAROLINE LEAVITT TELLS FOX NEWS DIGITAL TRUMP IS DEFYING MIDTERM HEADWINDS Video Trump stood at 36% approval in the latest Fox News national poll, his lowest level ever in a Fox News survey. But among self-described MAGA voters, the president's approval rating remained at a sky high 95%. "I know that Trump is always out for America's interests first. And that's what I really like about him," Bay City resident James Blake said. Linda Taggart of Marysville called the current high prices "short term pain for long term gain.... We see the long term goal and we support that." Port Huron resident Bob Kemp said Trump is getting the U.S. back on course following four years of Democratic control in the White House under former President Joe Biden, noting "whenever you're fixing something, it always gets worse before it gets better." Another Port Huron resident, Michael Bacheller, said the affordability issue wouldn't impact his vote in the midterms. "I think it's kind of a small price that we have to pay temporarily, and I think that's how Trump's, you know, putting it, and I can agree with that," he said. Asked if she blamed Trump for high prices, Judith Troy of Port Huron said "yes and no, you know, because he's doing what he has to do. Which causes, you know, prices to go up and that, but he's doing it for a good cause, so, you know, it's expected." Trump touted during his speech at the rally that "we are ensuring that Iran will never have, ever have, ever, ever a nuclear weapon," as he offered his reason for launching the war against Iran. The argument resonates with MAGA voters. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER President Donald Trump walks up to the podium as he arrives to speak at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Oct. 25, 2026 (Matthew Reidy/Fox News) "He's taken the fight to the terrorists over in Iran," James Blake said. Carol Mocan said she doesn't blame Trump for the high cost of living "because Iran needed to be taken care of. And no one else has done it for a long time, and I don't know who else would have, and I really think it needs to be shut down." Ken Gunnels of Clio, Michigan said, "I believe Iran was a genuine threat to this country. If a nuclear bomb went off in one of our major cities, I don't think any of us would have any idea the repercussions...that this country would suffer from that. I think those people are monsters, and I think we had to have a president that would stand up to them." Other MAGA voters said while the war and the economy are important, another issue takes precedence. "My biggest thing is the immigration. If you're here illegally, expect a knock on your door from ICE," Burtchville resident Steve Scouten said. WHO'S UP AND WHO'S DOWN IN THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS Bacheller, Scouten's longtime friend, agreed. "I'm with Steve. I think if I could pick one thing that Trump should really go down for is the immigration policy," he said. James Blake emphasized that Trump's "shut the borders." He added that the president has "also has advocated for no men in women's sports, which is a huge one for us. Also with no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security, that's huge, especially for a lot of members of my family." And Port Huron resident Rolande Debell highlighted she's "all for Trump" because "it's all about being American. It's all about our freedom. It's all about our rights. It's all about our Ten Commandments, and that's Trump." DEMOCRACY 2026: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB A MAGA float outside of a rally headlined by President Donald Trump, in Port Huron, Michigan on Oct. 25, 2026 (Paul Steinhauser/Fox News) None of the MAGA voters Fox Digital interviewed said they would vote for a Democrat in the midterms. "I don't like a lot of the things that they believe in," Judith Troy said. Carol Mocan argued that Democrats "don't live in the same world that that the rest of us do. They just don't, they don't think about the people. They think about their careers... whatever it takes to get elected." Asked why he won't consider voting for Democrats, James Blake said, "I'm not in the business of socialism. I don't think that's a good way to go, and I think that's where the Democrats are heading at this time." title: Robert Griffin III says he would '100%' take Baylor's vacant head football coach job
description: Robert Griffin III says he'd "100%" take the Baylor Bears head coaching job, revealing he's already spoken with athletic director Doug McNamee.
content: OutKick Robert Griffin III says he would '100%' take Baylor's vacant head football coach job The Heisman Trophy winner, who remains the Bears' only one in school history, said he spoke with Baylor's AD By Scott Thompson OutKick Published October 26, 2026 5:58pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Robert Griffin III on Baylor HC firing, USC struggles, J.J. McCarthy | FULL INTERVIEW | The Herd Robert Griffin III joins Colin Cowherd to discuss the firing of Baylor HC Dave Aranda, USC’s struggles under Lincoln Riley, and J.J. McCarthy’s performance against the Houston Texans. Could Robert Griffin III be the next Baylor Bears head football coach? If presented the opportunity, he told the "Dan Patrick Show" he would "100%" take it. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. "If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn’t just respectable on the football field, but one the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor," Griffin, a Heisman Trophy winner during his 2011 senior year at Baylor, said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Robert Griffin III, former NFL quarterback and TV analyst for ESPN, looks on before the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Cincinnati Bengals on December 4, 2023 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) "So yeah, I would 100% be interested. I talked with the athletic director, who is a guy in Doug McNamee that knows what it looks like to win at Baylor, know how you have to win at Baylor and recruit to Baylor to make those things happen." McNamee and his staff will be doing an extensive coaching search to find Aranda’s replacement, and it’s unknown if they’d want a familiar face in the building, let alone Griffin himself. However, Griffin makes a point: he knows what it’s like to win at Baylor and how much it means to the university and the community. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Though he went 25-21 during his four years there, Griffin went 10-3 with the Bears in his Heisman-winning season before being the Washington Redskins’ No. 2 overall pick in 2012. Baylor won the Alamo Bowl that season as well. To this day, Griffin remains the only Heisman winner in school history, making him quite the figure in Baylor athletics lore. But Griffin has never been a coach at any level, let alone a Division I football head coach. So, it will be very interesting if his former squad was among their list of candidates. ESPN college football and NFL analyst Robert Griffin III reacts on the sidelines before the 2024 AFC divisional round game between the Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, Md., on Jan. 20, 2024. (Tommy Gilligan/USA TODAY Sports) After a rollercoaster career in the NFL, Griffin quickly entered the media realm, joining ESPN at first and landing with FOX afterwards to cover both the NFL and college football. It was right after Griffin’s playing career ended in the NFL in 2020 when Aranda was hired by Baylor. He was a first-time head coach, though he was with LSU for four seasons as an assistant head coach and defensive coordinator before being hired by the Bears. Things were looking promising after a 12-2 campaign in 2021, especially considering Baylor went 2-7 during the COVID-shortened 2020 season. It was the most wins by the Bears in school history. Aranda was unable to follow that up in the coming years, but it looks like Baylor was going to compete this season for a playoff spot after going 4-1 to start the year. However, back-to-back losses to TCU and Kansas leaves the Bears 4-3 overall and 2-2 in the Big 12. Head coach Dave Aranda of the Baylor Bears reacts after the game against the TCU Horned Frogs at McLane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Waco, Texas. (Zach Del Bello/Getty Images) OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD As a result, Baylor decided to part ways with Aranda, leaving defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman as their interim head coach for the remainder of the season. title: Oregon Ducks' collapse continues, as loss to Illinois puts Dan Lanning on the hot seat in Eugene
description: Oregon Ducks football dropped from the AP Poll after seven turnovers against UCLA and a stunning loss at Illinois despite being 10.5-point favorites.
content: OutKick Oregon Ducks' collapse continues, as loss to Illinois puts Dan Lanning on the hot seat in Eugene After seven turnovers against UCLA and a loss at Illinois, Oregon didn't receive a single vote in this week's AP Poll By Ian Miller OutKick Published October 26, 2026 5:48pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Dan’s Suspicions of Dante Moore Confirmed in Humiliating Loss to Oklahoma State | Don't @ Me w/ Dan Dakich Is Oregon knocked out of the playoff race? Entering the 2026 college football season, the Oregon Ducks were widely believed to be in strong position for the program's first National Championship. Years of elite recruiting under head coach Dan Lanning, sustained success in the Big Ten Conference, and the return of starting quarterback Dante Moore set Oregon up to challenge for a conference championship and a spot in the College Football Playoff. Instead, the season went off the rails almost immediately. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. A close season-opening win over Boise State did little to inspire confidence, then the Ducks were demolished by a surprising Oklahoma State team, with the underlying performance far exceeding the final score. Still, Oregon had an opportunity to salvage their season with a trip to Los Angeles to play a then-ranked USC Trojans team. And despite Moore suffering a scary injury on an inexcusable hit from an SC linebacker, they did. DAN LANNING BLASTS USC AFTER OREGON'S WIN, AS LINCOLN RILEY OFFICIALLY ENTERS HOT SEAT IN LA Oregon head coach Dan Lanning stands on the field during the first half of an NCAA college football game against Southern California on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) Backup Dylan Raiola was outstanding, the defense did enough to stop Jayden Maiava, and the Ducks came away with an impressive 41-27 win. After the game, Lanning was effusive, saying, "I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon," referring to high school players from the Los Angeles and Southern California area. "If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here." Just a few weeks later, his comments immediately came back to haunt him. Hosting UCLA, the Ducks played arguably one of the ugliest games in program history. Somehow, incredibly, Oregon had seven turnovers in a 17-15 loss to an LA-based opponent. After their head coach proudly said that recruits should be heading to Eugene if they cared about winning games. Not a great look. It got worse this past Saturday. On the road at Illinois, Oregon was once again disappointing. Despite entering the game as 10.5-point favorites, the Ducks had a touchdown on their first drive of the game, only to muster just three points over the remaining 55 minutes. Their next four drives went punt, punt, fumble, missed field goal. All while gaining 22 yards on 16 plays. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE They finally put together a long scoring drive in the second to go up 10-0, only to immediately give up a 75-yard rushing touchdown to Aidan Laughery. Late in the second half, Oregon finally moved the ball more effectively, though were repeatedly forced to settle for long field goals, which they promptly missed. Meanwhile, Illinois put together multiple touchdown drives to effectively end the game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Head Coach Dan Lanning of the Oregon Ducks prepares for a play as his team takes the field during the second half of the game against the Boise State Broncos at Autzen Stadium on September 5, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. (Photo by Ali Gradischer/Getty Images) (Ali Gradischer/Getty Images) Yes, Oregon has been forced to start a backup quarterback. Yes, they've had a rash of poor conduct among their wide receiving corps. No, there's no excuse for the season going off the rails this much. To the point where the Ducks didn't receive a single vote in this week's AP Poll. And all of it's raising questions around Lanning's future in Eugene. A 9-3 season, with a big injury to Moore, would be one thing. But the Ducks' schedule doesn't get much easier. They host a rejuvenated, and ranked, Northwestern team on Saturday. They travel to Ohio State on Nov. 7, host Michigan on the 14th, then have to win a rivalry game against Washington to finish the season. Five losses suddenly looks possible, and six isn't off the table either. Lanning's earned quite a bit of the benefit of the doubt with multiple College Football Playoff appearances, and the Ducks won two games in last year's tournament. Including a shutout of a very good Texas Tech team in the Orange Bowl. Expectations in Oregon though, aren't what they used to be. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER The Ducks have one of the most expensive rosters in college football. They routinely spend to bring in big recruiting classes, and have a consensus top-4 class coming in 2027. Along with those investments come championship aspirations, which now seem further away than they did a few months ago. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Oregon Ducks head coach Dan Lanning looks on during the fourth quarter against the James Madison Dukes at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon, on Dec. 20, 2025. (Craig Strobeck/Imagn Images) Raiola clearly isn't the answer after Moore leaves for the NFL. The defense, which was a huge strength in 2025, has looked very average in 2026. And the discipline and toughness Lanning seemed to bring to the program hasn't continued in 2026, with some very poor off-field decision making this year. It's unlikely the Ducks make a move this season, but it seems clear that Lanning could go from championship contender to on the hot seat in just a few months. Few things move faster, or change as frequently, as modern college football. Ian Miller is a writer at OutKick. title: DOJ seeks to prosecute Comey over alleged national defense disclosure
description: The Justice Department filed a two-count criminal information accusing James Comey of communicating national defense information and conspiracy.
content: James Comey James Comey faces new DOJ case over alleged national defense disclosure The new criminal information marks the third criminal matter the Trump Justice Department has brought against Comey By Sophia Compton , David Spunt , Bill Mears Fox News Published October 26, 2026 5:46pm EDT | Updated October 26, 2026 6:21pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Comey calls latest DOJ action ‘appalling abuse’ of DOJ James Comey says he is innocent and will fight allegations that he willfully communicated national defense information during a 2016 incident, calling the Justice Department’s action an "appalling abuse." (Credit: Comey via Instagram) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! The Justice Department filed a criminal information against former FBI Director James Comey over allegations that he willfully communicated national defense information to an unauthorized person in connection with an alleged 2016 disclosure. Federal prosecutors filed the two-count criminal information in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, alleging Comey communicated national defense information and conspired with others to unlawfully disclose it. The Justice Department said that the filing was made to preserve the allegations before the statute of limitations expired as an investigation remains ongoing. NEW FEDERAL GRAND JURY SUBPOENA ISSUED TO FORMER JAMES COMEY ADVISOR IN LEAK INVESTIGATION: SOURCES The Justice Department has filed a criminal information against former FBI Director James Comey. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters) "The Department filed a waiverless criminal information to toll the statute of limitations as it relates to allegations concerning former FBI Director Comey," a spokesperson for the DOJ said. "Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further." Comey's attorneys have challenged the filing. They've argued that prosecutors cannot move forward with the case without first obtaining an indictment from a federal grand jury. U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden held an emergency, closed-door hearing on Oct. 9 after Comey’s attorneys moved to dismiss the case and unseal the proceedings. McFadden, who was appointed to the federal bench by President Donald Trump in 2017, granted the request to unseal the case but has not ruled on Comey's motion to dismiss. OBAMA JUDGE RULES TRUMP DOJ ILLEGALLY FIRED JAMES COMEY'S DAUGHTER, REJECTS SWEEPING ARTICLE II CLAIM The Justice Department said that the filing was made to preserve the allegations before the statute of limitations expired as an investigation remains ongoing. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images) It remains unclear when or if prosecutors will seek an indictment from a grand jury. Prosecutors allege that on or about Oct. 5, 2016, Comey knowingly and willfully communicated information related to the national defense to a person who was not entitled to receive it. Comey denied wrongdoing in an Instagram post Monday, calling the latest action an "appalling abuse of the Department of Justice." "Nothing's changed with me. I'm still innocent. I'm not afraid of these people. And I still believe in the independent federal judiciary," Comey said. He added that his family and legal team would "stand up in court and fight the latest and whatever comes after this." OKLAHOMA STATE AGENCY FIRES STAFF ATTORNEY AFTER ANTI-ICE SOCIAL MEDIA TIRADE The case marks the third attempt by the Justice Department to prosecute Comey. (Federal Court, sketch artist Dana Verkouteren) Prosecutors also allege Comey conspired with others to unlawfully disclose national defense information. The case marks the third attempt by the Justice Department under President Donald Trump to prosecute Comey. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A previous case accusing him of lying to Congress was dismissed, while a separate case stemming from his "86 47" seashell social media post remains pending. U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden held an emergency, closed-door hearing on Oct. 9 after Comey’s attorneys moved to dismiss the case and unseal the proceedings. McFadden, who was appointed to the federal bench by President Donald Trump in 2017, granted the request to unseal the case but has not ruled on Comey's motion to dismiss. OBAMA JUDGE RULES TRUMP DOJ ILLEGALLY FIRED JAMES COMEY'S DAUGHTER, REJECTS SWEEPING ARTICLE II CLAIM The Justice Department said that the filing was made to preserve the allegations before the statute of limitations expired as an investigation remains ongoing. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images) It remains unclear when or if prosecutors will seek an indictment from a grand jury. Prosecutors allege that on or about Oct. 5, 2016, Comey knowingly and willfully communicated information related to the national defense to a person who was not entitled to receive it. Comey denied wrongdoing in an Instagram post Monday, calling the latest action an "appalling abuse of the Department of Justice." "Nothing's changed with me. I'm still innocent. I'm not afraid of these people. And I still believe in the independent federal judiciary," Comey said. He added that his family and legal team would "stand up in court and fight the latest and whatever comes after this." OKLAHOMA STATE AGENCY FIRES STAFF ATTORNEY AFTER ANTI-ICE SOCIAL MEDIA TIRADE The case marks the third attempt by the Justice Department to prosecute Comey. (Federal Court, sketch artist Dana Verkouteren) Prosecutors also allege Comey conspired with others to unlawfully disclose national defense information. The case marks the third attempt by the Justice Department under President Donald Trump to prosecute Comey. title: Natalie Portman says being sexualized as a child star forced her to become a 'good girl' as protection
description: Natalie Portman reveals how she built a "good girl" persona to counter childhood sexualization in Hollywood and why it became a lasting trap.
content: Child Stars Natalie Portman says being sexualized as a child star forced her to become a 'good girl' as protection Oscar winner Natalie Portman said early Hollywood roles led her to craft a safety mechanism that shaped her image By Lauryn Overhultz Fox News Published October 26, 2026 5:40pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Divorce lawyer reveals signs that your spouse has emotionally checked out James Sexton, Esq., explains how emotional withdrawal develops between couples, and why renewed attention, affection and mindfulness can reveal whether both partners remain invested. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Natalie Portman learned early that growing up in Hollywood meant protecting herself from the very image that made her famous. The Oscar-winning actress opened up about the lasting impact of being sexualized as a child star, revealing how she carefully crafted a "good girl" image to shield herself from unwanted attention – only to find that the persona followed her well into adulthood. Portman began her career in films featuring dark themes, such as 1994 thriller "Léon: The Professional," "Heat" and "Beautiful Girls." BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA Natalie Portman said she adopted a "good girl" persona as a child star to protect herself from being sexualized in Hollywood. (Patrick Camboulive/Sygma) As Portman navigated the pressures of Hollywood at a young age, she and her parents made a deliberate effort to separate her on-screen persona from who she was in real life. Rather than embrace the provocative image associated with some of her early roles, Portman maintained a more reserved public image. She chose conservative, age-appropriate clothing for red carpet appearances while remaining focused on her education and academic success. "I think there was a conscious effort, because I was depicted as this sexualized Lolita, that I wanted to be like, ‘No, I’m serious, I’m a good girl, I’m a prude, I’m smart, I’m a student,’ emphasizing that as almost a safety mechanism," she told Harper's Bazaar. As her career progressed, Portman continued to gravitate toward complex, emotionally demanding roles. She eventually earned an Oscar for her performance in "Black Swan" and another nomination for "Jackie." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Natalie Portman won an Oscar for her performance in "Black Swan." (James Devaney/WireImage) But as her career flourished, Portman found that the serious image she had carefully cultivated, coupled with the demanding roles she continued to play, created a lasting misconception about her personality. "But then, over time, it became like everyone thinks I’m really serious," Portman noted. "I’m very silly, and I love to laugh more than anything, and I love to goof off. People always think I’m a perfectionist, I think, because of 'Black Swan.' I’m the opposite. I’m forgiving with myself. In college, we had a phrase: ‘Done, not good.’" After spending much of her career exploring darker, more complex characters, Portman said her priorities have shifted toward bringing audiences a sense of happiness. Natalie Portman said she's focusing on bringing more joy to audiences after years of portraying darker, emotionally complex characters. (Dominique Charriau/WireImage) LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Right now, it’s a lot of joy," she told the outlet of the current phase of her career. "I think it’s both for myself and what I hope to offer an audience, because it just feels … I mean, every time has dark moments, but it feels like there’s a lot of really heavy stuff going on. It’s just ever-present in our face, and so it does feel like the biggest service you can do right now as an artist is to deliver some joy." Portman has also found joy in her personal life, recently welcoming a child with her partner, Tanguy Destable. A few weeks after welcoming her third child, Portman told Harper's Bazaar she's been "full of wonder and joy at this magical little human." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Natalie Portman shares two children, Aleph and Amalia, with ex-husband Benjamin Millepied. The couple split in 2024 after 11 years of marriage. (Getty Images) Portman shares two kids, Aleph and Amalia, with ex-husband Benjamin Millepied. The two split in 2024 after 11 years of marriage. While Portman has been soaking up the early days with her newborn, she said the experience has also reminded her how fleeting those moments can be. "It gives me a whole new attention to my big kids too, as I am reminded of how recently they were these little fresh creations and how quickly they’ve blossomed into incredible humans with their own amazing personalities and senses of humor and ideas," she explained. title: Michele Tafoya: Peggy Flanagan “Is Not An Experiment Worth Retrying”
description: Full Interview: Full transcript: Guy Benson: Joining us now is former longtime NFL sideline reporter and now the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota, our friend Michele Tafoya. Michele, welcome back. Good to talk to you. I want to just start since…
content: Michele Tafoya: Peggy Flanagan “Is Not An Experiment Worth Retrying” Full Interview: Full transcript: Guy Benson: Joining us now is former longtime NFL sideline reporter and now the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota, our friend Michele Tafoya. Michele, welcome back. Good to talk to you. I want to just start since you’re such a football fan, I have to mention that it’s a pretty good time to be a football fans in your state, if I’m not mistaken. I think the Vikings are what 6-0 now and the Gophers just upset ranked Iowa. On the college side this weekend so I think you got a lot of very happy campers in your state. Michele Tafoya: This should tell you all you need to know. I was at church yesterday morning at the end of mass, the priest said, how about those golden gophers? How about that defense? And it was very funny and everyone was amazed. So yes, these are happy times for sports fans in Minnesota. Guy Benson: I will confess that several weeks from now I’m going to have to root very hard against the gophers. But you know why. We’ll get to that in due time. You get it. Michele, let’s talk about your race. So there was this viral moment at your debate with Ms. Flanagan, who is the sitting lieutenant governor who wants to be the U.S. Senator for Minnesota, a very, very hard left Democrat, more to the left even than Tim Walz, the governor, the failed governor there. And she was trying some sort of spin razzle dazzle deflection and you just called it out in this kind of went everywhere on social media cut forty one. Michele Tafoya: Listen, it is rich to hear my opponent talk about lost access to programs when under her watch while she was second in command of this state, Minnesota saw billions, and billions, and billions of fraud dollars walk out the door to fraudsters while Medicaid was gutted, while Feeding Our Future was gutted, while these programs for autistic kids were gutted. And she’s talking about access? All of that money left the state of Minnesota. This historic fraud happened under her watch, and suddenly she’s looking out for Medicaid and SNAP? Sell it to someone else, Peggy. We are gonna get. Guy Benson: Sell it to someone else, Peggy, like put that on a t-shirt, Michele, and here’s the thing, it’s obvious why she was not terribly eager to debate you, first of all. And then secondly, on a more serious note, I think a lot of people watching your race will say we really like Michele Tafoya, she’s sharp, this Peggy Flanagan seems pretty extreme even for Minnesota, but my gosh, it’s such a blue state and the environment for Republicans nationally seems so, so tough. Is something like this fraud issue really going to break through enough to give Michele Tafoya a chance to actually win in that really tough state for Republicans? How do you make that sale to voters? Michele Tafoya: Well, look, her record as 20 years as a politician, eight years as Lieutenant Governor in lockstep with Tim Walz, and as you said, even further to the left. If that’s not enough, look this is not theoretical what she does when she’s in charge. We lose money to historic fraud. We have Somali gang violence that she will not identify. We have a peak in violent crime. We have lows in test scores, and they oversaw a massive budget surplus turn into a deficit. This is not an experiment worth retrying. This is abysmal. This is just an abject failure to this administration. Tim Walz knew it was the end for him. He was in the middle of running for governor for a third term when he stepped away and said, eh, nevermind. Meanwhile, she wants a promotion? Hey, you know, in your career, in my career, in any normal job, you don’t get a promotion with that record. You get a pink slip and I think Minnesotans are fed up and they’re exhausted and we’re a state that is unique and independent and this really pisses people off. Guy Benson: Is the, because I know you’ve made fraud a huge, huge element of your campaign for obvious reasons. I mean, it’s been one of the, one of focal points in Minnesota politically now for a number of years, a huge black eye for the state over and over again, that the headlines have been so embarrassing. Is it, I know in theory, it should work and should resonate. On the ground, is that issue really penetrating? Michele Tafoya: Well, that’s what we’re hearing. And look, you know, you can talk about other issues, but I have been backed by the Minnesota Farm Bureau. So the farmers are on my side. I’ve been backed by the Minnesota Police and Peace Officers Association, along with a number of other major, you know, public safety organizations. So they are in my corner. Small businesses are in my corner, been endorsed by them. So I like our chances. If the DSA is in her corner, I’ll take everyone else in our corner. And that’s really the platform she’s running on. Medicare for all, a blow up ICE, as she calls it. And she was part of the defund movement. She participated in illegal riots. I don’t think Minnesota, we might be a blue to purple state, but we’re not an extreme state. And Hasan Piker has endorsed her. So that should tell you pretty much all you need to know. Mm-hmm. Guy Benson: Who believes America deserved 9/11 of course. Falsely, you just sort of briefly touched on it but I want to come back to it, Somali gang violence. We talked about on the show, we had Tom Emmer here on the show, the congressman as well. This was a homecoming football game that was cut short and then the homecoming dance canceled because of like foreign third-world gang violence in a tony Minneapolis suburb. I mean, if that doesn’t cut through some of the noise here. Especially when this has been allowed to fester. This is not a xenophobic thing. This is criminal violence on a large scale. And your opponent and a lot of the people running your state from one party seem to just have their head in the sand because they want all of those votes and they don’t want to call what’s happening by what it is, by its own name. Michele Tafoya: We have a deputy sheriff in Ramsey County, which is where St. Paul is, who is Somalian, who said, we have to own this. This is Somali gang violence. We have a number of law enforcement people coming forward and saying that. But she will not say it for the reasons you just articulated. She claims to have a lot of friends in that community, best friends, dear friends in the community. That’s fine, we’re not painting the entire community with one broad brush. But we are identifying the problem when we put out a five point plan to deal with it from the federal level. So yeah, it’s not only that homecoming game guy, we had a Catholic school. They found 55 shell casings on the basketball courts at a Catholic School. So they had to take down the baskets and the rims so no gangs could show up and play basketball anymore because of the threat of gun violence there. That was in another neighborhood, not far from where the homecoming was. So there was a park nearby in between those two points where there was another shooting. So yes, I’m hearing from parents. We’re having a roundtable tomorrow with moms from the area to talk about this. Guy Benson: It’s the violence and then coupled with the fraud and the dysfunctional failed governance from these people. And she, your opponent, is the lieutenant governor. When is enough, enough? Even in a blue state like Minnesota, Michele Tafoya on the ballot in eight days in Minnesota for the U.S. Senate. Michele, good luck. title: New test could flag which men need aggressive prostate cancer treatment and which don't
description: The Decipher genomic test could help doctors decide which high-risk prostate cancer patients need abiraterone hormone therapy and which can skip it.
content: Health New test could flag which men need aggressive prostate cancer treatment and which don't Researchers found the genomic test predicted which high-risk patients would benefit from abiraterone hormone therapy By Angelica Stabile Fox News Published October 26, 2026 5:06pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Young prostate cancer survivor credits routine doctor's visit with saving his life Musician Wayne Singleton shares how a routine physical led to a rare prostate cancer diagnosis at 33 years old, and encourages others to prioritize regular health checks. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! A new diagnostic test could improve the prostate cancer experience for millions of men. Researchers at University College London (UCL) analyzed a tissue-based molecular test called Decipher to determine which men with high-risk prostate cancer were most likely to benefit from stronger treatment — and which might avoid unnecessary medication and side effects. The analysis focused on abiraterone, a hormone therapy that was shown in the STAMPEDE clinical trial to cut the risk of death in half among men with high-risk, localized prostate cancer. The findings were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, held Oct. 23–27. JOE BIDEN SHARES HEALTH UPDATE AFTER PROSTATE CANCER DIAGNOSIS WHILE ISSUING WARNING TO OTHERS Not every cancer is alike, and treating someone more aggressively than necessary could have "increased side effects and poorer quality of life," noted a UCL news release. Because prostate cancers differ at the molecular level, not every patient benefits from adding hormone therapy. Adding a hormone therapy called abiraterone to standard treatment for men with high-risk, localized prostate cancer could cut the risk of death in half, the trial found. To determine whether Decipher could help guide that decision, researchers examined test scores from more than 27,000 patients in real-world data and 401 men with non-metastatic prostate cancer who had participated in the STAMPEDE abiraterone trial. PATIENTS REMAIN CANCER-FREE NEARLY 3 YEARS AFTER RECEIVING EXPERIMENTAL IMMUNOTHERAPY Higher Decipher scores predicted worse outcomes, meaning the cancer is more likely to spread and additional treatment may be valuable. A low Decipher score suggested more intensive treatment may be unnecessary. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Lead researcher Dr. Sarah Howlett of UCL Cancer Institute commented in a statement that for men with very high-risk prostate cancer, preventing spread of the disease is "critical." "Understanding who benefits most from additional treatment can make a meaningful difference," she added. A genomic test could help to personalize treatments for prostate cancer patients, the researchers suggested. (iStock) The findings suggest that genomic testing could help tailor treatment, according to the researcher. Men with high-risk prostate cancer and low Decipher scores may face a lower risk of spread and could avoid more intensive therapy, while those with high scores may be the strongest candidates for additional treatment. Identifying the same pattern in both a large, real-world dataset and a randomized clinical trial strengthens the findings, Howlett noted. CANCER WARNING SIGNS MAY APPEAR IN DNA YEARS BEFORE BLOOD TESTS DETECT TROUBLE "But further validation in other datasets is needed before the test is used routinely to make these decisions," she said. Elai Davicioni, medical director of urology for Decipher test maker Veracyte, also commented, "We believe this growing evidence gives physicians a stronger reason to use Decipher before making decisions that can affect both cancer outcomes and patients’ quality of life." Men with high-risk prostate cancer and low Decipher scores may face a lower risk of spread and could avoid more intensive therapy, while those with high scores may be the strongest candidates for additional treatment. (iStock) Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel, who was not involved in the study, also commented on the findings. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Prostate cancer varies from person to person," he said. "Medical science is increasingly aware that it is not one size fits all." Localized prostate cancer, which has not yet spread, may contain mutations that predict how aggressive the disease will be and indicate whether it could respond to targeted therapies, Siegel noted. About one in eight American men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime, according to the American Cancer Society. (iStock) Certain targeted therapies are being used more with widespread prostate cancer, according to the doctor, as they include "more powerful anti-androgens, which works not just on the testes, but on the adrenals as well." Hormone therapies have "significant side effects," including fatigue, and "don’t always help," he added. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Siegel said the study’s strength was its combination of a randomized treatment group with Decipher testing, which helped identify in advance which patients were most likely to respond to intensive hormone therapy. "This is the personalized, precise approach of the near future," he said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Prostate cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer death behind lung cancer, according to the American Cancer Society. About one in eight American men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime. Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital. title: Former Colombian president accused of exploiting dozens of women for presidential parties
description: Former Colombian president Gustavo Petro rejected claims he traded public contracts for sex amid broader allegations of corruption and drug trafficking.
content: Colombia Former Colombian president accused of exploiting dozens of women for presidential parties Petro denied exchanging government contracts for sexual relations and said the accusations were part of a political attack By Bonny Chu Fox News Published October 26, 2026 4:55pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Trump says Colombian President Petro needs to 'watch his a--' President Donald Trump said Colombian President Gustavo Petro should not feel relaxed after the U.S. operation in Venezuela, citing cocaine coming from Bogotá. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Former Colombian President Gustavo Petro has been accused of trapping and exploiting 48 women for presidential parties, with officials alleging they were hired "just to be with President Petro." Carlos Andrés Ríos, director of Colombia’s Administrative Department of the Presidency (DAPRE), claimed Petro oversaw a system that used service contracts to "systematically" control and weaponize the women, channeling public salaries in exchange for intimate relationships. "We are going to prove to the Colombian people how the Casa de Nariño was unfortunately set up, organized, and tailored for something completely different — not to govern, but to party there every single day, bring in women," Rios said during a congressional hearing last week. COLOMBIAN LAWMAKERS SEEK SUSPENSION OF TRUMP FOE GUSTAVO PETRO OVER ALLEGED MEDDLING IN UPCOMING ELECTION Former President Gustavo Petro rejected claims that women were hired to attend presidential parties and provide sexual favors. (AP Photo/Fernando Vergara, File) Petro issued a statement Sunday denying that he had used his public office to obtain sex. "I have never given out a contract in exchange for sexual relations. I would vomit on myself if I ever did such a thing," Petro said in a post on X. He argued that while his office provided state-funded aid programs for vulnerable women, he claimed that it is fundamentally different from giving contracts to individuals in exchange for sexual favors. TRUMP-BACKED 'EL TIGRE' LOOKS TO CRUSH CARTELS, END COLOMBIA'S SOCIALIST ERA IN PIVOTAL ELECTION The Casa de Nariño, the presidential palace, in Bogotá, Colombia, on Dec. 17, 2025. (Nathalia Angarita/Bloomberg via Getty Images) "Helping poor women, female heads of households, and those engaged in sex work so that they have different life options — as I have demonstrated in public administration through concrete and funded programs — is something very different from giving out contracts in exchange for sexual relations. No person who has participated in those public programs will ever be able to say that I have done anything of the sort," he said. Petro also acknowledged in the statement that he had occasionally visited establishments where sex work took place when he was young, saying he regretted the experiences and had stopped visiting such places decades ago. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "When I was very young, I occasionally visited places where sex work was practiced. There, I experienced that paying for sex felt dirty to me, and I perceived the sadness of the men and women who attended those places. That is why I stopped visiting them decades ago," he said. The accusations come amid broader criticism of Petro over alleged misuse of public funds, depletion of national budgets and drug trafficking. Petro has dismissed the allegations as politically motivated attacks by figures such as President Donald Trump and Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella. President Donald Trump and former Colombian President Gustavo Petro have previously escalated tensions amid a series of accusations and public disputes. (Mauro Pimentel/AFP via Getty Images; Francis Chung/Politico/Bloomberg via Getty Images) "After attempting to portray me as corrupt and a drug trafficker — an intention expressed by people like Abelardo de la Espriella and Donald Trump, without being able to present a single piece of evidence of corruption or drug trafficking, because I have never stolen a single peso from the public treasury and I have fought for over two decades against drug traffickers, exposing their political ties," Petro said. Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment. title: Dan Rather's withering criticism of CBS 'doesn't reflect reality,' network insider says
description: Dan Rather called the changes at CBS News "a disaster," but a network insider fired back sharply, saying his criticism doesn't reflect reality.
content: Media Dan Rather's withering criticism of CBS 'doesn't reflect reality,' network insider says Rather blasted his longtime employer, calling CBS News a ‘disaster’ under Bari Weiss By Brian Flood Fox News Published October 26, 2026 4:53pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google Former CBS News anchor Dan Rather. (Craig Barritt/Getty) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Former CBS News anchor Dan Rather blasted his former employer that's now under the leadership of lightning rod editor-in-chief Bari Weiss, raising the eyebrows of a network insider who doesn’t think the criticism reflects "reality." Rather, who famously stepped down from his role as CBS’ evening news anchor in 2005 and eventually left the network the following year after reporting a discredited story about then-President George W. Bush, joined a variety of liberal media watchdogs who have spoken out against Weiss over the past year. "What’s happened at CBS News is sad," Rather told Variety. "It is in many ways a disaster, not just for the people who work at CBS News — and there’s still a lot of really good people working there," Rather continued. "But this is a further example of big billionaire corporate power in bed with powerful people and the presidency to get control of these operations for their benefit." SCOTT PELLEY FIRED AT CBS NEWS AFTER BLOWUPS WITH BARI WEISS, NEW '60 MINUTES' PRODUCER Amid scandal, Dan Rather stepped down from his role as "CBS Evening News" anchor in 2005. (Reuters ) Rather also suggested that President Donald Trump has forced change at CBS News, as Skydance Media CEO David Ellison took control of the network last year through a long-planned merger that was approved shortly after CBS agreed to settle an election interference lawsuit with the president. "Donald Trump has expressed his extreme dislike for ’60 Minutes.’ So now, he’s gotten his way," Rather said. "He cleared the way for a consolidation of corporate power, which in turn cleared the way for doing what’s been done to ’60 Minutes.’ The wreckage of CBS News is everywhere and continues to this moment. I don’t see how to stop it." While anonymous CBS News staffers have objected to changes made under Weiss, newsletters aimed at progressive audiences have regularly attacked her. Other former CBS News stars, such as Scott Pelley, have spoken out against Weiss, but not everyone inside the network agrees with Rather. NORAH O'DONNELL URGES LIBERAL BARI WEISS CRITICS TO GIVE 'CBS MORNINGS' A CHANCE AS SHE RETURNS TO PROGRAM Paramount owner David Ellison tapped Bari Weiss as editor-in-chief of CBS News and acquired her outlet, The Free Press, for $150 million last year. (Charly Triballeau/AFP via Getty Images; James Leynse/Corbis via Getty Images; Noam Galai/Getty Images for The Free Press) "I’d point out that his criticism doesn't reflect reality," a CBS News insider told Fox News Digital. "Going further, ‘60 Minutes’ has done critical stories about the Trump Administration throughout this season," the insider added. Indeed, CBS’ "60 Minutes" has aired several stories that were critical of the Trump administration, including the story of people deported to countries they are not from, a look at the "pardon economy" and a report on the federal government inserting itself in elections. CBS BOSS FUELS LEFT-WING UPROAR AMID REPORT SHE URGED STAFF TO PROBE ALLEGED EL-SAYED, MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES Dan Rather called CBS News a "disaster," but said it still employs "a lot of really good people." (Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images) CBS’ parent company, Paramount, named Weiss the editor-in-chief of CBS News in 2025 following the company’s acquisition of The Free Press for $150 million. The hiring infuriated liberal journalists and media figures, as Weiss’ outlet has made waves for supporting Israel and challenging DEI and gender ideology. CBS News declined comment. Rather also told Variety he wasn’t familiar with Weiss before she took control of CBS News even though he criticized the network for hiring her only days after she landed the gig last year. "The American people will pay the price for this move, as will the journalists of CBS News who can no longer credibly serve as watchdogs because the ones they are meant to hold to account are signing their paychecks and hobnobbing with the president," Rather wrote on his Substack page. "It is a dark day in the halls of CBS News." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital’s Joseph A. Wulfsohn contributed to this report.
