title: Lincoln Riley’s USC tenure could end with loss against Ohio State’s backup quarterback, and $70m buyout
description: A reported $70 million buyout looms over USC as Lincoln Riley's Trojans must beat Ohio State's backup quarterback to keep CFP hopes alive this weekend.
content: OutKick Lincoln Riley’s USC tenure could end with loss against Ohio State’s backup quarterback, and $70m buyout The Trojans have not won more than nine games since 2022 and still face Indiana, UCLA to close the season By Trey Wallace OutKick Published October 26, 2026 2:37pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Ryan Leaf Speaks On College Football Playoffs Expanding To 24 Teams | The Craig Carton Show The College Football Playoffs are set to expand from 12 to 24 teams starting next season, and Craig Carton asked former Heisman trophy finalist and CFB analyst Ryan Leaf his take on the change. Should Lincoln Riley’s tenure at USC come down to what happens this weekend against an Ohio State team playing with a backup quarterback in what was supposed to be a marquee matchup for the Trojans? Absolutely, and now it's a must win. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. One way or another, everything could come to a head Saturday night in Los Angeles for a USC team coming off an embarrassing loss to Wisconsin in Madison. This was supposed to be the year for Lincoln Riley to have his team in the college football playoff and compete for a national championship. The pieces appeared to be in place, with quarterback Jayden Maiava leading an offense expected to rank among the Big Ten’s best. MORE QUESTIONS THAN ANSWERS: ARCH MANNING LIKES THE DISRESPECT, BIG 12'S DISASTER AND A CFP RACE IN DISARRAY Throw in a defense led by Gary Patterson, and the recipe for success was being put together inside the Trojans' football complex. Unfortunately for the USC fans that were praying for some type of return on investment after showing up on a weekly basis, sometimes in the blistering California heat, we are once again on the brink of total implosion for Lincoln Riley. And, the head coach had the nerve to sit at the podium after losing to Wisconsin and discuss a win at Penn State just two weeks prior. "You have to own it, this is the same team that played a way different brand of football at Penn State two weeks ago and we're very capable of doing that again in the coming weeks," Lincoln Riley said after the Wisconsin loss. "But we gotta do it, and it's gonna take all of coaches and players to do it, and that's what we're gonna do." Head coach Lincoln Riley of the USC Trojans argues a call in the first half against the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium on Oct. 24, 2026, in Madison, Wis. (Getty Images) Sorry, that isn’t going to make Trojan fans feel any better that you went on the road and beat a Big Ten team earlier in the month, then to turn around and lose to a Wisconsin team that was not on the same level when it comes to talent. A lifeless effort that saw the Trojans score just seven points in the game. Oh, and if USC fans wanted to feel even worse about the loss, Wisconsin passed for only 58 yards in the win over the Trojans. DAN LANNING BLASTS USC AFTER OREGON'S WIN, AS LINCOLN RILEY OFFICIALLY ENTERS HOT SEAT IN LA The reality is that this experiment feels all but over, and Ohio State could end up being the final nail in a coffin that has been in the process of being assembled for over a year. Pay for the buyout or pray Lincoln Riley takes another job? You wanna see things get contentious around USC? Have the administration get into a standoff with Riley and his agent over the reported $70 million buyout that USC would owe the head coach if he were to be fired. But in this era of college athletics, schools can no longer afford to sit around and pray it gets better. Okay, maybe Florida State can penny-pinch and hold off on firing Mike Norvell until they raise enough money by passing around the offering plate to boosters on a Sunday morning. Not USC, and not during one of the most chaotic times in college athletics. If Lincoln Riley could not win with Caleb Williams slinging the football, what makes fans think he can win now? COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S MEGA ROSTERS AREN’T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON PROVE We are also past the point of excuses. There is no conceivable reason why USC should have lost to a football team that passed for a total of 58 yards. And, there's no reason why the Trojans' season should come down to a game against Ohio State this weekend. Southern California head coach Lincoln Riley talks with quarterback Jayden Maiava between plays against Penn State during the second half of an NCAA college football game Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in State College, Pa. (AP Photo/Barry Reeger) Remember, the Trojans still have to play Ohio State, Indiana, Maryland and UCLA to finish out the 2026 season, and there is no wiggle-room for a loss thanks to that performance against Wisconsin. So, if things continue trending in the wrong way this weekend and Ohio State rolls into Los Angeles with a backup quarterback to beat the Trojans, it could be time for Lincoln Riley to finally waive the white flag. We all know he's a competitor, but leaving USC for a return to the Big 12 at a school like Baylor might not be the worst thing for a head coach who is hanging on by a thread at his current employer. It's either that or forcing USC to pay the buyout that will undoubtedly be mitigated in some form or fashion. And don't forget, these high-power schools can find a way to make the situation messy in the process. This is not what USC signed up for, or wrote massive checks they can't cash The Trojans have not won more than nine games since the 2022 season, where they finished 11-3. You think this is what USC donors had in mind when they signed Lincoln Riley to a lucrative contract that saw him leave Oklahoma? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! That's an easy answer. Absolutely not, and I can promise you the Big Ten conference is thinking the same. AFTER YET ANOTHER INEXCUSABLE LOSS TO WISCONSIN, THE LINCOLN RILEY ERA AT USC LOOKS TO BE NEARING AN END Head coach Lincoln Riley of the USC Trojans looks on prior to a game against the UCLA Bruins at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Nov. 29, 2025 in Los Angeles, Calif. (Harry How/Getty Images) A win against Ohio State on Saturday night would obviously keep USC within striking distance of the playoffs. But, they would also have to win out and beat UCLA to end the regular season, while also going on the road to Bloomington in three weeks to face Curt Cignetti's Indiana team that is still in the hunt despite a flaky offense. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP We have come to the old fork in the road in Los Angeles, and if USC doesn’t win this weekend against the Buckeyes, that highway could lead Riley straight out of California with a nice payday to make up for the embarrassing results he produced. title: Netanyahu fights for political future as Israel heads to polls with Iran threat looming
description: Israel heads into a high-stakes election with Benjamin Netanyahu's political future and legacy on the line as voters weigh his security record and the continuing Iran threat.
content: Benjamin Netanyahu Netanyahu fights for political future as Israel heads to polls with Iran threat looming Netanyahu faces criticism over his security record as polls show a tight race with the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot By Amelie Botbol Fox News Published October 26, 2026 2:36pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Netanyahu’s record takes center stage in Israel vote Conservative Israeli commentator Gadi Taub discusses Netanyahu’s record, political staying power and the security challenges shaping Israel’s high-stakes election. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 national vote, President Donald Trump issued a sweeping endorsement of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s re-election bid, calling him a "great warrior," an "even greater partner for peace" and an ally in the confrontation with Iran. The backing could give Israel’s longest-serving prime minister a boost ahead of the country’s first national vote since the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, massacre. The election is widely viewed in Israel as a referendum on whether to grant Netanyahu another term to pursue his war objectives, including disarming Hamas and Hezbollah and countering the nuclear threat from the Islamic Republic. In response, Netanyahu thanked Trump for his "extraordinary endorsement." "Together we will never let Iran’s regime get nuclear weapons," he said. TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE President Donald Trump speaks to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Oct. 13, 2025, in Tel Aviv, Israel. President Trump visited the country hours after Hamas released the remaining Israeli hostages captured on Oct. 7, 2023, part of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal to end the war in Gaza. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images) Addressing the endorsement, Doron Spielman, international spokesman for the Israeli Prime Minister’s Office, told Fox News Digital that no personal or professional bond in the history of U.S.-Israel relations compares with the current partnership. "Israel and the U.S. have stood together as the two countries bearing the torch for the West, and that is a direct result of the incredible relationship between President Trump and Netanyahu," he said. He reiterated Netanyahu’s long-standing foreign-policy priority and central campaign promise: ensuring that Iran does not acquire atomic bombs under his watch. "Israel prefers to do this with the U.S., which has been our greatest ally and friend, and who has already entered the front with us twice. But already at the time of Operation Rising Lion, Israel showed that it was willing to act alone. Israel acted for over a week before the U.S. joined," he said, in reference to the June 2025 military mission against Iran. Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, with roughly 20 years in office, Netanyahu began his diplomatic career in 1982 as deputy chief of mission at Israel’s embassy in Washington, D.C. He served as Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations from 1984 to 1988 before entering politics with Likud. He became the party’s chairman in 1993 and was first elected premier in 1996. After losing the 1999 election, Netanyahu returned to government in 2002 as foreign minister and later served as finance minister. He returned to the premiership in 2009, serving until 2021 and again from late 2022. He is widely credited with liberalizing Israel’s economy and helping transform the country into a global high-tech hub. FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER Israel's Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir speaks with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, during a session at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, before it dissolves ahead of the 2026 Israeli elections, in Jerusalem, July 16, 2026. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters) Netanyahu’s current political allies include Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Otzma Yehudit, Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism-Zehut, and the ultra-Orthodox parties Shas and United Torah Judaism. The newcomer Amcha Yisrael, led by Ofer Winter, could also join the bloc, although Winter is currently feuding with Likud over concerns that his party, which is hovering near the electoral threshold, could split the right-wing vote and potentially "waste" tens of thousands of ballots. According to most Hebrew-language media polls, neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot currently has a clear path to securing the 61 Knesset seats needed to form a government. If no candidate can assemble a governing coalition, Israel could head to another election, repeating the cycle of political instability that saw the country hold four national votes between April 2019 and March 2021. Dan Diker, president of the Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs, told Fox News Digital that any incoming government will face the same formidable security challenges as the current one, with few prospects for quick victories. A woman reacts as the community of Kibbutz Kfar Aza commemorates their members who were killed, taken hostage and who died in captivity, following the deadly Oct. 7, 2023, attack by Hamas terrorists, in Kibbutz Kfar Aza, southern Israel, Oct. 16, 2025. (Hannah McKay/Reuters) "The major challenge in this election will be what Netanyahu discussed in terms of adjusting the national security concept to prioritize prevention. That means taking very serious, assertive and aggressive military counterterrorism and nonmilitary actions against our enemies," Diker said. The Israeli left, center and even far-right believe Netanyahu has failed to meet the expectations associated with his image as "Mr. Security," according to professor Tamar Hermann, a senior researcher at the Israel Democracy Institute. ISRAEL DRILLS FOR SURPRISE ATTACK WITH MASSIVE MILITARY EXERCISE AS EXPERT INVOKES 1973 WAR "He promised to topple the Iranian regime, he promised to dismantle Hamas, he promised to crush Hezbollah. None of it was achieved," Hermann told Fox News Digital. "He gave a green light to not punishing vigilantes in the settlements who act against Palestinians. He also gave too much to the ultra-Orthodox parties, giving up on the idea of universal conscription." Hermann said that Netanyahu’s current term has been his least successful, beginning with the judicial reform push, which triggered mass protests in 2023, and followed by the Palestinian terror attacks on Oct. 7. Netanyahu subsequently faced public anger over his handling of the hostage crisis, although, in coordination with Trump and his envoys, he ultimately secured the return of all the captives. Memorials at the site of the Oct. 7 Hamas terror attack on the Supernova music festival near Kibbutz Re'im, Israel, on May 27, 2024. (Kobi Wolf/Bloomberg via Getty Images) "In the eyes of some, his legacy will be that he inflicted a huge disaster upon Israel in terms of what happened to civilians on Oct. 7 and the deterioration of Israel’s international image," she said. Michael Oren, a former Israeli ambassador to the United States, framed the upcoming election in terms of legacy and how Netanyahu will be remembered 50 years from now. "There are two types of leaders: leaders in history and leaders of history," he told Fox News Digital. "There are leaders who go into office and perform as best they can, and there are leaders who go into office and see themselves as transformative, as having a historical role like Abraham Lincoln, Roosevelt or Churchill. Benjamin Netanyahu belongs to this category." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stands on a platform overlooking the Gaza Strip during his first visit to Kibbutz Nir Oz since the Oct. 7, 2023, attack by Hamas terrorists, July 3, 2025. (AP Photo/Leo Correa) Oren said Netanyahu sees his mission as saving Israel from existential threats, foremost among them Iran, a goal he has yet to achieve. "He is willing to endure virtually limitless criticism and condemnation around the world, as well as mass demonstrations against him, to fulfill this one role," he said. "To understand that is to understand Benjamin Netanyahu: He is a leader of history." Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news. title: Schiff accuses DOJ of trying to 'subvert' elections as GOP alleges same-name candidate meant to confuse voters
description: Adam Schiff accuses Trump's DOJ of trying to subvert Alaska's Senate election over a namesake Dan Sullivan candidacy that could confuse voters.
content: Adam Schiff Schiff accuses DOJ of trying to 'subvert' elections as GOP alleges same-name candidate meant to confuse voters The DOJ sued to delay certification over a namesake candidate who could draw votes from Sen Dan Sullivan By Charles Creitz Fox News Published October 26, 2026 2:10pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Trump: We are 'looking into' Dan Sullivan campaign in Alaska Fox News correspondent Matt Finn has the latest on an Alaska midterm race in which both candidates share the same name, the confusion among voters and questions surrounding the unusual matchup on 'America Reports.' NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., accused President Donald Trump's Justice Department of trying to subvert elections through its lawsuit over Alaska's unusual Senate ballot, even as Republicans allege Democrats have propped up a Senate candidate with the same name as the GOP nominee to confuse voters. Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, R- Alaska, is running against Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who has no party affiliation. State courts ultimately allowed the second Dan Sullivan to remain on the ballot. Schiff argued the Justice Department has no business stepping into a matter Alaska's courts have already settled. Republicans contend Daniel Sullivan entered the race to draw votes away from the incumbent and help former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola — a claim the now- Senate candidate and her campaign deny. "They don't have standing to bring this kind of a suit. It's not the federal government's business to run Alaskan elections. It's Alaska's business to do that," Schiff told NBC News on Sunday. "They have already adjudicated this question, and the Justice Department knows this, but it just shows how complicit they are now in the Trump campaign to try to subvert the elections." ALASKA SENATE RACE’S ABSURD NAME PROBLEM GETS EVEN HARDER TO UNTANGLE Sen. Adam Schiff, left; Attorney General nominee Todd Blanche, right. (Al Drago/Getty Images; Eric Lee/Getty Images) Schiff has long been one of Trump's most prominent adversaries, serving as the lead House impeachment manager during Trump's first impeachment trial and later sitting on the House committee investigating the Jan. 6 Capitol riot. The Burbank Democrat has repeatedly accused Trump of undermining democratic institutions and election integrity, making his attack on the Justice Department the latest volley in a yearslong political and legal feud. Schiff drew a comparison to Trump's efforts to challenge the 2020 presidential election, arguing that senior Justice Department officials at the time, including Attorney General William Barr refused to support efforts to overturn the results — while accusing current DOJ leadership of being willing to go further. "This time, with [Attorney General Todd] Blanche, they are all in on this disgraceful campaign," Schiff said, predicting the case in the Last Frontier has "no chance of succeeding." The allegations come as candidate Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg received enough votes in Alaska’s unique primary system to appear beside Sen. Dan S. Sullivan, R-Alaska, on the general election ballot — along with Democratic challenger and former Rep. Mary Peltola. COURT KEEPS ‘DECOY DAN’ ON ALASKA BALLOT AS EXPERT WARNS RANKED-CHOICE SYSTEM CREATES VOTER ‘TRAPS’ State election officials initially disqualified the Petersburg Sullivan after raising concerns that his candidacy was intended to confuse voters, citing his requested ballot name, recent party registration and similarities between campaign materials. An Alaska Superior Court judge overturned the state's decision to disqualify Petersburg Sullivan, allowing the namesake candidate to remain on the ballot despite election officials' concerns about voter deception. The Alaska Supreme Court subsequently upheld that ruling, resolving the state ballot-access dispute, though DOJ is now pursuing a separate federal challenge in the event Petersburg Sullivan's candidacy could alter the election's outcome. TODD BLANCHE CHALLENGES DANA BASH FOR ONLY CITING PART OF CONSTITUTION DURING HEATED ELECTION CLASH Dan J. Sullivan, who has filed to run for U.S. Senate in Alaska, poses for a photo in Petersburg, Alaska, on June 26, 2026. (Katie Holmlund/Associated Press) Blanche’s DOJ filed suit last week after the state proceedings concluded, arguing that the namesake candidacy could mislead voters and seeking to delay certification if votes for Petersburg Sullivan could affect the result. The department's complaint, however, asks the court to prevent certification under a specific scenario: if incumbent Senator Sullivan loses but would have won had votes cast for Petersburg Sullivan gone to him instead. DOJ seeks to delay certification in that circumstance pending an investigation into whether voters intended to support the incumbent. Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the lawsuit Sunday, citing federal election law, while Schiff argued that the state had already adjudicated the dispute. "The sole purpose of his candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan," DOJ’s filing read in part, while also citing a letter from Alaska Division of Elections Director Carol Beecher alleging Petersburg Sullivan’s declaration of candidacy was not properly filed because it was not intended to declare an actual good-faith candidacy. GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, speaks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on June 30, 2025. (Mark Schiefelbein/AP) The filing also included a side-by-side comparison of Petersburg Sullivan’s dark blue campaign banner featuring a star and Senator Sullivan’s campaign banner featuring the Big Dipper — a reference to the constellation depicted on Alaska’s flag. When reached for comment, the DOJ provided Blanche’s defense of the suit, which highlighted that the agency does "not seek to stop any ballot from being cast or to stop the certification of Alaska's election." "This litigation seeks to ensure that after Alaskans cast their ballots, they are preserved in a manner so that only Alaska's governing officials have the information necessary to make a determination as to whether Alaskan voters were confused or mislead," Blanche said. "The lawsuit was written by Justice Department attorneys and the Department did not coordinate with any campaign or candidate, but rather relied solely on federal law." The case cited the National Voter Registration Act, which expressly identifies protecting election integrity as one of its purposes. When asked about the accusation from Schiff, the White House provided recent comments from Trump saying he "recommended" DOJ file the suit and that Petersburg Sullivan was put "up as a matter of confusion." SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "I think it's a disgrace," Trump said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Peltola placed first in the August primary, followed by Senator Sullivan and Petersburg Sullivan. Palmer drywall contractor Gerald Heikes, a Republican, will appear as the fourth candidate on the ballot after a Democrat who placed ahead of him withdrew. title: Terri Clark applauds Ella Langley's historic rise but says she 'would not want to trade places with her'
description: Terri Clark says she wouldn't trade places with Ella Langley despite her historic "Choosin' Texas" run, revealing the emotional toll of fame.
content: OutKick Terri Clark applauds Ella Langley's historic rise but says she 'would not want to trade places with her' The country veteran praised 'Choosin' Texas' but warned that level of fame is 'a blessing and a curse' By Amber Harding OutKick Published October 26, 2026 2:04pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Terri Clark praises Ella Langley's success, reflects on pressures of fame Country music legend Terri Clark tells OutKick OutDoors why she's thrilled about Ella Langley's record-breaking success while reflecting on the emotional pressures and loss of privacy that can come with superstardom. Country music legend Terri Clark knows a thing or two about making it in Nashville. But even after more than three decades in the business, she's not sure she'd want to trade places with Ella Langley right now. Langley has spent much of 2026 rewriting the record books, with her smash hit "Choosin' Texas" making Billboard Hot 100 history. And while Clark couldn't be happier to see another woman dominating country music, she also knows that kind of success comes with a price. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS "I would not want to trade places with her at all," Clark told OutKick OutDoors in an exclusive interview. Terri Clark helped pave the way for many female artists in country music, like Ella Langley. (Taylor Hill/FilmMagic & USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) In September, "Choosin' Texas" surpassed Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" to become the longest-running No. 1 song in Billboard Hot 100 history, logging its 23rd cumulative week atop the chart. Clark, who helped define country music's female-driven era in the 1990s with hits like "Better Things to Do" and "You're Easy on the Eyes," is thrilled to see Langley breaking barriers. But she wishes more women were enjoying that same level of success. "It's like women went from famine to feast all of a sudden, but it's not across the board," Clark said. "I wish there was more of that with other females as well. I wish it was spread out a little bit more as well." Watch Terri Clark's whole interview with OutKick OutDoors here: And although Clark believes women still have a long way to go when it comes to equal representation in country music, she's happy to see Langley leading the charge. "I'm just glad the person breaking all the records and shattering the glass ceiling is a female," Clark said. "I'm glad it's her, you know, and she's so good and she's so deserving." Clark also praised Langley's album, "Dandelion," and said the young star seems like a genuinely good person. "I often when I see her on Instagram and things, I often just want to give her a hug and ask her if she needs to go have coffee and talk because I can't imagine how she's navigating this," Clark said. "It's a lot emotionally and psychologically." Ella Langley performs onstage at the Billboard Women in Music 2026 held at the Hollywood Palladium on April 29, 2026, in Los Angeles, Calif. (Rich Polk/Billboard via Getty Images) Indeed, Langley's meteoric rise has come with plenty of unwanted attention. She's faced online backlash over resurfaced photos of her hunting deer in Alabama, while social media users have also scrutinized her perceived political affiliations and accused her of being an "industry plant" whose success was manufactured by the music industry. CHRIS JANSON HAS A MESSAGE FOR HUNTING CRITICS AS COUNTRY STARS FACE SOCIAL MEDIA BACKLASH None of those controversies was raised by Clark specifically, but they illustrate the kind of public scrutiny that can accompany sudden superstardom. The internet is always looking for ways to take you down. "That level of success is a blessing and a curse at the same time, and you gotta be able to manage both sides of that," Clark said. "And it takes a pretty special person to be able to do that. And I think she can." The freedom to be 'boring and normal' Clark has sold more than five million albums, earned 13 Top 10 singles and secured membership in the Grand Ole Opry. But despite her accomplishments, she's managed to hang on to something many superstars lose along the way: her anonymity. "I've always been able to go to the grocery store in a ball cap," Clark said. She pointed to country stars like Reba McEntire and the late Dolly Parton, whose fame makes ordinary outings considerably more difficult, and suggested Langley may now be experiencing something similar. "There are some people that, you know, their anonymity has been completely stripped from them, and they either have to embrace it, like I've seen some of them do so well, or it can destroy them." Clark isn't sure how she would have handled that degree of attention herself, especially in an era when social media puts celebrities under a microscope. "I'm not sure what would have happened to me if it had ever gotten to that level," she admitted. Terri Clark performs at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, Tenn., on Thursday, Aug. 29, 2024. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) But at 58, Clark has found a pretty comfortable balance. She can still tour, make music and enjoy a successful career without sacrificing the simple pleasures of everyday life. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "I'm very grateful to be able to go and make a living doing what I do, and still go to the grocery store, to still go to Bass Pro Shops, and then once in a while somebody will recognize me," she said. "But it's not anything at that level, which I'm grateful for." "I'm too boring and normal to be able to be that interesting to that many people." Amber Harding is a writer for OutKick. title: Trump's not on the ballot but swing state voters still cast ballots with MAGA in mind
description: Pennsylvania voters say they're voting Democratic in the midterms to rein in Donald Trump, even though some admit they don't trust the party.
content: Midterm Elections Trump's not on the ballot but swing state voters still cast ballots with MAGA in mind Voters in Pennsylvania expressed distrust of both parties on affordability and inflation — but ultimately want change By Hannah Brennan Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:55pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Swing state voters make their feelings about Trump clear in explosive midterm warning Voters in battleground Pennsylvania revealed their midterm plans, with some expressing fierce opposition to President Donald Trump while admitting they don't trust Democrats either. (Credit: Nicholas Ballasy for Fox News Digital) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Voters in the battleground state of Pennsylvania tell Fox News Digital they are driven at the ballot box by a desire to rein in President Donald Trump and his administration's agenda. While many voting in next Tuesday's midterm elections in the Keystone State don't trust Democrats, they are willing to give them a chance to change the trajectory of the country on a myriad of issues — including affordability and rising prices, the Iran war and corruption in Washington, D.C. "I didn't say I trusted the Democrats," Tomas from Doylestown, Pennsylvania, said when asked if he felt the opposition party would do better than the current one in power. "I'm just gonna vote for them because [Trump] is just taking us down the tubes." LEAVITT SAYS TRUMP IS DEFYING MIDTERM HEADWINDS AS HE BARNSTORMS COUNTRY President Donald Trump speaks during a midterm campaign rally at the Guardian Centers on Oct. 24, 2026, in Perry, Georgia. Trump is speaking in support of the Senate candidate, Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., who is trying to unseat Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., and Republican gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson. (Alex Wong/Getty Images) Clay, another Pennsylvania voter, told Fox News Digital, "I don't," when asked why he trusts Democrats to tackle affordability better than Republicans. "The party that we're currently working with is so f---ed up, we might as well change it. I don't trust the Democrats though," he added. Voters in Delaware County and Bucks County were pressed on the issue of affordability and whether Democrats would be better equipped to address bringing prices down, particularly after inflation surged during former President Joe Biden's administration. "Republicans have showed in the past two years that they really have made things worse," Chris from Doylestown said when asked if he believes Democrats will bring down prices. "Gas is way up, the energy is way up, food's way up. There's nothing that's cheaper, so they can't argue that." "I mean, Donald Trump's in office, how much worse can it get?" he went on. "Telling me that it can get worse than this? It's the worst it's ever been. You think that by having... Democrats in office... that somehow it's gonna make things go even higher? I don't think so." The results in Pennsylvania will play a key role in the battle for control of Congress, with Republicans fighting to maintain their majorities as Trump works to rally voters behind Republican candidates. The outcome of the midterm elections, just eight days away, could have major implications for the remainder of Trump's presidency, with a Democratic takeover of either chamber threatening to complicate his efforts to push his agenda through Congress. FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS Voters in Pennsylvania tell Fox News Digital they are voting Democrat in the closely approaching midterm elections in an effort to halt President Donald Trump's agenda. (Nicholas Ballasy/Fox News Digital; Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images) Many who spoke with Fox News Digital had broader reasons to vote Democrat in next week's midterms. "We have a mentally ill president," Nancy from Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, said. "We have a ball-less GOP party who will not rein him in." "I am voting for the Democratic congressional slate," Tom from Media, Pennsylvania, said. "I really think that Donald Trump has not been good for our country, and we sort of need to… slow down what he's doing." "I am voting straight Democrat," a voter Fox News Digital spoke with named Bill said. "And the reason why is because the Republican Party refuses to stand up to the fascist actions of Donald Trump." title: Major airline delays 150 passengers overnight following serious in-flight threat
description: United Flight 1681 made a swift U-turn back to Las Vegas after the crew flagged a potential security concern, triggering an overnight crew timeout, the airline confirmed.
content: Travel United Airlines delays 150 passengers overnight following serious in-flight threat Dante Milne was detained without incident after the United flight returned to Las Vegas By Jessica Mekles , Sophia Compton Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:55pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Cabin pressure emergency triggers rapid response as passengers get oxygen, pilot says Former American Airlines and FedEx pilot Matthew 'Whiz' Buckley discusses why a pressurization malfunction demands swift action. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! A 25-year-old man was arrested after allegedly making terroristic threats aboard a Newark-bound United Airlines flight, prompting the plane to turn around and return to Las Vegas late Saturday night, police said. The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department (LVMPD) said officers responded to Harry Reid International Airport on Oct. 24 after the passenger allegedly made threats aboard United Flight 1681. Officers detained the passenger, identified as Dante Milne, without incident after the plane landed safely, according to police. LVMPD investigators arrested Milne on suspicion of making a threat or conveying false information concerning an act of terrorism. He was later booked into the Clark County Detention Center. TRAVEL NIGHTMARE UNFOLDS AS MAJOR AIRLINE SCRAPS FLIGHT AFTER HARROWING 12-HOUR DELAY A 25-year-old man was arrested after allegedly making terroristic threats aboard a Newark-bound United Airlines flight. (iStock) "United flight 1681 from Las Vegas to Newark on Saturday, Oct. 24, safely returned to Las Vegas to address a potential security concern," United Airlines said in a shared statement with Fox News Digital. "The flight was delayed overnight due to crew timeout, and departed for Newark this morning," the statement continued. The Boeing 737, carrying 150 passengers and six crew members, landed back in Las Vegas at roughly 11:05 p.m. without any reported injuries, several news outlets reported. While the midair scare was resolved without physical harm, the diversion triggered an overnight delay after the flight crew timed out of their legally permitted working hours. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The flight diversion triggered an overnight delay after the flight crew timed out of their legally permitted working hours. (Al Drago/Getty Images) Fox News Digital reached out to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for comment. In an air traffic control audio recording that ATC.com obtained, a controller can be heard asking pilots if a passenger in question was "compliant or restrained." "The passenger does not know anything is going on," a pilot said. "The flight attendant saw him texting that he was going to hijack the aircraft and called me and we went lockdown. … No restraint, passenger is compliant because he’s unaware." The aircraft eventually departed for Newark Liberty International Airport the following morning. The FAA confirmed it is launching an investigation into the incident, Fox 5 Las Vegas reported. Fox News Digital reached out to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department for additional details. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department is investigating the incident. (Chase Stevens/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The pilot informed Air Traffic Control the aircraft was still "grossly overweight" and needed to burn excess fuel before touching down, the audio recording shows. An overweight landing risks adding stress to the plane's landing gear and structural parts, per SKYbrary Aviation Safety. To avoid potential damage during an unplanned landing, planes will sometimes dump fuel or fly longer to burn it off. Reflecting this, flight paths show the aircraft made two loops to burn fuel before returning to land at LAS, per FlightAware. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ In May, another United Airlines flight bound for Minneapolis, Minnesota, made an emergency landing in Madison, Wisconsin, after a passenger allegedly attempted to storm the cockpit, according to air traffic control audio. The flight, which took off from Chicago's O'Hare International Airport, "landed safely in Madison, Wisconsin to address a security concern with an unruly passenger," United Airlines previously told Fox News Digital. In May, another United Airlines flight bound for Minneapolis, Minnesota, made an emergency landing in Madison, Wisconsin. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images) The flight landed in Madison's Dane County Regional Airport roughly 90 minutes after takeoff, according to flight tracking data. title: Eric Bauza, 'Looney Tunes' voice actor behind Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dead at 46
description: Eric Bauza, the voice actor who carried on Mel Blanc's legendary "Looney Tunes" legacy, died Sunday at age 46 of hypertensive cardiovascular disease.
content: Departed Eric Bauza, 'Looney Tunes' voice actor behind Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dead at 46 Eric Bauza had more than 400 voice-acting credits including the iconic 'Looney Tunes' characters By Lauryn Overhultz Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:49pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video "Coyote vs. Acme" preview with voice star Eric Bauza & director Dave Green Bauza shares what it means to be such a big part of the Looney Tunes legacy & director Dave Green talks about creating the adventure, which in theaters this week following Wile E. Coyote suing Acme for all the faulty gadgets. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Eric Bauza, the voice behind iconic "Looney Tunes" characters including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, has died, Fox News Digital has confirmed. Bauza died Sunday from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. He was 46. Beginning in 2001, Bauza amassed more than 400 voice-acting credits in a career that gave voice to beloved characters in animated Looney Tunes series including "Puss in Boots," "Muppet Babies," "Avatar: The Last Airbender," and countless others. The voice actor's family confirmed his death on Instagram, but has not shared any additional details. HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026 Eric Bauza attends the "Space Jam: A New Legacy" party on June 29, 2021. (Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images) Fox News Digital reached out to Bauza's representative. Bauza's early breakthrough came when he voiced Stimpy in the 2003 series "Ren & Stimpy: Adult Party Cartoon," taking over the character previously voiced by Billy West. He became one of Hollywood's most recognizable voice talents, particularly for his work carrying on the legacy of legendary Looney Tunes performer Mel Blanc. "I’m a fan first when it comes to this franchise, this band of characters. Mel Blanc will always be the original gangsta, the godfather of voiceover," Bauza told Fox News Digital back in 2020. "He was the first voice actor credited on screen as a voice actor. They never did back in the day. And we’re talking about the ‘30s and ‘40s." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Eric Bauza voiced several iconic "Looney Tunes" characters, including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, and appeared in films such as "Space Jam: A New Legacy" and "Coyote vs. Acme." (Eric Charbonneau/Getty Images) "So he really paved the way to show the importance of vocal performance, not an on-camera one. And the fact that we’re sitting here now talking about his performance just shows you how incredible, impactful and influential his sound is." Bauza's Looney Tunes work included feature films such as "Space Jam: A New Legacy" (2021), "The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie" (2024) and this year's "Coyote vs. Acme." Bauza won three Children's and Family Emmy Awards during his career. Beyond bringing Bugs Bunny to life on screen, Bauza had a deep appreciation for the character's roots and what made him so beloved by generations of fans. Reflecting on Bugs Bunny's signature personality, Bauza once explained how the character's unmistakable New York accent came to be. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Eric Bauza once explained that Bugs Bunny's signature accent was inspired by a combination of Brooklyn and Bronx accents, a creative decision made by original voice actor Mel Blanc. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images) "And if you’re wondering where [Bugs Bunny] got that accent from, they say he’s a rascally rabbit," Bauza told Fox News Digital. "So [Mel] thought, he’s gotta be a tough character. And there’s no one tougher than a New Yorker, that’s what he said. He said it’s either Brooklyn or The Bronx. He mixed the two together, those accents. So that’s why he kind of has that street talk." "I think he represents the everyman, the every rabbit," he added. "He doesn’t have a lot of high demands in life. All he wants is a carrot and a nice afternoon where no one bugs him. And if you get on his bad side, that’s when you gotta look out. That’s when he becomes the trickster. But really, he’s just a simple rabbit, nothing to him. I think that’s why he’s so appealing. And I think that’s why when he gets in trouble, people want him to succeed." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Eric Bauza won three Children's and Family Emmy Awards during his voice acting career. (Tommaso Boddi/Getty Images) With hundreds of voice-acting credits across television, film and video games, Bauza built a career introducing classic cartoon characters to new generations while creating memorable performances of his own. His work helped keep some of animation's most enduring characters alive for modern audiences. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Associated Press contributed to this report. title: Angel mom confronts Indian illegal immigrant truck driver who killed her son, his wife in Oregon crash
description: An emotional video captures Erika Kirk-like compassion as a grieving mother speaks to Rajinder Kumar, the truck driver facing manslaughter in Oregon.
content: Blue City Crime Angel mom confronts Indian illegal immigrant truck driver who killed her son, his wife in Oregon crash Elizabeth Carter tells Rajinder Kumar, 32, through an ICE vehicle window: 'I pray for you' By Eric Mack , Bill Melugin Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:38pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Grieving angel mom forgives illegal immigrant trucker accused of killing newlywed son in Oregon crash Exclusive ICE video shows Elizabeth Carter offering prayers to Rajinder Kumar, 32, outside a federal vehicle as he faces manslaughter charges in the deaths of her son and daughter-in-law. (ICE VOICE Office) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! An emotional video shows a grieving mother delivering compassion to her son's alleged killer. Video from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement's Victims of Immigrant Crime Engagement (VOICE) office showed Elizabeth Carter, the mother of William Carter, speaking to the Indian illegal immigrant semi-truck driver charged with killing her son and his newlywed wife. The couple perished in an Oregon highway crash in November 2025. "Hello Mr. Kumar, my name is Elizabeth Carter; I'm William Micah Carter's mother," she told Rajinder Kumar, 32, fighting back tears and emotion as he appeared to struggle to meet her gaze. "And I wanted you to know that I pray for you and your family, I know you didn't get up that morning planning to kill two newlyweds. And I know your family is going through something important too." ANGEL MOM PLEADS WITH HER PARTY TO 'GROW UP' ON IMMIGRATION AFTER NEWLYWED SON KILLED IN TRUCK CRASH Self-identified "lifelong Democrat" Elizabeth Carter, left, testified that she is "ashamed" of her party's handling of the immigration issue after her son, William Carter, and daughter-in-law, Jennifer Lower, right, were killed in a car crash involving an illegal immigrant semi-truck driver. (Screenshot from House Judiciary GOP official YouTube livestream; DHS) The interaction took place at the passenger window of an ICE vehicle earlier this month as federal agents prepared to transfer Kumar back to Oregon state custody to face criminal prosecution. Kumar faces two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person in Deschutes County stemming from the fatal wreck. Kumar is accused of killing William Micah Carter, 25, and his wife, Jennifer Lynn Lower, 24, who had been married for just 16 days. The deadly collision occurred on Nov. 24, 2025, when Kumar allegedly jackknifed his commercial tractor-trailer across U.S. Highway 20, blocking both lanes of traffic. The couple’s Subaru Outback struck the semi, killing both passengers at the scene. WATCH: 'LIFELONG DEMOCRAT' ADMITS SHE IS ‘ASHAMED’ OF PARTY AFTER SON KILLED IN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CRASH William Micah Carter and Jennifer Lynn Lower were killed in a crash in Oregon just 16 days after getting married, according to the Department of Homeland Security. (Department of Homeland Security) Kumar was subsequently indicted by a Deschutes County grand jury. While he pleaded not guilty in state court, a jurisdictional battle erupted between federal and local authorities following his release. Court and immigration records show that Kumar entered the United States unlawfully near Lukeville, Ariz., on Nov. 28, 2022, when he was apprehended by U.S. Border Patrol and subsequently released into the country under the Biden administration pending removal proceedings. During that period, he was granted federal work authorization and later obtained a commercial driver's license (CDL) issued by the State of California. DOJ SUES CONNECTICUT, NEW HAVEN OVER SANCTUARY POLICIES: 'OPEN DEFIANCE' ICE lodged an immigration detainer against illegal immigrant Rajinder Kumar, who is allegedly behind a fatal crash that killed two. (Reuters; Department of Homeland Security) Following Kumar’s indictment in Oregon, ICE lodged an immigration detainer requesting that Deschutes County Jail notify federal agents before releasing him. County corrections officials declined to honor the federal detainer on April 2 and released Kumar into the community under Oregon’s state sanctuary policies. ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Seattle agents tracked down and arrested Kumar in connection with his immigration case on April 22, detaining him at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Wash., while moving forward with federal removal proceedings. EXCLUSIVE: DHS HONORS ANGEL FAMILIES DURING NATIONAL CRIME VICTIMS WEEK, CALLS CRIMES 'COMPLETELY PREVENTABLE' Video ICE ERO Seattle announced it has returned Kumar to Deschutes County authorities to ensure he faces a local trial on the felony manslaughter charges before any deportation orders are executed. "Two Americans lost their lives, and their families deserve accountability," ICE ERO Seattle acting Field Office Director Julio Hernandez said. "ICE worked closely with law enforcement partners to ensure Kumar is returned to state custody to answer for the serious charges against him. "This coordinated action protects the public, supports the victims' families, and ensures that an individual accused of these crimes does not evade justice." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Department of Homeland Security officials confirmed that federal deportation proceedings remain paused while Oregon state prosecutors pursue the criminal charges against Kumar, with criminal trial proceedings pending in Deschutes County Circuit Court. title: US taxpayer dollars allegedly fueled left-wing political causes in Latin America
description: Eduardo Bolsonaro claims over $60 million in USAID funds went to Brazil to support groups combating so-called right-wing misinformation online.
content: Latin America US taxpayer dollars allegedly fueled left-wing political causes in Latin America US and Latin American officials allege the dismantled agency ran its own foreign policy under the Biden administration By Pedro B Rodriguez-Aparicio Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:34pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google Then-President Joe Biden and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva meet during a working lunch at the G20 Leader's Summit at the Museum of Modern Art in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on Nov. 19, 2024. (Eric Lee - Pool/AFP via Getty Images) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! EXCLUSIVE: U.S. and Latin American officials are accusing the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) of using American taxpayer dollars for causes championed by left-wing candidates across Latin America. The allegations come after several countries in the region elected conservative leaders following the Trump administration’s decision to dismantle USAID and shift remaining foreign assistance functions to the State Department. "You have plenty of examples out there of how USAID was attempting to run its own foreign policy," U.S. Ambassador to Panama Kevin Marino Cabrera told Fox News Digital. BIDEN-ERA DIRECTIVE FOR DIPLOMATS TO PEDDLE DEI ON FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS SCRAPPED BY STATE DEPARTMENT Cabrera said USAID’s dismantling has allowed the State Department and U.S. Southern Command to work more closely with partner countries on disaster relief and recovery efforts. "When you look at a post-USAID world where we have forces from the State Department and U.S. Southern Command working together in Jamaica, Venezuela, Colombia and now Panama, they’ve had great success in responding to natural disasters," Cabrera said. AP POST ON USAID CUTS BACKFIRES AS CRITICS QUESTION TAXPAYER-FUNDED NEPAL TRANSGENDER JOBS "We’re focused on actual disaster relief and recovery. We’re not focused on these crazy agendas, like failed DEI policies that have nothing to do with foreign policy or disaster relief and recovery," he added. Cabrera also criticized what he described as a lack of leadership during the Biden administration, saying it allowed USAID to pursue programs that promoted left-wing causes in the region. Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks at the State Department on April 14, 2026. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images) TRUMP ADMIN'S PUSH TO SCRAP DEI IN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TAKES LANDMARK STEP WITH NEW HIRING RULE Eduardo Bolsonaro, a Brazilian politician and the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, made similar allegations in an interview with The Daily Signal earlier this month. Bolsonaro claimed that more than $60 million in U.S. taxpayer funds was sent to Brazil through USAID, the National Endowment for Democracy and the Atlantic Council to support organizations that combat what those groups describe as "right-wing misinformation." LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has recently positioned his administration as a global champion of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI), and has used high-profile international forums to criticize what he describes as a coordinated wave of right-wing disinformation. Flávio Bolsonaro entered the 2026 Brazilian presidential race after receiving an endorsement from his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. (Evaristo Sa/AFP via Getty Images) "This is foreign election interference," Bolsonaro told the outlet. "American taxpayer dollars were financing foreign censorship in the name of the left, which is completely contrary to why USAID was even created in the first place." Bolsonaro said President John F. Kennedy created USAID with good intentions but argued that the agency had since strayed from its original mission. The Atlantic Council and the National Endowment for Democracy did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. A manhunt is underway for a Tennessee inmate serving a life sentence for murder after he escaped from prison and stole a white heavy-duty pickup truck during his getaway. The Tennessee Department of Correction said that Jacob Allen Morley, 28, escaped the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, Tennessee, on Sunday. He was sentenced to life in prison after being convicted in 2025 of murdering Cody Birchfield three years earlier. Prison staff discovered Morley was unaccounted for around 11:30 p.m. Sunday and immediately conducted an emergency count and search of the facility, according to a Tennessee Department of Correction statement given to Fox News Digital. 'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN Surveillance footage shows convicted murderer Jacob Allen Morley inside Northwest Correctional Complex before his escape Sunday. Authorities said Morley was captured on security video breaching a prison fence. (Tennessee Department of Correction) Security video showed Morley breaching a fence while still wearing prison clothing. Around 1 a.m. Monday, video footage captured Morley stealing a vehicle on the 400 block of Keystone Drive, roughly two miles south of the prison, according to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation. The vehicle is a white 2008 Ford F-350 with Tennessee license plate 138BBQV. It is marked with the name Lindamood Planting Company on the side and has an air compressor in the bed, officials said. Tennessee Bureau of Investigation The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said Jacob Allen Morley stole a white pickup truck marked with Lindamood Planting Company on the side. (Tennessee Bureau of Investigation ) Morley is described as 5 feet, 11 inches tall and weighing 240 pounds, with brown hair and green eyes. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said he should be "considered dangerous," adding Morley is now on the state's most wanted list. MANHUNT TARGETS ‘ARMED AND DANGEROUS’ MURDER SUSPECT NOW ON STATE’S MOST WANTED LIST In addition to the first-degree murder conviction, he was also found guilty of burglary, vandalism, tampering with evidence and evading arrest. title: Trump isn't done overhauling the White House — and his next move could hit the media where it works
description: Trump says he's considering relocating the White House press corps to a different location but denies plans to replace the briefing room with an indoor pool.
content: Politics Trump isn't done overhauling the White House — and his next move could hit the media where it works The president denied a recent New York Times report that he planned to replace the briefing room with a swimming pool By Ireland Owens Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:05pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Supreme Court rules 5-4 to allow construction on $400 million White House ballroom Fox News chief legal correspondent Shannon Bream discusses the Supreme Court's decision on President Donald Trump's White House ballroom on 'Special Report.' NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! President Donald Trump is considering giving the White House press corps the boot from its longtime briefing room — and has another use in mind for the space that doesn't involve the swimming pool he insists was never on the table. Trump said Sunday he is thinking about relocating reporters to make room for other White House needs, a day after suggesting the press could be moved to a "less obnoxious location." "I am not building a swimming pool in the White House Briefing Room, and never had any intention of doing so," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "I am thinking about moving the Press, and putting them in a different location, but I will use that location for very badly needed space." The president’s comments come after The New York Times reported on Oct. 20 that Trump had discussed replacing the White House’s James S. Brady Press Briefing Room with an indoor swimming pool. DAVID MARCUS: KAROLINE LEAVITT’S LASTING LEGACY IS OPENING THE WHITE HOUSE TO INDIE PRESS President Donald Trump spoke during a news conference in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House on April 6, 2026, in Washington, D.C., where he warned journalists against publishing details of a U.S. military raid to rescue two airmen shot down over Iran, saying such reporting could jeopardize operations. (Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images) When reached for additional comment, the White House referred Fox News Digital to Trump's Sunday Truth Social post. In a separate Truth Social post published Saturday, Trump shot down reports he planned to build a swimming pool, insisting he would never consider doing "such a stupid thing." "There is a Fake News report out there that I am going to remove the White House Press Room and bring back the old Swimming Pool, which lies directly underneath," Trump wrote in the social media post. "Although I may move the Fake News to a less obnoxious location, the old swimming pool will never be brought back." President Donald Trump takes questions from reporters during a press briefing at the White House, on the one-year mark into his second term in office, in Washington, D.C., Jan. 20, 2026. (Jessica Koscielniak/Reuters) TRUMP THREATENS TO ADD NY TIMES' 'TREASONOUS' IRAN WAR COVERAGE TO $15B DEFAMATION LAWSUIT The White House’s indoor swimming pool opened on June 2, 1933, following a New York Daily News campaign to raise funds for a pool for President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who had polio and regularly swam in therapy pools at his Hyde Park home or at a rehabilitation center in Warm Springs, Georgia, according to the White House Historical Association. To meet the growing demand for television news, President Richard M. Nixon later arranged for a press briefing room to be constructed above the old pool. Press secretary Karoline Leavitt speaks during a briefing at the White House on July 16, 2026. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images) TRUMP BYPASSES MEDIA GATEKEEPERS AS GOV SANDERS REVEALS LEGACY OUTLETS ARE LOSING THEIR GRIP Trump touted the ongoing renovations to the White House during a rally in Florida last Friday, saying his administration is "building some beautiful things." He also personally paid to install two 88-foot-tall flagpoles at the White House last July. title: Michael Douglas doesn't 'feel bad' about affair revelations from 'before Catherine'
description: Michael Douglas revealed Catherine Zeta-Jones just got his memoir two days before his podcast appearance, joking their 25-year age gap softens the blow.
content: Entertainment Michael Douglas doesn't 'feel bad' about affair revelations from 'before Catherine' The actor's memoir 'One Helluva Ride' confirmed secret relationships with Kathleen Turner and Jeanne Tripplehorn By Ashley Hume Fox News Published October 26, 2026 1:00pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Michael Douglas admits he almost left his wife for his 'Basic Instinct' co-star after affair In his memoir, "One Helluva Ride," the actor admitted he had an affair with his "Basic Instinct" co-star, Jeanne Tripplehorn. (This video contains AI-assisted content.) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Michael Douglas gave a cheeky response when asked how his wife, Catherine Zeta-Jones, had reacted to his new tell-all, "One Helluva Ride." The 82-year-old actor's new memoir, published Oct. 6, contained revelations about his life, including his secret affairs with his former co-stars Kathleen Turner and Jeanne Tripplehorn, as well as his past cocaine use and struggles with addiction. During an appearance on the "Happy, Sad, Confused" podcast on the day of the book's release, host Josh Horowitz asked Douglas whether Zeta-Jones, 57, knew "everything" that he revealed in the book. MICHAEL DOUGLAS GETS EXPLICIT ABOUT HOW HE FILMED SEX SCENES BEFORE INTIMACY COORDINATORS "I'll be home to ask her because she just got the book two days ago. I told her this was all, as I say, B.C., before Catherine," Douglas said in the interview, which was published on Oct. 19. Michael Douglas admitted that he "doesn't feel bad" about his wife Catherine Zeta-Jones reading about his affair revelations in his memoir. (Getty Images for The Red Sea International Film Festival) "And you know, we have a 25-year age difference, so I'm looking at some of these films, like with Kathleen, and Catherine would have been seven years old," he joked. "I don't feel bad," Douglas added. "I think she understands." Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones married in 2000. (Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic) In "One Helluva Ride," Douglas confirmed that he and Turner, 72, had an affair in 1983 while filming the hit 1984 romantic adventure movie "Romancing the Stone," a rumor they denied for over 40 years. At the time, Douglas was legally married to Diandra Luker, with whom he shares son Cameron, though he said in his memoir that they were separated when production on the film began, and they were both having extramarital affairs. Douglas recalled that he and Turner continued to deny rumors that they were romantically involved during production of the sequel and even years later when they reunited on "The Kominsky Method." SALLY FIELD SAYS BURT REYNOLDS WAS ‘WONDERFUL’ BUT ‘FRIGHTENING,’ CLAIMS HE TRIED TO CONTROL HER CAREER The two told the public that while they "had amazing chemistry" and were "both tempted," they never acted on their feelings. Douglas joked that Zeta-Jones would have been "seven years old" when he and Kathleen Turner had an affair while filming "Romancing the Stone." (20th Century-Fox/Getty Images) "The truth is that during the production of ‘Romancing the Stone,' Kathleen and I fell hard for each other and began a relationship," he wrote. "It wasn’t a fly-by night affair; it grew naturally from how closely we were working together, how much pressure we were under, how much we respected and cared for one another, and how attracted we were to each other. Like every other guy in the world at the time, I was knocked sideways by Kathleen." PHIL COLLINS GETS FRANK ON MARRIAGE FAILURES AND LIFE REGRETS: 'I REGRET MY MARRIAGES FALLING APART' He noted that he and Turner kept their affair a secret for 40 years to protect Luker and Cameron. Douglas wrote that the two decided to end their relationship after Luker visited them on set with Cameron "and made it clear to her [Turner] that we were still married." After reports circulated about Douglas' admission, Turner said in a statement to People, "Good heavens, what a fuss about something 40 years ago! I love Michael, and I look forward to enjoying the book." Michael Douglas and Diandra Luker were married for 23 years, from 1977 until their divorce was finalized in 2000. (Sygma via Getty Images) SHARON STONE SAYS SHE 'NEARLY DIED' AFTER 'BASIC INSTINCT' OPENED THE DOOR TO HOLLYWOOD'S DARK SIDE Douglas also disclosed that he and Tripplehorn, 63, who was almost 20 years his junior, had an affair during the filming of their 1992 movie, "Basic Instinct." "The truth is, I fell very hard for Jeanne despite our nearly 20-year age difference," he wrote. "In fact, I was ready to officially leave my wife for Jeanne. I was crazy about her." Douglas also revealed that he had an affair with Jeanne Tripplehorn. (TriStar Pictures/courtesy Everett Collection) Douglas recalled that his "relationship with Jeanne lasted through production," but that they "went our separate ways" once production ended. "But I will always think of her as an amazing actress and a truly terrific woman that I was very fortunate to spend time with," he added. 'CADDYSHACK' STAR MICHAEL O'KEEFE CLAIMS COCAINE WAS BUDGETED ON SET, ADMITS FILMING SCENES HIGH Douglas maintained that he and Luker were still separated at the time. Luker filed for divorce in 1995, and their split was finalized in 2000. Tripplehorn has not publicly commented on Douglas' memoir, though the actor previously said she approved of him including their relationship in the book. During an interview with Page Six, Douglas said, "I talked to her before I put it in the book," adding that "she was fine" with it. Cameron Douglas and Michael Douglas attend the 2024 Vanity Fair Oscar Party at the Wallis Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts on March 10, 2024, in Beverly Hills, Calif. (Variety via Getty Images) The memoir also explored Douglas’ struggles with substance abuse, his complicated relationship with his late father, Kirk Douglas, and Cameron’s battle with addiction. Zeta-Jones previously confirmed that she had not yet read "One Helluva Ride" during an Oct. 8 appearance on "Today." "As much as I love my husband, when I’m tired at night, I have no intention of reading about him. At all," she joked. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The Oscar winner cited her exhausting schedule, having just wrapped up seven months of filming the third season of her Netflix series "Wednesday" in Dublin, while also working on her new Prime Video show "Kill Jackie" in London and traveling to Bilbao, Spain, before her press tour. Zeta-Jones previously said that she has not yet read the book. (Getty Images for Netflix) "But everyone else should [read it]," Zeta-Jones told the audience. "The book is called ‘One Helluva Ride,’ and I think everyone should hold on to their cowboy hats, because I think it is." During a subsequent appearance on "Jimmy Kimmel Live!," Douglas was asked if it "was for the best" that Zeta-Jones had not read his memoir. "Oh, yeah," Douglas quipped. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS In an Oct. 7 interview with Page Six, Douglas confirmed that he had already "talked" to Zeta-Jones about the book and expressed his confidence that she would be "very understanding." Douglas first fell head over heels for Zeta-Jones when she caught his eye in the 1998 movie "The Mask of Zorro." He went on to meet Zeta-Jones at the Deauville Film Festival in France. At the time, Zeta-Jones was aware of his reputation as a Hollywood womanizer and wary of starting a relationship with him. In his memoir, Douglas recalled that Zeta-Jones demanded monogamy, and he called five other women that day to end their relationships before committing to her. The couple share two children. (Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images) PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE The couple, who share the same birthday, Sept. 25, though 25 years apart, became engaged in December 1999 and tied the knot in November 2000. Douglas and Zeta-Jones, who are parents to son Dylan, 26, and daughter Carys, 23, separated in 2013 before reconciling eight months later in 2014. In "One Helluva Ride," Douglas wrote candidly about their separation and shared that he never gave up hope that they would reconcile. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I love Catherine in a way that I have never loved any other woman," he wrote. "She's my wife, my best friend, and my life partner. I could never lose her." title: JJ McCarthy opting not to wear eyeblack in Giants win over Texans likely linked to his hatred for Ohio State
description: JJ McCarthy ditched his signature eyeblack against the Houston Texans, and the reason traces back to his bitter recruiting history with Ohio State.
content: OutKick JJ McCarthy opting not to wear eyeblack in Giants win over Texans likely linked to his hatred for Ohio State McCarthy has a history of dropping the eyeblack against Ohio State players, dating back to his Michigan rivalry days By Mark Harris OutKick Published October 26, 2026 12:57pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Chazz Palmintieri LOVES J.J. McCarthy In New York | The Craig Carton Show Michigan fan and donor Chazz Palminteri is ecstatic for J.J. McCarthy getting traded to the Giants JJ McCarthy led the New York Giants to an overtime win over the Houston Texans on Sunday in what was his first start under center for his new team, and did so in a unique fashion, literally. McCarthy took the field in Houston without wearing any eyeblack on his face. Typically, a player choosing not to wear eyeblack for a game wouldn't be newsworthy, with most folks not even picking up on the change, but there is both history and quite the story involving McCarthy and the eyeblack in this scenario. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. McCarthy has worn a hefty amount of eyeblack throughout his career, even dating back to his high school playing days at IMG Academy, and did the same throughout his three seasons playing at Michigan. There was a notable exception to the look during his time with the Wolverines, however, as he never wore the eyeblack when they were taking on Ohio State. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) looks on before playing against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images (Thomas Shea-Imagn Images) OHIO STATE MOVES SENIOR DAY AWAY FROM MICHIGAN GAME IN AN EFFORT TO REMOVE 'DISTRACTIONS' As a football player at Michigan, McCarthy simply had to dislike Ohio State, but his hatred for the Wolverines' biggest rival ran a lot deeper. The former first-round pick was offered by the Buckeyes out of high school, but while reflecting on the recruiting process, he told The Athletic in 2019 that he felt like he was misled by Ohio State head coach Ryan Day about what his plans were for the quarterback room. Quarterback Quinn Ewers, the top-ranked recruit of the 2021 class, ended up at Ohio State along with four-star signal caller Kyle McCord. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) warms up before a game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images (Troy Taormina-Imagn Images) McCarthy chose to take his talents to Ann Arbor and went a perfect 3-0 against the Buckeyes during his time at Michigan, making sure Day "could see his face after he kicked his a - -," according to his quarterback coach at Michigan. McCarthy is on record stating that he used to "love" the Buckeyes, but wanted to "kill them" after his recruiting process and landing at Michigan. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) reacts after a play during the second quarter against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images (Troy Taormina-Imagn Images) OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD As for McCarthy ditching the eyeblack for Sunday's matchup against the Texans, it's safe to assume it had everything to do with the quarterback on the other sideline, CJ Stroud, who attended Ohio State. The no-eyeblack look could not have been just some coincidence. Stroud never beat Michigan in his two starts against the Wolverines, and he's still winless against a McCarthy-led squad after Sunday's contest. Mark Harris is a writer for OutKick. title: Democrats far less likely than Republicans to prioritize patriotism as key value, poll finds
description: A 40-point gap on patriotism marks the widest partisan divide in a new Gallup Poll examining what values Americans say the country needs most.
content: Politics Democrats far less likely than Republicans to prioritize patriotism as key value, poll finds 40-point gap on patriotism is the single widest partisan divide in a new survey of American values By Eric Mack Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:26pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Lee Greenwood reacts to Dem calling patriotism 'controversial,' relaunches spirits brand Singer-songwriter Lee Greenwood joins 'Fox & Friends' to react to an Iowa Democrat calling patriotism 'controversial.' He also discusses relaunching his patriotic spirits brand, Soldier Valley Spirits, which gives back to American heroes. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Democrats are far less likely than Republicans to prioritize patriotism as a core value the nation needs, marking the single widest partisan divide in a new survey examining the country’s values. According to a Gallup and With Honor survey released Sunday, 46% of Republicans ranked patriotism among the top three values the nation needs most, compared with just 6% of Democrats – a 40-percentage-point difference that dwarfs every other ideological disagreement in the poll. "Democrats are far more likely to say the country needs equality, fairness and kindness, while Republicans are far more likely to say the country needs responsibility and patriotism," according to Gallup. ONLY 27% OF DEMOCRATS WILL DISPLAY AMERICAN FLAG ON JULY 4: POLL This summer's World Cup brought patriotism to the forefront and helped unite Americans on the 250th anniversary of the nation's founding. (Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty Images) Overall, Americans view honesty (34%), responsibility (32%) and integrity (31%) as the values most urgently needed. Beneath that surface, though, the parties see starkly different remedies for what is most needed in the nation. STUNNINGLY LOW PERCENTAGE OF ADULTS IN US THINK AMERICA STANDS ABOVE EVERY OTHER NATION: POLL Video Republicans place the highest priority on patriotism (46%), followed by responsibility (41%) and honesty (38%). Democrats as a whole valued equality highest (44%), followed by fairness (34%) and honesty (32%). DEMS PUT ON BLAST OVER POLL THAT SHOWS RECORD-LOW PATRIOTISM IN US: 'TEAR OUR SOCIETY APART' Independents land between both sides, most frequently selecting honesty (34%), responsibility (32%) and integrity (31%), with only 15% selecting patriotism. Video Despite the large disparity between Democrats and Republicans on the value of patriotism, it was one of the most selected values that participants said they believed was shared by most Americans regardless of their political leanings. When given a list of 12 choices, 32% said they believed most Americans shared patriotism as a value, trailing only freedom at 38%. Those 12 values were: freedom, patriotism, service, kindness, respect, equality, fairness, responsibility, integrity, courage, honesty and humility. More than three-quarters of Americans (76%) believed people shared at least one of those values regardless of politics, while 59% said at least two, and 46% said at least three. INDEPENDENT VOTERS AREN’T PICKING A POLITICAL TEAM, THEY JUST FEEL PICKED ON Video Beyond patriotism, the second-largest partisan divide emerged around equality, chosen by 44% of Democrats compared to just 10% of Republicans – a 34-point spread. Fairness similarly split the electorate, chosen by 34% of Democrats versus 15% of Republicans. The findings also reveal an age divide that mirrors the political split. Adults aged 65 and older are nearly three times as likely as adults aged 18-39 to say the nation needs more patriotism (32% vs. 12%). Despite the deep differences in priorities, the survey revealed broad consensus on political tolerance. Nearly eight in 10 Americans (79%) – including 84% of Democrats, 81% of independents and 72% of Republicans – said respecting different values matters more than sharing the same ones. Additionally, 70% of respondents said elected leaders must be willing to compromise across party lines, even at personal political cost. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Perhaps, then, the ultimate shared value is that Americans agree to disagree," the Gallup analysis concluded. The survey was conducted May 12–22 among a nationally representative panel of more than 3,000 U.S. adults.
