title: LA mayoral hopeful Nithya Raman calls herself both a 'capitalist' and 'democratic socialist'
description: Nithya Raman called herself both a capitalist and a democratic socialist on CNN, drawing sharp criticism as the DSA considers challenging her endorsement.
content: Media LA mayoral hopeful Nithya Raman calls herself both a 'capitalist' and 'democratic socialist' The DSA member and Los Angeles city councilwoman challenging Karen Bass defended the two labels on CNN By CJ Womack Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:21pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video LA mayoral hopeful Nithya Raman embraces 'capitalist' label despite democratic socialist ties Nithya Raman called herself both a capitalist and a democratic socialist on CNN after previously declining to directly answer the question. The LAGOP criticized her remarks amid scrutiny of her DSA ties. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman declared herself both a capitalist and a democratic socialist during an interview Friday, raising questions about her political ideology as the Democratic Socialists of America considers challenging her endorsement from the organization just days before the election. Raman, a Los Angeles city councilwoman and DSA member challenging incumbent Mayor Karen Bass, defended the two labels when Michaelson pressed her about capitalism and the organization's political positions. "I am a capitalist, and I'm also a democratic socialist," she told CNN's Elex Michaelson. "I want the city to work and when the government is doing its job, it needs to work really effectively, and we need to make sure capitalism works without harm to workers, without worker exploitation, without exploitation of poor people. That's what I'm going to focus on." Los Angeles County Republican Party Chair Roxanne Hoge criticized Raman's remarks in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning how the mayoral hopeful could embrace capitalism while maintaining ties to an organization that advocates replacing it. DEPROGRAMMED: FORMER DSA INSIDER REVEALS ‘FRIGHTENING’ SOCIALIST AGENDA DROVE HIM FROM ‘EXTREME’ IDEOLOGY Los Angeles mayoral candidate Nithya Raman identified herself as both a capitalist and a democratic socialist during a CNN interview, despite previously avoiding a direct answer about capitalism. (Getty Images) "It's no surprise that Nithya Raman is confused by two mutually exclusive concepts. Perhaps she was in a fugue state when she agreed to co-govern with the DSA who proudly proclaim their desire to expropriate private property and to abolish the police," Hoge said. The Los Angeles Times reported Saturday that DSA national leadership was considering action against the Los Angeles chapter's endorsement of Raman over accusations she doesn't fully support the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement targeting Israel. At a forum last month, according to the LA Times, Raman referred to BDS as a "legitimate form of peaceful protest" without explicitly saying she supports the movement. Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't LA My Burbank PAC, criticized Raman's affiliation with the Democratic Socialists of America, pointing to the organization's communist roots and its current political program advocating greater worker control over private industries. "The founder of DSA-LA, Dorothy Rea Healey, was a longtime leader of the California Communist Party in California," she told Fox News Digital. "Her autobiography is titled: 'A Life in the American Communist Party.' The current Democrat Socialist Program for Los Angeles states, 'Capitalists extract massive profits by stealing the surplus value of working-class labor.'" She claimed the program's mantra involves organizing to rebuild worker militancy, expanding union density, dismantling the gig economy, and asserting democratic worker control over municipal and private industries. "This is who Nithya Raman will be expected to co-govern with. When people tell you who they are, believe them," Hoge said. Los Angeles County Republican Party Chair Roxanne Hoge criticized Raman's remarks in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning how she could embrace capitalism while maintaining ties to the Democratic Socialists of America. (Getty) 'DSA JIHADI': LA MAYORAL CANDIDATE TORCHED AFTER DEFENDING 'GENOCIDE' COMMENT DURING JEWISH FORUM Raman's remarks contrasted with the DSA's official description of democratic socialism, which calls for replacing capitalism with an economic system in which workers exercise greater control over businesses and major industries. The organization explicitly rejects capitalism in its explanation of its political philosophy. "Capitalism is a system designed by the owning class to exploit the rest of us for their own profit. We must replace it with democratic socialism, a system where ordinary people have a real voice in our workplaces, neighborhoods, and society," the DSA states on its website. Nithya Raman's DSA affiliation came under fire from the Don't LA My Burbank PAC President Lisa Cusack. (Eric Thayer / Getty Images) DNC CHAIR KEN MARTIN DEFENDS 'BIG TENT' STRATEGY WHEN PRESSED ON DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS Raman's latest comments also marked a change from how she answered the same question during a July interview with Michaelson. At the time, she declined to directly identify herself as a capitalist, instead emphasizing the existing economic system and the responsibilities of local government. When Michaelson asked whether she considered herself a capitalist, Raman acknowledged the economic structure under which Los Angeles operates. "You know, we are in a capitalist system. It's a city government," Raman said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Michaelson also asked Raman whether she supported abolishing police departments, prisons or the U.S. Senate. She rejected all three proposals. When Michaelson pressed her on how she reconciled her political affiliations with those disagreements, Raman defended the ideological diversity within the organization. "I don't, you know, I think democratic socialism is a big tent," she said. "The DSA is a big tent organization, and I'm in part of that tent and I think a lot of Angelenos are in that tent with me." title: Trump's brutal Truth Social attack on Bill Maher after dinner sparks confusion online
description: President Donald Trump called Bill Maher a "complete and total loser" on Truth Social, after the two met for a dinner at the White House earlier this month.
content: Media Trump's brutal Truth Social attack on Bill Maher after dinner sparks confusion online The president used Truth Social to describe the HBO host as a 'pothead' who 'looked like hell' at their second meeting By Lindsay Kornick , Brian Flood Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:17pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google President Donald Trump attacked Bill Maher after previously meeting with him earlier this month. (Al Drago/The Washington Post/Bloomberg via Getty Images; Alex WROBLEWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! President Donald Trump set social media ablaze on Sunday night with a lengthy Truth Social post slamming HBO host Bill Maher on the heels of a recent dinner between the two of them, leaving onlookers baffled at the sudden about-face. Trump hosted Maher for dinner at the White House earlier this month, marking the second time they have dined together. Afterward, Trump told reporters that the HBO comedian was "great," and that it "was a very informative dinner," but the president changed his tune on Sunday night. "Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher. He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement — But that’s all gone. It’s not 'HOT' anymore!" Trump wrote. Trump also described his past relationship with Maher's "Club Random" show producer Chuck LaBella from his days on NBC's "The Apprentice," claiming that LaBella would frequently encourage Trump to appear on Maher's show. BILL MAHER CLAIMS DONALD TRUMP FELT 'BETRAYED' BY HIM WITH 'SILLY' FEUD AFTER CORDIAL 2025 DINNER President Donald Trump claimed on Truth Social that Bill Maher invited himself to their most recent meeting. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images; Todd Owyoung/NBC via Getty Images) "When I became President, I agreed to meet, after the first one, and the last one, but never agreed to do his show, which he wants me to do, DESPARATELY [sic] — It won’t happen! When I have watched the show, which isn’t often, it always ends with dishonesty, about me at least, but, who cares?" Trump wrote. He described LaBella and singer Kid Rock arguing in favor of inviting Maher to the White House for a meeting in what ultimately became their April 2025 dinner, though Trump claimed Maher "invited himself." The president also wrote that Maher was in worse condition during their more recent meal. "Also, I wanted to tell Bill that he’s a major POTHEAD. He’s got to stop, it’s very bad for his health. He looked like hell this time. Bill was drunk and had alcohol in his hand as he walked through the White House. Stephen A. Smith and Kid Rock came along with him. Overall, I thought it was a good meeting. It didn’t last four hours, it lasted two hours, maybe less, and everybody was happy. We have the timestamps. I learned nothing, and felt it was a waste of time," Trump wrote. Trump claimed that since their second dinner, Maher's show has become "worse" than before and implored Maher and his team not to reach out to him again in the near future. TRUMP HOSTED A DINNER WITH – WAIT FOR IT – STEPHEN A SMITH, KID ROCK AND BILL MAHER President Donald Trump claimed that one of Bill Maher's producers frequently called him to set up a meeting. (Manuel Balce Ceneta/AP Photo) "There were so many other falsehoods Bill spewed, but I won’t waste time in FACT CHECKING him. He isn’t worth it. Bill: Don’t call anymore. It’s useless, and tell Chuck LaBella not to call so much, and say how much you love 'TRUMP,' and want to get together, because you’re a hopeless guy, who is just trying to cater to your small group of 'fans.' You’re also a coward who is afraid to tell the truth about how well our Country is running because of your few 'fans,' and how badly the Dumocrats have done, almost destroying the U.S.A.," Trump wrote. He concluded, "You’re not transformative, you’re a Loser! I never watched your show much, but I will never watch it again, because it is nothing more than FAKE NEWS that America, and the World, is unfortunately subjected to." When reached for comment, the White House pointed Fox News Digital back to Trump's Truth Social Post. Maher did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It was the longest post Trump has ever sent, according to CNN. Comedian Tim Young — the Heritage Foundation’s media fellow — feels there is only one explanation for the 1,300-plus word takedown. "I watched Bill Maher’s show this weekend and can’t figure out what set off Trump more than usual. Maher always regularly criticizes Trump," Young told Fox News Digital. THE FEUD BETWEEN TRUMP AND MAHER IS HEATING UP AGAIN AS HBO HOST RESPONDS TO THE PRESIDENT’S LATEST DIG Bill Maher has previously defended meeting with President Donald Trump for dinner. (Lionel Hahn/Getty Images) "Maybe it’s that Trump watched a full episode for once because Karoline Leavitt was on and realized just how much Maher criticizes him," Young continued. "That’s the only thing I can think happened. The president was friendly and didn’t realize just how much Maher takes cracks at him because he has never seen a full episode until now." Many others took to social media with thoughts on the lengthy post, with supporters basking in the takedown. Some pointed out that Trump casually noted he might move the press to a different location, while others were irked the president would spend so much time bashing a television host. Maher has previously defended meeting with Trump against liberal critics during the opening monologue of his HBO show "Real Time." "You know what? F--- you. I like these dinners," Maher said Friday. In 2025, Maher surprised liberal audiences by describing Trump as "gracious and measured" during their meeting in contrast to his public persona. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "You can hate me for it, but I’m not a liar. Trump was gracious and measured," Maher said. "And why isn’t that in other settings? I don’t know, and I can’t answer, and it’s not my place to answer. I’m just telling you what I saw, and I wasn’t high." Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. title: GORDON SONDLAND: France is burning, Europe's broke, and the revolution it really needs isn't violent
description: A former U.S. ambassador to the EU explains how excessive regulation and rigid labor markets fuel Europe's protests over rising living costs.
content: Opinion GORDON SONDLAND: France is burning, Europe's broke, and the revolution it really needs isn't violent The unrest in Europe reflects a growing anxiety that Europe’s economic and social model is no longer delivering By Gordon Sondland Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:16pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Widespread violent protests expand across Europe as riots grip France Massive protests and violent clashes erupt across European capitals as citizens express widespread anger. Heritage Foundation senior fellow Mike Gonzalez analyzes the root causes and predict what lies ahead for the continent. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Europe is in the streets. From Paris to Brussels, Milan to Lisbon, hundreds of thousands of citizens are protesting rising living costs, stagnant wages, unaffordable housing and deteriorating public services. In France, demonstrations have descended into burning barricades, looted businesses, and attacks on public buildings. Elsewhere, students, workers and frustrated families are demanding that their governments deliver the prosperity and security they have long promised. Most protesters are peaceful, but the unrest reflects a growing anxiety that Europe’s economic and social model is no longer delivering. The immediate grievances vary, but the underlying problem is more profound: too many European economies have become better at protecting yesterday’s arrangements than creating tomorrow’s opportunities. Excessive regulation, rigid labor structures, fragmented capital markets, and slow decision-making constrain the growth necessary to sustain Europe’s generous social promises. Europe has not run out of talent. It has made it unnecessarily difficult for talent to flourish. Having served as the U.S. ambassador to the EU, I have heard this firsthand from executives running the American operations of major European companies, particularly in Silicon Valley. Their message is remarkably consistent: they simply cannot innovate in Europe the way they can in the United States. These are Europeans describing the limitations of their own economic environment. They come to America because our ecosystem allows them to move faster, attract capital, take risks, recruit talent, and turn promising ideas into commercially successful businesses. FROM ARRESTS TO CRACKDOWNS, HOW EUROPE’S LEADERS ARE RESPONDING AS PROTESTS ROCK THE CONTINENT Think about the implications. Europe has extraordinary universities, brilliant engineers, world-class scientists, and sophisticated corporations. Yet many of those same corporations look to America when they want to push the boundaries of innovation. The problem is not imagination. It is an economic and regulatory structure that too often suffocates imagination before it can become commercial reality. Video There is another uncomfortable dimension to Europe’s predicament. For decades, the United States provided the military security umbrella under which European governments could devote comparatively modest resources to their own defense. While American taxpayers financed enormous military capabilities, many European countries concentrated more of their resources on generous pensions, health care, social benefits, and other domestic priorities. FRENCH CEO WARNS 'PURELY CHAOTIC' RIOTS PROVE THE COUNTRY HAS REACHED THE 'DEAD END OF SOCIALISM' Imagine if European governments had been required to spend 4% or 5% of GDP on defense throughout the past three decades. Would their social safety nets look anything like they do today? Perhaps Europeans would still have chosen extensive benefits, shorter workweeks and lengthy vacations. But those arrangements would have required far more difficult fiscal choices involving taxes, borrowing, spending and economic growth. American military power did not create Europe’s welfare state, but it helped make that welfare state easier to afford. HUNGARY AND POLAND DEFEND TOUGH MIGRATION POLICIES AS FRANCE REELS FROM VIOLENT UNREST The American security guarantee may also have distorted European perceptions of the threats themselves. When someone else bears much of the cost of protecting you, it becomes easier to discount the danger. Why acknowledge the full threat posed by Russia if doing so means telling voters they must sacrifice cherished benefits to purchase tanks, aircraft and missiles? Far easier for Europeans to conclude that Washington is exaggerating the danger, let America spend the money, and enjoy another three-hour lunch. Video Poland and the Baltic states have generally viewed Russia differently. But across much of Western Europe, American protection made strategic complacency easier to sustain. Now the defense bill is coming due. President Trump has pressed NATO allies to assume greater responsibility for their own security, and European governments have committed to substantially higher defense spending. Those commitments arrive just as their economies struggle to generate the growth necessary to finance them. FROM ARRESTS TO CRACKDOWNS, HOW EUROPE’S LEADERS ARE RESPONDING AS PROTESTS ROCK THE CONTINENT Europe needs an immediate regulatory reset, more integrated capital markets, flexible labor arrangements, faster permitting, affordable energy and an environment in which entrepreneurs can build global companies without crossing the Atlantic. Estonia’s digital government, Denmark’s labor flexibility, Ireland’s technology investment and Poland’s industrial development offer useful examples. What Europe lacks is not another commission or another report. It needs political leaders willing to confront the bureaucracies, vested interests and institutional inertia that prevent meaningful reform. Which brings us to America. We have our own protests, riots, economic inequalities, political dysfunction, and government bureaucracy. We are far from perfect, and we should never pretend otherwise. Millions of Americans struggle with housing costs, health care, education, and the fear that their children may not enjoy the opportunities they once expected. We have communities that feel abandoned, institutions that have lost public trust and political divisions that sometimes seem impossible to bridge. But America’s greatest strength has never been perfection. It is our extraordinary capacity for reinvention. Video Our system is built around the possibility of constant change. We experiment, fail, learn, improve and try again. Yesterday’s conventional wisdom becomes tomorrow’s obsolete business model. New companies challenge established giants. New technologies disrupt entire industries. Every generation has the opportunity to create something that did not exist before. That process can be messy, disruptive, and sometimes deeply unfair. But it creates something indispensable to a successful society: the belief that tomorrow can be better than today, and that individuals have the power to help make it so. This is the essential difference between American economic dynamism and the more rigid structures that constrain much of Europe. Our system does not guarantee success. It preserves the possibility of extraordinary success, and it gives people repeated opportunities to pursue it. COULD FRANCE'S RIOTS HAPPEN HERE? EXPERTS SEE PARALLELS IN SOCIALISM, IMMIGRATION — AND KEY DIFFERENCES Critics of American wealth inequality frequently point to our growing number of billionaires, and perhaps someday a trillionaire, as evidence of a system gone wrong. But the mere existence of extraordinary fortunes misses a fundamental point. The question is not simply how much wealth the richest American has accumulated. It is whether the next American, starting with little more than an idea, talent and determination, has a genuine opportunity to build something extraordinary. Video I want to wake up every morning believing the sky is the limit. I want every American to have that same opportunity. Not a government-imposed ceiling on ambition, not a predetermined limit on success, and not a tax system designed to punish exceptional achievement simply because it is exceptional. Why take the risk, invest the capital, work the extra hours or pursue the seemingly impossible if government has already decided how much success is enough? AMERICANS WARNED ABOUT PARIS TRAVEL AFTER VIOLENCE, LOOTING AND TEAR GAS-FILLED STREETS None of this means ignoring inequality. An economy in which wealth and power become permanently concentrated, established businesses suppress competition and children born into poverty have little realistic prospect of advancement would betray the very principles that make American capitalism work. Government has an essential role in enforcing the rule of law, protecting competition, providing education, maintaining a functioning safety net and ensuring that opportunity is not reserved for those who already possess wealth or influence. But there is an enormous difference between government creating the conditions for opportunity and government attempting to dictate economic outcomes. America should respond to Europe’s difficulties with neither arrogance nor indifference. A prosperous, innovative and militarily capable Europe is essential to our own security and economic interests. We should encourage European reform, welcome European investment and insist that our allies assume a greater share of their defense responsibilities. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION At home, however, we must be careful not to import the very economic rigidities Europe is struggling to escape. We should resist the temptation to address every imperfection with another layer of regulation, another barrier to investment or another policy that makes entrepreneurship less rewarding. A demonstration in favor of purchasing power, the protection of public services, and fiscal and social justice, in Paris on October 24, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilization bringing together former members of the Yellow Vest movement, labor unions, high school and university students. (Raphael Lafargue/Abaca for Fox News Digital) We should instead ask a simpler question of every major economic policy: Does this make it easier or harder for Americans to work, invest, innovate, start businesses, change careers and recover from failure? And we must make sure that the promise of advancement remains credible. That means better schools, affordable housing, competitive markets, access to capital, effective public institutions and opportunities extending far beyond a handful of prosperous technology centers. America’s protests remind us that economic growth alone cannot sustain public confidence if too many citizens believe the system is closed to them. Peaceful dissent must be protected, violence must be rejected and legitimate grievances must be addressed. A dynamic economy cannot remain politically stable if large portions of its population lose faith in their ability to participate in its success. The answer to inequality is not to suppress exceptional outcomes. It is to prevent inequality from becoming permanent exclusion. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The American dream was never a guarantee that everyone would become wealthy. It was the conviction that nobody’s future had to be dictated by the circumstances of their birth. The measure of a successful society is not how effectively it limits the fortunes of those at the top, but how convincingly it keeps the door open for those who aspire to join them. Demonstrators light flares during an anti-government protest organized by the Italia in Piazza movement, at Piazza Duomo in Milan, on October 17, 2026. (Piero Cruciatti/AFP/Getty Images) Europe’s unrest should serve as a warning about what happens when expectations grow faster than the economy’s capacity to fulfill them, and when political institutions become better at protecting yesterday’s arrangements than creating tomorrow’s opportunities. America’s greatest asset is not the wealth it has already accumulated. It is the wealth, discoveries, industries and opportunities that have yet to be created. Europe needs to rediscover economic possibility. America needs to protect it. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM AMB. GORDON SONDLAND Gordon Sondland served as the 20th U.S. ambassador to the EU. He is the founder of Provenance, a national hospitality business, and the author of, "The Envoy: Mastering the Art of Diplomacy with Trump and the World." title: Mom of 2 who died rescuing sons during Bahamas snorkeling trip is identified
description: Leanne Gregory of Nottinghamshire, England, was swept away by a strong current off North Bimini Island while trying to rescue her two sons during a family snorkeling trip.
content: Travel Mom of 2 who died rescuing sons during Bahamas snorkeling trip is identified Woman's mother-in-law said family were strong swimmers but 'the waters were too rough' By Andrea Margolis Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:14pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Husband tries to revive wife after strong current sweeps her away during vacation rescue A British mother of two died after being swept away by a strong current while attempting to rescue her sons during a family snorkeling excursion in the Bahamas, authorities said. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! A 36-year-old mother on a family snorkeling excursion in the Bahamas recently died while trying to save her two sons from a strong current, authorities said. The victim was identified as Leanne Gregory, 36, of Nottinghamshire, England, according to The Telegraph. The drowning, which took place on North Bimini Island, was announced by Bahamian authorities last Tuesday. THOUSANDS BOOKED TROPICAL BAHAMAS CRUISE AND ENDED UP IN FREEZING CANADA INSTEAD The Royal Bahamas Police Force said that around 10 a.m. Tuesday, officers at the Alice Town Police Station were alerted to an unresponsive woman at the North Bimini Ferry Dock. The woman had been snorkeling with her husband and two sons when a "strong current" swept the children away, according to the statement. A British mother, pictured on the left, died during a family snorkeling excursion on North Bimini Island after her two sons were swept away by a strong current. The mom has been identified as Leanne Gregory. She was 36 years old. (Leanne Gregory/Facebook; iStock) "In an attempt to rescue her sons, the woman was also swept away," police said in a statement. "She was later rescued and transported to the ferry dock, where CPR was reportedly administered." Both children survived the incident, according to The Telegraph. NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING' By the time officers arrived, they were told the woman had been transported to a clinic and pronounced dead by a local doctor "despite efforts to save her life," the report added. Authorities added that foul play "is not suspected at this time." "An autopsy will be conducted to assist in determining the exact cause of death," the report added. Leanne Gregory, 36, of Nottinghamshire, England, died while attempting to rescue her two sons from a strong current in the Bahamas. (Leanne Gregory/Facebook) In a Facebook tribute, Gregory's husband, Nathan, called his wife of 22 years his "childhood sweetheart" and "soulmate," according to the BBC. The outlet reported that on a GoFundMe page, he said she held onto one of their sons until he was rescued, but she "didn't have the energy to save herself." "My boys had to witness something nobody should ever have to see of any age, but they know [their mom] died an absolute hero," Nathan Gregory said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER In an interview with The Telegraph, Gregory's mother-in-law, Kim Jones, said her son had tried to give Gregory the "kiss of life" in an effort to revive her. "It is devastating," said Jones. "They can both swim, they’re good swimmers, but the current was too strong." Bahamian authorities said the mom was taken to a local clinic and pronounced dead despite efforts to save her life. (iStock) Jones added, "They were in difficulty, and she went out to rescue them. But the waters were too rough and choppy for her." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Gregory had reportedly loved traveling to Florida and the Caribbean, Jones said, and had been on a two-week vacation at the time of the drowning. Gregory's mother-in-law told The Telegraph the couple were school sweethearts who had been together for over 20 years. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "She was the best mom in the world, just brilliant — a lovely woman who would do anything for anyone," said Jones. "It’s all such a shock ... I cannot imagine how my son will be feeling." Gregory's death is among several recent vacation tragedies. The mother-in-law said the family was devastated after the 36-year-old died during a snorkeling excursion in the Bahamas. (iStock) In August, a Minnesota pastor died after suffering a severe spinal cord injury when he fell into a pool aboard a cruise ship in Italy while celebrating his son's wedding. title: Elon Musk vows to give every US child SpaceX stock
description: Elon Musk says he'll give one SpaceX share to every kid in America in 2027, but key details about eligibility and distribution remain unclear.
content: Elon Musk Elon Musk vows to give every US child SpaceX stock Elon Musk promises every US child a share of SpaceX in 2027. Here's what it could be worth and what parents need to know By Kurt Knutsson, CyberGuy Report Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:12pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Elon Musk plans SpaceX stock giveaway for American children Elon Musk announces a plan to give one share of SpaceX stock to every child in America. The 'Big Money Show' debates the business and charitable aspects of this multi-billion dollar giveaway, contrasting it with Anthropic's decision to commit five percent of its equity to a public benefit fund. Panelists discuss the motivations behind these high-profile corporate charity initiatives. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! You probably don't expect Elon Musk to show up in your child's investment portfolio. But that's exactly what could happen next year. The billionaire behind SpaceX has made a remarkable promise. He says he'll give one share of his space company to every kid in America. We're talking about a potential giveaway worth more than $10 billion. Free SpaceX stock for kids sounds appealing, especially when you're thinking about your child's financial future. But before you start looking for a way to sign up, there are some pretty important details Musk has yet to explain. Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed. Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com. NEW BOOK ON ELON MUSK EXAMINES THE BILLIONAIRE’S MIND, MOTIVATION AND MAKING LIFE MULTI-PLANETARY Elon Musk has pledged to give one share of SpaceX stock to every child in America in 2027, a potential giveaway valued at more than $10 billion. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images; Justin Sullivan/Getty Images) Elon Musk promises SpaceX shares to every US child Musk recently announced on X that he plans to give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America in 2027. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk wrote. That's a sweeping commitment. SpaceX, which went public in June 2026, operates the Starlink satellite internet network and develops rockets for commercial spaceflight. Now Musk wants millions of American children to own a tiny piece of the company. The promise has already attracted attention because of its enormous potential cost. However, Musk hasn't provided a detailed plan explaining how the shares would reach families or which children would qualify. How much would the SpaceX shares be worth? For perspective, SpaceX shares closed at $147.49 on Oct. 23. There are just over 72 million Americans under age 18. Using that closing price, giving every one of them a share would cost approximately $10.6 billion. For a family with two eligible children, that could mean roughly $295 worth of SpaceX stock based on the Oct. 23 valuation. Of course, that amount could change considerably by 2027. Stock prices rise and fall, and owning a single share offers no guarantee of future profits. Still, there's something intriguing about the idea of a child becoming an investor before graduating from high school. If SpaceX continues to grow, that share could become more valuable over time. On the other hand, families could also watch its value decline. Why Musk's SpaceX promise followed Anthropic's announcement The timing is especially interesting. Just one day before Musk made his announcement, artificial intelligence company Anthropic revealed a major philanthropic commitment of its own. The company behind Claude AI announced plans to commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, subject to stockholder approval. The fund could support nonprofit organizations or provide direct financial assistance to certain populations, including workers affected by AI-driven economic changes. The company also described a structure that could increase its contribution as its valuation grows, subject to future board decisions. Musk responded to Anthropic's announcement by recommending that companies give shares directly to the public. He then followed up with his own pledge involving SpaceX. This exchange raises an interesting question about the enormous wealth accumulating around AI. As technology companies become increasingly valuable, executives are facing greater scrutiny over how that wealth should benefit the public. SEN DAVE MCCORMICK: TRUMP ACCOUNTS GIVE ALL AMERICANS A STAKE IN PROSPERITY A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket launches with NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope onboard from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., on Aug. 30, 2026. (NASA via Getty Images) Could SpaceX shares be connected to Trump Accounts? Under the Trump Accounts program, the Treasury Department began automatically enrolling eligible children in tax-advantaged investment accounts on Oct. 1. Parents or guardians must still claim and activate those accounts before managing them. A separate federal pilot program provides a one-time $1,000 contribution for qualifying U.S. citizen children born between Jan. 1, 2025 and Dec. 31, 2028. Families must make an election to receive that contribution. SpaceX President and Chief Operating Officer Gwynne Shotwell and her husband, Robert Shotwell, previously pledged to donate one SpaceX share to the Trump Account of each of more than 2 million children. Their contribution targets children ages 11 to 17 in areas with lower-than-average household incomes, with additional emphasis on communities near their home in central Texas. New Treasury regulations that took effect Sept. 30 also allow qualifying donations of publicly traded company shares into Trump Accounts. Under those rules, donated shares generally must be held for five years or until the account's special growth period ends, whichever comes first. Musk's proposal could potentially use this system, but he has not publicly explained the exact distribution process. That's an important unanswered question because Trump Accounts have established eligibility requirements and investment rules. Musk's announcement appears to cover a much broader population of children, although he has yet to define exactly who qualifies. What questions remain about Musk's SpaceX giveaway? A pledge this large naturally comes with logistical challenges. For starters, Musk hasn't clarified whether every child under 18 would qualify or whether the giveaway would be limited to U.S. citizens. It is also unclear how children would receive their shares. If the giveaway uses Trump Accounts, families would need to understand how eligibility and account requirements apply. If Musk chooses another distribution method, parents may need some type of custodial account to hold stock for a minor. But Musk has not identified a specific process for families to claim his promised shares. There are also financial questions. Would families face any tax consequences? Could children sell their shares immediately, or would restrictions apply? And when during 2027 would the transfers happen? For now, there's no confirmed application process for Musk's nationwide pledge. Parents should be cautious of anyone claiming otherwise. UKRAINE'S STARLINK RESTORED AS ELON MUSK CLAIMS KYIV VIOLATED TERMS OF SERVICE 'TO KILL PEOPLE' Michael Dell, CEO of Dell Technologies, and his wife Susan speak alongside President Donald Trump during the announcement of a $6.25 billion donation from the Dell family to "Trump Accounts" in the Roosevelt Room of the White House on December 2. (Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP via Getty Images) What this means to you If you have children or grandchildren, this is certainly a development worth following. A free share of SpaceX could introduce young people to investing and give them a financial interest in a company developing space technology. But I'd encourage parents to be patient. Musk has not announced an official enrollment process for his proposed giveaway. That means you should be especially suspicious of websites or social media messages claiming you can already register your children for free SpaceX stock. We have previously reported on scams using Elon Musk's name to promote questionable products. A high-profile stock giveaway could provide another opportunity for impersonators to target families. Avoid sharing your child's Social Security number, financial information or other sensitive details with anyone promoting an unverified giveaway. For legitimate information about Trump Accounts, visit the IRS website at irs.gov/trumpaccounts directly. That official program already has an established enrollment process, but signing up for a Trump Account does not guarantee your child will receive a share from Musk's pledge. If SpaceX eventually announces a formal process, review the eligibility requirements and any account restrictions before participating. Kurt's key takeaways I've seen Elon Musk make some pretty ambitious promises over the years, but offering a piece of SpaceX to every child in America is certainly an attention-grabber. What interests me most is the idea of giving young people an ownership stake in a company helping shape the future of space exploration. There could be real financial value in that over time. Still, I want to see the details before getting too excited. A promise involving billions of dollars and millions of children deserves a clear explanation of how it will work. I also find the timing fascinating. With Anthropic making its own massive commitment to public benefit, we're beginning to see tech billionaires debate who should share in the wealth their companies create. I'll be watching to see whether Musk follows through and how much of that wealth actually reaches American families. Would you trust Elon Musk to give your child a financial head start, or do you think billionaires should do more than promise shares on social media? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com. description: Video shows Hector Rodriguez wheeled past cheering supporters as he left Penn Presbyterian two weeks after the ambush that killed Shane Seiber.
content: Philadelphia Shot 12 times in ambush that killed his partner, Philadelphia officer leaves hospital to cheers The Philadelphia officer was released from Penn Presbyterian two weeks after the attack that killed his partner By Greg Wehner Fox News Published October 26, 2026 12:11pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Ambulance carrying Philadelphia officer shot 12 times in ambush leaves hospital Philadelphia Police Officer Hector Rodriguez was released from Penn Presbyterian Medical Center after being shot 12 times during an ambush earlier this month. (Credit: @PhillyPolice/X) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! A Philadelphia police officer who survived being shot 12 times in an ambush that killed his partner was met with cheers over the weekend as he left the hospital to continue his recovery. Officer Hector Rodriguez III was released from Penn Presbyterian Medical Center just over two weeks after the Oct. 10 attack that killed his partner, Officer Shane Seiber, and led to more than 70 criminal charges against suspect Eric Lewis. Photos and video posted by the Philadelphia Police Department show Rodriguez sitting upright on a stretcher as he was wheeled through an entryway packed with cheering supporters before an ambulance carrying him pulled away. EMBATTLED SOROS-BACKED DA BLAMES ‘CRIMINAL’ POLICE MISCONDUCT IN ACCUSED PHILLY COP KILLER’S PRIOR MURDER CASE "This morning, we clapped P/O Hector Rodriguez out of Penn Presbyterian as he left to continue his recovery," the Philadelphia Police Department wrote on X. "Thank you to his medical team and everyone who has supported Hector, his family and our PPD family. We'll be beside him every step of the way!" Philadelphia police officers and other supporters gathered outside Penn Presbyterian Medical Center as Officer Hector Rodriguez III was released to continue his recovery. (Philadelphia Police X) Rodriguez, 33, has served with the Philadelphia Police Department for nine years and has been assigned to the 19th District since December 2018. DOJ SENDS GRAND JURY SUBPOENAS TO PHILADELPHIA DA KRASNER AFTER JUDGE'S REFERRAL, SOURCES SAY Rodriguez and Seiber were called to a residence in West Philadelphia at about 12:17 a.m. on Oct. 10 for a report of a man with a gun. Police said the officers found a man on the porch before a struggle broke out and both were shot. Other officers arriving at the scene found Rodriguez and Seiber unresponsive on the porch and rushed them to Penn Presbyterian Medical Center. title: Fines coming after Green Bay Packers put NFL officiating on blast for questionable calls in loss to Lions
description: Xavier McKinney called the officiating "bulls--t" after multiple controversial calls went against the Green Bay Packers in their Detroit Lions game.
content: OutKick Fines coming after Green Bay Packers put NFL officiating on blast for questionable calls in loss to Lions Xavier McKinney's locker room rant targeted a controversial unnecessary roughness that helped Detroit take the lead By Armando Salguero OutKick Published October 26, 2026 12:08pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Former NFL QB Sean Salisbury calls for referees to face questions after missed calls Former NFL QB Sean Salisbury tells OutKick that officials should answer questions immediately after games, be held accountable for obvious mistakes and stop escalating confrontations with players. After a short reprieve in which NFL officiating did not beclown itself for a couple of weeks, we saw the return of questionable and borderline unprofessional work by the league's men in stripes during the Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions game on Sunday. And as the most curious calls went against the Packers, it doesn't surprise that team's postgame media session was replete with a withering review of the poor officiating work – led by safety Xavier McKinney who called the officiating "bulls–t." This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. Yes, McKinney should expect to be fined for sharing his opinion, but he definitely got his money's worth during a one-minute rant on one controversial call in particular. Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams dives to the end zone during a touchdown reception in front of Green Bay Packers safety Xavier McKinney (29) during the first half of an NFL football game on Oct. 25, 2026, in Detroit. (AP Photo/Paul Sancya) NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 4 GOES TO A REFEREE NOW ON THE MOUNT RUSHMORE OF ANGRILY JUMPING TO CONCLUSIONS "I don't know how the NFL [is] going to treat it, but I'm not a big fan of the refs right now," McKinney told reporters in the locker room. "I don't think it's great officiating if I'm being completely honest. I think it's bulls–t a lot of the times." McKinney pointed to an obvious third-quarter situation in which Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown was wrapped up in what seemed like a tackle, but because he was on top of his tackler, he apparently decided he wasn't actually down. So, St. Brown got up and going as if the play wasn't dead. There had been no audible whistle. So, defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt tackled St. Brown. While these hijinks were going on, St. Brown's leg whipped upward and hit approaching umpire Terry Killens Jr. in the groin. Killens Jr. went down and proceeded to throw a flag while on his back. Unnecessary roughness on Wyatt. Amon-Ra St. Brown (14) of the Detroit Lions warms up before the game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on Nov. 09, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (G Fiume/Getty Images) SEAN MCVAY SAYS NFL HAS ADMITTED OFFICIALS MADE MAJOR MISTAKE THAT PROBABLY COST THE RAMS A LOSS VS DENVER The Lions used the penalty to draw closer to an eventual touchdown that gave them a 17-14 lead. "I think there are drives where they make calls that don't even make any sense," McKinney said. "We tried to get him down and then their player hit the ref and he falls. He gets mad on the ground and he just throws the flag. He don't even know who hit him. "So it's just like, it just be bulls–t that's going on, bulls–t calls." Yes, fine incoming because the NFL has a strict policy that says public criticism by players or club employees of game officials or officiating is prohibited and may result in a fine and/or suspension. That includes comments in press conferences, interviews, broadcasts, livestreams and social-media posts. The league can discipline someone when the criticism concerns a specific call or the general quality of officiating. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell addresses the media during the Super Bowl Winning Team Head Coach and MVP Press Conference at the Mandalay Bay North Convention Center on Feb. 12, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) NFL REVIEWING INCIDENT AFTER LINE JUDGE JEFF SEEMAN APPEARED TO HURL PROFANITY AT CARDINALS' TREY MCBRIDE But the discipline isn't the major point. The questionable officiating is. The NFL has had something of an officiating problem this year. The league recognized that when it suspended two officials in separate incidents Oct. 5. Also, penalty flags are near a historical high. And while commissioner Roger Goodell said last week that more flags does not necessarily equate to bad officiating, the league is concerned at some level. The league recently told officials to stay away from holding calls on the backside of plays, but the plays that draw attention have been a concern. NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent last week discussed the suspension of the two officials and said the league is currently dealing with "the consequences of a grievance" filed by referee Adrian Hill, who was suspended for one game for the manner he dealt with a player while unaware of the circumstances behind his reaction after being knocked down. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur reacts after a call during the third quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit, Mich., on Oct. 25, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) NFL'S MOST DEBATED WEEK 3 CALL HAS PEOPLE WONDERING HOW TO DEFY GRAVITY WHEN HITTING PATRICK MAHOMES Killens Jr. seemed to find himself in a similar circumstance as he lay on the turf while throwing his flag. Packers coach Matt LaFleur treaded carefully about the officiating at first, but left no doubt he was unhappy his team was penalized when there was no clear whistle to end the play. "There was no whistle blown, and the guy continued to run, and our guy didn't hear a whistle. He continued to play too, and then we get called for a penalty," LaFleur said. "So, I don't know. They were trying to tell me the play was obviously dead. I'm like, 'How do you know if you don't hear a whistle?'" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Referee Alex Moore didn't hear a whistle, either. But in a pool report after the game, he stated the play was over as if it was a known fact to everyone. "We ruled that the play was over," Moore said. "I can't honestly hear if there was a whistle or not, but the tackler made the tackle, the play was over. Then, there was an additional action, and he basically tackled him again with force after the play was over." This was the most controversial call in a game with multiple questionable calls, several of them resulting in eyebrow-raising flags against the Packers for roughing the passer. Defensive tackle Karl Brooks, who was called for one of those roughing penalties, declined to speak with reporters after the game. He's one of the few Packers players victimized by questionable calls on Sunday that knows he's not going to fined by the NFL for ripping the officials. title: Milwaukee Brewers' dominant bullpen and clutch offense put the Tampa Bay Rays on the brink
description: The Brewers send Robert Gasser to the mound in Game 3 as Milwaukee's dominant bullpen and clutch offense push them closer to a first World Series title.
content: OutKick Milwaukee Brewers' dominant bullpen and clutch offense put the Tampa Bay Rays on the brink Milwaukee sends Robert Gasser to the mound against former Brewer Freddy Peralta in a pivotal matchup By David Troy OutKick Published October 26, 2026 11:44am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video ‘Guys Don’t Give Up’ – Brewers Manager Pat Murphy on Game 2 Comeback Win Over Rays in World Series Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy discussed his team's resilience during his postgame press conference following a 5-4 comeback win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 2 of the World Series. Weekends in fall are typically dominated by football. College Football owns Saturday, and Sunday is taken over by the NFL. That's not a complaint, but it does overshadow a bit of the other stuff happening, like the beginning of the hockey and basketball season. And, more importantly, the World Series. Tonight brings us Game 3 of the World Series between the Brewers and Rays. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. The Milwaukee Brewers are going to win the World Series. I really don't think there is any way to look at this series other than with that view. Their bullpen has been ridiculously good, and their offense has gotten key hits at every turn. Whenever they do give up runs, the team almost immediately responds. I genuinely believe that the Brewers could've lost to the Padres, but this team never says die. Whenever another team does get the best of them, they don't step on their throat. Milwaukee just keeps themselves alive at every turn. Sal Frelick of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates with David Hamilton after hitting a solo home run against the Tampa Bay Rays during the sixth inning in Game 2 of the World Series at American Family Field on Oct. 24, 2026, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Getty Images) Tonight, they look to get one step closer to their first-ever World Series trophy. The team is sending out Robert Gasser to the mound in hopes of delivering them a good start. Gasser went 5-5 in the regular season with a 3.87 ERA and a 1.19 WHIP. In the postseason, he has allowed just one earned run on six hits and two walks over nine innings. Gasser has only faced Liam Hicks from the Rays, and he has held Hicks to no hits in the two at-bats. BREWERS RALLY PAST CHAOTIC LATE-GAME REPLAY, PREMATURE CELEBRATIONS TO WIN FIRST WORLD SERIES GAME IN 44 YEARS The Tampa Bay Rays have to win tonight's game. There is no chance in my mind for them to win the World Series if they go down 3-0. I already said I think this series is over anyway. It isn't that Tampa is playing all that poorly; it is just that the Brewers are playing that much better. The Rays took advantage of the mistakes from Milwaukee in the first inning of Game 2, but Milwaukee kept chipping away at the lead. The Brewers scored two runs in the bottom of the first and then just kept scoring a run at a time over the course of the game, eventually winning 5-4. Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta celebrates after the top of the fourth inning against the Cleveland Guardians in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series in St. Petersburg, Fla., on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. (AP Photo/David J. Phillip) Tampa's bullpen was fine-ish in the game, but Drew Rasmussen wasn't good enough. Tonight, the Rays turn to a former Brewer, Freddy Peralta. I've brought this up a ton, but the most impressive thing about Milwaukee over the years is how they improve by removing their best player. Peralta was a mainstay in their rotation for years, but they shipped him to New York over the offseason. He didn't have a great year and was traded to the Rays. He has been awesome in the playoffs for them. He has pitched 16.2 innings in the playoffs and allowed just two earned runs. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM William Contreras and Aaron Ashby of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrate after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 2 of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field on Oct. 24, 2026, in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Getty Images) CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Peralta will need to be elite today if the Rays want to get a win. However, the Brewers rocked Peralta in the lone start he made against them this season. He was with the Mets, and it was in Milwaukee, so perhaps there were some emotions. He went 5.1 innings, allowed seven earned runs on eight hits, and struck out six hitters. I like both teams in this one, but I'm not fading the Brewers at this point. Milwaukee has been amazing this postseason, and their bullpen has been unhittable. Give me the Brewers at -101. title: Ilhan Omar joins 'polarizing and dangerous' streamer at campaign event despite Democratic backlash
description: Rep. Ilhan Omar is set to share the stage with Hasan Piker despite fellow Minnesota Democrats urging her to cancel the appearance before midterm elections.
content: Ilhan Omar Ilhan Omar joins 'polarizing and dangerous' streamer at campaign event despite Democratic backlash The sold-out Minneapolis event comes eight days before midterms as Omar's campaign cites low early voting among young people By Alec Schemmel Fox News Published October 26, 2026 11:24am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Minnesota fraud is result of ‘single-party rule,’ Michele Tafoya says Minnesota GOP U.S. Senate nominee Michele Tafoya discusses her race against Democratic nominee Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan and the allegations involving Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., on ‘The Big Weekend Show.’ NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., is set to share the stage with far-left streamer Hasan Piker on Monday night despite mounting opposition from fellow Minnesota Democrats, some of whom have publicly urged the congresswoman to cancel the appearance just eight days before the midterm elections. Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., has called Piker's rhetoric "polarizing and dangerous" and said embracing him is "a mistake," while Sen. Amy Klobuchar's gubernatorial campaign called a number of his past statements "reckless and unacceptable." Other Democratic officials and party groups have gone further, calling on Omar and state Sen. Omar Fateh, who is hosting the sold-out Minneapolis event, to cancel the appearance. The controversy is exposing a divide among Minnesota Democrats in the closing stretch of the midterms over whether Piker's enormous following among younger progressives outweighs the political liability of his past rhetoric. University of Minnesota political science professor Larry Jacobs told FOX 9 the event would "create a split within the DFL," arguing it could distract statewide Democrats from their closing message and put candidates in a difficult position with moderate and Jewish voters. WHO IS HASAN PIKER? MEET THE FAR-LEFT STREAMER WHO IS STIRRING UP CONTROVERSY AND DIVIDING DEMOCRATS Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., is scheduled to appear alongside left-wing streamer Hasan Piker at a sold-out Minneapolis event Monday as Piker's participation draws backlash from fellow Minnesota Democrats. (Getty Images) Piker, who commands millions of followers across social media, has faced backlash over remarks involving the Sept. 11 attacks, Hamas, Israel and Jewish people. He later apologized for saying in 2019 that "America deserved 9/11" and has rejected accusations of antisemitism. Omar's campaign, however, has defended her decision to participate by pointing to Piker's appeal among the younger voters Democrats are trying to turn out ahead of Election Day. DEMOCRATS CONDEMNING HASAN PIKER AS BACKLASH SPREADS THROUGH PARTY Democratic socialist mayoral candidate Omar Fateh is seen in Minneapolis, Minnesota on July 19, 2025. (Omar Fateh campaign) "Early voting among people under 40 is down, and we need to do everything to get young people to the polls," Omar's campaign told FOX 9. "The Congresswoman knows the Democratic Party is a Big Tent party, and she's excited to join Senator Omar Fateh's event to mobilize young voters and get them to vote in this critical midterm election." During an appearance on "Pod Save America" earlier this year, Piker said he would "vote for Hamas over Israel every single time." He has also described Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and faced renewed criticism this summer over remarks warning that continued American Jewish support for Israel could provoke someone to "take action." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hasan Piker has backed several candidates, including Francesca Hong, who lost Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary in August 2026. (Joshua Lott/Getty Images) "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said in August. title: Major school district's pledge with teachers' union sparks racial discrimination complaint
description: Defending Education filed a civil rights complaint alleging Cherry Creek Schools in Colorado discriminates by race in its teacher hiring policies.
content: Politics Major school district's pledge with teachers' union sparks racial discrimination complaint The federal complaint alleges Colorado's fourth-largest district violates Title VI with its 'Educators of Color' policy By Ireland Owens Fox News Published October 26, 2026 11:00am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video DEI is racial discrimination, says White House senior policy strategist White House senior policy strategist May Mailman discusses the University of Pennsylvania allegedly violating Title IX on 'The Will Cain Show.' NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! FIRST ON FOX: One of Colorado's largest school districts is facing a new federal civil rights complaint over a pledge it made with its teachers' union to recruit, retain and advance educators of color. Defending Education filed a federal civil rights complaint Monday, which was first obtained by Fox News Digital, with the U.S. Department of Education alleging that CCSD is discriminating on the basis of race in employment. CCSD is notably Colorado’s fourth-largest school district, and serves 52,000 students and more than 300,000 residents in the southeast Denver metropolitan area, according to the district’s website. At the heart of the complaint is the district's June 2023 "Educators of Color Declaration," which commits Cherry Creek School District and its teacher’s union to recruiting, retaining and advancing educators of color, even as a separate provision in the same agreement calls for recruitment, hiring and advancement to be based on qualifications without regard to race. "Cherry Creek Schools has written racial preferences directly into its teachers’ contract. The district’s ‘Educators of Color Declaration’ commits it to recruiting, retaining, and promoting teachers based on the color of their skin — which means other equally qualified teachers are passed over for the same reason," Sarah Parshall Perry, Vice President and Senior Legal Fellow at Defending Education, told Fox News Digital. Hundreds protest outside a rally held by President Donald Trump at Macomb County Community College in Warren, MI, on April 29, 2025. (Getty Images/Dominic Gwinn) "That's not diversity; it's discrimination, and it is precisely what Title VI and the Fourteenth Amendment forbid. The Supreme Court could not have been clearer in Students for Fair Admissions: the law is colorblind, and a school district cannot cure a race-based hiring policy with generic 'equal opportunity' language." Title VI prohibits race discrimination in federally funded programs under specified conditions, while Title VII more directly governs employment discrimination, leaving the legality of Cherry Creek's teacher recruitment and advancement commitments dependent on how those policies are implemented. OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE CLEARS WAY FOR WHITE EMPLOYEE TO CHALLENGE SEATTLE'S DEI POLICIES The "Educators of Color Declaration" also commits the district and its teachers' union to intentionally recruiting highly qualified educators of color while making a concerted effort to retain those already employed by the district and help them advance into leadership positions, according to the district's negotiated agreement. A Department of Education sign is displayed outside of their federal student aid office on May 18, 2025, in Washington, DC. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)) JUSTICE DEPARTMENT LAUNCHES TITLE VI INVESTIGATION INTO DEI PROGRAMS AT ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY Additionally, the policy says that "to fulfill these goals, all policies in this agreement shall reflect Cherry Creek School District core values by grounding the work of negotiations in diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI)," according to the school district's 2026-2027 Negotiated Agreement. A Department of Education sign is displayed outside of their federal student aid office on July 17, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images) FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY HIT WITH FEDERAL CIVIL RIGHTS INVESTIGATION OVER RACE, SEX-BASED SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAMS "Cherry Creek is under no obligation to accept federal funding, but because it has, it cannot run a racial balancing scheme for its own workforce and still adhere to federal law," Perry continued. "We are asking the Office for Civil Rights to open an investigation and put an end to it." Defending Education's latest complaint comes after the Department of Education announced a separate investigation on June 8, into allegations that Cherry Creek School District sponsored racially discriminatory programs involving students, teachers and parents. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "These allegations of racially discriminatory conduct in this District seem to permeate almost every aspect of the school community, affecting students, teachers, and parents alike," Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kimberly Richey said in a statement at the time. "Federal law prohibits racial discrimination, which means that race cannot be a factor in how the school educates its students or trains its teachers." The Trump administration has been cracking down on DEI efforts across the nation's education system, including proposing new regulations in September that would revoke the tax-exempt status of private schools and colleges that consider race in admissions, scholarships or other school-administered programs. CCSD did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on Monday. When reached for comment, a Department of Education spokesperson told Fox News Digital that "the Department does not confirm complaints." title: Cowboys favored by 4.5 points as injury-ravaged Eagles face 'Monday Night Football' crisis
description: Sunday Night Football delivered an easy cash, and now Monday Night Football features Cowboys vs Eagles with Philadelphia's injuries mounting fast.
content: OutKick Cowboys favored by 4.5 points as injury-ravaged Eagles face 'Monday Night Football' crisis Jalen Hurts is on IR, Saquon Barkley is questionable, and DeVonta Smith is out for the NFC East rivalry game By David Troy OutKick Published October 26, 2026 10:50am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Falcons can shock 49ers, Jets cover, Can the Eagles upset the Cowboys on Nick’s Week 7 Picks? | FTF Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes preview Week 7 of the NFL season, and discuss the teams that are on upset alert, including the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs. Nick also makes his picks for the week, including the Atlanta Falcons upsetting the San Francisco 49ers, and the Philadelphia Eagles against the Dallas Cowboys. It was a solid Sunday for me in the NFL with a sweat-free cash on Sunday Night Football between the Chiefs and Seahawks. It was potentially one of the most boring games I've ever watched, but it still was an easy cash. That's more important to me than watching a fun game anyway. Tonight we have Monday Night Football as the Cowboys take on the Eagles. My victory lap will stop here because I have been dead wrong about the Dallas Cowboys. They were the team I expected to win this division, and I thought Dak Prescott would be the league's MVP. That doesn't seem to be the case, as the Cowboys are just 2-4 for the season, and they are 1-2 on the road this year. They've suffered some embarrassing losses this season, and need to turn it around quickly if they want to assure themselves of a spot in the postseason. Dak Prescott (4) and Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys hug after the game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the game at AT&T Stadium on Nov. 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Stacy Revere/Getty Images) The Cowboys have lost the past two games and three of their past four games. They dropped in an almost improbable fashion to the Ravens a few weeks ago. They found a way to beat the Texans on the road, and that was a bit of a shootout - their preferred style of play. They hosted the Buccaneers with a backup quarterback and got nothing going, losing 24-16. Then they lost to the Packers 23-13 last week. It wasn't a shootout; it wasn't a well-played game. The Philadelphia Eagles won the Super Bowl two years ago, and while you can't really go higher in success, it has been a steep drop since. Last year, the team had issues with their receiver A.J. Brown. Even Saquon Barkley struggled most of the year. It was a disjointed year, but the team still found a way to make the postseason. They lost immediately, and their quest for a repeat was put to an end. In the offseason, they traded away Brown and added some receivers, but it hasn't translated to much more success for the team. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) scrambles with the ball against the Dallas Cowboys during the second quarter of the game at Lincoln Financial Field on Sept. 4, 2025. (Bill Streicher/Imagn Images) This year has been a disaster for the team both on the field and off. Jalen Hurts, their star quarterback, was playing with a blood clot, and apparently the team knew about it and let him play (or worse, encouraged him). Looking at the Eagles' team leaders, Hurts is on the IR, likely out for the season; Barkley is questionable for the game and has just 182 rushing yards on 36 carries this year; DeVonta Smith is out for the game; and Nolan Smith Jr., their sack leader, is also out for the game. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, right, hands off to Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (26) who runs for a touchdown during the first half of an NFL football game against the New York Giants on Sunday, Oct. 26, 2025, in Philadelphia. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum) CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE I'm not really sure where the Eagles will get any type of offense from in this game. Essentially, they are starting a second-string team against the Cowboys, who need a win. Philadelphia is also 2-4 and needs a win, but I think this is way too much to ask of them. Philadelphia is too banged up, and this is a rivalry game. No game is easy to win in the NFL, but the Cowboys should be licking their chops, looking to get on the field and tear up the Eagles. Give me the Cowboys -4.5 on the road. I think they win this by 10 points or more.
