title: Former Israeli PM emerges as wildcard in high-stakes election with Middle East's future at stake
description: Naftali Bennett's Middle East vision includes expanding the Abraham Accords, but polls show him trailing Gadi Eisenkot and Prime Minister Netanyahu ahead of Israel's election.
content: World Elections Former Israeli PM emerges as wild card in high-stakes election with Middle East's future at stake The former Israel prime minister believes his business background could help him work with Trump to advance regional diplomacy By Efrat Lachter Fox News Published October 26, 2026 10:49am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Former Israeli PM Naftali Bennett thanks Saudi authorities A mid-air pilot stabbing causes a flight to Israel to nosedive before passengers intervene. Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett joins Harris Faulkner to analyze the investigation. Witnesses recount the terrifying moment the co-pilot attacked the pilot, attempting to crash the plane before being neutralized by travelers. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett is seeking a political comeback with an ambitious vision for the Middle East: expanding the Abraham Accords, building economic partnerships with Arab nations and rebuilding Israel's strained international relationships, particularly with the United States. For Bennett, whose American parents moved to Israel from San Francisco, the U.S. connection is both personal and political. The 54-year-old former technology entrepreneur, a familiar face on American television, believes his business background could help him work with President Donald Trump to advance regional diplomacy. "Naftali Bennett is the right leader to strengthen Israel’s global standing, including among the American people, thanks to his proven track record of working with world leaders and bringing people together, both as prime minister and as a successful businessman," Bennett’s campaign told Fox News Digital. "We are confident that our great friend in the White House, President Trump, and Israel’s allies around the world will welcome the opportunity to work with Bennett and the new government he intends to form. Together, we will revive the Negev Forum and expand the Abraham Accords, strengthening regional security and stability. That is why so many leaders across the Middle East and beyond who share a vision of a more secure, prosperous and stable region are eager to see Bennett lead Israel’s next government." TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS Naftali Bennett, former prime minister and head of newly merged Together party, speaks at a press conference at the Israeli parliament on May 20, 2026, in Jerusalem. (Amir Levy/Getty Images) "He was a businessman, not a career politician, same as me," Bennett told The Times of Israel in June, referring to Trump. "His worldview is, let's get stuff done. Let's look at results, not process. And that's precisely my view." Bennett said he would aggressively pursue regional agreements through economic cooperation, seeking to build on the U.S.-brokered Abraham Accords. But while his ambitions overlap with Trump's regional agenda, the president endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election on Oct. 18. Bennett also faces an unusual political challenge at home. His joint Beyachad, or Together, party with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid is polling behind both Netanyahu's Likud and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party. A Channel 12 poll published Oct. 23 projected 23 Knesset seats for Eisenkot, 21 for Netanyahu and 15 for Bennett and Lapid. Yet Bennett knows better than most Israeli politicians that leading the largest party is not necessary to become prime minister. In 2021, he took office despite his Yamina party winning just seven of the Knesset's 120 seats, demonstrating the power of coalition negotiations in Israel's parliamentary system. FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER FILE - Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, right, and Foreign Minister Yair Lapid attend a cabinet meeting at the Prime Minister's office in Jerusalem, June 19, 2022. Bennett's office announced Monday, June 20, 2022, that his weakened coalition will be disbanded and the country will head to new elections. Bennett and his main coalition partner, Yair Lapid, decided to present a vote to dissolve parliament in the coming days, Bennett's office said. Lapid is then to serve as caretaker prime minister. The election, expected in the fall, would be Israel's fifth in three years. (Abir Sultan/Pool Photo via AP, File) How a seven-seat leader became prime minister Born in Haifa to American immigrants, Bennett served in Israel's elite Sayeret Matkal and Maglan military units before co-founding cybersecurity company Cyota, which was sold for $145 million in 2005. He entered politics as Netanyahu's chief of staff, later led the Yesha Council representing West Bank settlements and served as economy, education and defense minister. A religious Zionist and longtime opponent of Palestinian statehood, Bennett stunned Israel's political establishment in 2021 when he formed a coalition spanning right-wing, centrist, left-wing and Arab parties, ending Netanyahu's 12 consecutive years in power. The coalition collapsed in 2022, leaving many former supporters accusing him of betraying his electoral promises. WHO IS ITAMAR BEN-GVIR, THE ISRAELI FIREBRAND RISING WITH THE POPULIST RIGHT ACROSS THE GLOBE? Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu waves from the stage next to his wife Sara during a Jewish New Year greetings event attended by Likud party members in Tel Aviv on Sept. 17, 2026. Israel heads to the polls on Oct. 27 in its first election since the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack, in what is seen as a referendum on the prime minister. (Jack Guez/AFP via Getty Images) Einat Halevy Levin, a strategic advisor who has known Bennett for years, described a politician who has spent his time outside office preparing for a second opportunity. "In 2021, he wasn't prepared. He hadn't built a governing party; he had built another election campaign," Halevy Levin told Fox News Digital. She said she met Bennett at his home in November 2023, following the Oct. 7 Hamas attack, when he had decided to return to politics. This time, according to Halevy Levin, Bennett spent years building a political organization, carefully screening candidates and developing the infrastructure needed to govern. "I've known him since he was economy minister. He was always daring and full of creative ideas, but was more inclined to stick to his own views," she said. "He has undergone a transformation." IS ISRAEL REALLY ISOLATED? POLLS AND DIPLOMACY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, speaks during an event presenting the party's full candidate list ahead of October's general election on Sept. 7, 2026 in Rosh HaAyin, Israel. Eisenkot, a retired chief of the Israel Defense Forces, has emerged as the foremost challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (Erik Marmor/Getty Images) A new Middle East vision meets old divisions Bennett's regional ambitions reflect an approach to diplomacy shaped by his business experience, according to Halevy Levin. She recalled attending a meeting with a senior official from a neighboring country who appeared astonished by Bennett's detailed knowledge of its economy and priorities. "He wasn't looking at the country through a military lens," she said, describing Bennett's focus on identifying shared economic interests rather than approaching every regional relationship primarily as a security challenge. In an interview with Israel's Channel 13 on Sunday, two days before the election, Bennett pointed to his meetings as prime minister with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Jordan's King Abdullah II and UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed as examples of the diplomacy he hopes to revive. He argued that Israel needs to present a new vision of a Middle Eastern renaissance and identified extremist settler violence in the West Bank as a major source of damage to its international standing. "We need to eliminate Jewish terrorism in Judea and Samaria, and I say this precisely as a supporter of the settlement movement," Bennett said. "They do not represent the overwhelming majority of settlers, but right now this is the problem causing us the greatest damage internationally." Bennett said he would direct Israel's senior police, military and intelligence officials to produce a plan within three days to crack down on extremist violence. Israeli settlers run from an Israeli military vehicle around Palestinian houses in the village of Qusra, south of Nablus, in the occupied West Bank, on Aug. 13, 2026. (Zain Jaafar/AFP via Getty Images) His foreign policy, however, remains firmly on the Israeli right. On Iran, Bennett has promoted his "Octopus Doctrine," advocating direct action against Tehran rather than focusing exclusively on Iranian-backed groups. "If Hezbollah fires at us, we strike Iran," he declared at an Aug. 19 policy conference. On Gaza, Bennett opposes Palestinian statehood and supports maintaining Israeli security control until Hamas is disarmed. He has also proposed excluding Qatar and Turkey from Gaza's future arrangements while involving Egypt. TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE Those positions raise questions about how significantly his government would depart from Netanyahu's policies. Danny Citrinowicz, a senior researcher at Israel's Institute for National Security Studies and former head of the Iran branch in Israeli military intelligence, argued that restoring Israel's diplomatic standing requires more than a change in leadership. The West Bank, also known as Judea and Samaria, is home to some 500,000 Israelis. (Mahmoud Illean/AP) "If Bennett thinks he can support annexing E1 (an area east of Jerusalem where planned Israeli settlement construction could further fragment the West Bank), oppose a Palestinian state, continue the occupation of Gaza and simultaneously meet with Sisi and Abdullah and attract investment to Israel, he simply doesn't understand the depth of the international crisis," Citrinowicz said. Citrinowicz argued that without a fundamental change in Israeli policy toward the Palestinians, replacing Netanyahu would not be sufficient to restore the country's international standing. His warning comes amid changing American public attitudes toward Israel. A February 2026 Gallup survey found 36% of Americans sympathized more with Israelis, compared with 41% who sympathized more with Palestinians, a statistically insignificant five-point difference but a significant shift from the long-standing pro-Israel advantage. Election banners with images of Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, leader of Jewish Power (Otzma Yehudit) party, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, leader of Likud party, in Sderot, near Israel's border with Gaza, in southern Israel, Oct.18, 2026. (Reuters/Amir Cohen) A comeback built on lessons from 2021 Beyond foreign policy, Bennett is promising a sweeping domestic overhaul. In an Oct. 25 manifesto, he pledged to redirect 30 billion shekels in government benefits toward families who work and serve in the military, reduce food prices by 30%, establish a state commission of inquiry into Oct. 7 and introduce an eight-year term limit for prime ministers. His alliance with Lapid gives him an established political organization, but he faces competition from Eisenkot and continuing attacks from Netanyahu, who has warned that a future opposition coalition could depend on left-wing and Arab parties. With Israel's fragmented parliamentary system requiring at least 61 seats to govern, coalition negotiations could prove as consequential as the election results themselves. Bennett has already demonstrated that political reality once. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP President Donald Trump shakes hands with Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, on Oct. 13, 2025, in Jerusalem. (Evelyn Hockstein/Pool/Getty Images) Now, four years after his first government collapsed, he is seeking to convince Israelis that the unconventional politician who became prime minister with seven seats has returned better prepared — and with a vision that could reshape Israel's place in the Middle East. Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events. Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science. title: 'Dandelion' keeps delivering as Ella Langley scores a sixth No. 1 on Billboard Country Airplay chart
description: Ella Langley's "Loving Life Again" hit No. 1 on Billboard's Country Airplay chart, making her the fastest female artist to reach six No. 1s.
content: OutKick Culture 'Dandelion' keeps delivering as Ella Langley scores a sixth No. 1 on Billboard Country Airplay chart 'Loving Life Again' is the fourth single from her 'Dandelion' album to reach the top spot By David Hookstead OutKick Published October 26, 2026 10:47am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Ella Langley on her sophomore album 'Dandelion' Ella Langley discusses releasing a series of singles and building momentum toward her sophomore album during coverage tied to the 2026 iHeartRadio Music Awards held March 26, 2026, at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. There's no question she's currently sitting at the top of the mountain. title: NYPD detective stabbed 10 times in Bronx robbery recalls chasing attackers while bleeding out
description: Detective Jose Mercedes reveals on "One Nation" how his blood-soaked phone prevented him from calling 911 while chasing attackers in the Bronx.
content: Fox News Flash NYPD detective stabbed 10 times in Bronx robbery recalls chasing attackers while bleeding out Detective Jose Mercedes said his police training kicked in when two masked men tried to grab chains from his neck By Max Bacall Fox News Published October 26, 2026 10:35am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video NYPD detective speaks out after being stabbed 10 times by illegal immigrants After allegedly being stabbed 10 times by illegal immigrants, NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes speaks out alongside Scott Munro on 'One Nation' with Brian Kilmeade. Mercedes shares details of the terrifying encounter in New York City. The guests strongly criticize sanctuary city policies, warning that current laws fail to protect both police officers and the public. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! An NYPD detective stabbed 10 times during a robbery in the Bronx revealed how he struggled to call 911 while tracking his fleeing attackers before recognizing the severity of his own injuries and the extent of his blood loss Sunday on "One Nation with Brian Kilmeade." Detective Jose Mercedes said in an exclusive interview with Fox News that he couldn't unlock his phone as he tried to report his attackers' whereabouts. Realizing that he was bleeding badly, he stopped following them — recalling cases he had investigated involving victims who suffered significant blood loss. "Suddenly, I grabbed my phone again, and it's completely filled with blood," Mercedes said. "And at that point is when I stopped running." NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes speaks outside the Detectives Endowment Association headquarters after surviving a robbery in which two illegal immigrants allegedly stabbed him 10 times and stole a gold necklace. (Fox News) Mercedes said his police training kicked in when two masked men approached him while he was retrieving belongings from his car's trunk on his day off work. One displayed a knife and attempted to grab the gold chains around his neck. ‘BONNIE AND CLYDE’ ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT COUPLE ACCUSED OF BRAZEN JEWELRY THEFT SPREE ACROSS FOUR STATES "The first thing that went through my mind was fear," Mercedes recalled. "The next thing that went through my mind was action." Mercedes said he managed to unmask both suspects during the struggle, despite fearing they might have additional weapons. He also said he would have tried to escape the confrontation if he had seen the men approaching. "The fear that comes upon you and your body turns cold," he told host Brian Kilmeade. "Thereafter, your adrenaline kicks in. And now it’s action time, and now I have to defend myself with all my might or die." D’Angelo Rafael Jean Caraballo, left, and Sneider Mejia Bautista, right, are walked from the 52nd Precinct in The Bronx, N.Y., on October 13. The men are Dominican citizens living illegally in the United States, and are accused of stabbing off-duty NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes earlier this month. (Dario Alequin for Fox News Digital) ILLEGAL SUSPECT IN NYPD DETECTIVE STABBING DENIES INVOLVEMENT AFTER EXTRADITION FROM MASSACHUSETTS Police identified the alleged attackers as D'Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24. Both are Dominican nationals living illegally in the United States and were arrested in Massachusetts after allegedly fleeing New York, Fox News Digital previously reported. Scott Munro, president of the Detectives' Endowment Association, criticized immigration enforcement policies during the interview, blasting what he described as a lack of respect for law enforcement. MULLIN CALLS MAMDANI'S ANTI-ICE RHETORIC 'DANGEROUS' FOLLOWING NEW YORK SHOOTING "They're taking politics before public safety right now," Munro said. "They're taking politics before law enforcement." Video Mercedes, who suffered wounds to both arms and his back, said the stress of the attack caused him to overlook a critical lifesaving measure despite his decade of police experience. title: Cam Young was out the door to LIV Golf, wind cuts PGA Tour event short, and gearing up for Mexico
description: PGA Tour star Cameron Young signed a document of intent to join LIV Golf after the 2022 Open Championship, newly revealed bankruptcy filings show.
content: OutKick Sports Cam Young was out the door to LIV Golf, wind cuts PGA Tour event short, and gearing up for Mexico Bankruptcy filings show the now world No. 4 was ready to leave the PGA Tour before ultimately deciding to stay By Mark Harris OutKick Published October 26, 2026 10:34am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Hunter Mahan talks about how he got started in posting golf content and eyeing a return to professional golf Former PGA Tour star Hunter Mahan talks about getting into posting golf content online and eyeing a return to professional golf. The PGA Tour returned this week, kind of, which means Par Talk is also back to its regularly scheduled programming as we gear up for four straight weeks of action to close out the Fall Swing. The Butterfield Bermuda Championship is sneakily one of the most entertaining events of the fall, with players competing for status on an island in some of the windiest conditions they'll ever play in. Unfortunately, the PGA Tour deemed the wind on Sunday and Monday to be too much and cut the event to 54 holes. There were eight players within three shots of the lead heading into the final round, but ultimately, the Tour let 54-hole co-leaders Austin Smotherman and Seamus Power duel it out in a Monday playoff at Port Royal. As for the biggest news out of the golf world from the past week, it involves bankruptcy, Cameron Young, and his signature on an agreement to join LIV Golf years ago. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. Cameron Young of the U.S. Team reacts to his putt to win his match 3&2 on the 16th green during Sunday's Singles on day four of the Presidents Cup 2026 at Medinah Country Club on September 27, 2026 in Medinah, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Cameron Young was out the door to LIV Golf Cameron Young was open about having interest in potentially joining LIV Golf during its inaugural season in 2022. The American openly stated at that year's Tour Championship in Atlanta that he was interested in making the jump to the then Saudi-backed circuit. Recently revealed court documents revealed that Young's interest in a move wasn't just a thought he was tossing around in his brain, but one he took legitimate action on. Cameron Young of United States plays his shot from the 17th tee during the third round of the PGA Championship at Aronimink Golf Club on May 16, 2026 in Newtown, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) ((Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)) JON RAHM WON'T PARTICIPATE UNDER LIV GOLF'S 'UNACCEPTABLE' NEW TERMS AMID LEAGUE'S BANKRUPTCY, LAWYERS SAY As LIV Golf is going through proceedings after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, documents revealed that the circuit paid $15.6 million in retention payments to executives before filing. Not lost in the shuffle, which showed that LIV CEO Scott O'Neil received a retention of more than $6 million, was Young previously signing a document of intent to join LIV following the 2022 Open Championship at St. Andrews. The 2022 Open Championship, while a classic finish with Cameron Smith edging out Rory McIlroy, was already remembered as 'The One With The LIV Distraction,' but even more so now. Smith joined LIV shortly after hoisting the Claret Jug, and with Young signing his intent dated July 24, one week after the final round, he was ready to follow suit. Cameron Young and his caddie, Kyle Sterbinsky, look on during the final round of The Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. (Tracy Wilcox/PGA TOUR) The speculation about Young jumping ship from the PGA Tour continued to gain steam for another four weeks before he ultimately grew tired of the questions and shared he had decided to stay on the Tour following the final round of the 2022 Tour Championship. Young was ranked 17th in the world at the time with zero wins on Tour to his name. Since then, he's moved up to No. 4 in the world, won three times, including the 2026 Players, and has represented the United States at both the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup. Austin Smotherman gets it done in Bermuda The PGA Tour was scrambling on Monday. Pun absolutely intended. With wind gusts over 50 mph coupled with rain on Sunday, the Tour was hopeful for a Monday finish, and while it got one, it was about as unique as they come. With the weather an issue again on Monday, the final round was scrapped, and Smotherman and Power went to the Par 3 16th for a playoff to determine a winner. Then they did it again, and again. The pair shared pars on the first and second times around playing the 16th, the staff then moved the pin placement, and Smotherman's third par in a row was enough to get the job done after Power couldn't get up and down from an awkward spot in the rough. It wasn't exactly the most exciting of finishes – players having to gut their way through 18 holes of pure hell in the wind certainly would have been – but when Mother Nature doesn't cooperate, and another event starts in less than four days' time, the Tour wasn't exactly left with another choice. Austin Smotherman of the United States celebrates with the trophy after a sudden death playoff following the weather cancelled final round of the Butterfield Bermuda Championship 2026 at Port Royal Golf Course on October 26, 2026 in Southampton, Bermuda. (Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images) (James Gilbert/Getty Images) CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE As for Smotherman, that's two wins in his last two starts after winning the Bank of Utah Championship at the beginning of October. For a player who had just two Top 25 finishes dating back to May, that's a big-time run for the 32-year-old. Mexico is finally back in our lives Oh, Vidanta Vallarta, how we've missed you. The 2025 Mexico Open at VidantaWorld, which was held in February, was one of those events that the golf sickos out there may never forget, and finally, after 20 months of waiting, we are back. If, for whatever reason, you forgot one of the greatest finishes we may ever see, let's take a look back at what went down early last year. Aldrich Potgieter, the South African whose superpower is being one of the longest hitters in the game, found himself in a playoff with Brian Campbell, who finished 161st out of 162 players in average driving distance this season. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Brian Campbell of the United States reacts with Aldrich Potgieter of South Africa after his birdie putt on the 18th hole during the second playoff hole to win during the final round of the Mexico Open at VidantaWorld 2025 at Vidanta Vallarta on February 23, 2025 in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico. (Photo by Hector Vivas/Getty Images) (Hector Vivas/Getty Images) THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The sudden-death playoff was held on the Par 5 18th hole, so advantage Potgieter. The two each made pars the first time around, and then came the tee shot heard 'round the world. Campbell ended up hitting the block of all blocks off the tee, with his ball entering what is a legitimate jungle guarding the right side of the fairway. His ball should have disappeared, and it did for a brief moment, before jumping back into play and into the right rough. Potgieter followed up Campbell's tee shot by hitting a 321-yard rocket into the fairway, leaving him 218 yards to the hole, while Campbell had 311 to the pin. Despite the almost 100-yard difference, Campbell was the one who made birdie while Potgieter missed a six-footer to extend the playoff. It was cinema, made practically no sense, and was a win for all short hitters around the globe. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Campbell and Potgieter are in the field this week. title: Inside House GOP's unprecedented push to monitor midterm elections and prepare for legal fights
description: House Republicans are sending dozens of congressional observers to monitor ballot counting in close midterm races and prepare for legal challenges.
content: Politics Inside House GOP's far-reaching push to monitor midterm elections and prepare for legal fights Committee on House Administration's program could pave the way for recounts and lawsuits if improprieties found By Elizabeth Elkind Fox News Published October 26, 2026 10:30am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Inside the House GOP's plan to ensure election integrity in the midterms Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil spoke with Fox News Digital about the election observer program seeing federal employees deployed across the country for Nov. 3. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! House Republicans are deploying "dozens and dozens" of staff across the country next Tuesday to ensure the midterm elections are being run cleanly and fairly as both parties fight tooth and nail for control of Congress. The Committee on House Administration, which has jurisdiction over federal elections, runs an annual election watcher program aimed at adding oversight in districts where races are anticipated to be particularly close, and in some cases, paving the way for legal challenges if improprieties are found. Rep. Bryan Steil, R-Wis., the panel's chairman, told Fox News Digital that this year's program will be "the most robust program the House has ever done." "We're building on the success that we had last cycle and recognizing that a large number of House races are likely to be close," Steil said. "The balance of power in the United States House of Representatives is at stake, and we wanna make sure that we have eyes and ears on the ground in close races across the country." BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE BLOCKS VOTER-FRAUD PROBES IN BATTLEGROUND STATES JUST DAYS BEFORE MIDTERMS Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil spoke with Fox News Digital about Republicans' nationwide election observer program. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images; Allison Joyce/AFP via Getty Images) How that plays out will vary from state to state depending on varying election laws, he explained. But many of those observers are potentially in for lengthy shifts. SENATE REPUBLICANS PUSH ELECTION DAY DEADLINE FOR CALIFORNIA'S MARATHON BALLOT COUNTS "Some jurisdictions that run their elections well, like Florida, their shift may end early in the evening. States that have kind of poor election policies, like California, those shifts go on for days on end until the counting is done," Steil said. "Two years ago, I went to Los Angeles County — about 10 million people — counts all their ballots at one location. And of course, we know California has bad election policy. They allow ballots to arrive after the polls have closed. And so I went to Central Count, met with our election observers as we watched ballots arrive days after the election. We want eyes and ears on the ground, recording what is occurring, and documenting what's happening, and making sure that the rules are followed." Steil also recalled an instance in Milwaukee where an issue arose during tabulation "where ultimately thousands of ballots would have to be recounted." People vote early at the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder's office on Oct. 19, 2026. (Jason Armond/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) But those poll watchers, trained under the jurisdiction of Congress, will often stay the entire time votes are being cast on Election Day. In some cases, they observe votes being counted as well. MAP IT: DOJ ILLEGAL VOTING CRACKDOWN SWEEPS 17 STATES AS RAZOR-THIN ELECTIONS FACE SCRUTINY "These are long days. I mean, polling locations are often open for a full 12 hours. They're arriving, they're staying often until the early evening or late evening, in some cases as the ballots are actually tabulated, but they play an absolutely essential role in verifying... our elections are run freely and fairly," he said. It is all part of a process to build a case in the event the results need to be re-examined. Their documentation could potentially lead to recounts in close races or even lawsuits. Residents vote in the state's primary election on Aug. 11, 2026, in Madison, Wis. (Scott Olson/Getty Images) "Not only are they documenting what they're seeing, but they're in direct contact with myself and the committee on Election Day, so that we're in a position to deploy additional resources, if necessary, to make any court challenges if that was required," Steil explained. "They are the first step in identifying if there is a problem, and then they notify our team and we get to work immediately." Election observers' jobs are federally protected under the Confirmation of Congressional Observer Access Act, which was enacted by Congress in 2024. The program is open to any staffer of the House of Representatives, save for interns. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Democrats are free to run their own program under the law, but they do not do so in coordination with Republicans. title: Mamdani message to residents on how to deal with ICE results in viral internet backlash: 'Treason'
description: Zohran Mamdani's Spanish-language video on handling ICE encounters drew over 7 million views and fierce backlash from conservative lawmakers.
content: Politics Mamdani message to residents on how to deal with ICE results in viral internet backlash: 'Treason' The socialist mayor's viral video on how to handle immigration enforcement drew sharp criticism from conservative lawmakers By Andrew Mark Miller Fox News Published October 26, 2026 10:12am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Mamdani blasts ICE as 'rogue' agency after NYC shooting, claims agents disregard law NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused ICE of terrorizing New Yorkers after an agent shot a man whose 5-year-old son was in the vehicle. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faced viral backlash on Friday after posting instructions in Spanish on how residents should handle interactions with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). "If you encounter ICE, here's what every New Yorker should know," the socialist mayor of the nation’s largest city posted on X on Friday in a message that quickly racked up over 7 million views. Mamdani explained "what every New Yorker should know" if they "encounter ICE," adding that ICE "cannot enter private spaces like your home, school, hospitals or private areas of a workplace without a judicial warrant signed by a judge." Mamdani reminded New Yorkers they have the right to remain silent and gives tips on best practices for interacting with ICE, saying that "these are very frightening times for many people." MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION' New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks at a press conference at Deno's Wonder Wheel on Coney Island in the New York City borough of Brooklyn on Feb. 15, 2026. (Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/Getty Images) Mamdani’s post was quickly criticized by conservatives on social media, with many characterizing the video as the mayor encouraging obstruction of federal law enforcement and encouraging illegal immigration. "It should be insulting to every American that the mayor of our largest city is a guy who became a citizen less than a decade ago and now spends his time coaching illegal aliens in a foreign language on how they can avoid being lawfully deported," Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, posted on X. MULLIN CALLS MAMDANI'S ANTI-ICE RHETORIC 'DANGEROUS' FOLLOWING NEW YORK SHOOTING Video "Unless you're here illegally, you have no reason to fear ICE," actor Dean Cain posted on X. "This wanker is dangerous." "At no point in this video is anyone urged to abide by the laws of the United States," Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, posted on X. "Because it was not made for the benefit of the people of the United States." "If you're here illegally, you're not a New Yorker," Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., posted on X. "Period." "Treason," Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, posted on X. "Here we are in 2026 with foreign born Democrats instructing illegals how to evade the law and remain in our country to suck off our system and best case scenario free load off our hard work," Fox News commentator Tomi Lahren posted on X. "Dangerous incitement full of disturbing falsehoods by communist terrorist supporter @NYCMayor," Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton posted on X. "This statement could put lives in danger." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a press conference at the site where a man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during an operation in the Bronx on Oct. 8, 2026, in New York City. (Ryan Murphy/Getty Images) Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani’s office for comment. Mamdani has repeatedly positioned himself against ICE and the Trump administration’s immigration-enforcement agenda. During his campaign and after taking office, he called for abolishing ICE and said the NYPD would not assist the agency with civil immigration enforcement. He has also described ICE operations as harmful to immigrant communities. As mayor, Mamdani signed an executive order strengthening New York City’s sanctuary policies. The order directs city agencies to limit cooperation with federal immigration authorities, protect personal information and establish protocols for handling ICE requests to access city property or records. It also called for expanded "know your rights" materials and training for city employees. Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter from Pasadena, California, who has been with Fox News Digital since 2021. title: Christian singer Natalie Grant urges fans not to 'ignore your body' after fall led to emergency surgery
description: Natalie Grant reveals how a fall outside a restaurant led to kidney bleeding, an ICU stay, and emergency surgery that could have ruptured her bladder.
content: Entertainment Christian singer Natalie Grant urges fans not to 'ignore your body' after fall led to emergency surgery The singer recently honored Dolly Parton at the 57th Annual GMA Dove Awards at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena By Lori A Bashian , Larry Fink Fox News Published October 26, 2026 10:00am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Natalie Grant suffered internal bleeding after she 'belly flopped' on her way to dinner The Christian singer told Fox News Digital about the time she tripped while on the way to dinner and suffered internal bleeding. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Christian singer Natalie Grant is opening up about a crazy health scare. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old singer discussed what it meant to her to honor Dolly Parton at the Dove Awards and how she ended up in the hospital with internal bleeding. Grant explained that after moving her daughter into her dorm room at college, they went out to dinner together with her husband, and on the way, her foot "caught this brick on the ground" and she "belly flopped" onto the ground. "I thought, 'Oh, maybe I broke a rib' or 'Man, that's gonna leave a bruise' or 'I kind of knocked the wind out of me,'" she said. "But then I got up and I kept walking to dinner. I'm like, I'm sore, but I'm gonna be okay. It wasn't until I realized that I was bleeding internally. And when I realized that it was an emergency, got to the emergency room. And they were like your bladder could rupture, because my kidney was bleeding, and I wasn't able to pass urine." Grant shared how a simple fall on the way to dinner led to internal bleeding. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images) She explained that when she initially arrived at the emergency room, doctors "were kind of confused about what was going on," and it wasn't until she was admitted into the ICU when they realized how serious her condition was. "I had a catheter so you could see the blood kept filling. I wouldn't stop bleeding, and I think that's when they were like we've got to get you in for surgery and figure out what's going on. But they all let me know like if you wouldn't have come in, like I talked about maybe going to a bigger hospital, and they said, 'No you were really smart to come as fast as you could and get here as quickly as you can,' because if I didn't, my bladder would have actually ruptured, and I wouldn't have known it." WATCH HERE: NATALIE GRANT SUFFERED INTERNAL BLEEDING AFTER SHE ‘BELLY FLOPPED’ ON HER WAY TO DINNER Video The singer went on to say that even through all her pain, she was thinking about her children and how they were feeling, noting that as moms, "we're always concerned about everybody around us," even when bleeding internally. While in the hospital, she was thinking of her daughter in the hospital with her, who "faints at the sight of blood," as well as her other two daughters back home in Nashville, and how she was going to tell them. Grant urges her fans to listen to their body when they feel pain. (Tibrina Hobson/Getty Images) GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I was in pain, but I didn't want to miss the moment. I was like, 'No, we are celebrating the fact that she has finished college, and we are going to dinner together, and we're going to make this memory,'" she said. "And I'm kind of like hurting and limping and not able to fully eat my meal. And I was, like, I don't think I can ignore this anymore, but that was just such a picture of what moms do." After her incident, Grant urges her fans not to "ignore your body," saying, "God created our body in such a way that it gives us signs" and too often, those signs go ignored until "it's too late." WATCH HERE: CHRISTIAN SINGER NATALIE GRANT IS 100 PERCENT HEALED FROM HER INTERNAL INJURIES SUSTAINED AFTER A FALL Video Months after the fall, Grant said she has completely healed, and that, "funnily enough," she did actually break a rib in the fall, and that has been the most painful part. WATCH HERE: DOCTORS WERE INITIALLY CONFUSED WHEN NATALIE GRANT CAME INTO THE HOSPITAL AFTER HER FALL Video "I just last week had my final cystoscopy which checked inside my kidney and my bladder and everything looks fantastic. It's 100 percent healed. You actually can see a scar from where it was and there's I'm like, there's a sermon in that. It's all healed, we still have the scar, but it's healed. And then I just had an ultrasound as well. So internally, everything is 100%. And I just, I thank God because that could have gone 100 different directions. But I'm very, very grateful for good medical care and for the faithfulness of God took care of me." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? title: NASCAR should be fuming over embarrassing 'Dega race, drivers are livid & controversial finish raises doubt
description: Kyle Larson surged from 11th to first at Talladega, but a yellow line controversy and an embarrassing fuel-saving Stage I stole the spotlight.
content: OutKick NASCAR should be fuming over embarrassing 'Dega race, drivers are livid & controversial finish raises doubt Drivers openly mocked the slow-speed opening stage over team radio as the entire pack crawled to conserve fuel By Zach Dean OutKick Published October 26, 2026 9:19am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Carson Hocevar isn't worried about social media drama Carson Hocevar is currently 12th in the cup series Monday Morning Pit-Stop is a weekly NASCAR column that runs on OutKick.com and Fox News Digital. If you're looking for a normal NASCAR recap, go check out insufferable ESPN ... assuming they still know NASCAR exists. I'm not even sure a great finish like that is gonna save NASCAR this week ... Lordy. What a day at Talladega. It had everything. It usually does. Cars flipping. Cars going airborne. One of the hardest hits I've ever seen. Kyle Larson going from 11th to first in about 10 seconds to win at the buzzer. NASCAR'S JOEY LOGANO RIDES ON HIS ROOF, RILEY HERBST NAILS WALL AT FULL SPEED IN DANGEROUS TALLADEGA WRECK This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom. Did he go below the 'yella line? Maybe. Maybe not. A tale as old as time at Talladega. Kyle Larson, driver of the No. 5 HendrickCars.com Chevrolet, takes the checkered flag to win the NASCAR Cup Series YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway on Oct. 25, 2026, in Talladega, Ala. (Getty Images) In between all that mayhem, we had — arguably — the most embarrassing sequence in NASCAR history. It was certainly the most embarrassing at a superspeedway. Drivers were so annoyed by it, they were openly mocking it over the radio ... as it happened! As they participated! It was pathetic. This Next Gen car is so pathetic, and so broken, and so far from what this series used to be, I don't even know where to go from here. Neither does Denny Hamlin. There's "fuel-saving," and then there's whatever the heck THAT was in Stage I yesterday. You'll see. Four tires, enough fuel to get through the final two races and crown Kyle Larson the champion (it's a wrap, folks), and maybe a Tylenol for Riley Herbst and Joey Logano ... Monday Morning Pit-Stop — the 'Gee, I Wonder Why Ratings Are In The Toilet?' edition — is LIVE! NASCAR has a mileage problem Look, we got a great finish yesterday as you can see — and we desperately needed one after the dud that's been the playoffs. There's been no drama over the past eight weeks, beyond Carson Hocevar stuffing Ryan Blaney in a locker. That's it. And we finally got some yesterday in the closing laps at Talladega. That's what I WANT to to start class with, but I can't. Can't do it. Not when crap like this is going in the opening stage: For those who can't tell what's going on, the entire pack — minus the RFK boys (MAHA!) — decided to save fuel during the opening stage so they wouldn't have to pit because this current car, combined with the stage lengths, make it almost impossible to run the race without running out of gas. CHASE ELLIOTT SAYS NASCAR'S GRUELING 10-MONTH SEASON CAN 'EAT YOU UP' WITHOUT AN ESCAPE As Denny Hamlin said after the race, "it’s a sports car not meant to be running 200mph." Correct. That's what NASCAR has created with this car + stage combo at superspeedways. Basically, if you don't run slow, stay in the draft, and save as much fuel as possible, you're gonna pay for it when it comes to pit stops. Drivers hate it, but they don't have much a choice. They were MISERABLE yesterday. Just listen to what Denny said during the race! If NASCAR doesn't fix this, it's over "This is some crazy s–t," he said. "This is like the Richard Petty Driving Experience at a race!" I've done the Richard Petty experience, and Denny is 10000% right. When you do that, they basically cap the cars at 175 MPH. That's what we had yesterday at 'Dega. Cars going as slow as possible to save enough fuel so they wouldn't have to pit. That should not happen at Talladega or Daytona. Those two are, easily, your best tracks, NASCAR. Trust me. You don't want to screw them up ... And you are screwing them up. Big time. It's pathetic. It's embarrassing. Folks will turn the channel. Hell, they already have! Take a look: Flips, hits & maybe dips (below the yellow line)? Lordy. Last Sunday's Cup race at Phoenix drew an audience of just 1.2 million viewers. That number is alarming, folks. I've seen a lot of bad TV numbers for NASCAR over the years. Believe me. That's really, really, really bad. You don't want to live in a world where the WNBA outdraws NASCAR, and we're teetering on that right now. It's unfathomable. It's unacceptable. It's also not surprising. Fans react as an on-track incident occurs during the NASCAR Cup Series YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway in Talladega, Ala., on Oct. 25, 2026. (Getty Images) Some thoughts on why, in order of importance: The TV deal stinks. It brought in a lot of money, but it's really poor for exposure. Do you know how many races have been on network TV this season? Eight, including yesterday at Talladega. Eight! Six on FOX, two on NBC. Before yesterday's race on NBC, there had been one race on network TV since the spring (Daytona in August). That's awful. The schedule stinks. I don't mean the tracks themselves, I mean the time of year. NASCAR is putting its 10-race "Chase" right up against college football and the NFL. That's like taking a knife to a gun fight. No sport is going to win that fight, much less NASCAR. Chase Elliott said it years ago, and it's still true today: The season needs to end around Labor Day weekend. There's no upside in going up against the NFL. The Next Gen car has been a bigger turnoff than a Kamala Harris cackle. You saw it on full display yesterday. Fans despise it. Drivers despise it. You can't pass. You can't push the car. It's very clearly piss-poor at saving fuel. God forbid you try to run in "dirty air." Folks aren't stupid. They've seen what it's done to these races, and they've lost interest. I'd also argue that the series no longer has any star power (Jeff Gordon, Dale Jr. and Tony Stewart have all left in the past decade), and there's also just a general lack of drama in these "playoffs." There's no more elimination race, which the hardcore fans wanted, but the casual fans probably miss. That's just the truth. OK, give me YOUR thoughts on this — and don't hold back! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com. Gulp. Now, let's get to a couple quick-hitters on the way out. First up? Congrats to Kyle Larson! He won yesterday in thrilling fashion, and will most likely be your champion here in two weeks. But ... did he do it legally? Thoughts? It's really close. Like, really, really, reaaaaaaallllly close. I think NASCAR made the right call, and I HATE siding with NASCAR. But fair is fair, and I do think Larson's tires stay on the line, albeit barely. Again, it was CLOSE: Does that angle change anyone's minds? Nope?! We're all just gonna be stubborn and set in our ways and argue till we're blue in the face? Okeedokee! Sounds good! Moving on ... I know Joey Logano flipping and landing on his hood gets all the clicks and the attention, but the hit Riley Herbst takes here is the most violent hit of the 2026 NASCAR season. Goodness: Just a massive hit for Riley Herbst, who is OK. I know NASCAR seemingly took forever to get over to him (listen to how frustrated the team is over the radio), but he spoke after the race and all seems well. But that was a massive hit. Ryan Blaney's taken a couple of those over the years, and they scare the bejesus out of me every time. When I saw this wreck happen in real time, my attention immediately went to Herbst over Logano. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Joey Logano, driver of the No. 22 Shell Pennzoil Ford, is involved in an on-track incident during the NASCAR Cup Series YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway on Oct. 25, 2026, in Talladega, Ala. (Getty Images) Cars that flip and go on their hoods are generally OK. Cars that go into the wall at 190 MPH are usually not. Feel like we dodged a bullet here. OK, that's it for today. Good work, everyone. On the way out, here's Jesse Love's girlfriend, Georgia Kryssing, enjoying a pumpkin patch as we start the final week of October. See y'all at Martinsville. Zach Dean is a writer for OutKick. content: OutKick Kylie Cantrall's World Series national anthem being called best since Whitney by some, NFL memes & Ric update The singer belted out the 'Star Spangled Banner' before Game 2 in Milwaukee, with fans calling it a top-five rendition By Joe Kinsey OutKick Published October 26, 2026 9:16am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Steelers-Saints fans sound off on Paris riots before NFL game OutKick spoke with NFL fans in Paris about the ongoing riots and whether the unrest affected their trips to the city for the international game. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun. title: Ex-NFL star says police aimed gun at him in front of his daughters amid incident with alleged reckless drivers
description: Footage shows a Southlake Texas police officer aiming a gun at Dez Bryant during a confrontation that ended with the former Cowboy in handcuffs.
content: OutKick Sports Ex-NFL star says police aimed gun at him in front of his daughters amid incident with alleged reckless drivers Dez Bryant received an assault citation after an encounter he says began with a shooting threat By Jackson Thompson OutKick Published October 26, 2026 8:53am EDT | Updated October 26, 2026 2:51pm EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Ex-NFL star Dez Bryant handcuffed on the ground following an incident A video shows former Dallas Cowboys star Dez Bryant on the ground in handcuffs after an incident. (Courtesy: Dez Bryant) EXCLUSIVE: Former Dallas Cowboys star Dez Bryant says a police officer aimed a gun at him in front of his daughters Sunday after a confrontation with a man he alleges threatened to shoot him following an encounter with two men who he accused or reckless driving. The incident resulted in Bryant receiving an assault citation, but began when the two men cut him off in traffic and put him in a dangerous situation, and he just tried to tell them to drive safer, he said. Footage provided to OutKick by Bryant showed an officer aiming a gun in Bryant’s direction. Bryant is also seen lying on the ground in handcuffs alongside the two other men in Southlake, Texas. Bryant ended up at the same parking lot with them, where he acknowledged knocking a phone from one man’s hand during their argument, but disputed how police handled the encounter and questioned why he received a citation after reporting that he had been threatened. ARIZONA STATE CHEERLEADER CHARGED AFTER CONFRONTATION WITH POLICE CAUGHT ON VIRAL VIDEO Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant warms up before the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, on Nov. 5, 2017. (Kevin Jairaj/USA TODAY Sports) "I was really more so concerned about my children, you know, looking at their dad, you know, being on the ground with a gun pointed at me," Bryant said. The citation reviewed by OutKick lists "Assault by Contact" and identifies the incident location as 2251 E. Southlake Blvd., the same address listed for Chiloso Mexican Bistro. It marks "Arrest: No" and instructs Bryant to appear at Southlake Municipal Court on or before Nov. 20 at 5 p.m. Bryant said the confrontation began after he encountered two vehicles whose occupants appeared to be interacting with one another at a traffic light. He accused the drivers of cutting him off and continuing to drive recklessly as they arrived at the restaurant, where he was also headed. Bryant said he told them to stop, acknowledging that he used profanity. He said an argument followed with one of the men, whom the former wide receiver described as a young adult. Video TITANS COACH PASSIONATELY DEFENDS JORDAN ELLIOTT AFTER GUN-RELATED INCIDENT LED TO RELEASE "He go to threatening me and basically saying, um, he’ll insinuate that he’ll, you know, he’ll shoot me or whatever," Bryant said. Bryant said he responded with a warning of his own. "You pull that gun, I’m telling you right now, you better use it because if you don’t I’m going to do something to you," he recalled telling the man. Asked whether the man actually drew a weapon, Bryant said: "No, he didn’t pull a gun out on me." Bryant said the man instead pulled out his phone and began recording him. "I told him, you know, get the phone off me," Bryant said. "So what I ended up doing is I knocked the phone out of his hand." The man then said he would call police, according to Bryant, who said he encouraged him to do so because he believed officers would investigate the alleged threat. Bryant said a responding officer drew a gun and ordered them to the ground. He said his girlfriend arrived with his two daughters and began recording the encounter. ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant (88) before the game against the Denver Broncos at Sports Authority Field at Mile High. (Isaiah J. Downing/USA TODAY Sports) "I get on the ground," Bryant said. "My lady pulled up, she got my children, and they seen everything that’s going on." According to Bryant, officers handcuffed the men, questioned them separately and placed him in a police vehicle before releasing him with the citation. He said the other men were allowed to leave. Bryant alleged that police relied on the other man’s phone recording without adequately investigating what preceded it. He said he asked officers to review surrounding surveillance footage, including any available video of the driving that led to the confrontation. "I would rather you guys take us all down to the police station and do the proper investigation instead of just taking somebody else, you know, side," Bryant said. "I felt like it was very one-sided." Bryant also claims an officer told him that he had to be "the bigger person." Under Texas law, assault involving offensive or provocative physical contact is generally a Class C misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of up to $500. The citation does not identify a specific statutory subsection. Bryant repeatedly described his actions as self-defense. Texas law makes that determination dependent on the circumstances, including whether someone reasonably believed force was immediately necessary to protect against another person’s use or attempted use of unlawful force. Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant (88) during an NFL game between the New York Giants and the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. He said his standing in the Southlake community, particularly among children who look up to him, motivated him to speak publicly about the encounter. "My reputation mean everything to me," Bryant said. Asked what he wanted from law enforcement moving forward, Bryant called for fairness and a thorough investigation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody fair. Treat everybody with respect," he said. "Do your due diligence on what’s actually going on." The Southlake Police Department has provided a statement to OutKick later Monday addressing the incident. "On Sunday, October 25, at approximately 12:59 p.m., Southlake officers responded to a reported fight in progress in a retail parking lot in the 2200 block of FM 1709. Several callers reported that multiple individuals were involved in the altercation as well as a possible weapon. Based on that information, officers drew their firearms upon arrival as a precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene. Several individuals were temporarily detained as part of the investigation. No firearms were recovered at the scene," the statement read. "The altercation reportedly began as a traffic incident near Kimball Avenue, where one of the involved individuals, identified as 37-year-old Desmond Bryant, reported he was cut off by another motorist. Both parties subsequently entered the parking lot, where an argument ensued and the alleged assault occurred. Following the investigation, Bryant, was issued a citation for Assault by Contact, a Class C misdemeanor, and was released at the scene." title: Alaska Dem Senate candidate suffers minor injuries in car crash, forcing her to skip campaign events
description: Democratic Sen.-nominee Mary Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries in an Anchorage crash, delaying her campaign tour in the Alaska Senate race.
content: Midterm Elections Alaska Dem Senate candidate suffers minor injuries in car crash, forcing her to skip campaign events Mary Peltola is recovering, 'eager to get back on the campaign trail' Tuesday, spokesperson says By Eric Mack Fox News Published October 26, 2026 8:36am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Trump claims midterm momentum in tarmac gaggle, attacks Dem rivals in Michigan and Alaska Senate races Speaking before departing for Michigan, President Donald Trump argued his campaign blitz has "turned the whole thing around," for the GOP. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola and members of her family were involved in a two-vehicle collision in Anchorage on Saturday night, prompting her campaign to adjust upcoming schedule commitments in the final stretch of the midterm race. The crash occurred Saturday in the vicinity of the Alaska Federation of Natives (AFN) convention, where candidate events and campaign appearances had been underway over the weekend. It happened when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, the campaign said. The family was on their way to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet. "Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits," campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement. "Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover." "Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families," Bruce added. TODD BLANCHE CHALLENGES DANA BASH FOR ONLY CITING PART OF CONSTITUTION DURING HEATED ELECTION CLASH Former Rep. Mary Peltola, D-Alaska, a U.S. Senate candidate, missed Sunday's campaign tour events and will be resting Monday before returning to the trail Tuesday for the final week before one of the most consequential Senate races on the midterm map. (Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images) The pause comes at a pivotal moment in Alaska’s high-stakes Senate contest between Peltola and incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, as both campaigns scramble across the state to mobilize voters and secure turnout ahead of the November midterm vote. DEMOCRAT'S DEBATE 'CUE CARDS' STEAL SPOTLIGHT IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE CLASH Video Peltola, an Alaska Native and former congresswoman, is hoping to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both she and Sullivan have tried to rally support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in the high-stakes race that has become one of the most watched in the nation. ALASKA HAS A VOTING SYSTEM LIKE NO OTHER STATE; REPUBLICANS WORRY IT COULD COST THEM IN NOVEMBER Video President Donald Trump — who held a rally in support of Sullivan earlier this month — said Friday he told his administration to sue to block certification of the race if the incumbent loses. The lawsuit cites potential confusion with another candidate who is listed on the ranked choice ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. Alaska allows voters to rank their top picks rather than choosing a single candidate. Voters will have four choices, including Sullivan, Peltola and the other Dan Sullivan, a candidate Republicans have called a decoy in what they believe is a Democratic effort to confuse voters. COURT KEEPS ‘DECOY DAN’ ON ALASKA BALLOT AS EXPERT WARNS RANKED-CHOICE SYSTEM CREATES VOTER ‘TRAPS’ Video "I revealed what everyone knows, that the Ranked Choice Voting Ballot is a TOTAL DEMOCRAT SCAM meant to confuse the Voter, so that Senator Dan Sullivan will lose Votes to a man who has never participated in Politics before, named Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr.," Trump wrote early Sunday morning on Truth Social. "He is only there because the Democrats want to steal the Election." It is a reason to vote out ranked-choice voting, Trump added. "The Democrats are trying to steal this important Republican Seat and, if that happens, everything we’ve done for Alaska will come to an immediate hault [sic]," Trump concluded. "VOTE 'YES' AGAINST RANKED CHOICE VOTING, on Ballot Measure 2. SAVE ALASKA!" Video CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Peltola has outraised Sullivan through October, $33 million to nearly $14 million, but Sullivan reported having more campaign cash, $5.1 million to Peltola's $3.2 million. Republicans have outspent Democrats in the race, $42 million to $38 million. The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report. title: Nikole Hannah-Jones laments 'pretty brutal' response to viral essay on sending daughter to public school
description: Nikole Hannah-Jones called the backlash to her New York Times Magazine essay on her decision to send her daughter to Black public schools "pretty brutal."
content: Media Nikole Hannah-Jones laments 'pretty brutal' response to viral essay on sending daughter to public school The 1619 Project founder told The New York Times she ultimately had no regrets publishing the essay By Lindsay Kornick Fox News Published October 26, 2026 8:29am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google Nikole Hannah-Jones faced backlash from conservative school choice advocates over her decision. (Jason Armond / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! New York Times journalist and 1619 Project founder Nikole Hannah-Jones reflected Wednesday on what she called the "pretty brutal" responses she received for her viral New York Times Magazine essay on sending her daughter to predominantly Black public schools. A decade after defending her choice, Hannah-Jones admitted in an essay last month that she regretted aspects of her decision to send her now-16-year-old daughter to these schools in an effort to combat school segregation, after her child informed Hannah-Jones that she did not receive the education she wanted. "Now I felt overcome with regret. Najya deserved better," Hannah-Jones wrote in her September essay. "They all did. But she was mine. This girl, my only child, looked to me to protect her, to give her what she needed to thrive. And I had not chosen her." KAROL MARKOWICZ: 1619 PROJECT FOUNDER NIKOLE HANNAH-JONES LEARNED THE HARD TRUTH ABOUT SCHOOLS Nikole Hannah-Jones, the controversial creator of the 1619 Project, published a viral essay regretting her decision to send her daughter to public schools. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters) Hannah-Jones' admission sparked intense backlash from critics who accused her of sacrificing her daughter's education for her progressive values. The pushback was strong enough for Hannah-Jones to question if she should have written the essay. "I know it would sound crazy if I say none of the critique was valid, but I’m like, what is the critique?" Hannah-Jones told The New York Times during an interview on Wednesday. "There was some online discourse that was pretty brutal. And, you know, I have experienced some brutal discourse through the years, but usually not about, like, me as a parent," Hannah-Jones said. "That was hard. And for a minute I’m like, ‘Man, should I have written this?’ And I’ve actually never, ever, as a journalist, questioned, 'Should I have written something?' And there was a moment where I was just like, ‘I did not have to subject myself to this. Should I have done this?’" However, Hannah-Jones concluded that she ultimately did not regret her actions despite the impact the essay had. NIKOLE HANNAH-JONES' FRIEND SENDS BLACK SON TO PRIVATE SCHOOL AFTER NYT WRITER HAS EDUCATION REGRETS Video "You know, in the end, I’m fine. I will be fine. My feelings got a little hurt because I’m a human being. But, in the end, like, people are talking about these kids who don’t have a platform, who don’t have a choice. The mayor of New York has been forced to respond. He’s now promised to release a plan to address it. That doesn’t happen without me writing a piece like this," Hannah-Jones said. She added, "And so, yeah, I have to remind myself that, like, my little bruised feelings in the end are meaningless. It is the power of what we can do with our platform, and what I would argue is our responsibility to do." Fox News Digital reached out to Hannah-Jones for comment, but did not immediately hear back. DENVER MOTHER FIGHTS FOR HER DAUGHTER'S EDUCATION AS ADVOCATES MAKE NATIONWIDE SCHOOL CHOICE PUSH Video Corey DeAngelis, a research fellow at The Heritage Foundation and longtime school choice advocate, accused the journalist of minimizing education concerns. "Calling the backlash 'brutal discourse' misses the point. People reacted because she publicly used her child as a prop for a political experiment, and the results were horrible," DeAngelis told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP He added, "School choice exists so parents can leave schools that don't work. You don't fix these schools by trapping more kids inside them and hoping your presence changes the system. Hannah-Jones tried that. It didn't work. Her daughter knows it. Parents across the country already knew it. Give families the money and the freedom to leave." Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. title: Tallahassee police arrest 15-year-old suspect after shooting near Florida A&M football stadium
description: Teen suspect arrested on 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder
content: Florida Tallahassee police arrest 15-year-old suspect after shooting near Florida A&M football stadium Teen suspect faces up to 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder By Eric Mack Fox News Published October 26, 2026 8:23am EDT | Updated October 26, 2026 10:31am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Florida shooting near FAMU stadium leaves 12 injured, including 6 children A shooting near Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee left 12 people injured, including six juveniles, with the youngest victim just 11 years old, as police investigate an altercation that preceded the gunfire. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! The Tallahassee Police Department on Sunday night arrested a 15-year-old suspect in connection with a Florida A&M shooting Saturday near the university's Bragg Memorial Stadium. "What should have been a weekend of celebration in our community instead became a night of fear and violence for the victims and their families," Chief of Police Lawrence Revell said in a Monday morning statement. "While this arrest marks a significant step forward, our work is far from over. We remain committed to holding those responsible accountable and getting answers for every family impacted by this tragedy." The teen is facing 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a delinquent, police said. 5 VICTIMS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL AFTER FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING, 1 REMAINS CRITICAL Video The gunfire erupted around 8 p.m. ET on Saturday near Perry and Manatee streets, leaving 12 people injured. Eleven individuals suffered gunshot wounds, while one person sustained an ankle injury while attempting to flee the gunfire. It is not yet clear how many shooters fired shots or the extent of the teen's involvement in the shooting. At least five victims have been released from the hospital, while six others remained hospitalized Sunday night, including one in critical condition, Revell said in a video update posted to X. SHOOTING NEAR BALTIMORE YOUTH FOOTBALL EVENT LEAVES 12-YEAR-OLD GIRL DEAD, 3 ADULTS WOUNDED Police responded to a shooting near the intersection of Perry and Manatee streets, close to Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium, on Saturday night. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters) A fight broke out before the shooting and detectives believe the shooting resulted from a dispute between individuals who knew each other. None of the 12 victims appear to have been the intended targets, according to police. Officers responding to the scene Saturday evening provided immediate medical aid to victims before the perimeter was fully secured. Sworn and civilian personnel — including detectives, crime analysts and victim advocates — have worked around the clock since the incident to process the scene and identify those involved. Police officials credited community cooperation for accelerating the case, citing a substantial influx of tips and public digital evidence submitted in the hours following the gunfire. VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY SHOOTING SUSPECT FOUND HIDING IN DORM CLOSET ARRESTED Image 1 of 3 next Twelve people, including six juveniles, were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee on Saturday night, according to police. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters) The investigation remains active and ongoing, noting that additional arrests are possible as detectives continue to review physical evidence, trace leads and establish the full sequence of events. "We will determine what happened, identify those responsible, and get answers for all of the victims, their families and everyone impacted by this tragedy," Revell wrote in a statement Sunday. "We know there are people who saw something, heard something or may have video that could help us piece together exactly what happened." TPD urges anyone with information to call the department’s dedicated tip line at 850-891-4610 or upload photos and video evidence via the agency's online portal. title: Medieval hospital built for victims of feared disease gives up long-buried secrets
description: A three-day dig at Lincoln's Hospital of the Holy Innocents in England uncovered small structures that may have served as private quarters for leprosy patients.
content: Discovery Medieval hospital built for victims of feared disease gives up long-buried secrets Hospital of the Holy Innocents housed up to 20 patients for nearly 500 years By Andrea Margolis Fox News Published October 26, 2026 8:00am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video Ancient hospital ruins yield clues to life with feared medieval disease Archaeologists in England have uncovered new remains at one of the country's oldest and largest medieval leprosy hospitals, revealing clues about how patients may have lived centuries ago. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! Archaeologists in England have uncovered new remains at one of the country's oldest and largest medieval leprosy hospitals, hundreds of years after the disease ravaged communities across Britain. The recent excavation, reported by British news agency Jam Press, centered on South Common in Lincoln, a historic English city roughly 140 miles north of London. The site was once home to the Hospital of the Holy Innocents, which was founded between the late 11th and early 12th centuries. MYSTERIOUS SETTLEMENT DISCOVERED AFTER RESIDENTS SEEMINGLY PACKED UP AND VANISHED During a three-day excavation, archaeologists from the British television program "Time Team" uncovered traces of medieval walls and possible living quarters. The hospital operated for nearly 500 years, housing up to 20 leprosy patients at a time, officials said. Archaeologists have uncovered new remains of a medieval leprosy hospital that operated for nearly 500 years. (Jam Press/City of Lincoln Council; Heritage Art/Heritage Images via Getty Images) The findings build on an excavation that took place last year, when volunteers unearthed walls, building surfaces and artifacts linked to the former hospital. This time, researchers identified traces of small, square features that may have served as individual living quarters or enclosed yards for patients. The structures have never been excavated before, researchers said, according to Jam Press. SHOCKING DISCOVERY OF ANCIENT BONES TURNS COUPLE'S KITCHEN RENOVATION INTO 'CRIME SCENE' The findings offer a rare glimpse into how leprosy patients may have lived during the Middle Ages, including who could afford to receive care. "You'd need to have resources to get in here," professor Carenza Lewis of the University of Lincoln said, according to Jam Press. Archaeologists investigating South Common in Lincoln have uncovered evidence of small, square structures that may have housed medieval leprosy patients. (Jam Press/City of Lincoln Council) "If you had enough money and could buy your way into a leper hospital, it's a bit like getting a place in a private care home or something like that." Historical documents suggest the hospital accommodated up to 20 patients, who may have lived in separate structures with small yards, Lewis said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "We know that they had little sorts of curtilages [enclosed plots of land], which implies they're separate little buildings, little houses with a little yard, perhaps," she said. Leprosy, also known as Hansen's disease, is a chronic bacterial infection that primarily affects the skin, nerves and eyes. The Hospital of the Holy Innocents, founded between the late 11th and early 12th centuries, once housed patients suffering from leprosy. (Pictures From History/Universal Images Group via Getty Images; Jam Press/City of Lincoln Council) Although the disease can cause severe disfigurement if left untreated, it is curable with antibiotics and still exists today. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The excavation is part of a three-year research project led by Anglia Ruskin University, which aims to learn more about the people who lived, worked and died at the medieval hospital. Leprosy is curable with antibiotics and still exists today. Tim Taylor, the creator of "Time Team," said the site could reveal more about Lincoln's archaeological past. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "Lincoln has an extraordinary archaeological story, and this site promises to give us the opportunity to uncover a fascinating part of it," Taylor said, Jam Press reported. Researchers say the newly identified structures may offer clues about how patients lived at one of England's oldest medieval leprosy hospitals. (Jam Press/City of Lincoln Council) The findings come after a similar discovery last year in York, England, where a sinkhole in a city street exposed the remains of one of northern England's largest medieval hospitals. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The remains were believed to belong to St. Leonard's Hospital and date back to the 12th or 13th century.
