title: Dem Senate hopeful rejects Schumer but benefits from millions in spending by his allies
description: Adam Hamilton distances himself from Chuck Schumer even as Senate Majority PAC pours millions into the Kansas Senate race against Roger Marshall.
content: Politics Dem Senate hopeful rejects Schumer but benefits from millions in spending by his allies Marshall questions how Hamilton can accept tens of millions in Dem outside spending and remain independent By Alex Miller Fox News Published October 26, 2026 8:00am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video GOP senator calls out Dem rival over millions in Schumer-linked support: 'Beholden to him' Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., told Fox News Digital that if Adam Hamilton really meant he would not support Chuck Schumer to lead Democrats, he would reject the millions flowing into Kansas from Schumer and national Democrats. NEWYou can now listen to Fox News articles! WICHITA, Kan. — National Democrats are pouring millions of dollars into Kansas to bolster Adam Hamilton, who has spent much of his campaign arguing that he would not be beholden to the top Democratic leaders in Washington, D.C. Tens of millions are flowing into Kansas to boost Hamilton, with a sizable chunk coming from Senate Majority PAC, a super PAC closely aligned with Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., whom Hamilton has repeatedly said he would not support as the Democratic leader should he win in November. But his opponent, Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., questioned how he could benefit from "$30 to $40 million from Chuck Schumer and not be beholden to him in some way?" THUNE MAKES BOLD PREDICTION ABOUT REPUBLICANS' SENATE CHANCES AS GOP PULLS MILLIONS FROM KEY RACES Democrat senatorial candidate Adam Hamilton answers questions from the media after a televised debate with Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., at WDAF studios in Kansas City, Mo., on Oct. 21, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images) "Regardless of what he says, if we lose this seat, then it's going to give the Senate control to the Democrats," Marshall told Fox News Digital during an interview on the campaign trail. "Chuck Schumer would be the leader of the Senate." "Look, if he's going to denounce Chuck Schumer, let's denounce him with his money as well," he continued, "Look, we're going to be outspent five to one, and we knew that." Candidates, notably, can’t directly accept outside funding from independent groups like the Senate Majority PAC, given the guardrails are established by federal election law, according to the Federal Election Commission. SCHUMER WARNS OF REPUBLICAN ADVANTAGE THAT COULD CHANGE THE BATTLE FOR SENATE CONTROL Video The Schumer-aligned group teed up $5 million in advertising spending in Kansas earlier this month, a sign that Democrats are bullish about flipping the seat in a contest that has gotten closer than Republicans expected. Hamilton's campaign pushed back on Marshall, arguing that the first-term senator has been given a lifeboat by national Republicans. Hamilton has vastly outraised Marshall, scoring nearly $14 million compared to Marshall’s almost $6 million, according to Federal Election Commission filings. "Adam has said repeatedly he believes it’s time for fresh leadership in Washington," Tyson Brody, a Hamilton campaign spokesperson, told Fox News Digital. "Adam will always put Kansas first. Meanwhile, Roger Marshall is totally dependent on Washington money to save his campaign because he has abandoned Kansas to support D.C. corruption, endless war and high prices." KANSAS DEMOCRAT BEGS KAMALA HARRIS NOT TO CAMPAIGN WITH HIM, ‘PLEASE DO NOT COME TO MY STATE’ Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., departs after a weekly Senate Democratic Policy luncheon at the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on July 29, 2026. (Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images) In all, national Democrats and their affiliated groups — combined with spending from Hamilton’s campaign — are slated to dump $38 million into the race, according to AdImpact. National Republicans, along with Marshall’s campaign, are putting $32 million into the contest. Marshall has sought to tie Hamilton, who is running as a moderate in ruby-red Kansas, directly to Schumer, a point he made several times during their final debate before Election Day this week. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hamilton pushed back, arguing that Marshall had mentioned Schumer "maybe 20 times so far." "I’ve already said I wouldn't support Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader if the Democrats took control of the Senate," Hamilton said. Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate. title: ESPN star calls out Jets head coach following team's loss to winless Dolphins
description: Mike Greenberg called New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn's game management "inexcusable" after a timeout blunder led to a costly Dolphins touchdown.
content: OutKick ESPN star calls out Jets head coach following team's loss to winless Dolphins Mike Greenberg, a Jets superfan, wrote that Glenn is 'as bad at it as any coach I've ever seen' at game management By Ryan Gaydos OutKick Published October 26, 2026 7:45am EDT Comments Facebook Twitter Threads Flipboard Print Email Add Fox News on Google close Video WWE's Michael Cole Loves the Jets and Mets His father was a fan and so is he. It’s unclear if a loss to the previously winless Miami Dolphins was a rock bottom moment for the New York Jets, but it feels as close as a team can get. Miami won the game 28-25 and outgained New York 377-360. The Jets put pressure on the Dolphins in the fourth quarter, outscoring them 11-7, but a crucial three-and-out led to a Dolphins touchdown on the team’s next drive, which only took just over a minute. New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn leaves after a news conference following the Miami Dolphins' victory over the Jets in an NFL football game in East Rutherford, N.J., on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. New York’s second quarter included an interception, a punt and one play to end the half. The Dolphins had two possessions – a punt and a 15-play, 91-yard touchdown drive. "Maybe we should've called our timeouts to get it back, but at that point, we just felt like we were going to stop them and be able to get the ball back," Glenn told reporters. "Game management is the most important part of this job and he is as bad at it as any coach I’ve ever seen. "There may not be any point in making the change now, but it’s over, it’s just a matter of when." New York is only 2-5 on the season. The Jets started with a win over the Tennessee Titans, nearly beat the Green Bay Packers, Detroit Lions and then topped the AFC North-leading Cleveland Browns. Other losses were against the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots. There have been highs but the lows have been almost too much to handle if you’re a Jets fan. New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn stands on the sideline during the first half of an NFL game against the Miami Dolphins in East Rutherford, N.J., on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger) OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The Jets have not made the playoffs since 2010 and it looks like the unfortunate streak is going to continue this season unless something really changes. content: Politics Embattled Ilhan Omar tells lefty antisemitic streamer Hasan Piker her ‘good’ looks are why media is fixated on her By Victor Nava Published Oct. 26, 2026 Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 10:37 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Embattled Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) joked with Hasan Piker that the media is fixated on her because of her “good” looks Monday ahead of a controversial event with the far-left antisemitic streamer. Omar made the remark during Piker’s livestream of his green-room couch conversation with the “Squad” rep before they took the stage at the event hosted by socialist Minnesota state lawmaker Omar Fateh. “I feel like the media has a tendency, you know, to highlight everything that you do,” Piker told Omar during their chummy conversation. “Some of the things that I do, like – we’re just normal Americans trying to go about our day-to-day and trying to organize against the Trump administration in the same way that, you know, white people are doing in general. 4 Controversial streamer Hasan Piker during his green-room couch conversation with embattled “Squad” Rep. Ilhan Omar before they take the stage at an event hosted by socialist Minnesota state lawmaker Omar Fateh on Oct. 26, 2026. twitch.tv/hasanabi 4 Omar came under fire for doing the event with the far-left influencer. twitch.tv/hasanabi “Why is that?” Omar responded: “We just look really good on their screens.” The event was described as the inaugural episode of Fateh’s “I’m The Host Now!” series. The host introduced Omar to the crowd as “my sister and congresswoman,” after touting that tickets to the event with “everyone’s favorite streamer” sold out in five minutes. The congresswoman, who is being investigated by the Trump administration over allegations of possible immigration fraud, boasted about Minneapolis’ Somali “network” and how difficult it has been for federal authorities to penetrate during the on-stage conversation. As an example of “just how much people fear us and understand just how strategically connected we are,” Omar recalled a meeting with DHS officials shortly after Trump took office last year. “It was a strategic meeting because we wanted to, you know, understand and be connected in case something was going to pop off like it did eventually pop off … and I remember their attorney said, you know, ‘I’ve been doing this for decades, and this is the one state I hate to be assigned to because it is the only state [that the DHS attorney had been assigned to] that has a network that is hard to penetrate,’” Omar said. “Two months prior to that, we had the extent of that network in our office and our conference room, talking and strategizing about, you know, what our response was going to be in case they targeted us,” she continued. Omar added: “Somalis are not the people to mess with.” Piker argued “jealousy” was to blame for why Minneapolis has been at the center of so many national issues in recent years. “White supremacist forces in this country have decided to target Minneapolis because of the successful Somali American community that has been able to thrive here,” he said. The event drew widespread condemnation from Republicans and Jewish groups. “Ilhan Omar knows exactly who Hasan Piker is and what he has said,” John Nagel, Omar’s GOP opponent in her midterm election race, fumed on X. Nagel highlighted some of Piker’s most outrageous commentary, including his belief that “America deserved 9/11” and that he’d vote for Hamas over Israel “every single time.” “This is not outreach. It is the normalization of antisemitism, support for terrorists and contempt for America,” Nagel argued, demanding that prominent state Democrats disavow Omar’s appearance with Piker. title: 49ers not trying out kickers despite Eddy Pineiro’s continued struggles
description: In Pineiro’s case, no news is good news.
content: NFL 49ers not trying out kickers despite Eddy Pineiro’s continued struggles By Evan Webeck Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:44 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Eddy Pineiro doesn’t have to worry about his job security … at least not yet. The 49ers maligned kicker missed his fourth extra point of the season Sunday against the Falcons, giving coach Kyle Shanahan something to talk over with general manager John Lynch on the cross-country flight back following the 29-20 loss in Atlanta. Some 24 hours later, though, Shanahan had no update to deliver when asked if Pineiro’s struggles would lead San Francisco to try out other kickers over its bye week. 3 San Francisco 49ers kicker Eddy Pineiro kicks an extra point after a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of an NFL football game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images “I haven’t discussed it with guys. I haven’t been told that we are,” Shanahan said. “As far as I’ve heard, we don’t have any plans on that right now.” In Pineiro’s case, no news is good news. The 31-year-old kicker signed a four-year, $17 million extension this offseason after acting as a saving grace for the 49ers’ kicking woes last year. Now, though, the same problems are rearing their head — only with Pineiro, rather than the erstwhile Jake Moody. Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance Pineiro made all but one of his 29 field goal attempts upon signing with San Francisco in Week 2, the best success rate in NFL history (96.6%). His only miss came from 64 yards. It’s been a different story this year, albeit a familiar one for 49ers fans. In addition to his four missed extra points in 25 tries, Pineiro has split the uprights on six of nine field goal attempts. His point-after woes came to a head this week, leaving the 49ers still trailing by two scores when Brock Purdy got the ball late in the fourth quarter for what turned into their final drive. 3 San Francisco 49ers place kicker Eddy Pineiro prepares to kick an extra point during the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, California, Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Pineiro missed the extra point after the 49ers scored a touchdown to cut the deficit to 26-20. Had it been good, the 49ers still would have been able to tie the game with a touchdown and a two-point conversion after the Falcons extended their lead to 29-20. The 49ers had an opportunity to cut the deficit to nine earlier in the fourth quarter after driving near the red zone, but faced with a fourth-and-10 at the Falcons’ 23, Shanahan decided to go for it. Purdy was sacked, giving the ball back to Atlanta still trailing 26-14. Shanahan said Pineiro’s struggles from short distance didn’t factor into his decision. 3 San Francisco 49ers place kicker Eddy Pineiro performs during the first quarter against the Denver Broncos at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “I didn’t consider the field goal, and it had nothing to do with whether I thought we’d make it or not,” Shanahan said. “It was a two-touchdown game at the time and I didn’t think a field goal was going to change much. I also thought we could get that first down.” Nevertheless, Pineiro hasn’t been as money as he was last year. Money, it turns out, could be a complicating factor in moving on from him. Although the 49ers have plenty of cap space, it would cost them $6 million in dead money next year if they were to cut him this season. Regardless, he should probably still be looking over his shoulder. content: WNBA WNBA championship celebration could be moved to practice court in unfortunate twist By Valentina Martinez Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:34 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source The Valkyries and Dream square off in Game 5 of the WNBA Finals Monday. The series is tied at two games a piece, making Monday’s matchup a critical turning point. If Golden State or Atlanta manage to win back-to-back contests, then Game 6 would be the clincher. 3 Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese dribbles the ball during Game 4 of the WNBA basketball finals against the Golden State Valkyries. AP Photo/Brynn Anderson 3 Atlanta Dream guard Allisha Gray gestures towards Golden State Valkyries guard Kaitlyn Chen (2) in the second half during Game 4 of the WNBA basketball finals. AP Photo/Brynn Anderson This is where things get complicated. Game 6 of the WNBA Finals is scheduled for 12:30 p.m. at State Farm Arena, home of the Hawks who are set to play the Cavaliers in the same arena at 8 p.m. There are reportedly concerns about having enough time for the WNBA champions to celebrate on the court before the arena is prepared for the NBA game, which could push the celebrations to a practice court if the title is won Thursday. The location of Game 6 was recently determined after reported frantic discussions, but the Dream hoped to play at a larger arena then their Gateway Center Arena, which holds 3,500 seats. Now, it appears if a WNBA champion is to be crowned after Game 6, the Valkyries or Dream may have to celebrate with fans in alternate location. title: Ben & Jerry’s founders explore deal to separate brand from owner after previous clashes: report
description: Ben & Jerry's owner Magnum sayd the ice cream brand isn't for sale.
content: Business Ben & Jerry’s founders explore deal to separate brand from owner after previous clashes: report By Reuters Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:29 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Ben & Jerry’s founders Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield are exploring a deal to separate their brand from its current owner, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday. The ice cream brand is owned by Unilever spin-off Magnum Ice Cream. The co-founders have been discussing a deal with Pete Stavros, founder of Expanding ESOPs, to carve out the business and structure it under an employee stock-ownership plan, WSJ said, citing Stavros and Cohen. Ben Cohen, left, and Jerry Greenfield at a protest in Washington in 2019. The Ben & Jerry’s founders are exploring a deal to separate their brand from its current owner. AP The structure would give rank-and-file employees stock while providing the company with tax benefits, the report added. But any deal would need to be approved by Ben & Jerry’s owner Magnum, which told Reuters in an emailed statement that “Ben & Jerry’s is not for sale and, more importantly, is thriving as part of The Magnum Ice Cream Company.” Explore More Apple addresses reports of cracked screens on $2K iPhone Duo just days after frenzied launch How to stop worrying about the $40 trillion – yes trillion with a ‘T’ – that’s now owed by the US government Forget Florida — Baby Boomers flocking to Eastern seaboard state for low taxes, sandy beaches “Taking Ben & Jerry’s out of Magnum would drive significant dis-synergies, investment in the social mission would fall, and selling prices per unit would inflate,” it added. Ben & Jerry’s has a history of vocal social activism and its founders and board have repeatedly clashed with former parent Unilever over political and ethical stances. title: California illegal migrant’s ICE fantasy implodes after she was busted on video at fast food joint
description: A scheming Los Angeles illegal alien admitted guilt in federal court after making up a bogus ICE kidnapping story that was meant to smear federal officers.
content: California News California illegal migrant’s ICE fantasy implodes after she was busted on video at fast food joint By Justin Choi Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:27 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source A Los Angeles illegal immigrant from Mexico admitted guilt in federal court after making up a bogus ICE kidnapping story that was meant to smear federal officers. Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón, 43, pleaded guilty Monday to staging a fake kidnapping where she said bounty hunters took her at gunpoint and tried forcing her to self-deport outside a Jack in the Box. “On June 25, 2025, Calderón falsely told an individual that ‘immigration’ was taking her while in or near a fast-food restaurant and that immigration officials had ‘turned the lights on,’ ‘threatened to break her window’ and were taking her into custody,” a DOJ press release wrote. She also called a third person and claimed that she was moved to an unknown warehouse where she was being held with other detainees. 6 Daughters Jennifer and Angie stand next to a picture of their mother, Yuriana Julia Pelaez Calderón, as lawyer Stephano Medina and community members hold a press conference. REUTERS 6 The June 2025 protest concerned the whereabouts of Calderón, following what community members and relatives describe as her abduction by men in unmarked cars and of unknown affiliation. REUTERS Calderón’s family and attorneys then held a press conference on June 30 of last year spewing her lies, which brought about false media coverage. Despite knowing about the false coverage, Calderón remained silent and even changed her appearance to make it seem like she had been mistreated. She also decided to stage her fake release and turned off her phone from July 3 to July 5. “Dangerous rhetoric that ICE agents are ‘kidnapping’ illegal immigrants is being recklessly peddled by politicians and echoed in the media to inflame the public and discredit our courageous federal agents,” United States Attorney Bill Essayli said last year. 6 Calderón was spotted at a shopping plaza parking lot on July 5. KTLA 5 6 She was seen walking around despite claiming she had been kidnapped. KTLA 5 A GoFundMe was created but has since been deleted. The 43 year old was eventually found in a shopping plaza parking lot in Bakersfield on July 5 but continued to assert she had been kidnapped. Calderón finally admitted guilt to one count of conspiracy to “impede, obstruct, impair, and defeat the lawful function of Homeland Security Investigations” and faces up to five years in federal prison at her sentencing hearing on Feb. 8, 2027. title: Steve Hilton has the only good idea for California’s failed fake train dreams
description: High-speed rail is a solution to a problem that doesn't exist: Californians can already travel easily and cheaply between San Francisco and LA.
content: Opinion Steve Hilton has the only good idea for California’s failed fake train dreams By CA Post Editorial Board Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:18 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Steve Hilton is right: California’s high-speed rail project belongs in a museum, not on a map — and certainly not on the state’s budget. The “bullet train to nowhere” was supposed to link San Francisco to Los Angeles in under three hours at a cost of $33 billion by 2020. Instead, it will only link a couple of towns in the Central Valley, at a cost of over $200 billion, by 2032 at the earliest. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story Check out more newsletters The Republican candidate for governor says he will end the project and “turn it into the Government Failures National Monument.” That might actually be a profitable idea. One can imagine something like the statue parks that sprang up in Eastern Europe after the fall of communism. These were monuments to the vanity of “proletarian” leaders who claimed to rule in the name of the working classes, while enriching themselves and crushing the freedom of other human beings. Even Gavin Newsom understood that the high-speed rail project was a disaster — and that was eight years ago. California Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton is right: California’s high-speed rail project belongs in a museum, not on a map — and certainly not on the state’s budget. AP Photo/Amanda Villegas When he took office, he told the state legislature that he was canceling the overall plan — because, as he said, “The project, as currently planned, would cost too much and take too long. There’s been too little oversight and not enough transparency.” But like every other failed project he attempted in two terms as governor, Newsom left that job unfinished. He didn’t cancel the whole high-speed rail project — just the part that connected the big cities where people actually wanted to go. The “bullet train to nowhere” was supposed to link San Francisco to Los Angeles in under three hours at a cost of $33 billion by 2020. Instead, it will connect some Central Valley towns by 2032. Reuters Today, Democrat Xavier Becerra says he wants to continue the failing high-speed rail project. When asked during a primary debate if he would keep it going, Becerra said: “The slow-speed delivery of high-speed rail, no; the high-speed delivery of high-speed rail, yes.” “What does that mean?” Hilton asked. Exactly. High-speed rail is a solution to a problem that doesn’t exist: Californians can already travel easily and cheaply between San Francisco and LA. Past governors have touted high-speed rail as an answer to climate change. But the construction process alone has emitted huge amounts of carbon, and involves other environmental challenges. Even private sector versions of high-speed rail, like the Brightline project between Las Vegas and Southern California, have run into trouble. Stop the madness. Turn the bullet train into the “Government Failures National Monument” — so that future generations of Californians can learn what the state cannot do with taxpayer money. title: DoorDash in talks to buy delivery rival Instacart in $17B deal: report
description: Instacart's deal talks with Uber are no longer active, a source told rivals.
content: Business DoorDash in talks to buy delivery rival Instacart in $17B deal: report By Reuters Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:18 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart in a deal that could value the grocery-delivery platform at about $17 billion, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Monday. A deal may be finalized as soon as Wednesday, although there are no guarantees it will come together, the person said. Instacart’s deal talks with Uber are no longer active, the person added. Shares of Instacart, which had a market value of about $13 billion as of Friday’s close, rose about 8% in regular trading, while DoorDash fell around 6%. DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart in a deal that could value the grocery-delivery platform at about $17 billion. Mojahid Mottakin – stock.adobe.com The Wall Street Journal first reported the developments on Monday. The food delivery industry has been grappling with rising labor costs, tighter regulation of delivery workers and growing competition after the pandemic-driven boom in online ordering faded. If successful, the acquisition of Instacart would give DoorDash access to the platform’s established marketplace and retailer ties, which it could combine with its own vast delivery network and customer base. The grocery platform has been exploring a possible sale and has held preliminary discussions with potential buyers including Uber and DoorDash, the Information reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Shares of Instacart, which had a market value of about $13 billion as of Friday’s close, rose about 8% in regular trading. REUTERS Instacart declined to comment when contacted by Reuters, while Uber and DoorDash did not immediately respond. “Strategically, DoorDash looks like the more natural fit for Instacart, given the complementary strengths of its restaurant delivery network and Instacart’s grocery expertise,” said Nick Smith, co-founder of growth strategy consultancy Manifesto Growth Architects. “For Uber, the opportunity would be to deepen its position as an everyday convenience platform. But an acquisition only makes sense if it delivers incremental customer value and profitable growth — not simply greater scale.” Separately, Instacart said in a regulatory filing on Monday it would wind down its Caper Cart smart shopping-cart business by the end of the second quarter of 2027, expecting pre-tax charges of $55 million to $80 million related to the move. title: Rick Caruso backs former rival Karen Bass for LA mayor, blasts Nithya Raman’s LAPD plans as ‘reckless and dangerous’
description: Rick Caruso has endorsed LA Mayor Karen Bass ahead of the Nov. 3 election, slamming challenger Nithya Raman's LAPD plans.
content: California News Rick Caruso backs former rival Karen Bass for LA mayor, blasts Nithya Raman’s LAPD plans as ‘reckless and dangerous’ By Jamie Paige Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:08 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Billionaire developer Rick Caruso is backing his former political rival, Mayor Karen Bass, just eight days before Election Day, blasting challenger Nithya Raman’s plans for the LAPD as “reckless and dangerous.” Caruso announced Monday in an Instagram post that he would cast his ballot for the mayor after working alongside her on recovery efforts following Los Angeles’ devastating wildfires. “For the love of LA, I must put the past behind me,” Caruso said in the statement. His endorsement came with a blistering assessment of Raman, particularly her pledge to replace LAPD Chief Jim McDonnell. “This is no time to turn the LAPD into a laboratory for risky DSA social experimentation,” Caruso warned. He also questioned Raman’s record overseeing homelessness policy at City Hall. 4 Caruso also questioned Raman’s record overseeing homelessness policy at City Hall. Jonathan Alcorn for CA Post “She’s led the city’s homeless policy. Does anybody think that is a success?” Caruso asked. Caruso’s announcement follows a week of speculation after he appeared alongside Bass at a Pacific Palisades rebuilding event but stopped short of revealing his choice. His decision also follows a similar declaration from Councilwoman Traci Park, whose district includes the Palisades fire zone. Park told constituents last week she would vote for Bass despite reservations about the mayor’s leadership, warning that Raman could reverse progress on public safety and wildfire recovery. “I hear you — I want some change too, but the alternative does not actually get us where we want to be,” Park told residents. “I think it actually impedes our progress and unfortunately will take us back to where we were.” The two backings come as Bass battles to secure a second term against Raman, who has the support of the Democratic Socialists of America and Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey Horvath. title: Alleged Dez Bryant assault victim tells The Post what set off ex-NFL star: ‘You going to die today’
description: The 19-year-old barber said Bryant went nuclear on him just outside of a Southlake restaurant.
content: NFL exclusive Alleged Dez Bryant assault victim tells The Post what set off ex-NFL star: ‘You going to die today’ By Edward Lewis Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:02 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Dez Bryant punched a teenager in the hand, scratched up his phone and repeatedly threatened to kill him during a heated dispute in a Texas parking lot on Sunday, according to the former Cowboys star’s alleged assault victim. In an exclusive interview with The Post on Monday, Noah Reyes, a 19-year-old barber, said Bryant, 37, put his hands on him just outside of a Southlake restaurant right after Reyes and some friends had attended church. See Also Former Cowboys star Dez Bryant handcuffed, held at gunpoint by cops in shocking new video Reyes told The Post Bryant became unhinged after he and his buddy, 19-year-old HVAC install technician Terrance Avery, were honking their horns and hitting the gas on their cars while they were next to the ex-NFL player on a nearby roadway. Both Reyes and Avery said Bryant followed them to their lunch spot’s location, got out of his vehicle and immediately started yelling. At one point, Bryant allegedly told Reyes, “You better not park that car and get out or I’ll stomp your face into this pavement.” “I was like, ‘OK, really?'” Reyes said of how he responded to Bryant. Reyes said he then got out of his car and went to put some items into his backseat, which ignited Bryant. “He thought that — he accused me of trying to get a gun,” Reyes said. “He thought I was going in my car to get a gun.” Bryant then allegedly went to the back of his own car. “He was reaching in the door,” Reyes said. “He was like come over here. He was like, ‘You over here threatening me? You threatening me?’ He was like, ‘You going to die today. I’ma shoot you. I’ma kill you. You’re not going to live to see another day.’ 6 Former Dallas Cowboys star Dez Bryant was handcuffed after an incident with teenagers. “He’s yelling that out loud.” Added Avery: “He didn’t flash a gun, but he sure acted like he had one.” Reyes said moments later, the altercation turned violent when he pulled out his phone to record Bryant “in case he tries to do anything.” 6 Noah Reyes, 19, said Dez Bryant punched him, threatened to kill him and scratched his phone on Sunday. 6 19-year-old Terrance Avery said Dez Bryant followed him and his friend, Noah Reyes, to a parking lot after they had honked their horns near the former NFL player. “As soon as I pull my phone out, whack,” Reyes said. “He smacks it straight out of my hand onto the ground. I kind of just stood there.” Bryant then allegedly picked up Reyes’ phone and spiked it into the ground. “My screen saver was shattered,” Reyes claimed. 6 Dallas Cowboys wide receiver Dez Bryant (88) scores a touchdown during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the New York Giants, Sunday, Dec. 10, 2017, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. Several individuals were temporarily detained as part of the investigation. No firearms were recovered at the scene.” Police investigated the situation, and ultimately issued Bryant a citation for Assault by Contact, a Class C misdemeanor, before he was released at the scene. 🚨OUTKICK EXCLUSIVE: A confrontation with alleged reckless drivers ends with Dez Bryant on the ground in handcuffs. Bryant was cited for assault following the incident. pic.twitter.com/DOpnR4WMLP — OutKick (@Outkick) October 26, 2026 Reyes said he’s now going to file a lawsuit against Bryant over the incident. “No questions asked,” he said. “He’s getting sued.” Reyes and Avery added they both would also like to see a public apology from Bryant. 6 Noah Reyes said Dez Bryant broke his screen protector during the incident in Southlake, Texas on Sunday. “He might be an ex-NFL superstar, but I’m still somebody to the community, you know?” Reyes said. “He’s ruining my reputation at the end of the day.” Bryant said during a sitdown with Outkick hours after the ordeal that the teens were the ones who were in the wrong, alleging that he was only acting in self-defense after one of them had threatened to shoot him. “I knocked the phone out of his hand,” said Bryant, who also accused the teenagers of cutting him off on the roadway. “And first thing he said was, I’m fitting to call the police. “I said, ‘Call them. You’re threatening me, so it’s all good. I have the right to protect myself.'” Bryant is due in court on Nov. 20 for a hearing on his citation. content: Metro Mamdani, pals use NYPD gym for late-night pickup basketball games By Craig McCarthy and David DeTurris Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:02 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Hizzoner has hoop dreams. Mayor Zohran Mamdani has been quietly playing pickup basketball with buddies at an NYPD gym in Queens, sources confirmed to The Post. The mayor has shot hoops a half-dozen times at the Det. Steven D. McDonald Police Academy in College Point since sometime in July, sources said. The mayor reportedly plays pickup ball in the training facility’s gym – which is located nearly 10 miles from Gracie Mansion – playing with several unidentified associates, according to the sources. Mayor Zohran Mamdani and friends have been using an NYPD gym in Queens for pickup basketball games. Stephen Yang for NY Post As first reported by Politico, Mamdani began balling at the gym not long after the Knicks historic championship win over the summer – and around the time he attended a July 16 ceremony that rechristened the academy after hero Det. Steven McDonald, sources said. Explore More Send Mamdani a message — vote ‘NO’ on all five New York City ballot proposals LA set to mirror NY with socialist supreme leader — but Dems have big problems for 2028 Haters hunt NYC’s Jews — and Kathy Hochul couldn’t care less The outlet reported that the mayor and his fellow ballplayers discreetly entered the facility through a loading dock around 10 p.m. or 11 p.m. Sources also told Politico that the mayor’s late night games reportedly “scrambled academy operations on several occasions” – a characterization The Post’s sources disputed. In a statement to The Post, Mamdani spokesperson Dora Pekec confirmed that Hizzoner has been “shooting hoops” at the facility, adding that staff were told playing ball wouldn’t disrupt training. “The Mayor would never want to interfere with recruit activities, and if his use of the facility were to cause any disruption, he would find a different place to shoot hoops,” Pekec said. The NYPD also confirmed Mamdani only used the gym during off hours and has not disrupted any recruit training. title: Luka Doncic and another Lakers star nominated for NBA Player of the Week
description: Luka Doncic, fresh off his 52-point performance on Sunday, was joined by a teammate to be nominated for their early-season excellence.
content: NBA Luka Doncic and another Lakers star nominated for NBA Player of the Week By Melissa Rohlin Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:00 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome and 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey have been named the NBA Western and Eastern Conference Players of the Week for the opening week of the season. The other nominees in the Western Conference included Lakers’ Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, as well as Timberwolves’ Anthony Edwards, Thunder’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Rockets’ Amen Thompson. Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers smiles while talking to the media during a game against the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Doncic is coming off a thrilling 52-point performance on Sunday afternoon against the Utah Jazz. Interestingly though, he did not play particularly well in the season’s first two games. Meanwhile, Reaves has looked incredibly steady to start the season. He is averaging 26.7 points, 6.3 assists, and is shooting a whopping 63% from the field over the Lakers’ first three games. In the Eastern Conference, the nominees included Pistons’ Cade Cunningham, Hawks’ Dyson Daniels and Jalen Johnson and Pacers’ Tyrese Haliburton and Pascal Siakam. Jerome, who’s in his second season with the Grizzlies, is leading the league in scoring with 34.7 points a game, ahead of Doncic who’s No. 2 with 34.3 points a game. Both Jerome and Doncic have led their respective teams to 3-0 starts. More From Melissa Rohlin No NBA GM voted for Luka Doncic for projected MVP? title: LA set to mirror NY with socialist supreme leader — but Dems have big problems for 2028
description: New Yorkers are already finding out what happens when the activists take power. Angelenos still have time to decide whether they want to find out as well.
content: Opinion LA set to mirror NY with socialist supreme leader — but Dems have big problems for 2028 By Jon Fleischman Published Oct. 26, 2026, 7:00 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source America’s largest city is run by Zohran Mamdani, a card-carrying member of the Democratic Socialists of America. Los Angeles, the second-largest metro, could follow: Fellow DSA member Nithya Raman seems poised to become its next mayor. A new California Post poll shows her leading Mayor Karen Bass. If Raman wins, DSA members will hold both mayors’ offices, forcing Democratic Party leaders to ask whether they still run their party, or whether they’re just chasing its socialist wing. Sign up for the California Morning Report newsletter The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now. Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story Check out more newsletters Mamdani and Raman aren’t political twins. Mamdani has charisma, social media savvy and a talent for political theater; Raman has considerably less star power. What they share is more useful: Opponents that voters can’t stand. Andrew Cuomo entered the final weeks of New York’s 2025 mayoral race with a 55% unfavorable rating in a Marist poll reported by the New York Post. In LA, a California Post-McLaughlin survey last week found 71.7% disapproved of Bass’ performance. Explore More Jay-Z to headline Super Bowl halftime show at SoFi Stadium Draymond Green doubles down on Luka Doncic never winning MVP award Nithya Raman campaign tries to slam ‘Poop Zone’ attack ads with ethics complaint, but group fires back Raman led the race 46.7% to 38.8%, even though 41% identified Raman as the more extreme candidate, compared with 16.4% for Bass. I’ve spent nearly four decades in California politics; I can’t remember an incumbent this weak in LA. Fed-up voters aren’t suddenly converting to socialism; they’re willing to gamble on someone further left because the people in charge have worn out their welcome. Socialists Zohran Mamdani and Nithya Raman aren’t political twins. Mamdani has charisma, social media savvy and a talent for political theater; Raman has considerably less star power. AP Photo/William Liang The DSA stands to benefit: its members are winning elections, taking office and — for once — holding the power to turn activist demands into government policy. These aren’t ceremonial jobs: New York’s mayor oversees a budget of more than $100 billion, the nation’s largest police department and the city’s public schools. The mayor of LA controls a budget of roughly $13 billion and appoints the commissions that run the LAPD, the port, the airport and the Department of Water and Power. That’s a lot of power to hand an organization with a written platform. Start with immigration: The DSA’s national program calls for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement, ending deportations and granting amnesty to illegal immigrants. On the domestic side, the agenda includes healthcare free at the point of service, free public college and cancellation of student debt. Then comes public ownership of major corporations and essential industries. That’s not a bigger welfare state: The DSA wants to replace capitalism itself. Republicans didn’t invent that claim — the DSA printed it. Raman doesn’t have to endorse every national DSA plank, but the LA chapter, which has endorsed her mayoral campaign, has its own radical demands, like ending ordinances making it illegal for homeless people to camp on the street. Mamdani needs Albany to advance his agenda; New York Gov. Kathy Hochul needs the party’s increasingly powerful left to help her win. Anadolu via Getty Images For years, Democratic leaders have welcomed the socialist left’s volunteers, money and enthusiasm while keeping its more radical proposals at arm’s length. That arrangement gets uncomfortable when the activists become mayors and start implementing policy. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has already felt the squeeze. Her lieutenant governor, Antonio Delgado, challenged her from the left with support from prominent DSA legislators. Hochul got Mamdani’s endorsement instead, and Delgado later dropped out after struggling to gain traction. Now Hochul and Mamdani are campaigning together, even as she resists the higher taxes the DSA wants. Mamdani needs Albany to advance his agenda; Hochul needs the party’s increasingly powerful left to help her win. The suburbs are another story: A Data for Progress survey found Mamdani was viewed favorably by 61% of New York City respondents but only 43% in the suburbs. That’s an 18-point drop once you cross the city line. Democrats running in competitive districts can’t afford to ignore that difference. California Democrats know the math. The state’s most competitive House seats are in Orange County, the Central Valley and the Inland Empire — not hipster-heavy Silver Lake. Republicans have spent the past decade fighting over the move from Reagan conservatism to Donald Trump’s national populism. That fight has been loud, public and bruising. Democrats’ version is just starting, and it may not stop at City Hall. Gov. Gavin Newsom has spent much of the past year cultivating a national profile and visiting early presidential primary states. Yet another California Post-McLaughlin survey found New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a DSA member, drawing 18% support in a hypothetical 2028 Democratic presidential primary among California respondents. Pete Buttigieg received 17%. Newsom only managed 14% — in his own state. New Yorkers are already finding out what happens when the activists take power. Angelenos still have time to decide whether they want to find out as well. Democrats in swing districts across both states will be living with that answer, and so will every Democrat who wants to run for president in 2028. The socialists stopped asking permission. Now they’re taking the party, one City Hall at a time. Jon Fleischman, a longtime strategist in California politics, writes at SoDoesItMatter.com. title: Rams coach Sean McVay reveals missing piece that showed out in decimation of Raiders
description: The Rams offense has not looked close to the same this season, but on Sunday, something missing finally returned.
content: NFL Rams coach Sean McVay reveals missing piece that showed out in decimation of Raiders By Vincent Bonsignore Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:57 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source When in doubt, line it up. Challenge your guys to be the more physical team. Then impose your will on the other guy. Somewhere along the way this season, Sean McVay and Rams had wandered from that identity. Too many possessions, too many stretches, too many games unfolded on someone else’s terms while losing four of their first six games. On Sunday, he and his team finally remembered who they were. And then they made the Raiders pay a dear price for it, running the football down their throat. 3 Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) runs the ball against Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses (35) during the second quarter of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images The Rams’ 35-21 victory wasn’t nearly as competitive as the final score suggested. They were tougher, more disciplined and better coached. They established the terms of engagement, then spent the afternoon making sure the Raiders abided by them. Thirty-nine carries for 198 yards will do that. So will two running backs, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, who each exceeded 90 yards rushing. They essentially turned the Rams run game into their own Las Vegas Grand Prix, accelerating through big holes and leaving defenders in the rear view mirror. When they weren’t playing bully ball and running through would-be tacklers, that is. More From Vincent Bonsignore 49ers fast start becomes a necessity as absurd storyline wreaks havoc Raiders’ season is slipping away — it’s time to see what Fernando Mendoza can do Raiders’ LA rejection turned into a Vegas jackpot As for all that running room? Thank the Rams offensive line, which spent the afternoon shoving people around and turning narrow lanes into open roads. As McVay acknowledged Monday, that identity had been missing through their first six games, too often leaving the Rams staring into a mirror and struggling to recognize the team staring back. Williams and Corum helped bring that picture back into focus, accepting the challenge to set a physical tone and giving the Rams a standard they now have to sustain. “Those guys did a great job. They were both awesome. They deserved well-earned credit as were the blockers,” McVay said of Corum and Williams. “When you do that, you’re not in a bad spot on 2nd and 3rd downs.” Then came the revealing part. 3 Blake Corum (24) of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled by Treydan Stukes (31) of the Las Vegas Raiders during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images “That’s the first time we’ve had that all season,” McVay said. For an offense with Matthew Stafford pulling the strings, the temptation is always to focus on what happens through the air. But the Rams are at their most dangerous when the defense has to respect everything. Sunday, the running game made that respect mandatory. Corum and Williams pressed the line of scrimmage, recognized defenders overplaying their assignments and found openings. Their blockers supplied the room and the attitude. “I thought our offensive line was excellent,” McVay said. “They had a great demeanor.” That demeanor became the afternoon’s defining characteristic. The Rams weren’t merely calling running plays. They were committing to a physical standard, one that spread throughout the team. 3 Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay reacts against the Las Vegas Raiders during the third quarter of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images Funny how that works. Start throwing your weight around on offense, and the other side joins the party. The payoff extended beyond rushing yards. Manageable downs gave Stafford options and kept the Raiders guessing. “Any good offense that we’ve had here that I’ve been a part of, you have to be able to do both,” McVay said. “You have to be able to have balance, or you at least have to have the threat of if they overcommit to something, then you have to be able to make them pay.” One afternoon doesn’t establish permanence. The Rams still have to prove this version travels from week to week. “It’s something that we have to build on because this is a long journey,” McVay said. At least now they have something to hang their hat on. Filed under Los Angeles Rams 10/26/26 Read Next J.J. McCarthy's resurgence took root long before joining G... title: We deserve answers on UFO sightings from the government — if the truth is really out there
description: Are we alone? Not alone? Are Buck Rogers types schlepping around the North Star? Outer space stuff littering our front lawns? We already got pilots spotting weird things whizzing past cockpits.
content: Cindy Adams Opinion We deserve answers on UFO sightings from the government — if the truth is really out there By Cindy Adams Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:57 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source An artist's interpretation of a triangular UFO that was spotted over a military base. US DOW / SWNS Orbiting the truth in Washington Are we alone? Not alone? Are Buck Rogers types schlepping around the North Star? Outer space stuff littering our front lawns? We already got pilots spotting weird things whizzing past cockpits. So, is there a Macy’s International? Outer space Gristedes? Neiman’s Nebula? OK, protect our security — but a coalition’s now requesting info. Why won’t Washington let the public hear it? What did our government know — and when did they know it? Washington is consumed by controlling the next Congress. Should America hide a truth of potentially historic consequence? Tell about the black hole, gravity, asteroids, dark matter, the Big Bang, suns, moons, dwarf planets, Jupiter, Saturn, comets, stars. Humanity deserves to see if we are not alone. Should extraordinary claims not withstand scrutiny, we should know that, too. If another country releases evidence first, Washington should explain why Americans may learn about it from some crappy sunken island! title: UCLA’s football buzz isn’t reaching the student section — Bob Chesney has a plan to fix it
description: The final frontier for UCLA’s undefeated football team might be getting more assertive – in connecting with classmates. With attendance at the Rose Bowl lagging even as the No. 7...
content: College Football UCLA’s football buzz isn’t reaching the student section — Bob Chesney has a plan to fix it By Ben Bolch Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:57 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source The final frontier for UCLA’s undefeated football team might be getting more assertive – in connecting with classmates. With attendance at the Rose Bowl lagging even as the No. 7 Bruins have emerged as the best story in college football, coach Bob Chesney said his players must help build buzz around this team. “You know,” Chesney said Monday, “we’ve probably got to just get a little bit more involved in making sure our guys in classes are talking about this with everybody and making sure they can connect a story and a face to this team, not just what this team is but ultimately the people on it.” 3 Members of the UCLA team celebrate after defeating Michigan State in an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Pasadena, Calif. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Student turnout appeared to dip noticeably last weekend for the game against Michigan State as part of the crowd of 33,757 – a figure that fell a little more than 2,000 from the previous week. “I think the student section was slow to get in there and then it felt like they left a little bit early,” Chesney said, referring to a halftime exodus, “and I think that they’ve got to do a better job too – we’ve all got to do a better job.” Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance UCLA’s average home attendance of 33,172 ranks second to last in the Big Ten, topping only Northwestern’s 29,261 since the Wildcats moved into new Ryan Field. However, it’s important to note that the Bruins changed their attendance policy this season to reflect actual people inside the stadium instead of announcing tickets sold or using other calculations that inflate the number. While the athletic department has helped by offering free student tickets and cheap bus rides to the Rose Bowl, there remains work to be done in getting the word out about the hottest team on campus. That could be a challenge for quiet players like running back Jaivian Thomas. “I’m not really a guy that talks a lot outside of football,” Thomas said, “so I haven’t really interacted with my classmates about any of this, to be honest.” 3 Head coach Bob Chesney of the UCLA Bruins leaves the field after defeating the Michigan State Spartans at the Rose Bowl Stadium on Oct. 24, 2026, in Pasadena, California. Getty Images But sometimes wearing football gear around campus is enough. Linebacker Sammy Omosigho said he got noticed while walking to practice at 6 a.m. “This guy comes while I’m walking to practice and he’s like, ‘You play football here?’ ” Omosigho said. “I was like, ‘Yeah.’ He was like, ‘Man, you’re doing a good job,’ and, like, six months ago that wasn’t the same feeling we’re having at school.” Curiously, not all of the buzz has been positive surrounding the only remaining unbeaten team in the Big Ten or SEC. 3 Ty Dieffenbach of the UCLA Bruins throws a pass in the first half against the Michigan State Spartans at the Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena, California, Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. Getty Images After UCLA pulled away from Michigan State on Saturday, CBS sports analyst Bryant McFadden compared the Bruins to “a rapper who raps with no substance in his lyrics.” Chesney unleashed a hearty chuckle when informed of McFadden’s appraisal. “I don’t even want to dig into that much in my mind,” Chesney said. “I’m not overly worried what anybody else says – it really can’t help us and it really can’t hurt us if we don’t let it. It’s irrelevant, what people have to say.” Sign up for the California Morning Report newsletter The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now. Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story Check out more newsletters Chesney has long told his players not to listen to outside praise because it will invariably be followed by criticism when things go bad for the team. The approach seems to be working given Thomas’ response when asked if he knew where the Bruins were ranked. “Uh, I don’t think so,” he said with a laugh. “I don’t really look into that either – it just is what it is, you know?” Ultimately, the Bruins might be best served by repeating the formula that’s worked deep into October. “Just avoid the good, avoid the bad, focus on the work that you’ve got to do,” Chesney said, “and at some point we’ll look back at the end of the year, see where we land and maybe take a time to enjoy that and tell some stories about it and reflect on it, but now is not the time; now is the time for us to just keep going with our work and not worry about what anybody on the outside thinks.” Filed under california los angeles michigan state spartans rose bowl ucla bruins 10/26/26 Read Next The Post's college football rankings: All eyes on Ohio Sta... title: Jewish rights group calls on Trump admin to probe NYC schools as parents pull kids out of classrooms
description: The National Jewish Advocacy Center filed a request with the Department of Justice Monday, citing evidence outlined in Post stories beginning in the aftermath of the Oct. 7, 2023 terror attacks on Israel.
content: Metro Jewish rights group calls on Trump admin to probe NYC schools as parents pull kids out of classrooms By Carl Campanile Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:52 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source A national Jewish legal rights group is calling on the Trump administration to probe the city Department of Education over reports parents are pulling their kids out of public schools because of rampant antisemitism. The National Jewish Advocacy Center filed a request with the Department of Justice Monday, citing evidence outlined in Post stories beginning in the aftermath of the Oct. 7, 2023 terror attacks on Israel. Enrollment at Jewish schools or yeshivas has increased while the student population in public schools has declined in recent years, said the letter sent to Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who heads the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. 4 PS 77 in Park Slope is pictured. Gregory P. Mango for NY Post “Parents of Jewish children who attend, or were driven from, the Board’s [NYC Board of Education/Department of Education] schools, and Jewish employees of the Board, are prepared to be interviewed,” said the complaint, addressed to Assistant AG Harmeet Dhillon, who heads the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. There are two pending federal probes regarding the Big Apple’s public school system. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed In April, the Trump administration’s Education Department launched a civil rights probe into the city DOE concerning a pro-Palestinian group of educators, NYC Educators for Palestine, for organizing a series of Israel-bashing lessons “focused on ‘Palestine, Zionism, and Resistance.'” “No child should be taught by his or her teachers to hate their peers,” said US Department of Education Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kimberly Richey at the time. Another federal civil rights “shared ancestry” investigation into the DOE was initiated in November 2023. 4 PS 77 Park Sple teacher Damien Neva posted “Long live Yahya al-Sinwar” in a Signal chat back in 2024. Diana/BFAnyc.com 4 Neva was featured on a Post cover earlier in October. The letter calling for another probe cited a report by United Jewish Teachers, a group of Jewish educators employed by NYC Public Schools, in August claiming at least 250 antisemitic and anti-Israel incidents in the schools since Oct. 7, 2023, It also pointed to recent cases, citing Brooklyn PS 77 Park Slope teacher Damien Neva, who brazenly posted in a 2024 Signal group chat, “Long live Yahya al-Sinwar,” according to a new legal filing against the Park Slope Co-Op. Al-Sinwar is the Hamas leader who orchestrated the 10/7 massacre. Meanwhile, George Trim, a social studies teacher at IS 181 in Bath Beach, Brooklyn, was disciplined for allegedly telling students that World Trade Center owner Larry Silverstein knew the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks were coming and did nothing to stop them. The letter noted that enrollment in Jewish day schools and yeshivas in New York State rose by 3,115 students in the 2025-26 school year, and in the city alone by 1,587, while nonpublic enrollment fell. 4 The National Jewish Advocacy Center has asked the Trump admin to probe the city’s Department of Education. National Jewish Advocacy Center Mark Goldfederr, CEO of the National Jewish Advocacy Center, said the Justice Department’s power is needed to clamp down on Jew hatred. A spokesperson for the Justice Department said, “The Department takes allegations of antisemitism seriously and is committed to enforcing federal civil rights laws that protect students from discrimination.” A city DOE spokesperson responded, “Every student is welcome at New York City Public Schools, regardless of background, identity, or religion. We have a zero-tolerance policy for hate of any kind, including antisemitism, and we investigate and respond to all reported incidents in accordance with our Chancellor’s Regulations and applicable laws.” The department does not track the religious beliefs of its students. title: Haters hunt NYC’s Jews — and Kathy Hochul couldn’t care less
description: Jewish families in NYC can't sit in a neighbor's house and talk about real estate without being hunted — and Gov. Kathy Hochul doesn't seem to care.
content: Opinion Haters hunt NYC’s Jews — and Kathy Hochul couldn’t care less By Jeffrey Lax Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:39 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Gov. Kathy Hochul speaks during a rally at New York's Medgar Evers College on Oct. 25, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Last week a notorious group of pro-Palestine activists set its sights on Riverdale in The Bronx, as it publicized plans to march on a Saturday-night meeting for Jewish families considering buying a home in Israel. The group, Pal-Awda, didn’t post an address for its action, and it didn’t need to; its people have gotten very good at finding Jews. The incident brought home two chilling facts: Jewish families in NYC can’t sit in a neighbor’s house and talk about real estate without being hunted — and Gov. Kathy Hochul doesn’t seem to care. Pal-Awda is the same group that massed a crowd outside Park East Synagogue last November to chant “globalize the intifada” and urge the “resistance” to “take another settler out.” Ever since, it’s waged a campaign of targeted harassment against Jews who want to learn about making a move to Israel. It’s effective: Late Friday, Pal-Awda claimed “Victory!” in a post on X, bragging that the Riverdale session had been cancelled due to its scare tactics. Explore More Jewish rights group calls on Trump admin to probe NYC schools as parents pull kids out of classrooms Abdul El-Sayed ad is vile, unapologetically Nazi drivel blaming Jews for everything bad American Jews who fled to Israel over rising antisemitism could prove decisive for Netanyahu’s future “We will keep shutting down these events and making them untenable in the City,” the group vowed Organizers of the real-estate event confirmed to me that the session was first set for a private home, and that the threats had indeed spurred them to cancel the in-person gathering and move it to Zoom instead. Earlier in the week, a group of Bronx Democrats including Rep. Ritchie Torres, Assemblyman Jeffrey Dinowitz and Borough President Vanessa Gibson had jointly denounced Pal-Awda for its plans. “Organizing a campaign to hunt down these gatherings and drive them out of our neighborhoods is an attack on Jewish New Yorkers,” they declared. They were right. Yet Hochul continued doing what she does best: ignoring threats to Jews and their communities. Last week she made a campaign swing through Riverdale for coffee with Dinowitz and Gibson — and on Saturday night, while Pal-Awda gloated, she tweeted about that friendly outing without a word about the targeting of Bronx Jews. Not even an election campaign can rouse her interest, it seems. Riverdale was Pal-Awda’s second “victory” this month, after it pushed a Nefesh B’Nefesh aliyah fair out of Queens hours before it was to open on Oct. 11. Funny how a fight over “stolen land” keeps landing outside synagogues, and now outside Jewish homes. The real-estate talk is thin cover for the true motive: antisemitic hate. New York law protects Jews wherever they gather. Synagogues and public venues are covered by laws that guarantee access to houses of worship and bar places open to the public from turning people away over religion or ancestry. A gathering in a private home falls under laws aimed squarely at anyone who threatens or intimidates Jews for who they are. The local law against discriminatory harassment lets the city go to court to stop such incidents, with fines of up to $100,000 for each threat of force; the state’s civil-rights law lets victims sue anyone who carries out or incites that kind of harassment, and menacing or coercion aimed at Jews is a hate crime. And yes, Zionist Jews are a protected group. Get opinions and commentary from our columnists Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter! Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story. Check out more newsletters A Riverdale family looking at apartments in Israel is acting on an ancestral, cultural and often religious bond with that land and its people, and the law protects that bond. What’s left unprotected is political support for the state of Israel — and nobody talking with neighbors about mortgages in Jerusalem is there to lobby for political action. Mayor Mamdani’s rhetoric has invited all of this: Pal-Awda is jumping on his dog whistles. Its Friday post tagged the mayor and told him he “can take tangible steps to put an end to this illegal activity once and for all” — meaning Jewish real-estate gatherings. The mayor has made no public comment about Pal-Awda’s bullying this month in Riverdale and Queens. His silence tells every Jewish family in the city that it’s on its own. These shameful threats hit home for me: One of Pal-Awda’s staunchest allies is CUNY for Palestine, a group of anti-Israel faculty and staff at my own workplace. Yet again, both Mamdani and Hochul have failed: by refusing to tell Pal-Awda that no synagogue, school or institution in this city will pay a price for welcoming Jews, and now by refusing to protect Jewish New Yorkers in their own homes. Pal-Awda and its cheerleaders on CUNY’s faculty think Jewish neighborhoods, and now Jewish living rooms, are fair game. And why not? Our governor and our mayor couldn’t care less. Jeffrey Lax is a CUNY professor of law and co-founder of Students and Faculty for Equality at CUNY. title: Disabled girl, 7, gravely injured during Oregon school shooting moved out of ICU — as nearly $1.1M in donations pour in
description: "Above all, please keep Saylor in your thoughts and prayers as she heals. We are beyond grateful that she is still here with us," Saylor Graham-Poarch's family said in a statement.
content: US News Disabled girl, 7, gravely injured during Oregon school shooting moved out of ICU — as nearly $1.1M in donations pour in By Zoe Hussain Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:38 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source A 7-year-old girl who was shot in the face by madman Griffin J. John II during his Oregon elementary school rampage has been moved out of the intensive care unit — as her family deals with the “hardest time of our lives.” Saylor Graham-Poarch, who is disabled and often used a wheelchair, was left in critical condition after John, 16, heinously opened fire — killing four — inside a special needs classroom at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend on Oct. 15. 3 Saylor Graham-Poarch, 7, has been moved out of the ICU after she was critically wounded in a mass shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School. GoFundMe Graham-Poarch is now stable and has been moved out of the ICU — though she has a long recovery still ahead of her, her family told KPTV. “Even as we’re grateful for Saylor’s progress, our hearts are broken for the families of the three children and the teacher who were killed. We are holding them close, and we grieve with them,” the family said in a statement. “Thank you to everyone who has reached out, prayed for Saylor, sent messages, and shown our family so much love during the hardest time of our lives. We can’t respond to everyone individually, but please know that every kind word, prayer, and act of support means more to us than we can say,” the statement continued. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed “Above all, please keep Saylor in your thoughts and prayers as she heals. We are beyond grateful that she is still here with us,” her family added. Two separate fundraisers to help Graham-Poarch’s family with medical expenses, lodging and other financial burdens neared $1.1 million as of Monday night. 3 Fundraisers to help Graham-Poarch’s family neared $1.1 million as of Monday night. South Oregon Sparrows Club The little fighter was already well known in the community for her bubbly personality and pink glasses, and the high school adopted her as a “Sparrow”— a term affiliated with a nonprofit where teenagers help raise money to fund a child’s medical expenses. “Saylor is the definition of light and joy. And one of those kids that, you know, when she’s in the room. You can’t think of anything else other than what Saylor’s doing; ‘I need to get to know her,’” Matt Sampson, Sparrow Clubs USA executive director, previously told the Central Oregon Daily. “She’s just very inspirational, very joyful, very courageous, and inspirational.” Saylor, who was also nonverbal, was adopted by Bend Senior High School as part of the nationwide program in the 2024-25 academic year. Although she frequently used a wheelchair, she was able to walk on her own, according to a 2024 announcement. The “sweet, happy, adorable, and resilient” girl battles CASK, a gene mutation that impacts her physical and cognitive development, as well as dysphagia, a disorder that makes it difficult for her to swallow food and drink, the announcement said. 3 Flowers and candles are seen at a makeshift memorial outside Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, a day after a deadly shooting. AP Photo/Joe Kline Griffin used his mom’s shotgun to blast through the door at Silver Rail before unleashing carnage inside, targeting his former special education classroom just before 1 p.m. on Oct. 15, police said. Three students — Rhoam Summer, 5, and two other unidentified students, ages 8 and 11 — were tragically killed in the gunfire, as well as teacher and beloved volleyball coach, Megan Lambert, 25. Teacher Becky Drury was also hospitalized after her hand was “almost completely severed” by gunfire. She has since undergone surgery on her left arm and right hand. Heroic dad Kaylub Giamanco, whose two daughters attend the elementary school, rushed into the school and fatally shot John to stop the massacre. Silver Rail remains closed indefinitely. title: College profs go gloriously old school to fight disturbing new trend sweeping schools
description: It’s true: Just because AI can do the work for you, doesn’t mean it should.
content: Opinion College profs go gloriously old school to fight disturbing new trend sweeping schools By CA Post Editorial Board Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:36 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Today, in a full-circle moment, cutting-edge technology has restored the need for pencil and paper — a welcome plot twist. UC Berkeley professor Richard Borcherds, a prominent mathematician, recently told the California Post that he now bases course grades primarily on in-person exams: no devices permitted. “Online exams are now a waste of time as several students just use AI to answer the questions,” the math professor said. “I notice the average score increases a lot in online exams.” Sign up for the California Morning Report newsletter The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now. Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story Check out more newsletters That certainly adds up: As AI has grown more prevalent and students (and others) have learned how to use it, it’s become easy, and tempting, to outsource the hard work of thinking. That temptation can be especially strong in college, where students feel the pressure to compete with others who embrace AI along with the pressure to earn high grades. So it’s good to see professors like Borcherds, who won the Fields Medal in 1998, install guardrails to help ensure genuine classroom learning. UC Berkeley mathematics professor Richard Borcherds has made headlines for grading primarily off of in-person examinations. Instagram/@quantumaths All humans benefit from taking the time to learn the material, rather than plugging variables into a computer and then regurgitating the answer in a report or on a test. Getty Images Students still benefit from working out math (and other) problems on their own. That’s how they acquire real-world skills, learn to actually derive the correct answers and develop the critical-thinking skills that are transferable to virtually all aspects of life. What if at some point AI’s not around to spit out an answer? Or what if the answer’s amiss and a deadline looms? Students — and all people — should be able to think on their own. To that end, there’s no substitute for studying. In fact, all humans benefit from taking the time to learn the material, rather than plugging variables into a computer and then regurgitating the answer in a report or on a test. Grasping the value of the learning process, even in a world of AI, is itself a worthy lesson. Yes, there’s a role for AI in life, work, play and even school, and it’s amazing to see the technology noodle, with some success already, some longstanding puzzles in math, science and medicine. But as a society, we must ensure that the rise of AI does not mean the decline of the human brain. Toward that end, universities — whose traditional mission is teaching students how (not what) to think — have a key role to play. So bravo to Professor Borcherds and others like him, for innovating, or improvising, by going back to old school. It’s true: Just because AI can do the work for you, doesn’t mean it should. title: 3-year-old ‘traumatized’ after police called after he was playing soccer ‘too good’
description: A pint-sized soccer phenom was “traumatized” over an incident that resulted in police being called over a strange youth soccer league dispute.
content: Soccer 3-year-old ‘traumatized’ after police called after he was playing soccer ‘too good’ By Christian Arnold Published Oct. 26, 2026, 6:36 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source A pint-sized soccer phenom was “traumatized” over an incident at a park in Winter Park, Florida, that resulted in police being called over a strange youth soccer league dispute. The now-viral video showed 3-year-old Nevada scoring multiple goals in an i9 Sports youth soccer game before it cut to his parents talking to police after the authorities were called to his game on Saturday morning by league director Thomas Hayes, who alleged in a 911 call that “there is a parent here that’s really, really disruptive.” In the video, the boy’s father, Don, could be heard saying that the police had been called because his son was “too good.” I spoke to the mom of the 3-year-old soccer star who was left "thinking he did something wrong" after a league official called police "due to a disturbance between parents" The youth sports league said they launched a review and reached out to the family https://t.co/idsWyGyTU6 pic.twitter.com/oZoaE0Qfe1 — philip lewis (@Phil_Lewis_) October 26, 2026 And in an interview with HuffPost, Nevada’s mother, Martasia, said the whole incident has “really traumatized” him. “He still wants to play soccer. He just doesn’t want to go back to that place. I don’t think that’s how he should be thinking, that as a 3-year-old he did something wrong,” she said. Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance Martasia claimed that Nevada had been targeted all season in a league in which he plays against 5-year-olds, and when the game on Saturday started, she said that she saw other parents, the director and some coaches circle up, “trying to figure out how to let us know that he can’t play so the other kids could play.” In a devastating turn, Nevada is scared that he created the drama, his mother said. Chaos breaks out at a youth soccer game after parents of opposing players complained that their children could not get the ball away from a dominant 3-year-old player, in Winter Park, Florida, on Oct. 25, 2026. TikTok/@nevadaney10 “It’s heartbreaking because now Nevada’s saying he doesn’t wanna go over there. He’s scared that he did something wrong,” Martasia said. The whole situation started when Martasia said that she had gone over to the huddled-up coaches, league director and parents to stand up for her son. She claimed that once she started defending Nevada, “they just called the police.” However, 911 audio obtained by The Post revealed that Hayes claimed that there was a parent “following me around, calling me names in front of the whole bunch of people that are here. I want to be done.” Police respond to a Florida youth soccer game after chaos breaks out over a dominant player, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Winter Park, Florida. TikTok/@nevadaney10 Two officers from the Winter Park Police Department arrived at the scene at 10 a.m. and a police report stated that the incident was a “civil matter” and not “criminal” in a news release. No arrests were made and no one was trespassed, according to police. The league has refunded Nevada’s family, Martasia told HuffPost.
