content: Politics Ex-FBI Director James Comey facing new criminal charges for allegedly leaking info to NY Times By Victor Nava Published Oct. 26, 2026 Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 6:39 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Former FBI Director James Comey was slapped with a fresh set of criminal charges Monday for allegedly leaking sensitive national defense information to the New York Times. The two counts against Comey mark the third time the Department of Justice has gone after the ex-lawman and Trump administration critic since the start of President Trump’s second term. Prosecutors accuse Comey of “knowingly and wittingly” transmitting national defense information as well as conspiring to do so in a “criminal information” filing made in the US District Court for the District of Columbia. Former FBI Director James Comey is facing federal charges for the third time in President Trump’s second term. AP The alleged crime took place on Oct. 4-5, 2016. Comey “through one and more co-conspirators directed Individual #1 to disclose national defense information to a reporter for a national news publication” in violation of federal law, according to prosecutors. Explore More Maurene Comey, daughter of ex-FBI director, unlawfully fired as federal prosecutor by Trump DOJ, judge rules Newly released documents open a path to the true origins of the Russia hoax FBI opened probe into whether Trump was Russian agent after he fired James Comey, newly revealed memos show The new charges stem from an Oct. 5, 2016, article in the New York Times, headlined “Yahoo Said to Have Aided U.S. Email Surveillance by Adapting Spam Filter,” written by reporter Charlie Savage. “The United States’ investigation has uncovered evidence that former FBI Director, James B. Comey, sought to correct misinformation which had appeared in the press by way of Reuters the day before,” Special Assistant US Attorney Dustin Farahnak wrote in a filing, according to NBC News. “The investigation has uncovered evidence that Mr. Comey directed staff to speak to Mr. Savage about specific accuracy concerns related to the Reuters article, and thereby illegally transferred classified information.” Comey claimed in a Substack video that he is innocent. James Comey / Instagram The alleged disclosure took place while Comey was head of the FBI under former President Barack Obama. He would be fired by Trump in May 2017. “Well, they’re back, again,” Comey said in a video posted on his Substack. “It would almost be funny if it wasn’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice, one that we cannot become numb to.” “Nothing’s changed with me,” the former FBI chief added. “I’m still innocent, and I’m still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent judiciary.” The case was filed under seal by the DOJ on Oct. 5 and made public after Comey’s lawyers filed a motion to unseal it. Comey’s attorneys have also asked the court to dismiss the case. A Justice Department spokesperson told The Post that the DOJ “filed a waiverless criminal information to toll the statute of limitations as it relates to allegations concerning former FBI Director Comey.” “Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals,” the spokesperson continued. “This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further.” The new charges against Comey surfaced on the same day a US district judge ruled that the former FBI director’s daughter, Maurene Comey, was illegally fired from the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York last year. The judge ordered the Trump administration to reinstate Maurene Comey and provide her with back pay. James Comey was indicted by a federal grand jury last September on charges of making false statements and obstruction of justice. The case was dismissed after a judge ruled Lindsey Halligan, then US attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, was unlawfully appointed. The former FBI director was indicted again in April on charges of threatening to kill Trump in May 2025 when he posted a photograph on Instagram of seashells arranged to read “8647.” Comey is still awaiting trial in the seashell case. title: Dictionary.com’s Word of the Year is one of the most viral — and controversial — terms to date
description: The Word of the Year already has people’s patience maxed out.
content: Lifestyle Dictionary.com’s Word of the Year is one of the most viral — and controversial — terms to date By Allison Lax Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:45 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Dictionary.com just dropped its Word of the Year — and it’s already maxing out people’s patience. In line with the growing social media trend toward seemingly never-ending self-optimization, the site has declared “maxxing” — meaning “maximizing” or “increasing” — as the top word of 2026. According to Dictionary.com’s research, “maxxing” was used almost 19 times more in 2026 than in 2025, with “looks-maxxing” showing up over 900% more often this year. In other words: People have been maxxing their use of the term “maxxing.” (Sorry.) “Maxxing” is Dictionary.com’s 2026 Word of the Year. AntonioDiaz – stock.adobe.com Explore More New ‘prestige porn’ makes sex the ultimate luxury — and hot older women the main characters My friend is reselling the expensive birthday gifts I give her son Paper straws worse for the environment than plastic ones: study The phrase can stand alone, or be used as a modifier for fitness and wellness activities. Among the most popular are looksmaxxing (optimizing appearance), fibermaxxing (getting the most possible fiber in one’s diet), proteinmaxxing and even productivity-maxxing. “In a year dominated by discussions of technology’s role in society, it’s only natural that we selected a word that was forged online,” the site’s announcement of the 2026 Word of the Year reads. But of all the ways to max, “looksmaxxing” has gotten the maximum exposure online. The term for ultimate appearance optimization, “looksmaxxing” began on shadowy message boards in the involuntarily celibate (or “incel”) community in the mid-2010s. It skyrocketed to mainstream status as TikTok creators began using it in the early 2020s, with disgraced livestreamer Braden Peters, a.k.a. Clavicular, leading the charge. Influencer Clavicular, also known as Braden Peters, led the looks-maxxing charge before recently pleading “not guilty” to felony sexual assault charges. Instagram/@clavicular0 Today, looksmaxxing is a mainstream slang term applied to everything from intense workouts to deep conditioners at the salon. On Instagram, a quick search of the hashtag reveals a staggering 523K posts. But when Dictionary.com announced their choice on social media, they were met with a maximum amount of digital groans. “I understand why, but I still hate this for us as a society lol,” said one fed-up commenter. “We are living in the worst timeline,” added another. Some reactions, however, were more positive. “Such a spot-on word for 2026! I’m definitely knowledge-maxxing by reading more every day,” said one cheery word-lover. Other contenders for Dictionary.com’s Word of 2026: “Affordability” (a hot topic these days, the wordsmiths point out); “data center” (AI panic, anyone?), “odyssey” (as in the Matt Damon movie) and “unc” — another internet slang term, short for “uncool” or “out of touch.” Say what you will about looksmaxxing, but at least it’s a word with actual letters. Last year’s Dictionary.com pick was “67,” the viral Gen Z and Gen Alpha term that serves as a catch-all phrase for middle school students — and, more importantly, works overtime to drive their Baby Boomer and Gen X teachers crazy. title: Ilhan Omar hurls the ‘genocide’ charge at Israel — but it belongs much closer to home
description: Nur Said's family escaped Somalia as “refugees” after Barre’s dictatorship collapsed, wining asylum in the US — improperly, it seems, as war criminals aren't entitled to refugee protections.
content: Opinion editorial Ilhan Omar hurls the ‘genocide’ charge at Israel — but it belongs much closer to home By Post Editorial Board Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:45 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Rep. Ilhan Omar speaks during a news conference on Jan. 28, 2026, in Minneapolis, Minn. James Keivom for NY Post Rep. Ilhan Omar’s apparent lies about her family and finances are bad enough, but nothing is as outrageous as the way she slanders Israel with the “genocide” libel when her own father in all likelihood took part in Somali dictator Siad Barre’s real genocide. Omar in her memoir calls her father Nur Omar Mohamed an “educator,” yet it looks like the only educating he did was teaching Barre’s enemies lessons in brutality as a colonel in the Somali Army in the 1980s. The Barre regime committed horrific atrocities against the Isaaq clan, killing at least 200,000 and displacing another 900,000 in a massive ethnic cleansing. The United Nations, Human Rights Watch, the International Crisis Group and virtually every other authority agrees that the campaign against the Isaaq was genocidal in intent and in practice: Government forces strafed fleeing civilians, planted land mines at wells and systematically raped girls and women. There can be little doubt that Omar’s dad was involved in the genocide. As historian and Oxford University doctoral researcher Mohamed Haji Ingiriis told The Post, “Nur Said was a military officer who was loyal to the regime until the end. He was part and parcel of those who caused and created the mayhem they ‘fled’ to live comfortably in the United States.” Nur Said and his family escaped Somalia as “refugees” following the collapse of Barre’s dictatorship, gaining asylum in the United States in 1995 — improperly, it seems, as war criminals are not entitled to refugee protections. More From Post Editorial Board Europe’s leaders still refuse to face the far-left’s assault on civilization Fast Takes: Ilhan Omar’s dad’s dubious past, Trump’s sensible appeal and more New York voters need more genuine general-election choices — or democracy is doomed Omar has long been blatantly antisemitic, with comments like “Israel has hypnotized the world” and saying Jews bought control of US policy because “It’s all about the Benjamins, baby.” Get opinions and commentary from our columnists Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter! Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story. Check out more newsletters But with her own family’s bloody history, it takes real chutzpah to join in the “genocide” slurs, e.g. by insisting Jewish students at Columbia University are “pro-genocide” and routinely condemning Israel’s supposed “genocidal” campaign against Palestinians. Omar’s scandals include messy finances and a possibly fraudulent marriage as well as serious questions about the legitimacy of her citizenship, but this hypocrisy takes the cake. America doesn’t believe in blood guilt, and we can’t blame Omar for her father’s history. But there’s something truly despicable about her rush to (falsely) accuse Israel of a crime against humanity when her own family looks to be knee-deep in a genuine genocide. title: Rays need to redisover what got them to the World Series — quickly
description: If they don’t revert to their usual form, the opportunistic Brewers will end things soon.
content: Jon Heyman Rays need to rediscover what got them to the World Series — quickly By Jon Heyman Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:43 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson (14) cannot catch a fly ball hit by Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — After winning the American League thanks to their defense, their baserunning, their perennially superb manager Kevin Cash and as mistake-free a game as you’ll find, the real Rays better return in World Series Game 3 on Monday at home in their dastardly dome. If they don’t revert to their usual form, the opportunistic Brewers will end things soon. The Rays reentered The Trop with a 2-0 deficit in games but did have the tying run on third in both defeats. So they might easily be up two-zip if they played to their norm. Better news: The Rays were an MLB-best 55-26 at home (tied with the Brewers). They have to hope their baseball-white roof will throw off the more buttoned-up Brewers here. The Rays also may need to better grasp the sense of urgency. They’ve lost two games by a run and somehow used struggling converted starter Steven Matz (5.49 regular season ERA) twice and nearly unhittable closer Bryan Baker no times. title: No NBA GM voted for Luka Doncic for projected MVP? You’ve got to be joking
description: Luka Dončić has a problem. He told us about it. But we didn’t listen. Remember when he was in the midst of one of the most remarkable stretches we witnessed....
content: Melissa Rohlin NBA No NBA GM voted for Luka Doncic for projected MVP? You’ve got to be joking By Melissa Rohlin Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:34 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source Luka Dončić has a problem. He told us about it. But we didn’t listen. Remember when he was in the midst of one of the most remarkable stretches we witnessed from any player last season? You know, when he averaged 37.5 points, eight rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.3 steals in March, leading the Lakers to a 15-2 record, yet he somehow fell in NBA.com’s MVP rankings at that time? 4 Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a 3-point basket during a game against the Utah Jazz at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “The better I play, the more I go down in rankings,” Doncic said last March. “So, I don’t know what more I can do.” Everyone turned their cheek. Why? Maybe people are inured to his greatness. Maybe all of his complaining to officials reduced that comment to white noise, even though it was his first and only time opening up about feeling snubbed last season. Maybe he doesn’t advocate for himself enough. Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance Doncic’s point was stunningly driven home again. Despite leading the league in scoring last season (33.5 points) and finishing third in assists (8.3), none of the NBA’s general managers believe Dončić will win MVP this season. In their preseason poll released October 15, Victor Wembanyama received 77% of the vote for projected MVP, followed by Nikola Jokic (10%) and Anthony Edwards (7%). Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jayson Tatum also received votes. Doncic? Zero. Nil. Nada. What were the league’s general managers thinking? Why is he being overlooked? What’s going on here? Those questions have been thrust to the forefront of our minds after Doncic finished with 52 points on 56.7% shooting, eight rebounds and 10 assists on Sunday, helping the Lakers storm back from an 18-point deficit to beat the Jazz, 132-123. 4 Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a free throw during a game against the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It was a masterpiece. Since the Mavericks traded Doncic to the Lakers in February 2025, he has had more 40-point performances (19) than LeBron James (18), who spent eight seasons in Los Angeles. It was Doncic’s 10th 50-point performance of his career. Since he was drafted by the Mavericks as the third overall pick in 2018, only James Harden (16) and Damian Lillard (11) have had more 50-point perforances than Doncic. It was the first time this season that anyone has scored 50 points. Doncic is a once-in-a-generation player. Why isn’t he getting more consideration for the league’s most prestigious individual honor? Doncic has never won MVP despite leading the league in scoring twice and carrying the Mavericks to the NBA Finals in 2024. Warriors star Draymond Green has a theory. “I still wholeheartedly believe he never wins an MVP because he’s in year nine and the people who vote, they’ve already moved on,” Green said on his podcast, “The Draymond Green Show. “…Voters get fatigued with seeing you being great over and over again, and if you haven’t jumped that threshold of the MVP great, then they move on. And they’ve moved on.” 4 Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers smiles while talking to the media during a game against the Utah Jazz at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It’s a shame for Doncic. The Lakers are now his team after LeBron James left in free agency for the 76ers in July. Doncic is taking that responsibility very seriously. He had a major say in the roster moves last offseason, including the Lakers acquiring Walker Kessler. And for the first time in his career, he hosted a mini camp in Slovenia in August so the team could build chemistry. Doncic didn’t hold back in an exclusive interview with the California Post about what winning MVP would mean to him. “It would definitely mean a lot,” Dončić told the newspaper. “Obviously a championship, that’s what you play for every game. That’s what you train for everyday. But obviously it would be nice to win the MVP also. Not everybody can say they have an MVP, so obviously that would be nice. “But that comes with the team first. If you don’t play good, you’re never going to win championships or MVP. So, we’ve got to play good. I’m very excited to go to war with these people. I think we had a great training camp and we’re ready to go.” For Doncic, who’s notably shy, that was him putting himself out there. He badly wants this. He’s never going to advocate for himself the way Victor Wembanyama did last season. He’s the best offensive player in the NBA, but the team-first European isn’t going to toot his own horn. But he shouldn’t have to. Voters shouldn’t need convincing. General managers are paid to know players’ games better than anyone. So, what’s happening here for Doncic, who finished fourth in MVP voting last season despite earning the scoring title and carrying the Lakers to a fourth-place finish in the West before suffering a strained hamstring in April that sidelined him all postseason? As Doncic asked last season: What more does he have to do? 4 Luka Doncic, Jake LaRavia of the Los Angeles Lakers, and Jaxson Hayes of the Utah Jazz hug after a game on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at Delta Center in Salt Lake City. NBAE via Getty Images Let’s go through the arguments against him. He complains too much to the refs. Yeah, so? Since when is that a metric that counts? Or a metric at all? He doesn’t play enough defense. That didn’t stop Steph Curry, Nikola Jokic or James Harden from winning MVPs. He can’t win unless his team finishes No. 1 in the West. Russell Westbrook won MVP in 2017 even though the Thunder finished sixth in the West. Jokic won the award in 2021 even though the Nuggets finished third in the conference. Let’s stop the excuses. Doncic has a point. Green has a point. The GMs? They missed the point. Let’s not punish Doncic because we’re so used to his stunning box scores that we’re no longer impressed by them. Let’s not fall into the lazy trope of only celebrating greatness from players who have already won the award — or looking at up-and-comers. Dončić has deserved to be at the top of the MVP conversation for a while now. And considering the stakes he’s playing for now as the face of a 17-time championship franchise, this might be his best season yet. Everyone needs to have their eyes wide open. Greatness fatigue can’t be a euphemism for blindness. Doncic has a point. Green has a point. The GMs? They missed the point. Let’s not punish Doncic because we’re so used to his stunning box scores that we’re no longer impressed by them. Let’s not fall into the lazy trope of only celebrating greatness from players who have already won the award — or looking at up-and-comers. Dončić has deserved to be at the top of the MVP conversation for a while now. And considering the stakes he’s playing for now as the face of a 17-time championship franchise, this might be his best season yet. Everyone needs to have their eyes wide open. Greatness fatigue can’t be a euphemism for blindness. title: Blakeman backed by police unions from across NYS as gov race enters final stretch: ‘Common sense’
description: New York law enforcement leaders from across the state endorsed Bruce Blakeman for governor on his Nassau County home turf — calling him the “common sense” choice over Gov. Kathy Hochul.  “This election is not about Democrat versus Republican. It’s about comm…
content: Metro Blakeman backed by police unions from across NYS as gov race enters final stretch: ‘Common sense’ By Alex Mitchell, Alex Oliveira and Brandon Cruz Published Oct. 26, 2026 Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 9:12 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source New York law enforcement leaders from across the state endorsed Bruce Blakeman for governor on his Nassau County home turf — calling him the “common sense” choice over Gov. Kathy Hochul. “This election is not about Democrat versus Republican. It’s about common sense,” Nassau Police Benevolent Association president Tommy Shevlin said outside the county’s third police precinct in Williston Park Monday afternoon. “It’s time to save our state before we all have to move to Florida,” he added. “Bruce Blakeman can save our state. He will make this the safest state in the country, just like he did here in this county.” 3 Nassau County Executive and gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman with police union leaders on Monday. Stephen Yang Shevlin was also joined by leaders from the Nassau County Corrections Benevolent Association, the Buffalo PBA, the United Coalition of Public Safety and Madison County Sheriff Todd Hood — who rallied behind Blakeman as a results-getter who could fix the state like he did Nassau. Blakeman — who is now serving as the elected Nassau County executive — has touted his Long Island community as “the safest county in America” throughout his campaign, citing the more than 25% drop in major crimes he oversaw since taking office in 2022. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed He’s vowed to roll out his crimefighting policies across the state if elected on Nov. 3, including promises to fill the state parole board with people dedicated to putting “community first” and keeping the streets free from offenders. Blakeman also notably said he’d pardon ex-Sgt. Erik Duran, the NYPD former officer sentenced to three years in prison after fatally hurling a plastic cooler at a drug suspect fleeing arrest. 3 Nassau Police Benevolent Association president Tommy Shevlin called Blakeman a “common sense” choice for Albany. Stephen Yang Blakeman on Monday accused Hochul of making the state less safe, saying there would be a “crisis on our hands” if Albany didn’t rein in socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and his leftist ideas. “Kathy Hochul won’t do that. We know she won’t do that because she’s in lockstep with him,” he said. “The 10 Commandments say, ‘Thou shalt not steal. She changed it to ‘Thou shalt not steal – except in New York.’ “People feel less safe in their communities because of Kathy Hochul’s policies, all they do is make it easier for criminals to prey on our communities,” Blakeman added. Blakeman wasn’t the only candidate to receive police backing on Monday, as Hochul was endorsed by the state police union. “Governor Hochul has invested nearly $4 billion on public safety initiatives that have benefited police officers, law enforcement agencies, and communities throughout New York State,” NYS PBA President Chris Rola said in a statement. “Her investments have resulted in a 10% reduction in index crimes, including a 60% decline in shooting related deaths.” 3 Gov. Kathy Hochul speaks during a press conference in New York, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, to announce that a joint investigative partnership by members of the New York State Police and the New York State Department of Financial Services resulted in the arrests of 16 individuals as part of ongoing auto insurance fraud investigations. Brian Zak/NY Post A Hochul campaign spokesperson blasted Blakeman for his ties to President Trump and hit the Republican for a cooperation deal between county police and ICE. “Governor Hochul has invested $4 billion in policing and public safety, from cops, cameras, and barriers on our subways to cracking down on hate crimes and ghost guns,” the spokesperson said. But not all cop groups joined in the endorsements this election cycle — with the NYC PBA and other city law enforcement unions notably declining to pick a side. At a rally on Long Island Monday night, Blakeman continued to attack Hochul on public safety while hammering her on high utility prices and cost of living. “Kathy Hochul, you don’t care about our state. You don’t care about our country. You don’t care about the city of New York. People are miserable with you as our governor, and I will make New Yorkers happy again,” Blakeman told a crowd of roughly 150 to 200 supporters in Nassau County. Saritha Komatireddy, the Republican candidate running to unseat state Attorney General Letitia James, made a surprise appearance at Blakeman’s rally and echoed his concerns around public safety. Komatireddy, who has received many of the same police endorsements as Blakeman, blasted the governor over her criminal justice reforms and said a vote for Bruce is a vote to make NY safer. “People want a safer New York,” she said. Hochul has maintained a steady lead ahead of Blakeman with just a week to go before the midterms — topping him by about 14 points at about 55% to 41%. title: Mona Lisa’s secret beauty struggle revealed by scientists
description: The iconic painting may reveal a hair-raising scientific secret.
content: Lifestyle Mona Lisa’s secret beauty struggle revealed by scientists By Faran Krentcil Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:26 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source The Mona Lisa may be known for her mysterious grin, but this week in Italy, scientists may have discovered that the iconic beauty had something else: chronic hair loss. Italian dermatologist Dr. Luigi Laino claims the Renaissance stunner, who was immortalized by Leonardo da Vinci in 1503, was likely suffering from alopecia areata, an autoimmune disorder that attacks follicles and causes sudden hair loss, especially after periods of stress or hormonal disruption. “Four findings are legible on the face of the Mona Lisa,” wrote Laino in the academic journal Clinics in Dermatology. “Total bilateral loss of eyebrows, total bilateral loss of eyelashes, a frontal hairline without transition, and intact, non-scarred skin.” The Mona Lisa, a 16th-century portrait painted in oil by Leonardo da Vinci, is exhibited in the Louvre Museum in Paris. Alfredo – stock.adobe.com Laino says there’s only one plausible scientific explanation for the masterpiece’s bare face. Explore More New ‘prestige porn’ makes sex the ultimate luxury — and hot older women the main characters Dictionary.com’s Word of the Year is one of the most viral — and controversial — terms to date My friend is reselling the expensive birthday gifts I give her son “Of all available explanations, only alopecia areata universalis accounts for all four; the solitary supraciliary hair revealed by multispectral imaging, far from contradicting the diagnosis, reproduces one of its most characteristic clinical findings.” Besides the visual evidence, Laino claims he’s got history on his (hairless, poreless) side: Lisa Gherardini, the real name behind the famous face, was the teen bride of a cloth merchant in Florence. Before she turned 30, she had six children — four of whom died — and lived during a period of political upheaval, religious wars and plague. The stress of just one of these catastrophes could provoke a hair-shedding episode in someone with alopecia, says the dermatologist. All of the disasters together would make it nearly impossible for Signora Gherardini to maintain a robust hairline. Alopecia affects nearly 7 million Americans. Janeberry – stock.adobe.com If true, the Mona Lisa may be the most famous person in history with alopecia — but she’s far from the only celebrity who deals with the autoimmune disorder. Jada Pinkett Smith, Viola Davis and Lili Reinhart have all revealed alopecia diagnoses in the past. On the Netflix hit documentary show “America’s Sweethearts,” Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Armani Latimer also revealed her alopecia struggles. Altogether, an estimated 6.7 million Americans have alopecia, according to Pfizer. Meanwhile, between 8 million and 10 million people view the Mona Lisa every year at the Louvre. In his scientific article, Dr. Laino wrote that they should know what’s on the wall: “I propose that the most contemplated face in the history of art be recognized for what, clinically, it has always shown,” he said. “A young woman with alopecia areata.” Filed under hair hair loss mona lisa the louvre 10/26/26 Read Next DeLorean 'time machines' swarm LA home for 80's classic fa... title: Blue states like New York might dash Democrats’ Blue Wave dreams
description: Could New York turn out to be the seawall that breaks this year's much-anticipated — and dreaded — Blue Wave? It's more than just wishful thinking.
content: Opinion Blue states like New York might dash Democrats’ Blue Wave dreams By Isaac Schorr Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:23 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Could blue states like New York turn out to be the seawall standing in the way of this year’s much-anticipated Blue Wave? It’s not just a pipe dream. The paradox is this: Nationally, polls show voters are dissatisfied with the ever-increasing cost of living, tired of President Donald Trump’s act and ready to punish the GOP. Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY) speaking at a campaign rally in Yorktown Heights on Oct. 25, 2026. Michael Nigro for NY Post But in places where unified Democratic control of state government has proven disastrous, there’s a lot less optimism about what Democrats would really do with still more power. Is the grass really greener on the other side? Their lives are proof to the contrary. Explore More Trump doubles down on Obama criticism as his voice starts to give out amid campaign rally blitz Katie Zacharia on Trump’s timeless 6-word message ahead of crucial midterms — and everything great he’s done for America already Embattled Ilhan Omar tells lefty antisemitic streamer Hasan Piker her ‘good’ looks are why media is fixated on her At a Sunday afternoon rally in Yorktown Heights, Rep. Mike Lawler — the independent-minded Republican fending off a tough challenge from Democrat Cait Conley in NY-17 — was joined by his colleague Nicole Malliotakis, gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman, newly-minted superstar Saritha Komatireddy and a number of local Republicans running for county and state office, all of whom made the case that New Yorkers should try something new. Looming particularly large over Lawler’s race is the shadow of Sheridan Gorman, a young constituent of his who was murdered in March. The man being charged with killing her is an illegal immigrant who had been inexplicably released back into the United States after having previously been arrested for shoplifting. Sheridan’s parents, Jessica and Tom Gorman, have emerged as powerful advocates against sanctuary policies — and for Lawler, who has championed their crusade in the months since their daughter’s tragic death. One rally attendee told The Post that he had turned out specifically to support the Gormans. See Also editorial Centrist champion for small business Mike Lawler is a far better vote than carpetbagging challenger Cait Conley “It brings me to tears, I have daughters that age,” he said. “It brings me to tears!” There’s sorrow, but just as much righteous anger. “Kathy Hochul is a liar,” warned Jessica Gorman in Yorktown after calling Lawler, Blakeman and Komatireddy their “hope.” Hochul “has never even pretended to care about victims.” Lawler slammed Conley for lacking the compassion — and common sense — to break with her party’s deranged orthodoxy. “My opponent, Cait Conley, couldn’t even be bothered to answer [the Gormans’] question when they asked her . . . ‘Do you support Kathy Hochul’s sanctuary state law?'” “And she looked this way, and she looked that way, and she looked down, she looked up. She couldn’t look them in the eye and tell them the truth: She does support Kathy Hochul’s sanctuary state law.” At the top of their ticket, Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James present major problems for Democrats. The former is a wide-eyed dunce who would seem out of her depth as a middle-school hall monitor, much less as chief executive of the Empire State. On her watch, energy costs have skyrocketed, economic growth has slowed and weary residents have fled; New York placed 50th in net population percentage change in fiscal year 2025. Get opinions and commentary from our columnists Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter! Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story. Check out more newsletters If Hochul wins reelection, she’ll have only partisan allegiance to thank. One recent Quinnipiac University survey suggested her image statewide is underwater, with 45% expressing a favorable and 46% expressing an unfavorable opinion of her. Among independents, Blakeman actually leads Hochul, 51% to 44%. James, meanwhile, has been an absentee chief law enforcement officer, more worried about wasting tax dollars on fruitless civil cases against the president than bringing criminals to justice or tackling a corrosive mental health crisis. Both were utterly humiliated during lopsided debates with Blakeman and Komatireddy, respectively. See Also Cait Conley calls Mike Lawler a ‘Trump puppet’ while dancing to Hakeem Jeffries’ tune Komatireddy’s performance was so dominant that she’s pulled within six points of James, according to one bombshell mid-October poll; she’s now the subject of a New York Times feature that grudgingly acknowledges her impressive candidacy. The lack of enthusiasm for the two top Democratic candidates could drag down turnout across the state. The other thing working against Conley and in favor of Lawler is their respective approaches to campaigning. Lawler is a product of a relatively inhospitable environment, and he’s a stronger candidate for it. To be successful as a Republican in a New York City suburb is to take nothing for granted, to treat every vote as gettable and to never, ever give it a rest. Take his schedule on Sunday for an example: The day began with an appearance at a Haitian church in Spring Valley. Then two rallies, the one in Yorktown to fire up members of his base — many of whom appeared to know him personally — and another in Monsey to reach out to its Orthodox Jewish community. But wait, there’s more. His nightcap was yet another visit to a Haitian church, where one attendee identified himself as a big supporter of the congressman, thanks to his work on behalf of Haitians whose legal status in the country has been threatened by the Trump administration’s withdrawal of Temporary Protected Status. “My fundamental issue is TPS . . . and he’s the one who’s been working on it, not just now, at the time of elections — he’s been working on it!” the supporter told The Post. “There are a lot of other issues . . . and [Lawler] seems to be on top of all of them.” For his part, Lawler began his remarks by observing, “This is not the first time I’ve been here, and this is not the last time I’m going to be here.” A pastor, meanwhile, told The Post that while he’d be happy to host Conley for a similar event at the church, he hadn’t heard from her campaign. Maybe she thinks that merely running as a Democrat in New York ought to be enough to get her over the finish line in 2026. But maybe the carpetbagger ought to have picked a district a little less fatigued by the destructive far-left agenda she would rubber-stamp. title: Fernando Mendoza’s time will have to wait — Raiders staying put at QB
description: The Raiders have a future to develop. But Klint Kubiak still has games he intends to win. And for now, the coach believes Kirk Cousins gives them their best chance....
content: NFL Fernando Mendoza’s time will have to wait — Raiders staying put at QB By Vincent Bonsignore Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:18 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source The Raiders have a future to develop. But Klint Kubiak still has games he intends to win. And for now, the coach believes Kirk Cousins gives them their best chance. Kubiak made that abundantly clear Monday, opening his weekly press conference by affirming Cousins remains the Raiders’ starting quarterback and dismissing the notion of a quarterback change. “Kirk is our starting quarterback,” Kubiak said. “There is no controversy.” 3 Kirk Cousins of the Las Vegas Raiders throws against the Los Angeles Rams in the third quarter at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada, Sunday, October 25, 2026. The Rams defeated the Raiders 35-21. Getty Images Fernando Mendoza’s opportunity will come. It just won’t come this week. The declaration settled the most pressing personnel question facing a team whose fourth consecutive loss Sunday against the Rams intensified calls to begin the next chapter at quarterback. At 3-4, with their promising start giving way to familiar frustrations, the Raiders face an increasingly difficult balancing act: trying to salvage the season in front of them while preparing the quarterback expected to define the seasons ahead. Kubiak’s decision makes clear which objective takes precedence this week. Winning. Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance And with the beatable Jets up next on the schedule, and a chance to get back to even and potentially position themselves to make a postseason run over the final nine games, they will continue to ride things out with Cousins. “Kirk’s playing really well, and we’re in the hunt,” Kubiak said. “It’ really important that we keep playing really well behind him and continue to develop Fernando.” That means sticking with Cousins, whose experience and familiarity with the offense remain central to the argument for keeping him on the field, even as the results make that position harder to sell. The Raiders used the first overall pick on Mendoza to change the trajectory of their franchise. Every week he watches is another week without the game experience that eventually must become part of his development. But Kubiak’s position reflects a different calculation: The Raiders still have something to play for, and he is sticking with the veteran to pursue it. 3 Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak looks on prior to a game against the Los Angeles Rams at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images That does not erase the questions surrounding an offense that continues to struggle in the red zone and coming out of halftime. Nor does it change the limitations that have fueled the conversation about whether Mendoza’s mobility and upside could provide a needed spark. It does establish that Kubiak is not ready to make that move. Yet. “Eventually, Fernando is gonna play football,” said Kubiak. “We have a plan.” Kubiak’s announcement also offered clarity after Sunday’s loss, when he acknowledged the Raiders needed to examine everything, including personnel and scheme, in trying to solve their mounting problems. Quarterback was an obvious part of that discussion. By Monday, Kubiak had publicly drawn the line for the coming week. The challenge now is making the commitment produce something beyond certainty about who takes the first snap. Cousins cannot repair a defense that continues to surrender too much on the ground. A quarterback change would not automatically solve that problem, either. The Raiders’ losing streak stretches across enough areas that reducing it to one position misses the scope of the trouble. 3 Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza works out prior to an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Las Vegas. AP Photo/David Becker Still, keeping Cousins ties the decision directly to the priority Kubiak has established. If winning now is the reason to wait on Mendoza, the Raiders need to start delivering wins. Otherwise, the argument for patience will become harder to sustain, and the future increasingly difficult to keep on the sideline. title: King tides swamp California city in floodwater as ocean surges up busy street
description: The ocean spilled into the upscale Orange County enclave as king tides battered the Southern California coastline.
content: California News King tides swamp California city in floodwater as ocean surges up busy street By Erica Andrews Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:12 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source A tidal surge swallowed streets in Newport Beach on Monday morning, sending knee-deep floodwater rushing into a picturesque coastal neighborhood as frantic residents scrambled to protect their homes and businesses. The ocean spilled into the upscale Orange County enclave as king tides battered the Southern California coastline, turning normally bustling streets into waterways and threatening another round of destruction in a city already reeling from severe flooding earlier this month. Aerial footage from KTLA showed residents desperately stacking sandbags along Edgewater Avenue and Washington Street on the harbor side of the Balboa Peninsula as murky water surged toward local businesses. Hong Elsewhere, streets near 38th Street and River Avenue, close to the entrance of Newport Island, disappeared beneath roughly a foot of water. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed And one longtime resident said the flooding was unlike anything the coastal community had ever experienced. “Not only have I never seen anything like this, there’s never been something like this,” Newport Beach resident Bill Sharp told the outlet. Sharp said a tidal gauge registered a staggering 8.3 feet at 9:18 a.m. Monday. “It’s a new record, and this is absolutely unprecedented,” he said. Fortunately, no injuries had been reported as of Monday morning. 5 The king tides turned normally bustling streets into waterways and threatened another round of destruction in Newport. AP Photo/Jae C. Hong The frightening scenes unfolded as city crews worked to fortify sand berms, deploy pumps and reinforce vulnerable sections of the coastline against the relentless onslaught of seawater. Newport Beach City Manager Seimone Jurjis told the Los Angeles Times officials had been preparing for the dangerous conditions and monitoring the situation. “Our City teams have been busy reinforcing sand berms, evaluating vulnerable seawalls, placing sandbags, inspecting storm drains and preparing additional pumps, heavy equipment and emergency resources,” Jurjis said. The latest flooding comes just weeks after Newport Beach declared a local emergency on October 9 when powerful swells and elevated tides sent seawater pouring through the Balboa Peninsula, leaving motorists stranded and vehicles partially submerged. 5 Henk Wiessner, president of Fun Zone Boat Co., stands in floodwaters with his dog Butters in Newport Beach. AP Photo/Jae C. Hong That earlier deluge, fueled by Tropical Storm Rachel and a Kelvin wave, prompted desperate efforts to rebuild protective sand barriers and pump water from flooded neighborhoods. Police warned motorists to steer clear of the peninsula and avoid driving through submerged streets. Now, the coastal paradise is once again facing a watery nightmare. And Newport Beach isn’t alone. The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings for Orange and San Diego counties through Thursday afternoon, cautioning that rising seawater could inundate homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. 5 One longtime Newport resident said the flooding was unlike anything the coastal community had ever experienced. AP Photo/Jae C. Hong Less severe coastal flood advisories were also issued for Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties. Long Beach has also endured destructive coastal flooding in recent weeks, with dramatic footage capturing waves crashing into waterfront properties, parking lots and boardwalks. The dangerous conditions have even disrupted transportation. Metrolink announced it would suspend service between the Laguna Niguel/Mission Viejo and Oceanside stations from Monday through Friday because of the elevated tides. Meanwhile, officials have secured millions in emergency funding to repair a massive crack that developed beneath Pacific Coast Highway near Laguna Beach during earlier October high tides. 5 The flooding unfolded as city crews worked to fortify sand berms, deploy pumps and reinforce vulnerable coastline. AP Photo/Jae C. Hong Forecasters say unusually warm ocean waters associated with an emerging El Niño pattern, combined with Kelvin waves, are pushing tides well above their astronomical predictions. And the danger may not be over. Additional exceptionally high astronomical tides are expected around Thanksgiving and Christmas, potentially delivering another punishing blow to already battered coastal communities. The National Weather Service urged residents to avoid flooded roadways, beaches, jetties and seawalls during the dangerous tidal conditions. For Newport Beach residents, Monday’s record-breaking flood was another alarming reminder of just how quickly their seaside paradise can be swallowed by the ocean. title: MTA’s $26.7M Yankee Stadium elevators racked up 41 outages, stranded riders
description: The MTA’s multi-million dollar overhaul of five elevators at the Yankee Stadium subway station has left riders contending with unreliable service -- including one lift that hasn't been working for months.
content: Metro MTA spent $26.7M on Yankee Stadium elevators but riders still face unreliable service — with two lifts not even working By Haley Brown and Kalohe Danbara Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:11 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source The Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s multi-million dollar overhaul of five elevators at the Yankee Stadium subway station has left riders contending with unreliable service — including one lift that hasn’t been working for months. The station’s new elevators logged 41 outages between April through September, including 35 unplanned interruptions, according to an analysis of MTA records. 4 Yankee Stadium subway station elevators logged 41 outages from April through September, including 35 unplanned interruptions, according to an analysis of MTA records. J.C. Rice The elevators were purchased as a part of a 14-elevator buy for $74.8 million, and the MTA spent about $26.7 million for the five elevators at the Yankee Stadium stop. “It’s really outrageous,” Marie McCullough, an elderly woman who lives near the 161st Street-Yankee Stadium station told The Post on Monday. “Many times I have not shopped downtown, even though I may have wanted to get some things because of the fact I knew the elevators weren’t working.” McCullough, who recently recovered from a torn meniscus, relies on the elevators for transporting her groceries. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed “I don’t want to have to ride up to 167 or 170 (streets) to get the elevator there because I’d still have to get downtown. I live down here. I don’t live up there,” McCullough explained. The elevator replacement project at the Yankee Stadium subway station began in November 2024 and all five elevators were supposed to be in service around April of this year, according to MTA documents. 4 The elevators were purchased as a part of a 14-elevator buy for $74.8 million, and the MTA spent about $26.7 million for the five elevators at the Yankee Stadium stop. MTA The MTA said three of the elevators are now working — and praised themselves despite barely half of the new elevators working. “Five elevators that were installed before Aaron Boone even played for the Yankees were not performing well and needed to be replaced,” an MTA spokesperson said. Boone, who is now the Yankees manager, played part of the 2003 season in New York. “Three of them are now back in full service. You could call it a rebuilding season,” the spokesperson added. In the meantime, subway riders are forced to face detours and stairs. 4 The broken elevators sometimes mean riders with strollers or heavy cargo are stuck taking the stairs. J.C. Rice A young mother waited Monday beside a broken elevator with a suitcase and a large stroller carrying two children too young to walk on their own. Regina Penny, 70, who lives across the street from Yankee Stadium, stopped to help the mother find someone who could carry the stroller up the stairs. “I have to stand with her and wait for somebody nice to come and help her,” Penny said. “It’s a shame. It’s been like that for a whole year. “It’s no respect for her. People with wheelchairs, walkers. It’s no respect,” she added. Elevator 135, which connects the mezzanine to the northbound B/D platform, already suffered an unplanned outage in April and recorded no operating time at all in July, August or September, according to MTA data. It is still out and expected to remain out until January of next year, according to the MTA website, which blames “Final contract items.” The MTA previously listed “Con Edison Power Issues” as the reason for elevator 135’s shutdown, according to a report by the publication The City Reporter. But the MTA has since removed that language from its site. 4 Some of the new elevators at the Yankee Stadium stop suffered outages as soon as they opened. MTA Con Edison told The Post the outages weren’t their fault. “We are confident the voltage levels are adequate on our end,” a spokesperson said. Another elevator — elevator 131 which links the street and mezzanine — had dropped to a 36.5% operating level by June, operated at a 31.8% rate in July, plummeted to 0% in August and only got up to 30.7% in September, according to MTA data. “I’m schlepping up the stairs with something that’s heavy. It’s ridiculous,” said McCullough as she prepared to lug her cart full of groceries up a flight of stairs. “It’s a terrible inconvenience,” she added. title: Apple addresses reports of cracked screens on $2K iPhone Duo just days after frenzied launch
description: Apple has acknowledged a problem with the inner screens of its new $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo after customers reported cracks and bright lines appearing near the hinge.
content: Business Apple addresses reports of cracked screens on $2K iPhone Duo just days after frenzied launch By Ariel Zilber Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:10 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Apple has acknowledged a problem with the inner screens of its new $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo after customers reported cracks and bright lines appearing near the hinge — in some cases within hours of unboxing the pricey gadget. The tech giant said Monday that it would replace affected devices — just three days after the highly anticipated phone went on sale Friday, drawing massive crowds and overnight lines outside Apple stores across the country. “We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” an Apple representative told CNBC. “If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.” 4 A display of Apple iPhone Duo smartphones is seen during a launch in a store in the Manhattan borough of New York City on Friday. Anadolu via Getty Images An Australian buyer posting as Midnight_Slump on Reddit said his Duo’s screen cracked after roughly six hours of ownership and fewer than 20 openings. The customer said he felt something beneath the display near the hinge while showing the device to a friend, then heard an audible crack as he continued unfolding it. Explore More How to stop worrying about the $40 trillion – yes trillion with a ‘T’ – that’s now owed by the US government Forget Florida — Baby Boomers flocking to Eastern seaboard state for low taxes, sandy beaches Brazil markets, currency reel from leftist Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election win After Apple offered an express replacement that required a hold for the full price of the phone, he went to a nearby Apple Store, where employees swapped the damaged handset for a new one on the spot. “Day zero, six hours of ownership, and already on my second phone,” he wrote. 4 A screenshot from a Reddit user shows iPhone Duos with damage in the exact same spots. reddit/Bitter_Offer7123 In Dallas, a Reddit user identified as leftyhyzer16 said his Duo’s hinge became unusually tight after being folded about four times during setup, then made a loud pop when he pushed past the resistance. The customer said AT&T warned that replacing the phone through the carrier could push him to the back of the order queue in January. “Drove down to the Dallas Apple Store and they thankfully had one in stock and swapped it out immediately, no charge,” he wrote. The complaints threaten to cast a shadow over Apple’s entry into the foldable smartphone market, where durability has long been a concern. “At $1,999, confidence is part of the product,” Ravi Sawhney, founder and CEO of industrial design firm RKS Design, told The Post. “People are buying the freedom to use something advanced without thinking constantly about how to protect it,” he added. “The risk for Apple is that opening the phone becomes a moment of hesitation,” Sawhney continued. 4 An image from a Reddit user shows an iPhone Duo with damage. reddit/robnaught “Once people start wondering whether an ordinary interaction could damage their purchase, that changes their relationship with the product.” Sawhney cautioned against assuming the hinge is responsible for the defects. “A bright line tells us the display has malfunctioned. It does not, by itself, tell us what caused it,” he said. “With a folding product, you have to examine the entire mechanical system: the display layers, their support, the hinge movement, the clearances and the assembly tolerances.” Investigators would need to compare damaged devices with unaffected phones from different production batches and attempt to reproduce the failures under controlled conditions, according to Sawhney. A recurring problem in properly assembled devices could indicate a design flaw, while defects concentrated in particular batches could point to manufacturing inconsistencies, he said. Apple has not disclosed the precise cause of the failures or how many devices have been affected. The company says most units are not susceptible to the problem and that affected phones tend to show symptoms quickly, according to Bloomberg. The financial stakes are substantial for buyers. Apple lists the cost of an out-of-warranty inner-screen repair at $999 — roughly half the Duo’s starting price — although that does not mean customers affected by the acknowledged issue will be charged for replacements. 4 An image from a Reddit user shows iPhone Duos with damage in the exact same spots. reddit/Bitter_Offer7123 The early troubles follow a frenzied debut that saw shoppers camping outside Apple stores, including one customer who reportedly waited 18 hours outside the Fifth Avenue flagship in Manhattan. Some locations exhausted their walk-in supplies shortly after opening, while others turned away disappointed customers who had spent hours in line. Sawhney said Apple’s handling of the complaints could prove critical to maintaining customer trust in the new product. “If these failures prove isolated and Apple handles them well, confidence can recover,” he said. “If uncertainty persists, prospective buyers may postpone purchasing — and that hesitation can extend to foldables generally.” Filed under apple iphone iPhones 10/26/26 Read Next Dollar chain faces FTC lawsuit for 'long-running deceptive... title: The two huge moments WWE has set up in women’s title scene — if they play their cards right
description: WWE’s women’s division is a healthy place — and set up for two huge moments for Tiffany Stratton and Roxanne Perez if done right
content: Joseph Staszewski The two huge moments WWE has set up in women’s title scene — if they play their cards right By Joseph Staszewski Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:10 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source IYO SKY, Tiffany Stratton and Chelsea Green look on during SmackDown at Toyota Arena on October 23, 2026. WWE via Getty Images WWE’s women’s division is a healthy place — and set up for two huge moments for Tiffany Stratton and Roxanne Perez if done right Stratton cashing in on WWE women’s champion Chelsea Green has felt inevitable since the moment the Money in the Bank match ended and did so again during SmackDown on Friday. There was just this shot of a disappointed Stratton standing right next to her on-screen bestie, Green, after she was unable to cash in on a perfectly weakened Women’s World champion Liv Morgan after the ref took an obscene amount of time talking to Stratton before never actually making the attempt official. We have seen this spot so many times that there is no excuse for it being mucked up this badly. Still, it only enhances the feeling that Stratton was going to take Green’s title away and turn heel again. So how do you make it different than Stratton’s first cash-in on Nia Jax in 2025? The easy way is she becomes the first woman to fail to cash in, and then you can still launch a program between her and Green with Stratton stopping at nothing to undo the embarrassment of her failed cash-in by becoming champion again. description: The throwback co-headliners will pour some sugar on MSG on June 23.
content: Entertainment What do the cheapest tickets cost to see Def Leppard with Goo Goo Dolls? By Matt Levy Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:08 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Featured pricing is subject to change. Your favorite group from the ’80s is teaming up with your favorite group from the ’90s for a “Rock Show of Ages.” From March through July 2027, Def Leppard will co-headline with The Goo Goo Dolls at arenas all over North America on their nationwide tour with special guest The Struts. That includes a pair of gigs in New Jersey and New York. They’re slated to take place at: Prudential Center Newark, NJ Saturday, March 13, 2027 Madison Square Garden New York, NY Wednesday, June 23, 2027 If you’d like to see the hitmakers live, tickets are available for all 45 upcoming concerts. At the time of publication, the lowest price we could find on seats for any one show was $101 including fees on Vivid Seats (that’s for the MSG show). Tickets start at $127 including fees for the Prudential gig. “[We’ll be] taking over North America next Spring with a night of non-stop hits,” Def Leppard shared on Instagram. They’re not lying either. The Rock Hall of Famers typically perform smash singles “Pour Some Sugar On Me,” “Hysteria,” “Photograph,” “Love Bites” and, of course, “Rock of Ages” at all shows, according to Set List FM. More importantly, Joe Elliott and co. still have the goods. Metal Talk attended a July concert of theirs in London and raved “if there were a university degree in playing arena shows, these guys would be tenured professors. And…despite playing so many absolute bangers over the course of almost two hours, they have so many more of those left out that you will inevitably [say]: ‘I would have also liked X and Y songs.'” Notable tracks that often make the cut at Goo Goo Dolls concerts include fan favorites “Iris,” “Slide,” “Name,” “Black Balloon” and “Broadway” among others. Can’t wait to “Pour Some Sugar” on “Iris”? For more information, our team has everything you need to know and more about Def Leppard and The Goo Goo Dolls 2027 tour below. Single and multi-day 2027 Tortuga Music Festival passes can be scooped up here. What songs does Def Leppard perform live in concert? On Oct. 24, Def Leppard rocked El Salvador’s Estadio Cuscatlán. Set List FM reported these were the songs they took to the stage. 01.) “Rejoice” 02.) “Animal” 03.) “Let’s Get Rocked” 04.) “Personal Jesus” (Depeche Mode cover) 05.) “Bringin’ On the Heartbreak” 06.) “Switch 625” 07.) “Just Like ’73” 08.) “Rocket” 09.) “Rock On” (David Essex cover) 10.) “White Lightning” 11.) “Slang” (with Nuno Bettencourt) (with interlude of “Get Up Offa That Thing” by James Brown & “Fame” by David Bowie) 12.) “Promises” (with a capella intro) 13.) “Armageddon It” 14.) “Love Bites” 15.) “Rock of Ages” 16.) “Photograph” 17.) “Two Steps Behind” (Joe solo; short acoustic version) 18.) “When Love and Hate Collide” 19.) “Hysteria” (with 1987-1993 bass intro) 20.) “Pour Some Sugar on Me” Which songs do The Goo Goo Dolls take to the stage? According to Set List FM, these are the 25 songs that The Goo Goo Dolls performed at Uncasville, CT’s Mohegan Sun Arena on Sept. 6. 01.) “Over and Over” 02.) “Dizzy” 03.) “Slide” 04.) “Home” 05.) “Here Is Gone” 06.) “Lucky Star” 07.) “Big Machine” 08.) “Long Way Down” 09.) “Black Balloon” 10.) “I’m Still Here (Jim’s Theme)” (John Rzeznik song) 11.) “Miracle Pill” 12.) “Sympathy” 13.) “Acoustic #3” 14.) “Name” 15.) “Naked” 16.) “Run All Night” 17.) “Life’s a Message” 18.) “Nothing Lasts Forever” 19.) “Stay With You” 20.) “Let Love In” 21.) “Ocean” 22.) “Bringing On the Light” 23.) “Better Days” 24.) “Broadway” 25.) “Iris” Who are The Struts? The British rockers formed in Derby, United Kingdom in 2010 and have been delivering crowd-pleasing, high-energy glam rock ever since. Just a few of our favorite tracks of theirs include the hard-charging “Could Have Been Me,” groovy, slinky “Body Talks” and charming, summery bop “Kiss This.” To hear for yourself, you can find The Struts’ complete discography here. Def Leppard new music This year, Def Leppard have released a handful of singles. Up first was the searing stadium anthem “Rejoice,” which is big, bold arena rock at its brashest and most in your face. Soaring guitars, pitch-perfect harmonies and a singalong chorus all make for an excellent throwback jam that fits right into the group’s catalog. Then, more recently, the Rock Hall of Famers dropped faithful — if bombast-ified — covers of The Beatles’ catchy “Revolution” and David Bowie’s transcendent “Heroes.” Goo Goo Dolls new music In 2026, The Goo Goo Dolls rolled out just one new song. “Postcards from Paradise” sounds like a lost B-Side from the group’s ’90s output. Plucky guitar, evocative lyrics and a fist-pumping refrain — “you send me postcards from paradise” — make for a winning listen. Huge ’80s stars on tour in 2026-27 If you’re still stuck in the 20th century, you’re not alone. After a bit of parsing the web, we found that many of the biggest names from rock and roll’s heyday are striking out yet again in ’26. Here are just five of our favorites you won’t want to miss live when they take their hits to the people. • Bon Jovi • RUSH • Sting • Metallica • Aerosmith Also, Stevie Wonder is striking out on a brief tour celebrating the 50th anniversary of his seminal 1976 album “Songs in the Key of Life.” Don’t miss out- we have a feeling those shows will be special. title: Bronx and Queens DAs urge prosecutors to downgrade charges to keep illegal immigrants in US, House GOP report finds
description: WASHINGTON — New York City’s elected Democratic district attorneys are bending over backwards to keep illegal immigrants in the US, instructing prosecutors to downgrade charges to those considered “a non-deportable offense,” according to a stunning House Judi…
content: Politics exclusive NYC’s sanctuary DAs ordered prosecutors to downgrade charges to keep illegal immigrants in US, House GOP report finds By Josh Christenson and Thomas English Published Oct. 26, 2026 Updated Oct. 26, 2026, 6:55 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source WASHINGTON — New York City’s elected Democratic district attorneys are bending over backwards to keep illegal immigrants in the US, instructing prosecutors to downgrade charges to those considered “a non-deportable offense,” according to a stunning House Judiciary Committee report shared with The Post. The GOP-led panel found that Bronx DA Darcel Clark trains her subordinates “to conceal facts from the record of conviction” and “pursue alternative charges” that would keep non-citizens free to roam in America. Not even cases involving child sex crimes are off-limits — with Clark’s office asking assistant DAs in a 2019 guide to “immigration-conscious plea bargaining” to “[o]ffer something that does not have the child’s age as an element of the crime.” Meanwhile, in Queens, DA Melinda Katz has told her prosecutors to “exercise extreme caution” and “not get caught up in the label of [f]elonies, [m]isdemeanors” for illegal aliens, according to the report published five months after the committee sent requests for information on the Big Apple’s so-called “sanctuary” policies to prosecutor’s offices in all five boroughs, as well as the NYPD and Department of Correction. Those policies have had deadly consequences, as in the case of a 92-year-old Queens woman who was murdered by a Guyanese migrant, Reeaz Khan, after a federal detainer was lodged against him in 2020. 10 Bronx DA Darcel Clark, left, and Queens DA Melinda Katz, seen on Aug. 11, 2026, instructed prosecutors to downgrade charges on illegal immigrants, according to an alarming House Judiciary Committee report shared with The Post. Stephen Yang for NY Post Explore More Mamdani’s latest anti-ICE move not only abets criminals, it may BE criminal Mamdani plans to ask NYC garage owners to block ICE usage in guilt-tripping letter: sources Rep. Mike Lawler rips Cait Conley’s support of sanctuary policies, portrays her as phony New Yorker in fiery final debate Katz’s office later secured a 22 years to life sentence against Khan. The report found versions of the practice in every borough. The Brooklyn DA’s office has explicitly sought an “immigration-neutral” disposition since 2017, having staff trained “to avoid disproportionate collateral consequence, such as deportation, while maintaining public safety.” In some cases, prosecutors in Brooklyn DA Eric Gonzalez’s office are instructed to offer “a plea for a lesser offense in light of the disproportionate immigration consequences a higher level offense may result in.” 10 House Judiciary Committee Staten Island DA Michael McMahon has a whole unit dedicated to asking ICE to delay deportations. But Manhattan DA Alvin Bragg’s office told the committee his once-expansive immigration policy is “outdated,” while admitting prosecutors still consider citizenship status on a case-by-case basis. In 2022, Bragg had issued a memo to prosecutors requesting that they “seek dispositions that avoid immigration consequences for all misdemeanors, and all felonies for which non-carceral outcomes are the presumptive outcome.” “When did protecting a criminal’s immigration status become a part of a DA’s job description?” asked New York City Council Member Joann Ariola. “Our DA’s are entrusted with upholding the law and protecting the public,” Ariola told The Post. “If that’s not their priority, then they’ve got it backwards.” 10 The cover of an interim staff report by the House Judiciary Committee titled “NEW YORK CITY: THE DANGEROUS CONSEQUENCES OF SANCTUARY POLICIES” is seen. House Judiciary Committee 10 House Judiciary Committee According to the report, the NYPD has received nearly 10,000 detainer requests from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for illegal aliens charged with crimes in the past 12 months — and honored none. The Department of Homeland Security revealed earlier this month that 16,070 detainer requests had been ignored by authorities across the Empire State, which, like New York City, doesn’t cooperate with federal immigration officials as a sanctuary jurisdiction. In a report authored by Katz’s office last year, the Queens DA was confirmed to employ an “immigration specialist,” whose sole purpose is helping assistant DAs “navigate through plea options and assist in framing dispositions that will prevent unwanted immigration consequences.” 10 Bronx DA Darcel Clark announces changes to state discovery laws in Manhattan on May 7, 2025. James Messerschmidt 10 Queens DA Melinda Katz announces the sentencing of Jaime Huiracocha and Victor Murillo for their role in staging three car crashes on local Highways and seeking insurance payouts on Aug. 27, 2026. Brigitte Stelzer for NY Post In 2020 alone, the “immigration specialist” helped get 21 convictions reduced or thrown out entirely. In six cases, Katz urged then-Gov. Andrew Cuomo to grant a pardon to prevent deportation. Bronx DA Clark has also bragged that since 2020, “[p]rosecutors in my office must thoughtfully consider employment, immigration, family unification, and the broad range of other potential collateral consequences when initiating a prosecution.” The House Judiciary Committee obtained office training materials from March 2023 titled “Crimmigration,” in which Bronx prosecutors were explicitly told to, “[a]s appropriate,” “strive to ensure that a conviction for certain offenses does not lead to unintended and severe consequences such as deportation that can tear families apart and destabilize communities.” 10 House Judiciary Committee 10 House Judiciary Committee Screenshots of the “Immigration-Conscious Plea Bargaining” training from 2019 reproduced in the report also revealed that prosecutors were urged to “Offer a Non-Deportable Offense” for defendants to consider copping to. Those training materials further suggest that prosecutors should consider pursuing charges for so-called “legally impossible” offenses — when a defendant believes they are committing a crime, but actually are not — because “[l]egally impossible crimes cannot serve as the basis for [immigration] removal proceedings” when appealed in the US federal court system. The legal impossibilities often have a defendant being accused of having “two contradictory mental states … at the same time,” per the report. 10 Republican Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan speaks during a House Judiciary subcommittee hearing on sanctuary city policies on Capitol Hill on June 30, 2026. REUTERS 10 Chairman Rep. Tom McClintock (R-Calif.) listens during a hearing before the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement of the House Judiciary Committee in DC on Sept. 1, 2026. Getty Images In cases involving weapons offenses, Bronx prosecutors are instructed in training materials to “[k]eep the firearm out of the record of conviction” and “[o]ffer something that does not specify a firearm” in plea bargaining. Accused wife-beaters get the same treatment. Prosecutors are told to “[k]eep the domestic relationship out of the record of conviction.” In stalking cases, they’re encouraged to offer a charge without “repeated instances or an intent to instill fear.” Republicans argue this practice carries consequences beyond immigration court, and the same omissions that keep a defendant off ICE’s radar can keep him out of sight of law enforcement as well. In Queens, the approach shows up in practice, not just in training. In a May 26 email obtained by the committee, an assistant DA in Katz’s office told a NYPD detective the office had “basically made a [plea] deal which is ‘immigration safe,’” assuring them that the defendant still pleaded guilty to multiple crimes and spent time behind bars. Ken Frydman, a Democratic operative and also a police union rep, said, “Immigration specialists typically help immigrants navigate the immigration process, not help get convictions reduced or thrown out in order to keep illegal immigrants in the US.” According to the Judiciary Committee, Katz spurned the committee’s initial May request, arguing state prosecutions fall outside Congress’ oversight jurisdiction. She relented only after Chairman Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) and Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement Subcommittee Chairman Tom McClintock (R-Calif.) sent a second letter in August warning they might issue a subpoena. Reps for the Queens, Bronx, Brooklyn, Staten Island and Manhattan DA’s offices didn’t respond to requests for comment.
