title: Workers at OpenAI, Anthropic made to ditch company logos as it makes them targets for spies, seduction
description: Silicon Valley’s top AI workers are being told to hide any company logos in public as working for the hottest companies marks them as targets for spies and angry protesters. OpenAI tells staff not to wear anything bearing its logo outside their offices and tr…
content: Tech Workers at OpenAI, Anthropic made to ditch company logos as it makes them targets for spies, seduction By Vivi Lin Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:07 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Silicon Valley’s top AI workers are being told to hide any company logos in public as working for the hottest companies marks them as targets for spies and angry protesters. OpenAI tells staff not to wear anything bearing its logo outside their offices and trains them to watch for spies offering cash, friendship or romance. Anthropic — which has just filed for what analysts are predicting will be a record-busting Initial Public Offering on the stock market — has all but banned branded merch, reminds employees to conceal their badges when leaving the premises and has reported people trying to photograph its offices. 8 Attendees at OpenAI’s DevDay 2026 in San Francisco. Staff are told to leave the logo at work. AP Photo/Jeff Chiu “I strongly support this approach,” Miao Hong, managing partner of Silicon Valley Future Capital and investor in OpenAI and Anthropic, told the Post. Explore More Microsoft announces buyouts for 60K employees — quarter of workforce — as part of AI transformation Anthropic’s delay in reporting ‘rogue agent’ Georgia vote hack alarms government officials Ex-Yahoo CEO under fire for bragging about birthday message to daughter — written by AI: ‘Who would do this?’ Hong said he sees AI employees approached again-and-again by people hunting for inside information — and he doesn’t know their intentions. “Everyone wants to find out about developments and information at the cutting edge of technology. They want firsthand information. They want to talk to these employees, but the employees generally avoid discussing anything,” he told The Post. 8 Miao Hong, managing partner of Silicon Valley Future Capital and an investor in OpenAI and Anthropic, backs AI companies telling staff to hide their logos in public. Courtesy of Hong Miao The father of one Anthropic employee says his son and his colleagues steer clear of shop talk after work. “I also pay attention to safety and remind my child to be careful, because he can easily become a target. They try not to talk about their work at all. They keep it more about sports, hobbies, hiking and food,” the father, who asked not to be named, told the Post. Espionage tops the list of fears. OpenAI’s security sessions warn AI rivals or spies working for rogue nations use techniques ranging from something as simple as eavesdropping in cafes to bribes, or even using romance. 8 A ChatGPT hat on display at an OpenAI developers conference at Fort Mason in San Francisco on Sept. 29, 2026. The company sells its branded merch to the public, even as it tells staff not to wear the logo outside the office. Getty Images 8 Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national who worked as an OpenAI engineer, was arrested Oct. 9 and charged with planting a recording device in an executive conference room at the company’s San Francisco offices, prosecutors say. X/@alfozan In one example, a stranger made small talk with an OpenAI employee at a San Francisco playground, but then steering the conversation to the employee’s work. That person was a spy, according to the Wall Street Journal. Employees are also reminded to use privacy screens on public transit and to wipe meeting-room whiteboards when they leave. Bringing into focus the kind of threats faced, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national who worked as an engineer at OpenAI was arrested Oct. 9 and charged with trying to intercept private conversations. He had hidden a recording device wrapped in toilet paper behind a TV in an executive conference room, according to the federal complaint against him. OpenAI fired him and he is currently in jail while awaiting his case, as he is deemed a flight risk. He has yet to enter a plea. 8 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, left, with Salesforce’s Marc Benioff at Dreamforce in San Francisco on Sept. 15. His company keeps its logo off its employees. Getty Images 8 Corgi co-founders Nico Laqua, CEO, and Emily Yuan, COO at a company launch. Laqua says passersby stop daily outside the startup’s 24-hour San Francisco cafe to shout and curse about AI. Corgi Executive-focused espionage often begins with social engineering, San Jose-based JPT Security notes, claiming bad actors “manufacture reasons to get close to a senior leader, their staff, or their family members.” With a sometimes controversial industry like AI, encounters can sometimes be hostile. Passersby stop daily outside the 24-hour San Francisco cafe run by AI insurance startup Corgi where they shout and curse, CEO Nico Laqua told WSJ in July. Some blame AI for rising rents and water use in the area, he said. 8 A protester holds an anti-AI sign outside an OpenAI office in Manhattan’s SoHo on Oct. 20, 2026, during “Freeze AI,” a nationwide day of walkouts organized by the advocacy group Irreplaceable calling for a pause on AI development. AI workers increasingly face anger in public. Getty Images 8 A man wears a jacket branded with Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI coding tool. Fans show off AI company swag, while Anthropic has all but banned branded merch for its own staff. Bloomberg via Getty Images In March, activists chalked the sidewalk outside OpenAI’s San Francisco offices urging employees to quit over the company striking a defense deal with the Pentagon. Messages included “Is it time to quit?” and “Will you spy on your neighbors?” CEO Sam Altman’s home in the city was also targeted twice in separate incidents in April 2026. One suspect threw a Molotov cocktail at his home then threatened to burn down the OpenAI HQ. Two days later two other suspects fired a shot outside his house. All three were arrested, charged and are awaiting trial. They have all pleaded not guilty. Anthropic disclosed in their IPO filing with the Securities and Exchange commission that it spent $2.7 million in “personal security services” for its CEO, Daroi Amodei. Meanwhile, the father of the Anthropic worker says his son has trouble figuring out who he can trust because of his status. “Whether you’re going to a party, looking for a partner or making friends, people focus on your company and your wealth,” he said. “They overlook your character and your values.” Filed under Anthropic future tech OpenAI silicon valley spy 10/26/26 Read Next Microsoft announces buyouts for 60K employees — quar... title: Vanity Fair stays mum despite facing lawsuit over explosive article claiming Jared Kushner oversaw secret Saudi, UAE slush fund
description: Vanity Fair was tight-lipped on its decision to publish a book excerpt accusing Jared Kushner of overseeing secret bank accounts funded by Middle Eastern leaders to the tune of at least $2B.
content: Media exclusive details Vanity Fair stays mum despite facing lawsuit over explosive article claiming Jared Kushner oversaw secret Saudi, UAE slush fund By Alexandra Steigrad Published Oct. 26, 2026, 5:04 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Vanity Fair was tight-lipped Monday on its decision to publish an inflammatory book excerpt accusing President Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner of overseeing secret bank accounts funded by Middle Eastern leaders to the tune of at least $2 billion — as questions about the piece’s accuracy and credibility mounted. The mag was silent despite Kushner lawyer Chad Mizelle’s demand that it take down the excerpt from journo Matthew Cole’s new book “Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East.” “We formally put Vanity Fair and Condé Nast on notice regarding the false and defamatory allegations published about our client, Jared Kushner,” Mizelle, a former Justice Department chief of staff, wrote on X Saturday. 5 Jared Kushner is hitting back over claims made in Matthew Cole’s new book, “Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East.” Bloomberg via Getty Images “Serious questions are now being raised about the credibility of this reporting, including by independent journalists,” he added. “Despite repeated requests, the author has failed to produce a single bank statement, wire transfer record, account number, or other verifiable evidence supporting these extraordinary accusations.” Explore More Charlie Kirk’s mother pushes back on Erika Kirk rumors, says she has ‘grown closer’ with widow Holy vestments now on par with Prada as Pope Leo tops ‘Vanity Fair’ best-dressed list Lindsay Clancy reporter sparks backlash for grinning at camera, forcing Vanity Fair to pull her credentials Vanity Fair never reached out to Kushner to fact-check the article or even ask him for comment before publishing the piece last Thursday, according to sources close to him. A Vanity Fair rep failed to answer a Post inquiry Monday asking why it didn’t reach out to Kushner or whether it did its own fact-checking of the piece — or simply relied on the book’s publisher, Simon & Schuster. Meanwhile, Kushner is expected to sue both Simon & Schuster and Cole as early as this week, with a potential suit against Vanity Fair to follow. 5 Jared Kushner slammed Matthew Cole’s new book on his alleged business dealings. Atria Books Simon & Schuster released Cole’s book on Sunday — two days ahead of the originally scheduled release date. In a Thursday letter to Vanity Fair and its parent Condé Nast, Kushner’s attorneys at Clare Locke LLP called the article “defamatory,” adding that the allegations against their client are “false” and “outrageous.” Kushner and his legal team pushed back hard on Simon & Schuster and Cole, denying the book’s claims in a separate 13-page letter. Kushner echoed the sentiment on X, writing Thursday: “The allegations made by this author are completely insane and never happened. “We denied every claim on the record, yet the author provided not a single shred of verifiable evidence to substantiate them,” he added. 5 Kushner and his lawyers are demanding that Vanity Fair take down its excerpt of Cole’s book. The mag’s editorial director Mark Guiducci is seen here. Getty Images for Vanity Fair 5 Kushner is prepping a lawsuit against publisher Simon & Schuster, claiming Matthew Cole’s latest book is defamatory. Matthew McDermott for NY Post In the excerpt, Cole alleged that Kushner oversaw secret bank accounts funded by leaders from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. At least $2 billion was allegedly funneled into accounts in Azerbaijan and with Israel’s Central Bank, with about half of the funds intended for Kushner’s “personal benefit,” according to the journo. But critics have questioned Cole’s reporting, with the Bank of Israel telling reporter Neria Krause that it was not aware of any such arrangement. Cole’s article even notes the central bank does not offer personal accounts. The article’s assertion that Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu played a role in accessing the purported central bank account drew scrutiny from Axios’ Barak Ravid, who noted accounts there “are under significant monitoring by career civil servants.” 5 The threat of a lawsuit against Condé Nast comes as the media company is scrambling to find a new permanent CEO. Gregory P. Mango The piece also claimed Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman moved “roughly $1 billion to Israel via Azerbaijan for Kushner.” It included a convoluted back-story in which Dutch spies allegedly cottoned on to a Russian scheme to monitor Kushner’s phone — leading the Dutch to track it, too, according to Cole. On Friday, The Jerusalem Post removed an article about Cole’s reporting, citing “significant factual questions about the alleged financial transactions.” This is not the first time Kushner has pushed back against questionable reporting. Earlier this month, he put out a lengthy “fact check” to a New Yorker piece that takes up “familiar accusations” linking his diplomatic efforts in the Trump administration to his own private equity firm’s bottom line. The latest controversy comes at a delicate time for Vanity Fair and Condé Nast, which is scrambling to hire a CEO after Roger Lynch resigned last month. Meanwhile, the magazine has come off a turbulent year under its new boundary-pushing editorial director Mark Guiducci, who got heat last year for hiring scandal-scarred political reporter Olivia Nuzzi. Nuzzi had been fired from New York Magazine in 2024 for not disclosing a relationship with then-2024 presidential candidate Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whom she interviewed for the glossy. Three months after landing the Vanity Fair gig, she was let go as a fresh wave of scandals were revealed by her ex-fiancé and fellow journalist Ryan Lizza. The Post has sought comment from Cole and Simon & Schuster. title: Fast Takes: Ilhan Omar’s dad’s dubious past, Trump’s sensible appeal and more
description: What we know about “Nur Omar Mohamed’s military career” in the Somali army makes it “very doubtful” that Rep. Ilhan Omar’s father “met the US legal definition of a ‘refugee’,” argues Jim Geraghty.…
content: Opinion editorial Fast Takes: Ilhan Omar’s dad’s dubious past, Trump’s sensible appeal and more By Post Editorial Board Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:56 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington, DC home was raided by Homeland Security agents over immigration fraud allegations. James Keivom for NY Post From the right: Omar Dad’s Dubious Past What we know about “Nur Omar Mohamed’s military career” in the Somali army makes it “very doubtful” that Rep. Ilhan Omar’s father “met the US legal definition of a ‘refugee’,” argues National Review’s Jim Geraghty. One obituary noted that his “prestigious career in the military ended in 1991 after the Barre regime was ousted.” Notes Geraghty: “The Somali government was using its military to commit genocide for the better part of three decades, intensifying in the late 1980s.” Credible sources discredit the notion that her father could “rise to the rank of colonel with no role in that military’s massive-scale genocide.” How was a Somali colonel “qualified as a refugee” when he may have “ordered, incited, assisted or otherwise participated in the persecution” of civilians? Midterm watch: Trump’s Sensible Appeal President Trump “has been widely mocked for asking voters to ‘pretend I’m on the ballot,’ ” notes the Washington Examiner’s Byron York. Yet appealing to “low-propensity voters” — such one ones who won’t normally vote unless Trump’s on the ballot — “makes sense.” A 2025 Pew Research study found eligible voters nationwide who didn’t vote in 2020 and ’22 but did in ’24 backed Trump 55%-41%. “This was not just a tiny group of people”: “2024-only voters made up 12% of the entire electorate in the presidential race that year. It made a big difference for Trump.” So, “if Republicans are trying to turn out low-propensity voters” now, “it makes sense to ask them to pretend that Trump is on the ballot.” More From Post Editorial Board Send Mamdani a message — vote ‘NO’ on all five New York City ballot proposals Europe’s leaders still refuse to face the far-left’s assault on civilization Ilhan Omar hurls the ‘genocide’ charge at Israel — but it belongs much closer to home From the left: Our Scammy Fundraising Problem “Democrats should think hard about” the “broad spectrum of sketchy fundraising behavior, from outright scams to bad ideas,” argues Slow Boring’s Matt Yglesias after getting a “rather absurd request” from Gov. Maura Healy (D-Mass.), who’s in zero danger of losing. People “acutely frightened about the state of our country” must “be smart with our resources, not throwing them at dumb stuff” like unwinnable or unlosable races, or ones without “large strategic implications.” Never forget: “People make money off of political campaigns” — “vendors and consultants” who “benefit specifically from donations” to candidates who’ve hired them, “even if other candidates would be a better use of your money.” And “outright scams” include “PACs that say they’re supporting candidates but mostly just fund themselves.” To keep “the small-donor engine running,” Democrats should be “giving donors some assurances that their money is being well spent.” Get opinions and commentary from our columnists Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter! Thanks for signing up! Enter your email address Please provide a valid email. By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Never miss a story. Check out more newsletters Conservative: Say No to Toxic Candidates The major political parties “keep force-feeding us s—t sandwiches and telling us to like them,” fumes Erick Erickson at The Free Press, and insisting that “we must debase ourselves a little further every cycle.” We’re told to “hold our noses” and “pull the lever” for “white nationalists, racists, and antisemites” and “crooks, frauds, charlatans, and those who’d attack the victim of molestation,” or else face “the end of America.” We “have heard that message every two years for 20 years,” but “America is still here” even as the “candidates keep getting worse.” No! Of every election requires us to swallow something rotten, we might as well starve.” America will never be made “great again” if we are “continually descending into the sewer to find candidates.” Foreign desk: DC Must Protect Machado María Corina Machado’s return to Venezuela “poses a challenge to the ruling regime of Delcy Rodríguez, but also to the Trump Administration,” frets The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Board. Machado had left “the country in fear for her life” but now as promised has returned “to participate in a transition back to democracy” following former President Nicolás Maduro’s arrest. But Rodríguez “refuses to set a date for new elections.” Amid that stall, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and President Trump must ensure Machado’s safety: “It’s all too easy to imagine her suddenly dying in a car ‘accident’ or from a mysterious illness” — and Trump’s Venezuelan oil deal “won’t be worth much unless Venezuela has a government with democratic legitimacy,” something “that should start with a date and a credible process for a free and fair democratic election.” — Compiled by The Post Editorial Board Filed under democrats donald trump editorial fast takes fundraising genocide Ilhan Omar midterm elections 2026 political action committees republicans somalia venezuela 10/26/26 Read Next Abdul El-Sayed ad is vile, unapologetically Nazi drivel bl... title: Unhinged NC state Senate candidate arrested after live-posting through police standoff: ‘I have 6 rounds and the high ground’
description: Jonathan D. Miller, the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina's 16th Senate District in the suburbs of Raleigh, was taken into custody Monday afternoon with no shots fired, WRAL reported.
content: US News Unhinged NC state Senate candidate arrested after live-posting through police standoff: ‘I have 6 rounds and the high ground’ By Jared Downing Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:52 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source An unhinged North Carolina state Senate candidate live-posted his own armed standoff with cops Monday, posting alarming updates from the woods as he claimed officers were closing in on him. Jonathan D. Miller, the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina’s 16th Senate District in the suburbs of Raleigh, was taken into custody Monday afternoon with no shots fired, WRAL reported. Miller began posting Sunday night that he intended to take his own life — then gave live updates when cops showed up to his apartment in Cary, outside Raleigh, Monday morning. Miller refused an order to keep his hands away from a pistol at his hip and then ran into some nearby woods, he told WRAL. 3 Jonathan D. Miller, he Libertarian candidate for North Carolina’s 16th Senate District. “The whole police department is chasing me with guns drawn. This should be fun,” he wrote on X after fleeing. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed Miller posted that he “has six shots and the high ground” as officers closed in, adding that he hoped police wouldn’t find him but that a confrontation would be “a hell of a show.” “I f—-d up and talked to the negotiator on the phone long enough for them to box me in. They have dogs so I’m probably done for,” he later wrote. Miller, who describes himself as a carpenter and former small-business owner, is running against a Democratic incumbent and a Republican contender in the Nov. 3 election. 3 Jonathan D. Miller, the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina’s 16th Senate District, posts updates while in an armed standoff with police. 3 Cops swarm around Miller’s apartment. WRAL He called a local news station during the standoff and explained his reasons for the suicidal threats. “Last night I was pretty depressed and suicidal, and I sort of put a suicide note on X, and it has gone quite viral … I spent all night crying, and angry, and upset, and depressed, and all the emotions. And this morning I was tired, but I had things I needed to do. And I didn’t kill myself,” he told WRAL. “So I got up and made coffee … and while I was having a cigarette, a police officer approached me, knew my name, saw that I had a holstered revolver on my hip, so he drew his weapon and told me to keep my hands away from mine. I told him I was going to refuse that order, and I backed away slowly until I was far enough away from him to turn and run, and then I turned and ran into the woods,” he continued. The Libertarian Party of North Carolina were “aware of the situation,” and thanked the Cary Police Department for “pursuing a solution without involving violence,” a spokesperson told The Post. The Party declined to comment on Miller’s condition and past or future involvement. If you are struggling with suicidal thoughts or are experiencing a mental health crisis and live in New York City, you can call 1-888-NYC-WELL for free and confidential crisis counseling. title: John Harbaugh has rescued the dysfunctional Giants — now comes the interesting part

content: New York Giants Mike Vaccaro John Harbaugh has rescued the dysfunctional Giants — now comes the interesting part By Mike Vaccaro Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:46 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. The Giants have been an unserious operation for years. From the moment they affixed Harbaugh’s signature to the bottom of his five-year, $100 million contract, that changed in theory. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. SIGN UP NOW It has changed in practice. Already. title: Hulk Hogan’s daughter lashes out with claim $5.9M family home was sold for ‘dirty money’
description: Hulk Hogan's daughter, Brooke Hogan, took aim at someone who she claimed is responsible for the sale of the late wrestling legend's Clearwater, Fla. home in a series of emotional Instagram Stories on Sunday.
content: Wrestling Hulk Hogan’s daughter lashes out with claim $5.9M family home was sold for ‘dirty money’ By Jenna Lemoncelli Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:37 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Hulk Hogan’s daughter, Brooke Hogan, took aim at someone who she claimed is responsible for the $5.9 million sale of the late wrestling legend’s Clearwater, Fla. home in a series of emotional Instagram Stories on Sunday. Hulk, whose real name is Terry Bollea, died of a heart attack at age 71 in July 2025 at his home. Brooke shared a photo of Hulk’s home with a “sold” sign. 6 Brooke Hogan and Hulk Hogan. Instagram/Brooke Hogan Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance “Enjoy your dirty money,” she wrote. “You took my dad.” It’s unclear who exactly Brooke is referencing with her claim. Brooke, 38, explained that her and Hulk’s second ex-wife, Jennifer McDaniel, were the “nurse crew” that took care of the WWE legend. McDaniel and Hogan were married from 2010-21. 6 Jennifer McDaniel (left) and Brooke Hogan (right). Instagram/Brooke Hogan “The sick feeling is indescribable,” Brooke wrote. “This house was where dad and Jen envisioned growing old together. Where we brought him back to … surgery after surgery. Pool days. The smell of gasoline in the his garage. His workouts downstairs. “We cooked, we watched Jerry Springer, we played music , we cried. I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he’d open the garage door. I’d sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in. “His whole environment, his energy, his work, his relationships: First Jen – who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone… the truth teller… I’m sure to everyone’s delight. And now it’s all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him… used for f–king everyone else’s gain. Saddest ending I’ve ever seen. You know who the f–k you are.” Brooke, who shared past photos of her and Hulk, explained that she was there for him for 15 years before “vultures swooped in conveniently,” adding that she tracked every medication he had to take. 6 Hulk Hogan’s daughter, Brooke Hogan, shared a scathing message after the alleged sale of his Florida home on her Instagram Story. Brooke Hogan/Instagram 6 Brooke Hogan with her dad, Hulk Hogan in the hospital. Instagram/Brooke Hogan Brooke, who asked to be removed for Hulk’s will in the summer of 2023, went on to praise Jennifer and shared photos of the pair caring for Hulk at home and at the hospital. “This woman spent more time in the trenches than ANY of us did,” Brooke wrote of Jennifer. “He LOVED her dearly. And she loved him. She wanted to be there till his last breath despite the trauma she endured that I witnessed .. She asked for nothing .She could have fought for money. She left with a tiny fraction, a Tahoe, and a 2 bedroom house. And vanished. No smear campaign. Just grace. “… Their breakup was devastating for me. I loved her, but I knew my dad was in the best care with her too. “… An I’ve had to hear everyone say I’m the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior an brainwashing, fake greedy people… ‘I should have been there. Everyone else’ was there till the end. 6 Brooke Hogan said she tracked her dad, Hulk Hogan’s, medications and shared an image of a pill body. Instagram/Brooke Hogan “NO. They were there AT the end. To collect.” Hulk and Jennifer were married in December 2010 at his home in Clearwater, and he filed for divorce in October 2021. In February 2022, he shared that they were divorced in a post on X. Hulk married Sky Daily in September 2023. 6 Hulk Hogan and Sky Daily. Instagram/Sky Daily Hulk and his first wife, Linda, were married for 26 years before their divorce was finalized in 2009. They share Brooke and son, Nick Hogan. Hulk’s manner of death was ruled natural, according to the Pinellas County Forensic Science Center records obtained by Page Six. The report also stated that Hogan had leukemia and atrial fibrillation, or an irregular heartbeat. title: Giants’ John Harbaugh declares himself ‘day-to-day’ after getting tackled by Devin Singletary: ‘I just felt so weak’
description: Harbaugh was able to laugh off the mishap in part because it came immediately following another victory for the NFC East-leading Giants.
content: NFL New York Giants Giants’ John Harbaugh declares himself ‘day-to-day’ after getting tackled by Devin Singletary: ‘I just felt so weak’ By Dan Martin Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:31 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source John Harbaugh proclaimed himself “day-to-day” Monday after the head coach was tackled by Devin Singletary following Singletary’s game-winning touchdown in the Giants’ 27-21 overtime win in Houston on Sunday. Harbaugh was able to laugh off the mishap in part because it came immediately following another victory for the NFC East-leading Giants as they head into a bye week, but the coach, in his first year with the Giants, acknowledged it was not his finest moment on the field. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW “It’s so terrible,” Harbaugh said with a smile on a Monday Zoom call. “As I was going down, all I could think was I just felt like a total non-athlete, over the hill [and] washed up. I don’t know. I just felt so weak, so pathetic.” That embarrassment didn’t last long, as Harbaugh will take any win, no matter how it looks or what happens in the aftermath — including getting pulled to the ground by Singletary, whose 30-yard scoring run ended the game and moved them to 4-2-1. “Once we were on the ground, laughing and enjoying the moment and celebrating the football joy moment of a touchdown run, it made all the sense in the world,” Harbaugh said of the tackle. “It was just a great moment… We talked with our team about football joy. We talked about playing with joy. What is football joy? It’s different than other kinds of joy… Football joy is kind of gritty, kind of tough. That was a football joy moment. That’s why we do it. That’s why the fans love it.” Harbaugh tackles Singletary after OT Win 🙌 Singletary gets tackled by his coach after game-winning TD pic.twitter.com/wHpduP4wOv — New York Post Sports (@nypostsports) October 25, 2026 Giants running back Devin Singletary (26) tackles head coach John Harbaugh to the ground after a win over the Texans on Oct. 25, 2026. title: Ex-NJ cop’s son reveals new strategy to get him off the hook for murder of 2 girls in wealthy town
description: The New Jersey teen accused of fatally ramming into two high school girls with a Jeep last year plans to use an insanity defense at trial, it was revealed in court Monday.
content: Metro Ex-NJ cop’s son reveals new strategy to get him off the hook for murder of 2 girls in wealthy town By Fenix Suriel and Priscilla DeGregory Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:28 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source The teenage son of an ex New Jersey cop who is accused of murdering two high school girls in a hit-and-run with his Jeep last year plans to use the insanity defense, his lawyers revealed in court Monday. Vincent Battiloro’s attorneys told a judge that they would bring up the teen’s mental health to try to get him off the hook for killing 17-year-old Cranford High School seniors Maria Niotis and Isabella Salas on Sept. 29, 2025. “The court has received … the notice of defenses that you have put forward of diminished capacity and insanity,” Union County Judge Lisa Walsh said. 5 Vincent Battiloro appears at his arraignment in Union County Court, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. Battiloro, the son of a police officer, allegedly stalked and ran over Maria Niotis and Isabella Salas with his truck while they were riding an electric bike in Cranford. Gregory P. Mango for NY Post “Thank you, your honor,” responded Batttiloro’s lawyer, Rubin Sinins. Sinins entered a plea of not guilty on Battiloro’s behalf during the minutes-long hearing in an Elizabeth courtroom, where his client appeared stone-faced, wearing khaki jail clothes and handcuffed at the front of his body. Explore More One dead, at least three injured in NJ vigil shooting: report Another Royal Caribbean cruise reroutes from sunny hotspot to chilly Canada — which is shockingly legal: experts Sobbing moms stare down stoned-face teen accused of stalking, running down daughters in wealthy NJ town Meanwhile, the moms of Niotis and Salas sobbed and stared Battiloro down in the courtroom as they wore t-shirts with photos of their daughters that said, “Justice for Bella and Maria.” 5 Maria Niotis and Isabella Salas were allegedly killed by Battiloro. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Battiloro, the son of a retired cop and nephew of a local police chief, is accused of stalking Niotis for months before the alleged murders, lawyers for the victims claimed. The then-17-year-old Garwood teen was allegedly out for revenge after Niotis reported him to the police and got him suspended from school for harassing and stalking her, and her family, according to prosecutors. The parents for Battiloro, now 18, had also called the cops on him four times in the weeks before the killings, asking for advice from the police on how to handle their troubled son. His own dad claimed Battiloro sprayed him in the face with mace and took his car, according to prosecutors. 5 Battiloro allegedly stalked Maria Niotis for months leading up to the alleged murders. Outside of court Monday, Salas family lawyer, Cory Rothbort told reporters he wasn’t surprised Battiloro planned to use the diminished capacity and insanity defenses. “I don’t think that surprises anyone,” Rothbort said. “That’s their strategy. That’s their tactic. We prepared the families for that.” Still, “It doesn’t take away the grief,” Rothbort said. Niotis family lawyer Brent Bramnick said, “they’re going to use every possible way they can to defend themselves.” During the hearing, Sinins also said the defense would be seeking to have Battiloro’s case moved to a different jurisdiction, in part because of the media attention it has gotten. 5 Foula Niotis, left, and Mary Salas, right, the mothers of two daughters killed last year, sit in court during the arraignment of Vincent Battiloro at the Union County Courthouse. Gregory P. Mango for NY Post “There have been things that happened in the public eye as well as in the media since the outset of this case that already give rise for the basis of the motion,” Sinins said of his intention to ask for the case to be moved to another court. Jillian Reyes, with the Union County Prosecutor’s Office, told the judge her office wasn’t offering any plea deal to Battiloro. “At this point in time, the state is not giving an offer to the defense,” Reyes said. Battiloro faces up to life in prison if convicted on the two counts of murder he faces. 5 Maria Niotis, left, and Isabella Salas were 17-year-old seniors at Cranford High School. Facebook/Mary Salas The teen was initially charged as a juvenile but this summer a judge approved the case getting tried in adult court. Monday was Battiloro’s first in-person appearance. The day of the killings, Battiloro allegedly got into his Jeep and parked near one of the girls’ homes in Cranford, prosecutors claimed. Battiloro saw the duo riding e-bikes in the opposite direction down the quiet road of the affluent town, before he whipped his car around and floored it, mowing them down at 70 mph in a 25-mph zone, prosecutors claimed. He fled on foot and was arrested that day but was released mere hours later into his dad’s care. Battiloro was then arrested again two days later. The lawyers for the victims’ families Monday called for the state attorney general’s office to probe if cops improperly handled Battiloro’s case because of his family cop ties. Battiloro’s dad, Jeffrey Battiloro, is a retired Chatham Borough cop and his uncle is a police chief near Westfield. title: Trump offers $1M for voter fraud reports 8 days before midterms, suggests Brazil election ‘rigged’
description: Trump also said that the Brazilian election, in which President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term, "looked so corrupt, so terrible" while calling a two-hour voting extension "very strange."
content: Politics Trump offers $1M for voter fraud reports 8 days before midterms, suggests Brazil election ‘rigged’ By Steven Nelson Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:27 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source WASHINGTON — President Trump offered $1 million Monday to anyone whose tips about voter fraud lead to convictions — as he ripped Sunday’s triumph by Brazil’s leftist leader as “another rigged election.” “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!” Trump wrote in a social media post shortly before departing the White House for a pre-midterms rally in Mississippi. The president explained to reporters moments later that he was “going to be issuing a million-dollar bonus or reward or whatever you want to call it for anybody that reports voter fraud leading to the arrest and conviction of somebody.” “We give you, that person, a million dollars,” he added under the wing of Air Force One. President Trump speaks to the press before boarding Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland en route to a midterm rally in Mississippi on Oct. 26, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Trump also said that the Brazilian election, in which President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in an upset after promising government handouts, “looked so corrupt, so terrible” while calling a two-hour voting extension “very strange.” Explore More White House defends Trump after archbishop calls prayer moment ‘manipulated’ ahead of midterms Trump blasts Senate for not making daylight saving permanent, jokes clock changes makes him late DHS suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals amid birth tourism, security concerns Lula, as he is commonly known, defeated conservative Flavio Bolsonaro by more than 4 million votes. In 2023, a mob claiming fraud ransacked Brazil’s legislature after Flavio’s father, Jair Bolsonaro, lost to Lula by a narrower margin. Trump’s Truth Social post about putting a bounty on election fraud from Oct. 26, 2026. Truth Social Trump did not specify a particular reporting mechanism to potentially receive the new financial award. Last week, the Justice Department rolled out a new bounty of $30,000 for tips that lead to fraud charges, with an emphasis on social services. Voter fraud charges are relatively rare. The conservative Heritage Foundation’s election-fraud database lists just 557 proven instances nationally between 2016 and 2025, with that figure including criminal convictions or other judicial or official findings. The Justice Department has increased its attention to the matter recently, particularly focusing on deterring non-citizen voting. The DOJ announced 48 such indictments Monday, while 16 others were made public Oct. 12. Trump alleged that voter fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election, though no courts upheld his claim — and the president’s own supporters have on occasion been busted. A 32-year-old Trump supporter was sentenced in July to six months of house arrest, three years of probation and $6,200 in fines for voting in both Pennsylvania and Florida in 2020. title: Luka Doncic exploded for 52 points — but his defense is what spurred the Lakers’ comeback over Jazz
description: Luka Doncic’s defense deserves more (positive) attention.
content: NBA Luka Doncic exploded for 52 points — but his defense is what spurred the Lakers’ comeback over Jazz By Khobi Price Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:27 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source SALT LAKE CITY — Luka Doncic’s offensive flurry to close out the Lakers’ comeback road win over the Jazz on Sunday drew all of the attention. And understandably so. His 52 points at Delta Center are the most scored by a player so far in the 2026-27 season. 3 Luka Doncic has the highest-scoring game by a player so far this season. NBAE via Getty Images The trio of 3-pointers he hit in the final few minutes of the game were all consequential: The first tied at the game at 116 apiece with just over four minutes left; the second gave the Lakers a five-point lead with 2:22 left in the game; and the third not only gave Doncic’s team a 127-121 lead with 1:42 left, but also gave him his 10th career 50-point game (third as a Laker). And that’s not even factoring in him assisting Austin Reaves on a 3 that iced the game, putting the Lakers up 130-123 with 34 seconds left while Doncic and Reaves taunted the crowd. Explore More Pat McAfee vows not to return to University of Utah: ‘I was very uncomfortable’ Saquon Barkley suffers new injury in disastrous Eagles return Giants reveal rookie kicker’s fate after ugly performance But it was his contributions on the less glamorous end of the floor that put the Lakers in the positions they were in to come back from an 18-point deficit. In the midst of the Slovenian superstar’s offensive onslaught was one of the biggest defensive plays of the game. After making the 3 that tied the game at 116, the 6-foot-8 guard slid into the proper help defensive position to take a charge against Keyonte George driving into the paint before the Jazz guard could make the kickout pass to Doncic’s man, Ace Bailey, in the corner. 3 Luka Doncic drawing a charge against Keyonte George was a game-changing play late in the fourth quarter. Getty Images Doncic made a pair of free throws on the Lakers’ ensuing possession after drawing a foul to give his team a lead they held for the remainder of the game. “At the end of the day, he’s a competitor, he wants to win,” Walker Kessler said. “He wants to do what it takes to win. That charge was not only a great play, but just a great momentum change.” Doncic had a momentum-changing defensive play earlier in the game that led to an immediate offensive payoff. He closed out the second quarter by stripping Bailey on his drive to the rim before hitting a pull-up 3, giving the Lakers a 74-71 lead going into halftime after they trailed by 18 earlier in the quarter. 3 Luka Doncic’s stepback 3 over Ace Bailey to close out the first half wouldn’t have happen without the defensive stop he made beforehand. AP Photo/Bethany Baker Coach JJ Redick said Doncic’s 3-pointer right halftime was when he realized he found his offensive rhythm. But that 3 doesn’t come without the defensive stop and playmaking that preceded it. “I told him this earlier [on Sunday]: Defensively, he’s been really good,” Redick said. “He didn’t start the game with the right physicality on Bailey. He’ll own all that stuff. As the game progressed, it was the defensive version of Luka that we love to see.” Doncic acknowledged his subpar defensive play earlier in the game, particularly boxing out Bailey, who had five of his six offensive rebounds in the first quarter. “Ace Bailey got like three offensive rebounds on me, so that was my bad point,” he said, “But otherwise, pretty solid.” But he made a significant defensive turnaround just in time to lead the Lakers to their straight win. title: Dollar chain faces FTC lawsuit for ‘long-running deceptive’ practices — multiple states join in
description: The states and FTC claim that Dollar General had “extensive corporate knowledge of the problem.”
content: US News Dollar chain faces FTC lawsuit for ‘long-running deceptive’ practices — multiple states join in By Associated Press Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:17 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source The Federal Trade Commission has sued the bargain chain Dollar General for what it characterized as “long-running deceptive pricing practices” by charging customers more once they reach the register than the prices that are displayed on shelves and in advertisements. Twenty states joined in the complaint, filed by the US District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee. It said that Dollar General failed to correct the issue despite what it said was “extensive corporate knowledge of the problem.” Dollar General have been sued by the FTC and 20 US states for “deceptive pricing practices.” AP Photo/Charles Krupa The lawsuit claims that Dollar General would charge customers more at checkout than what was listed on shelves and advertisements. REUTERS “Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last,” wrote Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection. Dollar General, based in Goodlettsville, Tennessee, just outside of Nashville, did not immediately return a request for comment from The Associated Press. description: “When I posted this, I was like, ‘They’re going to think we planted this. It was fake.’ But it’s real,” he said.
content: US News Magnet fisherman makes shocking discovery while casting for treasures: ‘Why was it in the water?’ By Jared Downing Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:17 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source A family that lost their loved one’s cremation box in a river was finally reunited with it — thanks to a magnet fisherman. Lucas McGuire, 24, of Rome, Georgia, made the shocking discovery while rooting around the water for his lost line and magnet, which he had accidentally dropped while casting for metallic treasures at the bottom of the Oostanaula River. “I was really upset because it was a $400 magnet. So I got my wet suit on, got in, and that’s when I found this box,” McGuire told The Post last week. McGuire then set out to track down the dead person’s family. “I got this feeling, this is someone’s loved one. Why was it in the water? I felt like I had to find them,” he said. McGuire’s family happens to be in the funeral business and used an ID tag from the box to eventually locate the deceased woman’s kin. 5 Magnet fisherman Lucas McGuire finds a box of human ashes in a Georgia river. 5 McGuire stumbles on the discovery during an equipment mishap. 5 The fisherman is shocked by what he finds. The fisherman had discovered the box in 2022 and got it back in the right hands months later, but only recently posted about the ordeal on his OutdoorsWithLucas Facebook page. The woman’s family declined to speak to The Post, but her daughter told McGuire they were overjoyed to have the remains located. “I am still so incredibly grateful for your honesty and kindness,” she told McGuire in a recent text message. McGuire — who now works in the funeral business with his dad — said he is just happy he could be in the right place at the right time. “When I posted this, I was like, ‘They’re going to think we planted this. title: 4 unusual ways daylight saving time ending can harm your health — and how to minimize the damage
description: An expert shares how the extra hour of sleep may come at a cost to your brain, heart and blood sugar — especially if you have certain health conditions.
content: Health 4 unusual ways daylight saving time ending can harm your health — and how to minimize the damage By Patrice Peck Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:13 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source The clock is falling back — and your health might, too. The end of daylight saving time (DST) on Nov. 1 gives us an extra hour to snooze, a welcome perk, considering quality shuteye is essential to good health. But experts warn the time change can actually take a devastating toll on certain groups of people. That extra hour could have a not-so-cozy impact on your physical health. Graphicroyalty – stock.adobe.com For most healthy people, gaining an additional hour of sleep isn’t a huge deal. A healthy body will naturally reset within a few days to a week by soaking in morning sunlight and sticking to one’s usual social routines. Explore More Cocaine, affairs, $200K phone bills and private jet fast food detours: The rise and fall of CrossFit’s cult-like founder A game-changing new treatment just arrived for one of the deadliest cancers — here’s why doctors are so excited Men battling baldness may soon have a new pill to turn to Dementia may worsen However, shifting the clock can be much harder for others, including people with dementia. According to Dr. Courtney Stefanski, DST changes can disrupt already-vulnerable biological clocks, leading to broken sleep, restless nights and extra confusion. To ease this transition, Stefanski suggests getting into the morning light, using bright indoor lighting in the late afternoon and sticking to evening routines. “If confusion or agitation increases, reduce background noise, offer reassurance and check for potential triggers such as pain, dehydration or hunger,” she advised, though any sudden or significant changes in confusion should be examined by a healthcare professional. Heart health could take a hit Sleep is particularly crucial for a healthy heart because your blood pressure naturally drops and rests while you sleep. Shifting the clock can be much harder for those living with certain medical conditions, including dementia and cardiovascular issues. nenetus – stock.adobe.com That means that even a minor disruption to your sleep schedule can alter your heart rate and blood pressure if you already struggle with cardiovascular issues. When the clock changes, Stefanski suggests cutting back on caffeine late in the day, keeping up with regular blood pressure checks and sticking to one’s medication schedule as normal. She added that any confusion regarding medication timing after the time change should be cleared up by a healthcare provider, not resolved through self-adjustment. Blood sugar can go off track Your body’s internal clock also dictates how you process sugar and react to insulin, which can make DST changes especially tricky if you’re living with diabetes. A good way to handle the time shift is to proactively align your meals and medicine with the new clock time while sticking closely to your overall treatment plan. See Also Why permanent daylight saving time may be better for your health — as Congress revisits clock change Stefanski recommends that if you use insulin, a continuous glucose monitor or a blood glucose meter, you should continue to monitor it as recommended by your diabetes care team and watch for readings outside your usual range. But if you are unsure how to adjust insulin or other medication timing, seek guidance from your diabetes clinician or pharmacist rather than changing doses yourself. Fall risks rise Older adults, especially those with mobility or balance problems, need to take extra care during this transition. Disrupted sleep can make you tired and unsteady during the day, Stefanski points out, which raises the risk of falls, particularly if taking medication that causes drowsiness or dizziness. Falls are the leading cause of fatal and nonfatal injuries for adults aged 65 and older, affecting 1 in 4 older adults — over 14 million people — each year, according to the CDC. But many are preventable. “To improve evening and overnight safety, use nightlights, keep pathways clear and essential items within reach, and sit on the edge of the bed before standing if prone to lightheadedness,” said Stefanski, a board-certified physical medicine and rehabilitation physician, in partnership with Opera Beds. “Seek medical advice for new dizziness, unsteadiness or falls, and consult a healthcare professional before making any medication changes.” Sleep Better Tonight Editor’s Pick Sports Research Sleep Complex Skip the grogginess. title: Three stranded on exposed 8,600ft California mountain summit — as daring rescue launched
description: A search and rescue operation was launched after one stranded hiker's Garmin inReach satellite communicator sent out an SOS alert from Sierra Buttes.
content: California News Three stranded on exposed 8,600ft California mountain summit — as daring rescue launched By Sheetal Banchariya Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:07 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source A satellite communicator saved the lives of three hikers stranded on an 8,600-foot summit in the Tahoe National Forest. The Sierra County Sheriff’s Office launched a search and rescue operation after one of their Garmins sent out an SOS alert from Sierra Buttes around 2:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials called in mutual aid from Nevada County’s Search and Rescue Mountain Rescue Team and Washoe County’s RAVEN helicopter unit. title: Another Royal Caribbean cruise reroutes from sunny hotspot to chilly Canada — which is shockingly legal: experts
description: A second Royal Caribbean cruise has been rerouted from its intended tropical destination to chilly Canada this month – and there's shockingly little recourse for upset customers, per industry experts.
content: US News Another Royal Caribbean cruise reroutes from sunny hotspot to chilly Canada — which is shockingly legal: experts By Georgia Worrell Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:06 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source Two Royal Caribbean cruises have been rerouted from their intended tropical destination to chilly Canada because of nasty weather so far this month — and there’s shockingly little recourse for upset customers, industry experts told The Post. Last weekend, vacationers expecting a five-night Bermuda getaway onboard the cruise liner’s Independence of the Seas were suddenly slapped with a whole new plan: They were sailing to Saint John, New Brunswick, instead, according to a last-minute email sent to passengers and obtained by the Royal Caribbean Blog. The 3,858-passenger vessel was rerouted because of inclement weather off the East Coast – just hours before it was scheduled to embark from New Jersey’s Cape Liberty on Saturday, the outlet reported. 3 Last weekend, vacationers expecting a five-night Bermuda getaway onboard the Royal Caribbean’s Independence of the Seas were suddenly informed they would be sailing to Canada instead. be free – stock.adobe.com “Make sure you pack some light sweaters and clothing for cooler temps, the current forecast is in the mid-50s during the day in port,” Royal Caribbean wrote to passengers who, up until that point, had expected to enjoy Bermuda’s balmy climate. The company’s latest itinerary overhaul comes after more than 5,000 passengers expecting a week of fun in the sun in the Bahamas instead found themselves headed for Halifax, Nova Scotia, after bad weather forced their cruise to change course on Oct. 18. Explore More Trump admin slams CBS for leaving out ‘absurd bit of fraud’ from ‘60 Minutes’ profile of deported husband and father Mom arrested for leaving 4 kids — ages 9 to 14 — home alone during work trip to Vegas New details emerge after United ‘hijacking’ threat — as 25-year-old suspect’s chilling messages are revealed Actress Mikayla Iverson and other passengers from that voyage expressed frustration about not being given enough notice of the switch-up, which cost them the opportunity to trade in their bathing suits for winter boots. “Just got told after landing in Newark that our family Bahamas cruise leaving in literally 12 hours, we will now be going to Nova Scotia?!? And that we will not be allowed to leave the ship all week. @royalcaribbean, we don’t have the clothes for this,” Iverson wrote in an Instagram video that racked up a whopping 1.5 million views. Aside from expressing their outrage, there is little that disgruntled passengers can do in such situations, according to industry experts. 3 Earlier this month, more than 5,000 passengers expecting a week of fun in the sun in the Bahamas instead found themselves headed for Halifax, Nova Scotia, aboard another Royal Caribbean cruise liner. Matthew Latham/Wirestock – stock.adobe.com “Cruise lines basically have broad authority to alter itineraries if due to several factors, but primarily due to weather…or other circumstances that put the ship in a safety issue or something like that,” veteran cruise journalist David Yeskel told The Post. “So there’s a cruise line contract that every guest signs – but nobody reads, because it’s very long – when they’re buying their ticket, whereby they agree to this clause as well as other clauses,” he explained, adding that the clause was “standard across the industry.” In “extreme examples” of this clause coming into play, such as during the recent Royal Caribbean reroutes, impacted customers are often left with no other choice but to accept the company’s offers in exchange for the inconvenience, Yeskel said. During both of those voyages, the cruise liner offered onboard credits ranging from $100 to $600 per person depending on guests’ stateroom category, according to the Royal Caribbean Blog. Passengers onboard the rerouted Bahamas trip were also given 50% off a future cruise with the company. “We truly appreciate your understanding and flexibility regarding this unexpected change,” the company’s letter read, per the outlet. “I think it was fair under the circumstances,” Yeskel said about those offerings. 3 Longtime maritime attorney Frank Spagnoletti encouraged disappointed Royal Caribbean customers to band together and consult a lawyer about their rights. CTV News Longtime maritime attorney Frank Spagnoletti, on the other hand, blasted Royal Caribbean for its “discourteous disregard of their passengers” – whom he said the company treats “like maritime property” instead of paying guests. Despite the language in any cruise liner contract, Spagnoletti encouraged disappointed customers to band together and consult a lawyer about their rights. “Even though [cruise companies] put that kind of language in [contracts], when they try to enforce it like that – not really giving you a choice – you can challenge it,” he said. “You know, there are 4,000 people on that vessel. So if you aggregate a thousand of them or 500 of them, then it makes it economically viable to try to correct the problem by bringing in the law,” the Houston-based attorney continued. The Post reached out to Royal Caribbean for comment. Several other Royal Caribbean cruises embarking from the New York metro area were delayed and saw their itineraries altered during a powerful nor’easter that ravaged the East Coast last month. title: Trump fires back at Obama over ‘Cheesecake Factory’ jab about White House: ‘Shows why you were a lousy president’
description: The president also claimed Obama allowed the White House to fall into disrepair during his eight years in office.
content: Politics Trump fires back at Obama over ‘Cheesecake Factory’ jab about White House: ‘Shows why you were a lousy president’ By Emily Goodin Published Oct. 26, 2026, 4:02 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make New York Post a Preferred Source WASHINGTON — President Trump fired back Monday at Barack Obama’s weekend jab comparing Trump’s White House renovations to a branch of The Cheesecake Factory, claiming his predecessor did not take proper care of the historic residence. “For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory — that just shows why you were a lousy president,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews before departing on a campaign trip to Mississippi. “We have to explain that to Obama because he doesn’t understand it because he’s not a smart guy,” the president continued. “He’s not smart at all because of the way he ran the country. Only a stupid person would run the country like that.” 5 President Trump, seen in Michigan on Oct. 25, 2026, blasted former President Barack Obama’s comments about his White House renovations. AP Photo/Duane Burleson 5 Obama, seen at a rally for Democratic Ohio Senate candidate Sherrod Brown in Cleveland on Oct. 24, 2026, said Trump’s changes have the “White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki 5 Trump holds a rendering of the planned White House Ballroom on Oct. 22, 2025. Bloomberg via Getty Images Trump also claimed Obama allowed the White House to fall into disrepair during his eight years in office. “He doesn’t notice dirt and filth that hadn’t been cleaned, where the walls hadn’t been cleaned for years. He doesn’t notice areas that haven’t been painted,” Trump said. “Guys like Obama don’t see it. You don’t see dirt. He doesn’t see filth. He doesn’t see broken ornaments on a building.” Explore More White House defends Trump after archbishop calls prayer moment ‘manipulated’ ahead of midterms Trump blasts Senate for not making daylight saving permanent, jokes clock changes makes him late DHS suspends visa-free travel program for Chinese nationals amid birth tourism, security concerns 5 Trump meets with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in his redecorated Oval Office on Oct. 22, 2025. AFP via Getty Images The president defended his renovation work — which has included tearing down the East Wing to build a ballroom, repairing and repainting the North Portico columns of the residence, paving over the Rose Garden and blinging out the Oval Office in gold wall fixtures — as necessary for proper upkeep. “I’ve taken care of the White House. I fixed it with the finest artisans in the world,” he said. “We have to explain to Obama that the White House is a symbol of America, and it has to be maintained properly.” Even the White House’s official X account weighed in, poking fun at the restaurant’s massive menu – which averages about 20 pages and 250 items. “Since we’re talking about The Cheesecake Factory … The only thing bigger than the menu is the list of President Trump’s accomplishments,” it posted along with a photo of a mock menu offering a list of “accomplishments” options, including more than one million private sector jobs created and no taxes on tips or overtime. Obama, while campaigning for Democrats in Ohio Saturday, told supporters Trump “should be on HGTV” due to his focus on construction. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” added the 44th president, who has faced his own criticism over the design of his post-presidential library and museum on the South Side of Chicago. 5 Trump shows Chinese President Xi Jinping the revamped White House Presidential Walk of Fame on Sept. 24, 2026. White House The towering, disk-shaped, concrete-and-stone building has been mocked by some wags as an “Obamalisk” and likened to the Death Star space station from “Star Wars.” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent responded to Obama’s comments Monday by visiting a Cheesecake Factory in Washington, DC for lunch. “This is the man who built the museum who looks like Darth Vader’s tomb,” the South Carolina native told reporters. “I had a great meal. I always have a great meal. I would tell the Martha’s Vineyard set to give it a try.” The Obamas own a home on the tony island off the coast of Massachusetts, where there is no Cheesecake Factory outlet. title: Airbnb hosts throw tantrums over strict rule changes as site loses its shine
description: They're taking their spare keys and going home.
content: Lifestyle Airbnb hosts throw tantrums over strict rule changes as site loses its shine By Bianca Zalben Published Oct. 26, 2026, 3:58 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Make California Post a Preferred Source They’re taking their spare keys and going home. Airbnb hosts around the world are hopping mad over the short-term rental giant’s sudden, sweeping crackdown on onerous demands made of customers — a move that appears to have sparked a global revolt, with many landlords threatening to leave the platform for good. The new rules rolled out by the tech titan take effect Nov. 20 — and will generally prohibit hosts from requiring guests to complete housekeeping tasks like washing dishes, stripping beds, starting laundry or hauling garbage off-site. Airbnb’s message to operators was brutally simple: Stop making vacationers do the job of a maid, especially after pocketing money for cleaning fees. Pixavril – stock.adobe.com “When adding a request, remember that most guests want to avoid unexpected chores,” the company warned hosts. “Asking them to do things a cleaner should handle can negatively affect their stay and your reviews.” Rather than take a hint, property holders are staging a hissy on Airbnb’s in-house community forums — wailing that the new rules will turn their cash-cow rentals into animal houses. Getty Images/iStockphoto “They will rob us of toilet paper, destroy our towels and linens, leave holes and dents in walls,” one Airbnb host wrote, first reported by SFGATE. “And now you are ALLOWING guests to come in and be slobs.” As a result, some say they’re prepared to take their business elsewhere. “I get the feeling that Airbnb is asking me to leave the platform and look for alternative solutions, because everything is getting worse,” one host in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, fumed in an Airbnb community discussion. 3 Visitors can be asked to put dirty dishes in the sink, gather used towels, separate recycling and switch off air conditioning before leaving the property. Portland Press Herald via Getty Images “We do NOT agree with the new house rules and call on Airbnb to withdraw them,” another host in Switzerland wrote. “Every day, we ask Airbnb in writing how we should deal with mice, rats, and vermin when trash is left in the house. How is kitchen hygiene to be maintained if dishes are left dirty?” See Also Airbnb bans ‘unreasonable’ requests like cleaning dishes, stripping beds “We already pay professional cleaners to prepare our home for the next guests,” a Fair Oaks, California host chimed in. “Your new policy will increase cleaning costs, create additional work, and ultimately contribute to higher rental rates.” The uproar isn’t just about scrubbing pots and pans. Under the overhaul, Airbnb is limiting hosts to seven categories of standard house rules — any additional instructions must qualify as reasonable requests, the company said. Still, guests won’t be entirely banned from lifting a finger. According to the new rules, visitors can be asked to put dirty dishes in the sink, gather used towels, separate recycling and switch off air conditioning before leaving the property. The rebellion comes as sentiment has increasingly soured around the once-beloved home-sharing platform. What originally launched as a budget-friendly way to travel has over time become known as a corporate juggernaut. Costs have soared in many cities, add-on fees have become the norm, with commercial operators listing scores of pricey managed flats flooding many markets, crowding out the mom-and-pop energy that once fueled the site and made it so popular. None of this appears to have stopped the company from excelling — Airbnb just announced one of its best growth quarters in years. But while bookings aren’t evaporating, the way people feel about the experience has changed significantly; many hailed the recent announcement, saying they’re tired of paying resort prices, only to be treated like unpaid janitors before check out. “That is what gets me,” a disgruntled guest wrote on Reddit. “Either ask me to clean OR charge me a cleaning fee. The scandal is the latest chapter in a disastrous saga for the San Francisco Bay Area district, which granted Rudolph a $98,259 taxpayer-funded payout to resign quietly in November 2024 without suing. title: Fighters exploited & forgotten in failing system - Smith
description: Fighters are being "hurt, exploited or forgotten" in a failing system, says former boxer Paul Smith, who has criticised a lack of support for athletes.
content: Fighters exploited & forgotten in failing system - Smith Image source, Martin Rose/Bongarts/Getty Images Image caption, Former British champion Paul Smith is one of the key people behind the initiative ByPaul Battison BBC Sport Journalist Published 26 October 2026 Fighters are being "hurt, exploited or forgotten" in a failing system, says former boxer Paul Smith, who has criticised a lack of support for athletes. Smith is part of a team set up to represent fighters and safeguard their futures, with the group aiming to launch the "biggest ever inquiry into health and safety in combat sport". The group, called the Global Fighters' Association (GFA), wants the inquiry to provide the platform for it to become "the new umbrella organisation for all combat sport". It was set up last year with the aim of creating a union to safeguard fighters' futures. The GFA says it wants to campaign for fair contracts and better pay, insurance and pensions, proper health and safety standards and somewhere for fighters to report problems to an official channel. It points to public fundraisers in recent months which have helped fighters such as Lee Reeves pay for emergency care after serious injuries. Smith, who challenged three times for a super-middleweight world title before his retirement in 2017, says it is a "failing" of the system when fighters like Reeves have to raise money to pay for recovery. "Every week, somewhere in this sport, a fighter is hurt, exploited or forgotten, and the only safety net is whatever the boxing community can scrape together after the fact," said Smith. "That's not a system. That's a failing. We are not aware of anyone, ever, who has properly invested the time and resources to get under the bonnet of this sport, work out exactly where it is failing fighters, and publish actionable recommendations to fix it." The GFA says it has secured respected barrister Jonathan Caplan KC to lead the process of conducting the inquiry, which will look into the "safety, governance and treatment of combat sports participants at all levels", from grassroots to professional. He will be tasked with producing a report back on the evidence and testimonies gathered. The GFA is a non-profit organisation and is aiming to raise £500,000 to fund the inquiry via a crowdfunding campaign. Chair designate Simon Bazalgette says the group wants to provide fighters with the same support available to athletes in other sports. "Over the last decade or so, professional sports such as rugby, football and horse racing have raised their game when it comes to the welfare of the participants," said Bazalgette. "It is striking that combat sport is one of the last workplaces with no professional representation for its workers, meaning little protection, no minimum health and safety standard, no independent pension scheme, no insurance floor, and no single body a fighter can turn to when something goes wrong. "The GFA has been formed to rectify this, to help the sport create a stronger bond of trust with its participants and its audience, and thereby give a stronger foundation for growth." Earlier this month, British mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter Michael 'Venom' Page urged fighters to form a union to campaign for better pay. He pointed to the Muhammad Ali Act - a 2000 US law designed to protect boxers' rights and combat potential monopolies - as something he would like to replicate in MMA. UFC president Dana White has been spearheading a push to amend the act - a move which GFA acting general secretary Paul Maloney says should cause alarm bells in fighters. "It's the one piece of legislation anywhere in the world that gives fighters a level of workplace protection, and it's currently being rewritten in a way critics say favours the promoters and networks that already hold most of the power," said Maloney. "If it can be stripped back there, it can happen anywhere else that lacks its own independent, respected voice for fighters - which is exactly why the GFA exists." title: Hearts chairman calls for greater transparency on key decisions
description: Reflecting on last season's final-day title disappointment, Hearts chairman Calum Paterson calls for "greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football".
content: Hearts chairman calls for greater transparency on key decisions Image source, SNS Image caption, Hearts lost a final-day decider at Celtic Park after leading the way for most of last season Published 26 October 2026 Heart of Midlothian chairman Calum Paterson is calling for "greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football". Talking to club media to mark his first year in the post, Paterson spoke with pride about coming so close to a first title in 66 years, but also voiced frustration around how last season's thrilling climax unfolded. The Edinburgh side topped the Premiership table for 250 days but finished two points behind Celtic after a dramatic final-day defeat in Glasgow. Lawrence Shankland struck first for the visitors, only for the reigning champions to find two late goals for a 3-1 victory, sparking a pitch invasion from jubilant home fans and a hasty exit for the beaten challengers, who expressed safety fears. "The final week was difficult on a number of fronts," said Paterson. "Among other things we were disappointed by the unprecedented decision that as the team leading the league at the time of the split had to play our final game away from home. "The circumstances at the end of that game were, from our perspective, completely unacceptable. "We took advice and made our concerns very clear to the football authorities. Standing back from it all we'd like to see greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football. "Standards and processes matter, particularly at important points in the season and there's room for improvement." The SPFL did explain their scheduling in April, with Celtic due three home matches post-split to Hearts' two. City derbies are ruled out on the final day for public safety reasons, which meant the league body was unable to have both Glasgow or Edinburgh sides play at home on the final two fixture dates. Having come so close to ending four decades of Old Firm dominance, Paterson added: "The way it ended was really disappointing, especially after everything the players and staff had put into it. "I think they deserved a better outcome, but we should recognise and pay tribute to them for what they did achieve, which was actually exceptional." Paterson addressed frustration surrounding the club's communication in the aftermath, stressing that it should have been clearer. "The supporters should know that we did everything we could to stand up for Hearts and we haven't forgotten what happened last season," he continued. "Our focus now has to be on putting Hearts in the best position for this season and beyond and communicating better along the way." Investment talks & CEO search Paterson also spoke of the search for increased investment at Tynecastle, where Brighton owner Tony Bloom is a high-profile investor. "We've had some discussions and those are going well," he said. "I don't want to get ahead of them but if they do conclude successfully, that would be another positive step for Hearts. "The purpose would be to build a stronger football club fundamentally and to ensure we have resources in place to pursue our ambitions. "At the same time we're continuing to develop a player trading model which we expect to become an increasingly important contributor to the club's long term financial sustainability." On the search for a new chief executive to replace Andrew McKinlay who departed in August, Paterson said there are "very strong candidates in the process".
