title: Japan indicts U.S. Marine on murder charge over woman's killing
description: Police arrested Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, on suspicion of strangling Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel.
content: Crime U.S. Marine indicted on murder charge over woman's killing in Japan Updated on: October 26, 2026 / 7:13 AM EDT / CBS/AFP Add CBS News on Google Japanese prosecutors have indicted a U.S. Marine on suspicion of murdering a woman on Okinawa, a court spokesman told AFP on Monday, in a case that prompted public outrage. The alleged killing of the 39-year-old Japanese woman caused Japan's premier to slam the "heinous crime" and reignited controversy over the heavy U.S. military presence on the southern island. "The case was indicted on October 25," said the spokesman for the court in Naha, confirming media reports that the suspect had been indicted on charges of murder and robbery. Okinawa prefectural police said they arrested Lance Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who is stationed at Futenma Air Station, on suspicion of strangling Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in the island's capital city of Naha. The Yomiuri Shimbun reported that, according to the indictment document, the suspect allegedly strangled the woman from Naha in a hotel with a telephone cord on Oct. 3. He is also accused of stealing a backpack containing the woman's wallet and other belongings, the newspaper said. The Marine denied the allegations at the time of his arrest but has now made statements that imply some involvement in the case, the Yomiuri and other media said, citing investigative sources. U.S. Marine Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard leaves a police station to be sent to prosecutors over the killing of a Japanese woman in Naha, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, Oct. 5, 2026. Kyodo/via REUTERS Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-runs and drunk driving by U.S. military personnel have long triggered protests on the southern Japanese island, which has for years urged other regions in the country to share the burden of hosting U.S. troops. Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi has said that officials were reviewing the off-base code of conduct for U.S. troops in Japan following the alleged killing. The high-level bilateral consultations will examine off-duty conduct and the "liberty" policy governing off-base private activities of U.S. military personnel, he said. "We plan to hold discussions including whether the existing rules are effectively functioning," Motegi said, adding that "matters such as patrols and curfew management" would be under review in talks with the United States. The existing policy, updated in 2024 following a string of sexual assaults by U.S. military personnel in Okinawa, includes a ban on U.S. military personnel drinking in public off base between 1 a.m. and 5 a.m. or going to bars during those hours. The U.S. military enacted a two-day operational pause after the Marine's arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a month-long curfew. Previous incidents have strained relations Crimes committed by U.S. personnel have been a thorn in relations between the close security allies. The number of arrests related to U.S. service members and their families exceeded 100 last year, according to prefectural police. Last year, a Japanese court sentenced a U.S. Marine accused of choking and attempting to rape a woman in her 20s to seven years in prison. In 2017, a former U.S. Marine and civilian military base worker was sentenced to life in prison for the rape and murder of a local woman in Okinawa. The same year, U.S. Forces Japan banned all personnel from consuming alcohol after an intoxicated U.S. Marine crashed his vehicle into a mini-truck, killing its 61-year-old local driver. In Japan, once a suspect is formally indicted, the conviction rate stands at more than 99%. The justice ministry says the near-perfect rates are because prosecutors only pursue airtight cases, they are confident about winning. Why are so many bases concentrated in Okinawa? Okinawa was under U.S. occupation from World War II until 1972. Today Okinawa hosts 70% of America's military facilities and most of the 54,000 U.S. troops based in Japan today, despite comprising just 0.6% of Japan's landmass. In the wake of World War II, Japan regained its sovereignty under the San Francisco Peace Treaty of 1952, but Okinawa remained under American control, making it a hub of U.S. military build-up. The 1972 return of Okinawa's sovereignty to Japan did little to diminish the number of U.S. bases on the island, leading to the disproportionate burden it is saddled with today. title: Woman, 93, outwits scammer, helps get him arrested, police say
description: A 93-year-old woman in western Japan outsmarted a suspected scammer by pretending to fall for the scheme and helping police arrest him at her home, an officer said.
content: Crime Woman, 93, outwits would-be scammer, helps get him arrested, police say October 26, 2026 / 6:22 AM EDT / AFP Add CBS News on Google A 93-year-old woman in western Japan outsmarted a suspected scammer by pretending to fall for the scheme and helping police arrest him at her home, a police official told AFP on Monday. Japan has the second-oldest population in the world after Monaco, and senior citizens are often targeted by fraudsters, who last year collectively stole around 325.7 billion yen ($2.0 billion) from their victims. The woman, who lives in the Shiga region, received telephone calls from Wednesday through Thursday last week from a man who claimed to be a police officer. The caller falsely informed her that her bank account had experienced an unauthorized withdrawal. The woman was told to give her ATM card to a man, posing as a police officer, who would visit her so authorities could verify her account. Suspecting a scam, the woman consulted her son and the police as she waited for the man to visit her house. "The person's family reached out to the police on Wednesday evening, and we were able to have officers at her house" before the scammer arrived on Thursday, a local police official told AFP on the customary condition of anonymity. When a 47-year-old man appeared at her doorstep, waiting officers arrested him on the spot, the police official said. "The person (the woman) is someone in good health and highly articulate," the official said, while urging other elderly residents to consult family members when they suspect fraud. title: Trump attacks El-Sayed over his faith, calls him "jihadist"
description: President Trump is making his case for Republican candidates in Michigan; he spoke at a rally in Port Huron on Sunday ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
content: Politics Trump attacks El-Sayed over his faith during Michigan rally, calls him "jihadist" By Nicholas Lentz Updated on: October 26, 2026 / 4:36 AM EDT / CBS Detroit Add CBS News on Google President Trump is making his case for Republican candidates in Michigan. He spoke at a rally in Port Huron on Sunday ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. During his speech at McMorran Place, the president said Michigan was built by "American patriots who shed their blood, sweat and tears." He praised Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, as "one of the most respected men in Washington" and targeted Rogers' Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed. "I'm here to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator," Mr. Trump said. CBS News Detroit has reached out to El-Sayed's campaign for comment on the president's visit and Mr. Trump calling El-Sayed a "jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member," but has yet to hear back. At a town hall meeting earlier this month in Caro, Michigan, a man asked the U.S. Senate nominee whether he would disavow the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed said "absolutely." Rogers and El-Sayed clashed on Wednesday during their second, and final debate in Southfield, Michigan. Mr. Trump also voiced support for Republican gubernatorial candidate John James, saying he would "fight for jobs" and "lower prices." In response to the president's visit, Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said, in part, "By standing with Donald Trump today, Mike Rogers, John James, and Michigan Republicans made it clear they are fully endorsing and ready to rubber stamp Trump's toxic agenda." On Saturday, former President Barack Obama was in Detroit to drum up support for El-Sayed, Democratic nominee for Michigan governor Jocelyn Benson and other candidates for state office. El-Sayed appeared at a rally with Sen. Bernie Sanders at the DeVos Performance Hall in Grand Rapids on Sunday evening. Sanders said Mr. Trump and his allies were using Islamophobia because they have "nothing to say" about the issues most important to working people, such as health care, housing and income inequality. "All they can do is foment hatred and divisiveness," Sanders said. Vice President JD Vance is set to stump for Republicans at CHI Aviation in Howell, Michigan, on Tuesday. title: Jordan says 3 arrested in deadly attack on Greek Orthodox church
description: Jordan says its security forces arrested three men Monday for an attack on a Greek Orthodox church that killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen.
content: World Jordan says 3 arrested in deadly attack on Greek Orthodox church October 26, 2026 / 3:10 AM EDT / CBS/AP Add CBS News on Google Amman, Jordan — Jordanian security forces arrested three men Monday for an attack on a Greek Orthodox church that killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen. The Public Security Directorate said the three suspects were arrested following a dawn shootout and that all three were wounded. No members of the security forces were injured in the dawn operation in Karak governorate, south of Jordan's capital, Amman. Karak is home to a minority Christian population. The attack on the Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak took place Friday during a funeral. Three men were reported to have taken part in the attack. Some 3,000 people attended a funeral on Oct. 25, 2026 for victims of a terrorist attack two days earlier at a Greek Orthodox church in Hammoud, Jordan. Salah Malkawi / Getty Images There was still no claim of responsibility, and no armed group has been accused of the attack. Jordan's Interior Minister, Mazen Al-Faraya, identified the three men as those responsible for the attack. "The security services have fulfilled their duties, resulting in the capture of those who carried out this terrorist act," he said in a phone interview with state TV Al-Mamlaka. "They put up fierce resistance against the security forces, but were ultimately subdued and taken into custody, having sustained severe injuries." A bloodstain is seen in Saint George's Greek Orthodox Church, where gunmen opened fire during a funeral on Oct. 23, 2026 in the village of Hammoud, in Karak governorate in Jordan. Alaa Al Sukhni / REUTERS He added that there "are three individuals involved; they were identified early on in the wake of the terrorist incident, and the security services employed all the means at their disposal to apprehend them." The directorate said, "Terrorism has no place among us," and that the three had met their "just fate," according to the Reuters news agency. The directorate didn't name the suspects or point to any possible links to any Islamist militant groups, Reuters added. King Abdullah II directed authorities to respond with "an iron fist" against what he called the outlaws of Islam and anyone attempting to undermine the unity of the Jordanian people. title: Eric Bauza, actor who voiced Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies at 46
description: Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning actor who voiced iconic "Looney Tunes" characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, died on Sunday, according to his manager. He was 46.
content: Local News Eric Bauza, actor who voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and other cartoon characters, dies at 46 By Dean Fioresi Dean Fioresi Web Producer, CBS Los Angeles Dean Fioresi is a web producer for CBS Los Angeles. He covers breaking news throughout Southern California. When he's not writing about local events, he enjoys focusing on sports and entertainment. Read Full Bio Dean Fioresi Updated on: October 26, 2026 / 7:54 PM PDT / CBS LA Add CBS News on Google Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning actor who voiced iconic "Looney Tunes" characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, died on Sunday, according to his manager. He was 46. "Eric was a unique and versatile voice actor who was loved by everyone he knew and worked with," said Judy Coppage, Bauza's manager. "His sudden passing is a shock to all of us, and he will be deeply missed. It's a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and his fans." Bauza, who was born in Canada, died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. His family posted a brief statement on his Instagram page, adding that more details would come later. Bauza had more than 400 acting credits listed on his IMDb page. In addition to voicing Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, Bauza is credited with voicing other "Looney Tunes" characters such as Porky Pig, Pepé Le Pew, Marvin the Martian, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Tweety Bird and Road Runner. He also voiced characters in the most recent "Space Jam" film, alongside LeBron James. Beyond "Looney Tunes," Bauza was known for his voice work on shows such as "Avatar: The Last Airbender," "Puss in Boots," "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles," "Woody Woodpecker," "Bob's Burgers" and "Teen Titans Go!" A statement from Warner Bros. Chairman Channing Dungey and Warner Bros. Pictures Animation President and CCO Bill Damaschke noted Bauza's impact on the "Looney Tunes" franchise. "Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. During his 15 years at Warner Bros. Animation, he was the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck among countless other characters. He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc," the statement said. "Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life. In addition to his incredible talent, Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones." Bauza won Children's and Family Emmy Awards in 2022, 2023 and 2025 and was nominated in 2026. He was also nominated for five Daytime Emmy Awards from 2016 to 2021. He joined CBS LA in August to discuss his latest film and the newest "Looney Tunes" installment, "Coyote vs. Acme." "All of my work is based off of the original voiceover artist, the great Mel Blanc; he was the original. I like to call him the blueprint of these characters," Bauza said. "They're not just voices; these are personalities that we've been familiar with now for 90 years — it's like your oldest family members. So, that's my history with them." Bauza said his favorite character to voice was Bugs Bunny, but as he got older, he felt more like Daffy Duck.
